papers.title: Nonperturbative theory of thin-vapor-layer linear optical properties: towards the optimal design of alkali-metal vapor nanocells
papers.abstract: Hot alkali-metal vapors confined inside nanometer-thick spectroscopic cells are highly suitable media for miniature and cheap frequency standards, magnetometers and atomic sensors. Yet, their linear optical properties in case of low to moderate atomic densities are not fully understood. The primary reason for that is the complex, strongly nonlocal optical response of such systems to the incident resonant radiation arising as the result of the free motion of atoms and their collisions with the walls. To date, calculations of reflection and transmission spectra of these cells has been restricted to perturbation theory in atomic density for the case of quenching atom-wall collisions, which substantially limited the scope of their practical applications. Here we introduce the rigorous numerical approach for computing thin-vapor-layer spectra with an accurate account for the nonlocal optical response at arbitrary optical density and layer thickness. Our model predicts a density-dependent blue shift of the resonance that is absent in the first-order perturbative description. We show that its values are comparable to the natural linewidth of an atomic transition and, therefore, too large to be neglected in most use cases. Inspired by recent experiments, we then explore a wide range of vapor layer thicknesses and study how the reflectivity and its derivative with respect to the laser detuning depend on the layer thickness. Finally, we derive an approximate expression for the thickness at which the first derivative of the reflectivity reaches its maximum that agrees closely with the rigorous numerical model and reduces to the first-order analytical result. These results provide a practical design tool for nanometer-thick spectroscopic cells in different applications as well as a starting point for further development of the theory.

authors.name: Andrei V. Ermolaev
authors.institution: Franche-Comté Électronique Mécanique Thermique et Optique - Sciences et Technologies

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Conditional Code in Android Apps
papers.abstract:
Android OS runs on a highly diverse set of devices, spanning entry-level phones and flagships with substantially different hardware characteristics, including memory capacity, processors, displays, cameras, and sensors. Through APIs, apps can query device information at runtime, such as memory, hardware features, and manufacturer, among other device properties, allowing developers to execute different code paths on different devices. Existing studies cover only specific compatibility bugs or brand-specific behavior; however, the broader use of hardware information in app logic has not been comprehensively explored.
  We address this question with a large-scale empirical study of hardware-related if statements in Android apps. We statically analyze 50,000 apps to identify the if statements whose conditions depend on the values of hardware-related APIs, and extract their conditions together with the code of their branches. Our results show that 95% of successfully analyzed apps contain at least one such statement, with an average of 74 per app, which suggests that hardware-related logic is widespread. We then apply an LLM-assisted open-coding process to the extracted code to build a structured taxonomy of the purposes behind hardware-related conditional code. The resulting characterization shows that developers use hardware information for feature availability checks, UI adaptation, emulator detection, device tiering, and resource management, among others.

papers.title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
papers.abstract: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. Unlike the equilibrium case, reversibility out of equilibrium imposes a stringent condition: the accumulated dynamical phase must be an integer multiple of $2\pi$, i.e., $\Delta\phi = 2\omega_{0} s(T) = 2n\pi$, where $\omega_{0}$ is the initial trapping frequency and $s(T)$ is the rescaled time after a total evolution time $T$. We demonstrate the reversibility of an initial nonequilibrium state in an isotropic unitary Fermi gas by driving the optical trap through a round trip. We find two types of reversible pathways, the space-time scaling-invariant and polynomial shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) protocols. The phase condition restricts the round-trip time $T$ to discrete values, a distinguishing feature of nonequilibrium dynamics. Our work establishes a clear criterion for the quantum control of nonequilibrium many-body systems beyond linear response and provides practical pathways to reversibility.

authors.name: Kaijun Jiang
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Multi-Turn Semantic Caching for Low-Cost LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Semantic caching lowers the cost of serving large language models (LLMs) by reusing stored responses for similar requests. In multi-turn conversations, whether a cached response is acceptable depends on both conversations' histories, which embedding similarity of requests and histories predicts poorly (AUC 0.62--0.74 on five workloads). We therefore learn the \emph{reuse risk}, the probability that a cached response is unacceptable, from judge feedback, and choose a budgeted set of conversation states to cache by weighing the generation cost a reuse avoids against a price for unacceptable reuse. We propose CUCB-SC-MT, which learns a cache from logged conversations with a suboptimality guarantee, and CLCB-LS-MT, which learns online and has $\tilde O(\sqrt N)$ regret over $N$ requests when conversation states recur. On math-tutoring (SocraTeach) and movie-ticketing (Taskmaster-3) conversations, both achieve lower loss than prior semantic caching approaches: ContextCache, multi-turn variants of ElastiCache and vCache, and single-turn semantic caching at every cache budget. With 1,000 cache entries, CLCB-LS-MT avoids 35--41\% of the generation cost through acceptable reuses, against at most 22--25\% for the baselines, and lowers estimated serving latency by 19--35\%.

papers.title: Channel Estimation for Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces with Mutual Coupling
papers.abstract: Channel estimation for stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) has relied on the cascade model, which ignores mutual coupling and inter-layer reflection. Under a coupling-consistent multiport model, we show that the pilots are linear in the unknown channel segments and derive least-squares and linear minimum-mean-square-error estimators, an identifiability condition and an exact error decomposition for the reactance training schedule, and a gradient-based schedule design. Cascade-based estimation floors above $0$~dB normalized error at practical layer spacings and collapses the sum rate below that of the bare feed, whereas the proposed estimators retain about $80\%$ of the perfect-channel-knowledge sum rate.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits and Joint Design for Monostatic Joint Communications and Sensing in LEO Satellites
papers.abstract: Monostatic joint communication and sensing (JCAS) from a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite requires full-duplex (FD) operation, with self-interference (SI) $80$--$100$~dB stronger than the ground echo. The echo returns milliseconds after transmission, whereas the onboard coupling spans a few symbols. We develop a theory and a design that exploit this separation. Restricting the analog and digital cancellers to the short SI support is without loss of optimality and essential in practice: a least-squares canceller whose support contains the target delay absorbs the coherent echo and reduces the radar SINR by a closed-form factor, about $18$~dB for a vessel at its zero-Doppler crossing. Modeling the SI that no linear canceller can reconstruct as spatially white and accounting for ADC quantization, we derive in closed form a ceiling on the radar SINR, the minimum pre-ADC SI power under a canceller tap budget, the budget for full cancellation, and the sensing weight at which the optimal design changes over from communication to sensing. We then maximize a weighted sum of the communication and sensing SINRs, each normalized by its half-duplex benchmark, over the beamformers, sensing covariance, combiners, and cancellers for $K$ users and $Q$ targets, using an alternating algorithm with closed-form updates. Simulations confirm the closed forms. The joint design gains up to $13\%$ in the normalized objective over a sequential design that cancels the SI only at the receiver, and more than $10$~dB of downlink and radar SINR with $4$-bit ADCs and in the 10th-percentile worst-target SINR of four targets, whereas ignoring the SI overloads the ADCs.

papers.title: Topological Defect Statistics in a Weakly First-Order Phase Transition
papers.abstract: The celebrated Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) characterizes the nonequilibrium dynamics of second-order phase transitions and predicts universal scaling of the average number of defects with the quench time. However, the KZM is not directly applicable to first-order phase transitions, where defect formation is instead governed by nucleation processes. Here, using a Ginzburg-Landau model, we investigate the defect-number statistics in a weakly first-order phase transition. We show that the resulting statistics contain signatures of both Kibble-Zurek dynamics and nucleation, revealing the interplay between these two defect-formation mechanisms. In particular, we find that the defect-number distribution evolves from approximately Gaussian to nearly Poissonian across the crossover from the KZM regime to nucleation-dominated defect formation. While the first two cumulants are well described by a simple additive estimate of the KZM and nucleation contributions, the third cumulant exhibits a plateau and an enhancement beyond this estimate, providing a sensitive probe of the interplay between the two defect-formation mechanisms.

papers.title: Local Zero-Shot Latency Prediction for Low-End GPUs
papers.abstract: Quantifying execution latency is an important consideration across Machine Learning. Existing latency-prediction approaches typically train ML models on traces collected from workload execution on target hardware. Collection of representative traces across many consumer GPUs is expensive both in organizing the devices and in manpower, causing existing work to mainly focus on a limited set of high-end GPUs available in cloud computing. To offset this cost, we show that a local host GPU can be configured to reproduce the execution performance of less powerful target GPUs. Through selectively modifying device parameters, we obtain locally measured latencies that closely approximate those observed on the target hardware. We reformulate the latency-prediction task: instead of fitting a prediction model to a dataset of execution traces, we identify local configurations that best reproduce target devices' performance, enabling zero-shot prediction. We evaluate our approach against real measurements from 60 computer-vision models executed on 21 consumer GPU models. Our method achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 14.21%, compared with more than 25% for comparable baselines, reducing relative prediction error by 43.6%. Predicted and measured latencies exhibit an average Spearman correlation of 0.961 across training tasks, demonstrating that the method also accurately preserves performance rankings across devices.

papers.title: TopoQuant: Topological Framework to Characterize Behavioral Shifts in Quantized Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the com putational cost of large language models (LLMs), but it can introduce internal structural and behavioral changes that are not captured by traditional metrics such as accuracy and per plexity. We present TopoQuant, a topological framework that uses topological data analysis (TDA) to quantify structural drift in self-attention weights and relate it to behavioral changes in quantized LLMs. Across four LLM families and multiple quantization levels, we show that topological drift remains stable at moderate compression levels but increases sharply below 4 bit precision, closely tracking declines in attention agreement. Our results reveal a strong relationship between topological drift and attention agreement, indicating that structural changes in model parameters closely reflect behavioral degradation under quantization. We further demonstrate that topological features can accurately predict attention consistency using lightweight machine learning models, achieving R2 scores of up to 0.85. Predicting attention agreement enables efficient assessment of be havioral consistency in quantized LLMs, allowing quantization induced degradation to be detected without running expensive downstream tasks. The results indicate that topological drift pro vides an efficient early-warning signal for quantization-induced degradation and can help identify safe compression limits without extensive downstream evaluation.

authors.name: Lorenz Sparrenberg
authors.institution: Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Rafet Sifa
authors.institution: Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Artificial signal injection into real data is a key tool in time-domain radio astronomy, with particular import to the study of pulsars and Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). Many surveys inject into the time series to probe observational biases impacting the detection of radio transients. In the case of the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stack Search (CHAMPSS), the computational demands of both hardware and software time series injections force an alternative approach. We present methods for injecting artificial pulsar signals into the Fourier power spectrum. The injection process detailed here is computationally negligible compared to the overhead of the CHAMPSS search pipeline. We use injections to probe the in-system biases of the CHAMPSS survey. CHAMPSS is most sensitive to pulsars with frequencies on the order of 0.1 - 100 Hz and fluxes > 1 mJy. Our injections show weak overall sensitivity dependence on other factors such as dispersion measure (DM), duty cycle, and sky coordinates, but complex non-monotonic interactions between all parameters. Our findings suggest that frequency-dependent noise, especially low-frequency or "red" noise, and sampling limitations at higher frequencies are the dominant extrinsic factors decreasing CHAMPSS' sensitivity to pulsars.

authors.name: Robert Main
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

papers.title: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons
papers.abstract: In solid-state physics, the ability to open and tune an electronic energy gap provides a direct route to controlling charge transport and accessing distinct electronic phases. In solids with physical boundaries, a bulk energy gap formed exclusively by extended bulk states is conventionally expected to be governed primarily by the interior bulk region, with only a minor contribution from the boundaries. Here we show that, in stark contrast to this conventional expectation, the bulk gap of armchair graphene nanoribbons in the $N_w=3p+2$ family with $p\in\mathbb{Z}\ge 0$ can be fully controlled through the hoppings solely at the boundaries. This full boundary control originates from an exact cancellation between the gap contributions of long-range hoppings along and across the ribbon in the bulk region. It persists in the presence of Hubbard interactions and holds irrespective of ribbon width in this family. Our findings establish boundary dynamics as an unexpectedly powerful means of manipulating bulk electronic properties, enabling width-preserving engineering of one-dimensional (1D) band structures and topological phases, with potential applications in qubits, artificial quantum spin chains, topological quantum dots and other quantum devices.

authors.name: Lin Wang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
papers.abstract: We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657-0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657-0406A is in a long-period ($P_b \sim 37$ days) and eccentric ($e \sim 0.12$) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance $\dot{\omega} = 0.00090(13)$ degrees per year, which implies a total system mass of $2.5(6)$ solar masses, assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

authors.name: Lijing Shao
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

authors.name: Yujie Lian
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

papers.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.abstract: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$\beta$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$\beta$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$\beta$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

authors.name: Shivangi Pandey
authors.institution: Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences

authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

papers.title: Unconfoundedness as an Information Constraint
papers.abstract: This paper provides an information-theoretic characterization of unconfoundedness within a general class of models allowing for endogenous selection. We impose a conditional mutual information (CMI) restriction requiring that the information about treatment contained in a potential outcome, conditional on covariates, does not exceed that contained in its latent heterogeneity. Under the maintained model conditions, this restriction is equivalent to a multiplicative factorization of treatment probabilities into separate functions of latent heterogeneity and covariates. Although the CMI restriction permits endogenous selection, sufficiently rich variation in treatment probabilities across covariate values makes it equivalent to unconfoundedness for the corresponding potential outcome. For binary treatments, any nonconstant propensity score suffices; for multiple treatments, a full-rank condition on the second-moment matrix of the propensity-score vector is sufficient. State-specific restrictions bound residual selection and imply exogeneity for individual treatment states under boundary-support conditions. Extensions cover continuous treatments and instrument exogeneity.

papers.title: Agent-Based Disruption Simulation on an Edge-Level Product-Annotated Supply Network of the Automotive Industry
papers.abstract: Disruptions spread through supply networks when customers cannot replace the products they lose. We ask how portfolio-overlap and product-specific rules for selecting candidate suppliers change cascades when customers search for new suppliers and form new supply edges. From the MarkLines database, we construct a product-annotated network of about 77,000 firms and 197,000 supplier-customer edges in the global automotive industry. We extend an agent-based disruption model with edge-level products, a product-specific substitution rule based on the semantic similarity of product names, and calibrated capacities and inventories. Only 6% of the edges carry observed products. We impute the others and test the imputation against the annotated edges. We run 119,000 simulations. With all other mechanics fixed, the product-specific rule makes the cascades after a hub failure four to five times larger than the portfolio-overlap rule of the original model. Under alternative imputations and similarity thresholds, the factor ranges from 1.2 to 18. Within the simulations, substitutability also shapes which suppliers are critical. Network topology largely determines which firms a shock reaches, and substitutability determines how many of them fail. Of the 50 most damaging suppliers under random disruptions, topology alone identifies 20 and an index that adds product substitutability identifies 32. The index carries over without refitting to a regional scenario modelled on the 2011 Tohoku Earthquake. Supply network risk assessment should account for product-level substitutability and therefore needs product data on supply relationships.

authors.name: Sebastian Lang
authors.institution: Fraunhofer Institute for Factory Operation and Automation

papers.title: The maximum concentration of results in incomplete round-robin tournaments
papers.abstract: The Herfindahl--Hirschman Index (HHI), a standard measure of market concentration, is widely used to quantify competitive balance in sports tournaments. To enable comparisons over time or across leagues, both its minimum and maximum should be known. The minimum is usually trivial. Our paper provides results on the maximum HHI in incomplete round-robin tournaments, where the set of matches is represented by a regular but not complete undirected graph. We prove that the lower bound of maximum HHI is reached when the tournament consists of independent round-robin groups, while the upper bound of maximum HHI is reached when the set of matches is represented by a bipartite graph. Maximising HHI is computationally difficult even for highly structured graph types corresponding to real-world tournaments, where the teams are partitioned into pots and play the same number of matches against opponents from every pot. The complexity of the problem does not depend on the scoring system or the number of opponents from a pot.

papers.title: Wideband Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) for Frequency-Flat and Frequency-Selective Processing
papers.abstract: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) has been proposed as an analog processing architecture to perform efficient computation in the microwave domain. Consisting of reconfigurable impedance networks, a MiLAC can extract many of the gains of large multi-antenna systems without costly digital processing, e.g., achieving capacity in narrowband multiple-input single-output (MISO). However, the behavior of wideband MiLAC, required to support high data-rate transmissions, is widely unknown. The impedance components of MiLACs have non-trivial frequency-dependent response, requiring specific implementations to characterize it. In this work, we consider MiLAC implementations based on LC resonators with tunable capacitance, which allow synthesizing near-arbitrary passive lossless impedance matrices at individual frequencies using inductors and varactors. We characterize the mapping between optimal MISO precoding at a reference frequency, and the vector of capacitances configuring the MiLAC. We derive the degrees of freedom (DoFs) remaining after fixing such optimum precoding at the reference frequency, and show that these DoFs can be exploited to tune the frequency response of the MiLAC. We propose two techniques to exploit these DoFs: a closed-form approach for frequency-flat MiLAC processing, and a numerical approach for multi-frequency MiLAC processing, optimizing processing at frequencies other than the reference one. The frequency-flat approach shows satisfactory performance in a simulated frequency-flat millimeter-wave scenario, approaching the performance of digital processing. The multi-frequency approach can adapt to the frequency-selectivity of a simulated sub-6GHz scenario, attaining gains over frequency-flat digital processing. This constitutes the first demonstration that realistic MiLAC implementations can be configured to perform independent computations at different frequencies.

papers.title: A Data-Driven, Gain-Scheduled Equivalent Circuit for the B-H Behavior of Power Ferrites
papers.abstract: An equivalent circuit for the dynamic B-H behavior of power ferrites is identified from measured transients. It consists of classical elements of hysteresis modeling: a nonlinear inductor for the reversible curve, six viscous play branches (inductors in series with diode-bridge sliders) that form a Prandtl-Ishlinskii model, two R-L branches for the magnetic after-effect, a mean-field feedback of H as in the Jiles-Atherton model, and a measurement path. All elements are positive apart from the feedback sources, and the circuit can run in SPICE. Discretized at the sampling step, the circuit is a difference equation with 32 parameters per material, fitted by backpropagation through time. On the 15 materials of the MagNet Challenge 2, the mean sequence relative error is 7.33 % against 7.77 % for the challenge-winning recurrent network with 336 parameters, and the circuit is more accurate on 12 of the 15 materials. The accuracy can be scaled up by gain scheduling, where a small network per material sets the element values at every step from the excitation, while the hysteresis memory stays in the circuit, such that the error drops to 5.25 % with 656 parameters per material. Thus, an interpretable model is demonstrated that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy.

papers.title: NIR: Approximate Neural Instance Retrieval for ALCIQ
papers.abstract: Instance retrieval is the main bottleneck of concept-learning systems based on refinement operators. We present NIR, a family of neural instance retrievers for ALCIQ that output graded membership scores from knowledge graph embeddings. We compare tokenization-based encoders (GRU, LSTM, Transformer) with a Compositional encoder that mirrors DL operators via primitive sub-networks. On eight benchmarks, all variants approximate Pellet closely on complete knowledge bases, while the Transformer model is most robust under incompleteness. The source code of our approach is at https://github.com/dice-group/owlapy.

papers.title: Bg-Mix: On Using Image Backgrounds for Data Augmentation in Electron Microscopy Images
papers.abstract: Electron microscopy (EM) serves as a cornerstone in virology enabling the visualization of viral particles and is widely used in research, diagnostics and morphological characterization of pathogens. Computer-assisted image analysis can help facilitate and speed up this labor-intensive method, however, typical EM virus datasets are small and sparsely labeled, resulting in a lack of readily available deep learning models due to training limitations. To overcome data shortages and leverage content-rich, diverse sample backgrounds, we employed background-based data augmentation. To this end, we propose Bg-Mix, a form of data augmentation method, which decomposes training images into foreground objects and backgrounds and subsequently rearranges both into novel augmented images. This not only enhances the performance of object detection models but also increases the diversity of the training data. Using Bg-Mix provides an increase between +0.8 and +3.3 box mean average precision (mAP) points over the baseline when tested across two datasets using two architectures, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness.

papers.title: Kinematic analysis of the TNG50 Milky Way and Andromeda analogues
papers.abstract: We investigate whether Ogorodnikov-Milne (O-M) parameters can serve as kinematic tracers of spiral structure in four Milky Way- and Andromeda-like disc galaxies from the TNG50-1 simulation at z=0. Stellar particles are analysed in disc-aligned reference frames, with velocities referenced to the mass-weighted mean stellar velocity within one stellar half-mass radius. Local O-M fits on a regular grid yield centroid velocities and the components of the velocity-gradient tensor, characterising local deformation and rotation. We compare their spatial distributions with stellar surface-density and relative overdensity maps and examine the influence of parameter uncertainties. The galaxies exhibit diverse coherent kinematic patterns. Features selected using the generalised Oort constants A, B, and C+K display partial correspondence with stellar overdensities, depending on the galaxy and the adopted centroid-selection criteria. For TNG50-456326, a galaxy-specific selection enables us to fit four logarithmic spiral branches and determine their geometrical parameters. Their morphology suggests two principal arms and two secondary branches. We compare the fitted spirals with stellar- and gas-mass overdensity and radial velocity maps and examine the spatial relationship between the identified stellar structures and the gas distribution. Qualitative similarities to the morphology and kinematic patterns of the Milky Way make TNG50-456326 a promising candidate for further investigation as a kinematic analogue. Our results support the use of local O-M parameters as complementary diagnostics of non-axisymmetric disc structure, while highlighting the need for galaxy-specific selection criteria.

authors.name: S. I. Denyshchenko
authors.institution: V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University

authors.name: D. V. Odynets
authors.institution: V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University

papers.title: RESONATE: a Real Social Navigation Testbed for Autonomous Service Robots
papers.abstract: Social navigation is essential for autonomous service robots operating in human environments, but progress remains constrained by the lack of extensive real-world benchmarks. This paper presents the Real Social Navigation Testbed (RESONATE), a reproducible benchmark for human-aware navigation based on a unified robotic platform, a shared ROS 2 software stack, precise trajectory ground truth, and structured social interaction scenarios. We evaluate eight controller configurations, combining classical and predictive local planners with different social modeling strategies, over eight representative scenarios with five repetitions each, yielding 320 physical experiments. The benchmark combines quantitative navigation and social metrics with participant-based qualitative assessments to jointly measure efficiency, safety, comfort, and perceived social behavior. Results reveal scenario-dependent trade-offs among the tested methods. The algorithms that stands out for their performance are the DWA with Gaussian social costmaps for its reliability, and the SFM-MPPI to provide the best balance between robustness, navigation efficiency, and social acceptance. Overall, RESONATE supports the robotics community with a real-world benchmark, reusable baselines, data, and testbed, and a consistent evaluation protocol for advancing socially aware navigation research.

papers.title: From PID to Reinforcement Learning in Building HVAC Control: A Control-Architecture Review of Tuning Strategies, Formulations, and Deployment Trade-offs
papers.abstract: This paper reviews control architectures for building heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, addressing the tension among energy demand, occupant comfort and equipment operability, and situating proportional-integral-derivative (PID) regulation within a layered control stack that also includes rule-based and model-based supervisory control and data-driven reinforcement learning (RL). It examines the thermostat-PID layer from two-position and scheduled setpoint control through proportional, PI and PID regulation and their tuning, then formulates RL for building control as a Markov decision process. Its central contribution is a taxonomy of where RL meets PID: RL as a gain tuner for an existing loop, as a direct replacement for the regulatory controller, as a hybrid with model predictive control, and as supervisory setpoint and schedule generation. Across these classes, the review establishes that the physical loop remains invariant while the intervention point changes, and that the classes differ in their requirements for actuation authority, state information, modelling, commissioning and constraint handling. It further establishes that PID is inexpensive and well codified but limited by nonlinearity, time variation, discrete mode switching, loop interaction and slow plant dynamics, while RL's admissible position must be argued rather than assumed. The paper concludes that these architectures are not competing philosophies of control but nested points of attachment on one HVAC plant, with hybrid implementations possible, and that deployment trade-offs must be assessed according to the specific control interface and scaffolding required.

papers.title: Susceptibility optimization for wisdom of crowds: A social power reformulation and realization framework
papers.abstract: Whether social influence makes a crowd wiser or more biased hinges on who yields to others and who holds firm. Such heterogeneous susceptibilities to social influence, together with the influence network, determine the weight each agent's initial estimate carries in the collective estimate, known as social power. This paper studies susceptibility optimization for maximizing the wisdom of crowds under the Friedkin-Johnsen model. Minimizing the squared collective bias over susceptibilities leads to a nonconvex problem. To overcome this nonconvexity, we develop a social power reformulation and realization framework, which decomposes the problem into two stages: first characterizing the social power that minimizes the collective bias, then determining the susceptibilities that induce such social power. Social power reformulation yields a quadratic program over the probability simplex. Under uniform-sign biases, the optimal social power concentrates on the least biased agents and immediately determines the optimal susceptibilities; under mixed-sign biases, its geometry enables a linear-time construction algorithm. For social power realization, we introduce the notions of susceptibility realizability and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for them, under which we derive all optimal susceptibilities in closed form using the Laplacian pseudoinverse and eigenvector centrality. These results yield a unified algorithm that solves the original problem globally, with worst-case complexity cubic in the number of agents when realizability holds. Finally, we develop a fully distributed implementation with linear communication complexity, illustrating how collective intelligence can emerge from local interactions.

authors.name: Long Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
papers.abstract: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

authors.name: Koustav Banerjee
authors.institution: TH Köln - University of Applied Sciences

authors.name: Kathrin Bringmann
authors.institution: TH Köln - University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Zero-field plasmon splitter: Controlled interaction between quantum anomalous Hall edge states
papers.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect provides chiral edge states without the need for an external magnetic field, but unlike in conventional quantum Hall systems, their trajectories cannot be readily controlled electrostatically. Here, we engineer Coulomb interactions between two spatially separated, counter-propagating QAH edge channels using a floating metallic island. Microwave measurements reveal frequency-dependent redistribution of injected edge plasmons between two output channels, demonstrating interaction-induced hybridization of the collective modes. A long-range interaction model quantitatively reproduces the response and reveals a very low plasmon velocity in the coupling region, strongly reduced by electrostatic screening. Our results establish engineered Coulomb coupling as a route to control collective excitations in QAH edge states and provide a building block for chiral plasmonic circuits and electron quantum optics in magnetic topological insulators.

papers.title: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
papers.abstract: Contingency analysis repeatedly solves the power-flow equations under many single-element outages, an increasingly demanding workload as operating margins tighten and renewable variability grows. Graphics processing units (GPUs) are attractive for this task, but a change in topology alters the sparsity pattern of the Jacobian, preventing the uniform batched factorization on which efficient GPU solvers rely. This paper presents a GPU-parallel Newton--Raphson solver for $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis that separates the change in operating state from the change in topology. A single reference Jacobian is inverted once and reused across all contingencies. Each topology change is expressed as a low-rank Woodbury correction, while the residual state-dependent perturbation is handled by an inner iterative solve, a truncated Neumann series or the biconjugate gradient stabilized method. We analyze the spectral radius and condition number of the resulting iteration matrices and show that the reference Jacobian is an effective preconditioner. On transmission-scale benchmarks, the method attains per-topology solve times competitive with an optimized 80-core central processing unit baseline, with the low-rank correction accounting for approximately 1--2\% of the workload. This makes GPU-parallel $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis feasible at transmission scale without per-topology refactorization.

papers.title: Two-level additive Schwarz preconditioners with GDSW coarse spaces for high-order discretizations in 3D
papers.abstract: Overlapping Schwarz methods are among the most successful domain decomposition preconditioners for large-scale finite element simulations. In this work, the Generalized Dryja-Smith-Widlund (GDSW), GDSW$^*$, and Reduced GDSW (RGDSW) coarse spaces are studied for three-dimensional high-order finite element method (FEM) and virtual element method (VEM) for the Poisson equation and the equations of linear elasticity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study of GDSW-type coarse spaces for polynomial degrees $k\ge 3$ in three dimensions, for either discretization. In 3D VEM, the face degrees of freedom (DOFs) are moments instead of point values. The kernel of the differential operator, which defines the interface values of the GDSW coarse basis functions, must be represented through these moments. The construction is therefore no longer purely algebraic and, without this correction, the coarse level loses its effect for $k\ge 3$. FEM and VEM are tested on hexahedral meshes, and VEM is additionally tested on polyhedral ones. Polynomial degrees up to $k=5$ and runs on up to $4\,096$ subdomains and parallel cores are included in the numerical study. Numerical experiments show scalable iteration counts for all coarse space variants for the Poisson problem, illustrating the expected trade-off between the coarse space size and robustness. Further experiments for linear elasticity confirms that the moment-based construction extends naturally from the scalar to the vector-valued problem.

papers.title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.abstract:
For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,\pi^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_\nu$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively.
  We also consider the first time $\tau_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $\tau_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[\tau_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\log\tau_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $\tau_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.

papers.title: Spatial Transfusion: From Structured Spatial Scene Understanding to Generation and Editing
papers.abstract: Spatial audio conveys not only what sounds are present, but where they originate and how they interact with the environment. Recent audio-language models increasingly understand and reason about such scenes, yet spatial audio understanding, generation, and editing remain largely separate. We present Spatial Transfusion, a unified first-order ambisonics (FOA) framework that extends a pretrained spatial audio understanding model to generation and editing through flow matching over VAE latents. We formulate editing as a structured scene transformation over a taxonomy of atomic edits. Keeping the pretrained backbone frozen, we introduce modality-based LoRA routing and a curriculum that progressively adds generation, editing, and natural-language interaction. Experiments show that Spatial Transfusion largely preserves spatial understanding while outperforming full fine-tuning in generation and editing. The resulting model supports controllable FOA generation and editing through both structured and natural-language interfaces. Audio samples are available at https://microsoft.github.io/spatial-transfusion/

papers.title: Short-Circuit Current Calculation in DC Shipboard Microgrid Using Operational Admittances
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of DC shipboard power systems is driven by the need to integrate energy storage systems seamlessly onboard. In this context, accurate calculation of short-circuit current transients is critical for sizing fast-acting protection devices. This paper proposes a methodology to calculate short-circuit current transients based on operational admittance modelling of network elements and power converters. The superposition principle is then applied to calculate current contributions and voltage time profiles. The methodology is validated with a detailed EMT model of a notional LVDC shipboard microgrid section consisting of an active front end, a bidirectional buck-boost converter and two special loads. Results demonstrate that the methodology accurately tracks nodal voltages and the fault current contributions dynamics up to the prospective fault current peak, thus providing a computationally efficient tool for fault analysis and protection coordination in LVDC microgrids.

authors.name: Fabio D'Agostino
authors.institution: Saint Camillus International University of Health and Medical Sciences

papers.title: BeyondContact: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Airflow-Based Non-Contact Manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact-based robotic manipulation is constrained by end-effector reachability and the mechanical properties of objects. Airflow can exert forces without direct robot-object contact, enabling manipulation of objects beyond the reach or when direct contact is undesirable. However, the lack of suitable simulation has hindered the application of reinforcement learning to airflow-based manipulation, limiting the broader adoption of this mechanism compared with contact-based methods. To address this gap, we developed a robot- and task-agnostic airflow extension for Isaac Lab that supports massively parallel training. The extension uses experimentally identified airflow models to compute the forces and torques exerted on objects. Based on this extension, we train a hybrid push-blow (HPB) policy that combines contact-based pushing with airflow manipulation and a rectangular reorientation (RR) policy that controls a cuboid's heading using airflow alone. To enable physical execution, we design a lightweight, high-speed blower that coexists with a gripper. In zero-shot real-world deployment, HPB achieves an 80% success rate over 20 trials, while RR achieves a mean absolute heading error of 2.6 degrees across four target headings. The project materials are available at https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/BeyondContact.

papers.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
papers.abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

papers.title: Multi-Antenna Channel Prediction in 5G and Beyond using Data driven approach
papers.abstract: As Wireless Communication evolves towards 5G and beyond, it satisfies Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of users by utilizing beam forming, adaptive transmission and multi antenna communication techniques. It is essential to have accurate channel information at Base station (BS) to provide satisfactory QoS to users. Traditional channel estimation approach involves transmitting pilots from User Equipments (UEs) and estimating the channel at BS, increases computational complexity as it is periodic process. It also increases communication complexity as number of antennas at BS increases which leads to increase in pilots. In this paper, we consider channel vector prediction using Machine learning approach at 7GHz. In this work, we generated data using ray tracing mechanism and used this generated data to train Machine learning models. We Considered XG Boost regression and Multilayer perceptron regression model.

papers.title: SCRAMJet: An Ultra Low Latency JetClass-Scale Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger
papers.abstract: Level-1 Triggers at the LHC classify collisions within a few microseconds on FPGAs, where a network is a fully unrolled circuit whose cost is area rather than time. We present SCRAMJet, a transformer encoder that replaces multi-head attention with a low-rank projection, trains under per-parameter learned fixed-point quantization, and compiles to Verilog with distributed arithmetic optimization. On the ten-class JetClass dataset it reaches $71.4 \pm 0.6\%$ accuracy with 0.157M multiply-accumulates, 6.1 accuracy points above the strongest published resource-constrained model at an eighth of the operations, and meets timing on a Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P at 147 ns using 25.7% of the logic. We also show that resource-aware training silently removes attention channels: one whose learned bit-width reaches zero still carries signal during training but is absent from the compiled circuit, so the loss never sees it go. We call these virtual channels, and a floor on the attention datalane that prevents them is worth 3.1 accuracy points at matched budget. Code and trained checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Aaddy-1/hgq-jetformer.

authors.name: Lauri Laatu

papers.title: Evaluating Context Sensitivity of Collaboration Behavior in Multi Party Simulation Frameworks
papers.abstract: Group Social Behavior is increasingly used as a lens to study Large language model (LLM) simulations to aid model training and evaluation. However, little prior work has examined how contextual factors such as team size and goal type manifest in long running simulations. To overcome this gap, we conduct a controlled, full-factorial study examining how contextual factors affect collaboration behavior across multi-party simulation frameworks. Using well established social science taxonomies, we quantify context sensitivity of collaboration behavior in simulated teams. Our analyses reveal significant effects of contextual factors such as simulators consistently favor smooth collaboration over disagreement, negotiation pressure, and coordination breakdown. These findings provide the first systematic evidence of how contextual factors influence emergent collaboration in LLM based multi-party simulation frameworks, offering both guidance and empirical results for the use of such simulations.

papers.title: A Scalable Two-Stage Back-End Architecture for 400GbE Data Acquisition Systems
papers.abstract: A primary challenge in High Energy Physics (HEP) data acquisition is the aggregation of numerous low-speed (10 Gb/s) radiation-hard data links into high-speed back-end interfaces. While high-end FPGAs traditionally perform this task, transceiver density and speed in modern devices can limit cost-effective scaling. This study proposes a two-stage architecture that utilizes mid-range FPGAs for decoding and Ethernet conversion, followed by a Microchip META-DX2+ Ethernet PHY that aggregates these streams into a 400 GbE interface. This study evaluates the design's performance, validating it as a scalable and cost-effective architecture for next-generation HEP data acquisition systems.

papers.title: Sealed, Lightweight gRPC-Based Muon Telescopes for Muography Applications
papers.abstract: Portable muon detection systems are increasingly in demand for muography applications in environments requiring flexible installation and transportability. We present the ongoing development and implementation of portable muon tracking systems based on glass Resistive Plate Chambers (gRPCs). The work addresses the fabrication and assembly of compact, position-sensitive RPC detectors, along with their performance when operated with a standard gas mixture and coupled to external front-end electronics and a scalable multi-channel data-acquisition system. The system design prioritizes modular construction, mechanical robustness, operational safety, autonomous functionality, and cost-effectiveness. Measurements with atmospheric muons demonstrated stable detector performance and reliable tracking capability, confirming the suitability of this architecture for muographic measurements. We conclude with an outlook on further developments of the detection system.

papers.title: Count-Density Networks for Modal Plate Parameter Estimation
papers.abstract: We describe two submissions to Task B of the 1st DAFx Parameter Estimation Challenge, which estimates an unknown number of modal frequency, decay, and gain triples from a synthetic plate-reverb impulse response. The first method combines pooled spectral features with time-domain and absolute-scale conditioning in a real-valued convolutional count-density network, while the second uses a complex-valued Transformer count-density network. Both methods jointly infer the modal count and per-mode attributes directly from the IR. On an independently generated 100-IR comparison set, the two neural estimators achieve lower overall challenge error than the evaluated classical baselines, with frequency and decay estimation substantially more accurate than gain estimation.

papers.title: Inline inter-core phase control in multi-core fiber with a commercial polarization controller
papers.abstract: Inter-core phase control is a prerequisite for interferometry in multi-core fiber (MCF), but no compact inline element for this purpose is presently available, and existing approaches require fanout to single-mode fiber or free-space optics. We show that a commercial inline polarization controller, a low-loss and widely available component, can be operated as an inline inter-core phase shifter. Two-core interferometry on a jacketed four-core patchcord gives a reversible inter-core phase of $0.95 \pm 0.02$~rad from a single device, with an operating-point-independent lower bound of $0.38$~rad, driven through repeated load-unload cycles at a rate set by the actuator. A diametrically compressed disk model is used to predict the operating condition: with the input polarization aligned to a principal stress axis the device imparts a relative phase between cores without rotating the polarization state of either, which we verify by polarimetry on all four cores. The response is polarization dependent, falling to less than $0.58$~rad for the orthogonal input. The result is a practical, inline route to inter-core phase control and stabilization in all-MCF interferometers, requiring neither fanout to single-mode fiber nor free-space optics.

papers.title: The search for the Higgs Boson and the EBH mechanism
papers.abstract: The searches for the Higgs boson at LEP and the Tevatron between 1980 and 2000 are set in the context of the underlying theory of spontaneous symmetry breaking and early phenomenological studies. The evolution of direct searches at LEP and the Tevatron are reviewed, as well as indirect constraints from precision electroweak data. Finally, the state of play in 2000 is summarised, together with the perspectives it offered for later searches.

papers.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they interact and coordinate with other agents, yet honesty is mostly measured in single-turn, single-agent benchmarks that pressure the model to deceive. We study deception that emerges in multi-agent interaction without any instruction to deceive. We introduce Kradle, a platform for evaluating AI models, and Four Bridges, an information asymmetry game in which four agents distribute across four rooms: one is the death room, the others hold food worth more if not shared. One agent, the informed agent, knows which room is the death room and can withhold or disclose that information. We evaluate eight frontier models as the informed agent. Deceptive behavior appears in every model and in 73% of all runs (6% to 100% per model), and does not decrease with capability tier within a model family. When the informed agent does disclose, the warning is often challenged, and agents that challenge it enter the death room twice as often as those that do not. Telling all agents that one of them knows the death room collapses deception in six of eight models; telling the informed agent that the room is permanently fatal moves only one. On an open-weight model, an honesty steering vector reduces deception to 0% and adversarial honesty training to 6%. The platform and game provide a testbed for measuring deceptive behavior and comparing interventions.

papers.title: The Neptunian ridge through the lens of TESS
papers.abstract: The Neptunian desert and savanna are separated by a ridge, an overdensity at orbital periods of approximately 3-6 d identified with Kepler. Like the hot Jupiter pileup at larger radii, this feature has been linked to the accumulation of successful outcomes of high-eccentricity migration (HEM). We revisit the ridge independently using TESS occurrence posteriors for FGK main-sequence stars. We quantify its excess over adjacent regions and compare six occurrence profiles using leave-one-out cross-validation and Bayesian evidence. For planets with radii of approximately 5-8 $R_\oplus$, the ridge has twice the occurrence density of the denser neighbouring region ($J=2.05^{+0.52}_{-0.44}$), with 99.9% posterior support (one-sided Gaussian equivalent of $3.1\sigma$). This contrast agrees with the discovery study and earlier Kepler occurrence measurements. Both predictive performance and Bayesian evidence strongly favour profiles peaking within the ridge over a single power law. The lognormal is preferred, suggesting a narrower inner wing and a more extended outer wing, although evidence for asymmetry remains weak. In the same period window, the analysis recovers the hot Jupiter pileup (approximately 10-16 $R_\oplus$) with a contrast consistent with that of the ridge and excludes an analogous excess among sub-Neptunes (approximately 2-4 $R_\oplus$) with $3.4\sigma$ posterior support. TESS thus provides an independent detection of the Neptunian ridge. Its possible asymmetry would be compatible with HEM, in which tidal disruption could produce a sharper inner edge and variations in circularisation efficiency a more gradual outer decline. Establishing whether the ridge has this shape requires more precise occurrence measurements, with PLATO's expected planet yield offering a promising opportunity to help unveil its morphology.

papers.title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
papers.abstract: In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
papers.abstract:
This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough.
  In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

authors.name: Andrey Yurkov
authors.institution: Leibniz Institute DSMZ – German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures

papers.title: Does reflective LLM feedback survive a wet-lab-scale label budget?
papers.abstract: Can reflective language-model feedback improve a biological predictor when each cycle buys only one plate of labels? We separate three possible sources of benefit: proposing model edits, choosing measurements, and revising decisions through repeated feedback. We replay $36$ ProteinGym assays, starting with $96$ labels and acquiring $96$ per round for six rounds, with a sealed test set and a shared edit schema. The pre-specified comparison of full LLM control against random edits detects no advantage in test rank correlation ($\Delta z=-0.008$, $95\%$ CI $[-0.034,+0.018]$); equivalence is also unestablished. Exploratory ablations nevertheless identify useful model editing. With random acquisition fixed, LLM edits improve Fisher-transformed test Spearman by $0.043$ over no edits; with acquisition fixed to upper confidence bound, they improve normalized top-variant recovery by $0.023$. LLM acquisition alone does not detectably outperform fixed adaptive rules, and repeated feedback does not detectably outperform one initial recommendation under full control. Thus, the observed gains support constrained specialist editing, while the incremental value of recursive reflection remains unestablished at this label budget.

papers.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.

papers.title: Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets
papers.abstract: Global tractography offers a theoretical framework for reconstructing white matter connectivity from diffusion MRI by jointly inferring all streamlines and their consistency with the diffusion signal and underlying anatomical priors. However, its sequential nature and log-linear complexity make it computationally prohibitive at the scales demanded by neuroimaging, from large population cohorts such as the Human Connectome Project (HCP) to ex vivo ultra-high-field acquisitions at mesoscopic resolution. In this work, we present ExaTract, a parallelized spin-glass tractography framework designed for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Implemented as an open-source MPI+Kokkos application, ExaTract partitions the tractography domain into spatially overlapping regions processed across distributed memory nodes, with regular synchronization of boundary modifications to preserve global convergence guarantees. We validate ExaTract on both in vivo and ex vivo diffusion MRI data: the complete HCP dataset demonstrates population-scale throughput, while the high-resolution Chenonceau dataset provides the first mesoscopic structural connectome derived from global tractography.

papers.title: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
papers.abstract: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the $n$-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all $n$-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral $p$-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.

papers.title: Emergent Control of Ant Learning Walks in a Mobile Robot
papers.abstract:
Before foraging, desert ants perform learning walks (LWs) to acquire visual memories around their nest. With experience, these walks expand, become straighter, and contain fewer visual scans. We previously proposed a model in which these behaviours emerge from the angular mismatch between path integration (PI) and a mushroom-body-inspired visual compass (VC). Here, we test whether this mechanism can generate learning walks on a physical robot, despite the sensory and motor noise inherent to real-world conditions.
  We implement the model on a four-wheeled robot equipped with a panoramic camera, an IMU and wheel encoders providing compass and stride information for PI, and test it outdoors using a replicated desert-ant experimental setup. The PI--VC mismatch regulates walking speed, turning, pirouettes, and returns to the nest, while PI provides a teaching signal for visual learning. The robot autonomously decides when to acquire visual memories, while its behaviour gradually shifts from exploration towards foraging as visual learning progresses.
  The robot reproduces desert-ant LW features, including expanding and straightening trajectories, decreasing pirouette frequency, and improved visual homing. These results demonstrate that a simple error-driven mechanism can generate key features of learning walks under real-world conditions, supporting its plausibility as an explanation for active visual learning in desert ants. More broadly, this work illustrates how physical robots can be used to test biological models.

papers.title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_\omega^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.

authors.name: Fan Gu
authors.institution: Changsha University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$
papers.abstract:
The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic.
  We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form $A\Longrightarrow B$ with $A,B$ strictly positive formulas. In particular, the new calculi do not use (multi)sets nor nested sequents.
  For both ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ it is shown that the cut-rule is admissible. As a consequence, it is proven that the calculi are deductively equivalent to $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The cutfree systems are used to prove uniform interpolation for the two reflection calculi.
  In addition, ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ is used to give a syntactic proof of Dashkov's Theorem to the extent that $\mathsf{RC}_1$ is the strictly positive fragment of the provability logic ${\mathsf{GL}}$.
  The paper also introduces non-analytic calculi that are conceptually easier but proof-theoretically behave badly. It is shown that even those systems allow direct cut-elimination: the benefits of the strict positivity outweigh the draw-backs of a non-analytic calculus in these cases.

authors.name: Cosimo Perini Brogi
authors.institution: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca

papers.title: Simulating winds in the Galactic centre. II. Observational biases on HI clouds and a multi-wavelength comparison
papers.abstract: High-velocity neutral hydrogen (HI) clouds found up to several kiloparsecs above the Galactic centre (GC) provide some of the most direct evidence for a nuclear wind in the Milky Way, yet the properties inferred for these clouds are influenced by how they are observed. Starting from a magnetohydrodynamical simulation in which supernova feedback drives a multiphase nuclear outflow, we generate mock HI observations matched to the angular resolution and sensitivity of Green Bank Telescope (GBT) surveys of the GC and analyse them in the same way as the real data. We find that observational effects substantially reshape the cloud population: beam smearing makes clouds appear larger, rounder and more diffuse, while noise erases faint clouds and strips low-density gas from the others. These effects combined, together with confusion with foreground disk emission, prevent the detection of more than 80% of the clouds (up to 95% during more quiescent phases), while those detected appear less massive, less turbulent and less elongated, with column densities underestimated by a factor of two; only their velocities are reliably recovered. Once these effects are included, the simulated clouds broadly reproduce the properties and sky distribution of the GBT population, but lack the fastest (> 250 km/s ) and highest-latitude (b > 10{\deg} ) clouds. Mock UV absorption and soft X-ray observations support this picture, with warm-ionized gas column densities at the low end of the observed range and X-ray emission measures too low at b > 10{\deg} . Our results imply that the true GC cloud population is more numerous, massive, turbulent and elongated than observed, and that fully reproducing observations may require a stronger recent starburst or additional feedback.

papers.title: Informative Fisher Modes in Neural Networks as a Result of Explicit Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: Learning in a neural network takes place on a high dimensional, non-convex loss landscape, the Hessian curvature of which dictates the learning dynamics. Despite its high dimensionality, the large number of architectural symmetries explains some of the geometric of this landscape, in particular flat directions, i.e. near-zero modes of the Hessian. These architectural symmetries have therefore been suggested as an organizing principle of deep learning. It remains an open question, though, wether there are additional organizing principles in the remaining degrees of freedom in the learning dynamic. Here we identify task-dependent contingent symmetries as such an additional organizing principle. We show that non-flat learning directions emerge due to explicit breaking of these contingent symmetries. We isolate this symmetry in an analytically solvable minimal model. Furthermore, we show that, by tuning an L2 penalty, signatures of the symmetry breaking become measurable. As a consequence of the same mechanism, adding noise to the data drives the model through a sequence of broken symmetry recoveries in the form of Baik-Ben-Arous-P\'ech\'e (BBP) transitions. We demonstrate analytically for linear and numerically for deep linear networks that the contingent symmetry group remains explicit, and that the symmetry-breaking mechanism identifies which Hessian modes carry task-specific information. These signatures are measurable without a symmetry-group description and, hence, offer a route to study symmetry breaking as a more general principle in nonlinear networks and other learning systems.

papers.title: ODC: Orthogonal Drift Correction for Improved Text-to-Image Semantic Alignment at Inference
papers.abstract: Text-to-image models have achieved remarkable success in generating high-quality images from textual descriptions. However, they often struggle with "semantic drift," where the generated output fails to precisely align with complex or nuanced text prompts. While recent approaches have attempted to address semantic errors regarding attribute binding or object presence, there remains a gap for a more holistic method that addresses these issues by directly refining the text embeddings of the initial user prompt. In this work, we introduce Orthogonal Drift Correction (ODC), an inference-time guidance method designed to mitigate semantic drift without requiring model retraining or additional user inputs. ODC guides image generation through a two-stage process. In the first stage, it identifies the semantic drift by evaluating the initially generated image against the user prompt in a shared vision-language embedding space. It then isolates the component of this drift vector that is orthogonal to the prompt's direction and translates it back into text via a vocabulary-based surrogate mechanism. In the second stage, it produces refined text conditioning for a second generation pass by feeding both the initial text embedding and the re-embedded drift representation into an adaptive rank-reduced concept removal module. Our experiments demonstrate that ODC consistently improves prompt-image alignment, increasing CLIP scores by up to 5.4% over the baseline on the COALBench-300 and PartiPrompts benchmarks. Furthermore, on the T2I-CompBench complex subset, ODC improves the average 3-in-1 score by 4.5% over the competing methods. As a plug-and-play module, ODC offers a practical and efficient method for improving the reliability of text-to-image models. Code is available at https://github.com/kasrakamali/ODC.

papers.title: Weak-Signal Amplification through Stochastic Resetting
papers.abstract: Stochastic resetting (SR) offers a distinct route to amplifying weak periodic signals in nonlinear systems. Here, we demonstrate SR-induced resonance (SRIR) in a system with double-well potential driven by a weak periodic force, where the amplitude of the mean periodic response exhibits a pronounced maximum at an optimal SR rate. The underlying mechanism exploits dynamical instability: SR repeatedly brings the system close to an unstable state, where the phase of the periodic force at each reset biases the subsequent motion toward one of the stable states. The local instability then amplifies this weak bias into a large-scale response. The SRIR arises from a competition between rare resets that limit phase-dependent state selection and frequent resets that prevent the system from fully relaxing to the selected state. We develop a general renewal formulation for the periodic response and a coarse-grained approximation that predicts the optimal resetting rate, revealing the low-frequency scaling $r_{\rm opt}(\omega)\propto\omega^{2/3}$, in agreement with numerical simulations. SRIR is fundamentally distinct from conventional noise-induced resonance (NIR), which relies on noise-activated interwell transitions whose rates are periodically modulated by the external driving force. In the weak-forcing and slow-driving regime, SRIR can achieve much stronger signal amplification than NIR. SRIR persists for a finite spread of resetting positions, and our framework extends beyond bistability. We further discuss how SRIR and NIR can be selectively controlled. Our work proposes a novel approach to the classical paradigm of stochastic resonance.
