papers.title: Three New Phases in the Two-Dimensional Potts Model at Complex Temperature
papers.abstract: The complex-temperature phase structure of the two-dimensional Potts model has remained largely unresolved despite decades of study. Here we determine the complex-temperature phase diagram of the 3-state Potts model, and uncover three gapless phases beyond the familiar ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases. This is done by combining tensor-network free energies with the Poisson equation to compute the Fisher zero density in the thermodynamic limit. The resulting zero distribution unifies and revises long-standing conjectures on the zero loci, and outlines each phase. One is a non-conformal gapless phase, with an exponentially growing number of low-lying transfer-matrix levels distributed across all momentum sectors. The other two are Luttinger-liquid phases with complex-valued Luttinger parameters related by the Kramers-Wannier duality. At the antiferromagnetic critical point, the Luttinger parameter equals 3, while its limit from the adjacent Luttinger-liquid phase is 6. These findings reveal rich phase structures and unconventional critical behavior in a classical textbook model.

papers.title: Shared relations, specific choices: conditional sensitivity and competing pathways in language models
papers.abstract: How does a relational representation shared across queries drive a query-specific choice? Controlled entity-binding experiments with GPT-2 Small, Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B reveal a low-dimensional relational background that is predominantly shared across query roles and transfers to new names. Same-domain interactions persist when another attribute domain is queried. After removing this component, restoring independently trained relation directions brings output contrasts closer to their original values than sign-reversed or equal-norm random controls in all three models. Yet a transferable relational representation need not have a transferable functional sign. In Qwen2.5, fixing model weights, the training-mean relation vector and edit dose yields opposite selection effects across binary and lexical-mapping prompts with different answer vocabularies. A factorial contrast of downstream sensitivities across attribute-query combinations determines the shared direction's local signed selection gain. In a separate eight-condition protocol, mean local gain is positive in Qwen2.5 and negative in Llama3.2. Late-component clamps resolve opposing pathway contributions: in Llama3.2, negative transmission through selected attention-only paths is partially offset by positive transmission through paths traversing both selected attention and MLP sets. Source-coordinate analyses establish distributed factor coverage, hidden-receiver readouts reveal layout-dependent combination, and instance-geometry interventions separate response direction from amplitude. These findings show how conditional sensitivity and competing pathways give shared relational structure its effect on specific choices.

papers.title: Learning-to-Memorize: Dynamic Context Management for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generation has achieved impressive results on short clips, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to error accumulation over extended horizons, where each predicted frame depends on potentially imperfect previous frames. Existing approaches typically rely on static context management strategies, such as sliding-window caches that discard early frames or fixed sink frames that permanently preserve initial content. These designs either lose critical long-range context or anchor generation to outdated information, which can lead to degraded fidelity, motion stagnation, and reduced diversity. In this paper, we propose Learning to Memorize (L2M), a learned context memory management framework that dynamically retains, evicts, and evolves historical frames according to predicted importance. The framework consists of an importance prediction router that estimates the relevance of each historical frame, degradation-aware training that improves robustness to noisy or corrupted context, and a dynamic memory initialization and evolution mechanism that updates long-term memory using exponential moving average (EMA) importance scores. This allows high-quality frames to replace stale anchors and enables memory to adapt naturally to scene evolution. Trained with a teacher-student distillation objective and sparsity regularization, L2M makes efficient use of a fixed KV-cache budget while preserving the most informative contextual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that L2M improves long-horizon video generation quality and temporal consistency over existing baselines, providing a learned strategy for context memory management in long autoregressive video generation.

papers.title: Generalized Hamiltonian gradient flow of contact type II: singularities, cut locus, and controllability
papers.abstract: We study singularities, cut loci and controllability for time-dependent contact Hamilton--Jacobi equations. A contact version of Arnaud's theorem identifies the superdifferential graph of an evolved profile with the contact Hamiltonian image of the differential graph of its positive Lax--Oleinik regularization. This representation defines intrinsic singular characteristics and determines their initial velocity through a minimum-energy selection on the space-time superdifferential. The curves are continuous and locally $1/2$-H\"older, but they need not be locally Lipschitz. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal even for a quadratic Hamiltonian. The intrinsic characteristic issued from a cut point is singular at every later time in the short-time interval. We also establish the contact Lax--Oleinik commutator identities, which identify the superlevel and sublevel sets of the cut time with the corresponding terminal momentum graphs through bi-Lipschitz maps. For reachable terminal data we characterize the associated calibrated sets, and we describe all continuous initial data that reach a prescribed semiconcave profile. The proofs use Herglotz' variational principle and short-time estimates for contact fundamental solutions.

papers.title: Beyond Prompt Injection: The Tool Update Gap in LLM Agent Security
papers.abstract:
Large language model based agents increasingly rely on external tools to invoke services and interact with web resources. These tools can evolve through software updates, yet agentic frameworks may continue trusting them without re-verifying their safety after implementation changes. This tool update gap creates a supply-chain vulnerability in agentic systems: because updated tool code executes outside the LLM's context window, malicious functionality embedded in tool updates can bypass defenses centered on model-visible interactions, leaving agents exposed to stealthy, persistent threats that existing in-context defenses can hardly address.
  To thoroughly investigate this threat, we introduce ETUDE (Exploiting Tool Updates for Direct Execution), an attack that embeds malicious functionality into updates of initially benign tools to produce compromised tools, while preserving their legitimate tool functionality. Unlike prompt-based attacks, ETUDE operates entirely outside the LLM's context and requires no adversarial instructions, thereby bypassing defenses restricted to model-visible content. We evaluate ETUDE across three representative attack workloads and seven widely used commercial and open-source agentic frameworks, including Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and Claude Code. The results show that ETUDE achieves a 97.6% ASR while maintaining a 95.9% legitimate task completion rate.
  We further examine existing defenses and find that they provide insufficient protection against this threat. These findings expose a fundamental blind spot in current agent security practices: trust established for a tool does not necessarily remain valid after its implementation updates.

papers.title: SurgStream: A Workflow-Anchored Proactive Streaming Framework and Benchmark for Real-Time Surgical Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Surgical video understanding is essential for intraoperative assistance such as workflow monitoring, instrument preparation and procedural documentation. Delivering such assistance in real time requires a model to jointly perceive the ongoing scene, remember past surgical events, and respond before clinically relevant moments pass. Existing approaches provide limited support for jointly retaining procedural evidence and deciding when to respond in streaming surgical video. In this work, we propose SurgStream, a workflow-anchored proactive streaming framework for real-time surgical video understanding. We first introduce Workflow-Anchored Memory (WAM) to record structured instrument-action-target observations and fold them into phase-level summaries, providing compact and queryable surgical memory. Deadline-aware Transition Learning (DTL) is then devised to supervise response states within clinical windows, enabling timely responses before procedural deadlines. We further introduce SurgStream-Bench, comprising 11.7K streaming interactions across various tasks covering real-time perception, backward memory queries, forward proactive QA, proactive alerts and caption memory. Experiments on SurgStream-Bench show gains over state-of-the-art methods, especially in memory and forward proactive QA. The source code will be available.

papers.title: The Agentic Observer Hackathon: Autonomous Decision-making in Simulated Astronomical Surveys
papers.abstract: Astronomical surveys must allocate observing time while responding to changing conditions and competing scientific priorities. We present the Agentic Observer Hackathon (AOH), a community challenge for studying autonomous survey operations. Within a synthetic multi-object survey with prescribed exposure responses and assignment constraints, decision systems select pointings, assign targets and choose exposure configurations while responding to observing requests, instrumental faults and data loss. We evaluate systems submitted by 102 teams on campaigns reserved for evaluation and analyse target completion in a reference campaign. The leading systems combine numerical exposure planning with language models for interpreting operational information and supporting longer-term decisions. Exploratory tests show improved fault reporting with model access in several systems, while revised scientific priorities produce substantial changes in ranking. The reference campaign traces target completion and diagnoses errors in the baseline's inference of prescribed quality bands. The released simulator and reference strategies provide common survey conditions for comparing exposure allocation, target selection and recovery from interruptions.

papers.title: Multi-criteria Rating and Review based Recommendation Model
papers.abstract: These days, due to the advancement of information technology, recommendation system has become one of the key tools for e-commerce business. E-commerce platforms allow users to provide feedback in both written comments and numerical ratings. Recommendation systems are utilized to recommend users to new or unseen items based on these previously collected comments or ratings. In recent years, multi-aspect or multi-criteria based recommendation systems have been studied a lot by the recommendation research community. However, these research works are conducted either with reviews or ratings, not with both. In this project, we argue that integrating both textual reviews (with multiple aspects) and numerical multi-criteria ratings can further enhance the overall rating prediction accuracy. We propose a Multi-criteria Rating and Review based Recommendation model (MRRRec). We show that incorporating multi-criteria ratings into multi-aspect ratings from reviews has a great impact on performance. Our proposed model outperforms several state-of-the-art models such as ANR, DeepCoNN, and Deep Multi-criteria Recommendation System in terms of MSE, MAE, precision, recall, and F1. We show that our proposed model achieves an average of 19% and 23.0% lower MSE and MAE respectively and 7.0%, 1.0% and 3.8% higher precision, recall, and F1 score respectively. We further show that our model performs significantly better with Word2Vec word embedding than the GloVe word embedding method.

papers.title: Liouville theorem for monotone solutions of the Lane-Emden system in a half-space
papers.abstract:
The Lane-Emden system is an important model case of Hamitonian elliptic systems. We here consider the zero-Dirichlet problem in a half-space for arbitrary powers $p,q\ge1$. We prove that any nonnegative classical solution that is nondecreasing in the normal direction is necessarily trivial. No bound at infinity of any kind is assumed and this extends the known scalar monotonicity theorem.
  We also obtain the same conclusion for the scalar equation $-\Delta u=f(u)$ when $f\in C^1([0,\infty))$ is nonnegative, $f(0)=0$, $f\not\equiv0$, and $f(s)/s$ is nondecreasing for $s>0$. This relaxes the convexity and $C^2$ regularity requirements on $f$ in previous works.
  To prove these results we introduce a new method, completely different from the normal convexity approach from previous works, which relies on a delicate combination of techniques and could be applied to more general systems. Our basic tool is a suitable average of the linear interpolant between the solution and its normal limit on each finite strip. We next use stability estimates, combined with an energy argument for the scalar equation, or a contraction argument relying on Bessel potentials and the Schur test for the system. Increasing the strip height then forces the solution to vanish.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: FOLLIE: Automated Reasoning over the First Dataset of Sentences with their First-Order Logical Representation for French
papers.abstract: FOLLIE (for First-Order Logic for Language Inference and Entailment for French) connects French sentences, compositional first-order representations and automated natural language inference (NLI). The first French NLI-ready, NL-to-FOL resource, it contains 19,983 inference records and 36,987 non-empty sentence-slot--formula mappings from six heterogeneous NLI sources, retaining French lexical material and source problem structure. Its silver annotations are produced by a neural--symbolic pipeline, with 111 separately identified LLM-assisted additions. The construction combines morphosyntactic analysis, probability-conditioned categorial multitagging, grammatical proof search, discourse representation and first-order semantic construction. Stage-wise experiments show substantial gains in derivation coverage; analyses of conjunction distributions, logical-operator incidence and scope alternation characterise the resulting resource. We then develop an automatic inference engine whose input-conditioned background theories address lexical relations, quantification, quantities, event structure and temporal dependencies. Prover9 supplies proofs for entailment and contradiction, while Mace4 supports bounded consistency checks. Three-way accuracies are 65.37% on all 335 FraCaS-FR problems, 70.33% on 300 GQNLI-FR problems and 71.35% on 9,399 eligible SICK-FR records pooled across splits. Agreement with reference labels among committed decisions is 93.53%, 100.00% and 98.66%, at commitment coverage of 41.49%, 37.00% and 15.05%, respectively. Worked constructions, axiom schemas and proof analyses explain these outcomes and identify the contributions of scope, reference, lexical knowledge and numerical structure. FOLLIE provides a French experimental basis for studying the representations and assumptions that connect sentence interpretation to deductive inference.

papers.title: Current Sheets and Magnetic Reconnection statistics by Solar Orbiter at few to tens of Ion Inertial Lengths II: Conditions for Reconnection, and Current Sheet Planarity
papers.abstract: We present a statistical study of magnetic reconnection and current sheet (CS) properties at scales from the ion inertial length ($\delta_i$), up to 86.4 $\delta_i$. We analyze 103 hours of high-cadence (4 samples/s) in-situ Solar Orbiter ion data, collected from July 2020 to September 2022, which correspond mainly to slow and Alfv\'enic solar wind. We applied an automatic detection algorithm to find CSs of thicknesses near and above the ion inertial length ($\delta_i$), and classify them as Alfv\'enic or reconnecting. The orientation of the CSs is consistent with an isotropic distribution of the discontinuities. The median ratio of reconnection jet velocity to theoretical outflow velocity is 0.71. We find that the diamagnetic drift reconnection suppression mechanism has no impact on the cataloged CSs, due to the symmetry of their upstream conditions. We find that a flow shear in the reconnection direction suppresses magnetic reconnection, and it is consistently greater for Alfv\'enic than for reconnecting CSs. Flow shear in the guide-field direction is too small to suppress magnetic reconnection in ion scale solar wind CSs.

papers.title: The nucleon is not a hard sphere: screening fifth forces with Skyrmions
papers.abstract: Laboratory searches for chameleon and symmetron fifth forces increasingly rely on individual nucleons as sources or probes, but model them as uniform spheres. Motivated by the Skyrme picture, we instead consider a nucleon profile with a constant-density core and an $r^{-6}$ pion tail, together with its exponential truncation at the physical pion mass. We derive analytic screening charges for the uniform sphere and the $r^{-6}$ profile, and extend the comparison to the exponential truncation at the physical pion mass using numerical solutions. Because the outer tail is too dilute to be screened at any coupling strength, the $r^{-6}$ tail produces a power-law enhancement over the sphere charge in strong screening, and the exponential tail has a weaker, logarithmic enhancement. Propagating this difference through the published analyses, nucleon-sourced exclusion regions extend systematically further into the strongly coupled regime. For example, symmetron constraints from neutron interferometry at $\mu=1\,\mathrm{keV}$ reach maximal self-couplings about $1.4$ orders of magnitude higher than for a uniform-sphere neutron ($3.0$ orders of magnitude in the chiral limit),and at the dark-energy scale the hydrogen $1s$--$2s$ chameleon bound reaches couplings $1.8$ orders of magnitude weaker than for a uniform-sphere proton ($2.4$ in the chiral limit), overtaking the muonium bound.

papers.title: SVD-Prune: Spectral Vision Token Pruning under Extreme Compression
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models process hundreds of visual tokens, making visual representations a major computational bottleneck. We argue that visual token pruning should be formulated not as identifying individually important tokens, but as preserving the dominant low-rank spectral structure of the visual representation. Based on this formulation, we introduce SVD-Prune, a training-free framework that leverages Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and statistical leverage scores for globally informed token selection. SVD-Prune is architecture-agnostic and can be applied at different stages of the multimodal pipeline, including encoder-side, decoder-side, and hybrid configurations Extensive experiments across VLM and VLA benchmarks demonstrate strong robustness under extreme compression. SVD-Prune reduces the visual token. SVD-Prune cuts the visual token budget by up to 99.3%, while, at a 16-token budget, encoder-side pruning lowers inference FLOPs by 82.4% and achieves a 4.18x end-to-end speedup, including pruning overhead.

papers.title: Small-time controllability of affine systems and quadratic Lie brackets
papers.abstract: We prove a new sufficient condition for small-time global exact controllability of finite-dimensional control-affine systems. It points out that, under a natural Lie algebra rank condition, quadratic Lie brackets are the only possible obstacles to controllability. This result extends to infinite-dimensional settings such as the global approximate controllability of diffeomorphisms. It also allows us to interpret recent results in PDE control theory.

papers.title: The Hubbard-Wigner model: from Aubry-Mather theory to Fractional Quantum Hall Effects
papers.abstract:
The Hubbard-Wigner model describes binary lattice configurations with convex repulsive pair interactions. We give a unified classification of its periodic minimizers, minimizing invariant measures, and Aubry sets through a positive block-count identity, recovering explicit plateau widths and a complete devil's staircase for the minimizing density. This variational structure parallels Aubry-Mather theory and the authors' work on Aubry's completeness conjecture, where the staircase is related to the sliding and pinning mechanisms underlying the conducting and insulating interpretations of particle chains. In the binary model, completeness follows from discrete convexity and an exact sum of plateau widths.
  We then study how this classical structure persists for interactions arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect on a thin torus. At rational density $p/q$, the diagonal reference has a $q$-dimensional lowest eigenspace, a spectral gap uniform in the number of repeated periods, and an associated bundle of Chern number $p$. For the full $V_1$ operator, we prove persistence of a density-$1/3$ plateau and a positive spectral gap, uniformly in system size at sufficiently small fixed transverse circumference; the lowest-eigenspace bundle has rank three and Chern number one. For the full periodic Coulomb operator, we establish multiplicity, spectral-gap, and Chern-number conclusions at bounded denominators, and quantitative bounds on plateau-endpoint displacement and loss of width under explicit joint conditions on size and geometry.

papers.title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
papers.abstract: Coupler geometry controls both the frequency splitting and the dissipation of coupled polygon resonators. We develop a continuum model for two identical square-shaped resonators coupled by a shared tether and compare the analytical predictions with finite element simulations. The model relates the coupler length and width to the frequency splitting and dissipation dilution of the two coupled modes. In the short-coupler limit, $k_cl_c\ll1$, the symmetric-mode coupler undergoes nearly uniform rotation, and its torsional strain energy vanishes asymptotically. The remaining loss contributions arise from polygon-side bending and supporting-tether torsion. The reduced supporting-tether contribution allows the symmetric-mode dissipation dilution to exceed that of an isolated polygon with the same side and supporting-tether dimensions. The antisymmetric mode retains torsional strain in the coupler and has an additional loss contribution. We also derive an expression for $Q\cdot f$ in the short-coupler and short-tether limits, where $Q$ is the mechanical quality factor and $f$ is the resonance frequency. This expression gives the dependence of $Q\cdot f$ on tensile stress, film thickness, and supporting-tether geometry. For a coupler length of $100~\mu\mathrm{m}$ and width of $2~\mu\mathrm{m}$, finite element calculations give a frequency splitting of $17.7~\mathrm{Hz}$ and a symmetric-mode dilution factor approximately $13\%$ above the analytical isolated-polygon value.

papers.title: Moir\'e reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
papers.abstract: Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moir\'e physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moir\'e-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moir\'e of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moir\'e-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moir\'e reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

papers.title: To Coordinate or Not to Coordinate? Learning to Swim with Eight Soft Arms
papers.abstract: Does effective swimming with multiple underactuated soft arms require explicit coordination between arms? We hypothesize that an eight-arm swimmer can control its swimming speed and direction by independently learning each arm's actuation amplitude under a shared rhythmic drive, without prescribed inter-arm phase coupling. To test this hypothesis, we compare three reinforcement learning-based control strategies using proximal policy optimization (PPO): (1) learning arm-specific actuation amplitudes without inter-arm phase coupling, (2) learning actuation amplitudes with prescribed inter-arm phase coupling, and (3) directly learning actuator commands through end-to-end PPO without an explicit rhythmic structure. Across 200 episodes with randomized three-dimensional velocity commands, the controller without phase coupling satisfies the tracking criterion in 169 episodes, compared with 117 for the phase-coupled controller and 28 for end-to-end PPO. Straight-line swimming and commanded direction-change trials further demonstrate more accurate velocity tracking without phase coupling. These findings suggest that effective eight-arm swimming does not require prescribed inter-arm phase coupling, but can instead be achieved through learned arm-specific amplitude modulation within a rhythmic control structure.

papers.title: Characterisation Methodology for Persistence and Anti-persistence in IR Detectors for the Euclid and SVOM Space Missions
papers.abstract: H2RG and ALFA are the infrared detectors used in the Euclid and SVOM space missions. These types of detectors may be affected by persistence and anti-persistence, phenomena that distort pixel responses after exposure to light due to simultaneous trapping and release of charges within the pixel. These phenomena have shown to cause biases in flux measurements and potentially false detections, among other effects. This article presents a universal methodology for characterising persistence and anti-persistence using differential ramps, Savitzky--Golay filtering, and non-linearity correction. When applied to ground characterisation data, this approach reveals spatial inhomogeneities, environmental dependencies (in particular fluence, flux, temperature and wavelength), and unexpected spectral effects in ALFA. These preliminary results validate the method and pave the way for in-flight correction models capable of meeting the missions' accuracy requirements.

papers.title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
papers.abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.

papers.title: Impact of Rapid Acceleration on Beam Dynamics in the Rapid-Cycling Synchrotrons of a Muon Collider
papers.abstract: Circular muon colliders offer a promising route to multi-TeV centre-of-mass energies with high luminosity. The baseline design for the high-energy complex includes a chain of four Rapid-Cycling Synchrotrons (RCSs) accelerating the beam from \qty{63}{\GeV} to \qty{5}{\TeV}. The chain combines a conventional synchrotron with three hybrid synchrotrons, which use fixed-field superconducting dipoles and rapidly ramped normal-conducting dipoles. The short muon lifetime (\qty{2.2}{\micro\second} in the rest frame) imposes stringent constraints on the acceleration process: achieving the target luminosity requires a muon survival rate of up to \qty{70}{\percent} throughout the acceleration chain, with the full acceleration completed in approximately \qty{10}{\milli\second}. These demanding acceleration conditions raise several beam-dynamics challenges, investigated in this work. First, the impact of the RF cavity distribution on transverse emittance growth is studied. Second, the mismatch between the discretely increasing beam energy and the continuously ramped fields of the pulsed dipoles and quadrupoles is modelled analytically, and its impact is evaluated through tracking simulations. Finally, the sensitivity of the beam trajectory, optical functions, and emittance growth to magnetic-field ramp jitter is assessed.

papers.title: Structure of energy flux densities in Earth's magnetotail reconnection regions: Bridging simulation and observation
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection is important in both space and laboratory contexts because it changes the topology of magnetic fields and converts magnetic energy into particle energies. Establishing where this energy conversion occurs is critical for understanding how reconnection partitions energy. Using a novel machine learning approach based on simulations that explicitly identifies the separatrix regions for the first time, the partition of energy flux densities within the magnetic reconnection site is evaluated through statistical study of magnetotail reconnection events observed in situ. The separatrices are found to have the largest electron energy flux densities, roughly twice those in the exhaust, and Poynting flux densities about four times those in the inflows, whereas typical ion enthalpy flux densities are largest in the exhaust. The separatrices are therefore sites of intense electron and electromagnetic energy transport, although their small thickness means that the exhaust may still carry most of the total energy flux.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

authors.name: Pascal Auscher
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates
papers.abstract:
Online political discussions increasingly involve AI-mediated participation, as users invoke LLMs to assess contested claims, arbitrate disputes, and respond to opposing viewpoints. As these systems become participants in online exchanges, they may alter which speakers and argumentative strategies receive validation within the discussion.
  We study this interactional dimension by reconstructing 5,376 Debate.org debates as LLM conversations and running nearly 150,000 controlled multi-turn conversations that vary user political orientation, expertise, rhetorical strategy, and defended position, including conversations with competing users.
  Across naturalistic and controlled debates, we find that LLMs are systematically more receptive to left-leaning than right-leaning users. The asymmetry persists when users with different political orientations defend the same position and when opposing users appear in the same conversation, indicating that it is not fully explained by stance agreement or simple accommodation to the current speaker. Repeated interaction increases receptiveness without eliminating this ordering; expertise also matters, while rhetorical differences are smaller. The pattern appears across multiple models, but is not fixed: fine-tuning on different political corpora can largely erase or reverse it. These results show that LLMs can respond systematically differently to participants in the same political debate, making such interactional asymmetries important for understanding their emerging role in online public discourse.

papers.title: Small-Scale Magnetic Fields of Hyades M Dwarfs: Evolution with Age from the Pleiades to Field Stars
papers.abstract: Small-scale magnetic fields are derived for 18 M-dwarf stars in the Hyades open cluster through an analysis of Zeeman broadening in magnetically sensitive lines from the APOGEE spectra, resulting in mean magnetic fields ranging from 0.7 to 4.3 kG. Comparison with results for field stars hosting exoplanets and stars in the Pleiades open cluster from our previous works reveals distinct distributions of mean magnetic fields, reflecting differences in stellar age. Pleiades stars exhibit stronger fields ($2965\pm632$ G) and are predominantly in the saturated regime, while the roughly 500 million years older Hyades sample has weaker fields ($1925\pm1028$ G) with a larger dispersion, spanning both saturated and unsaturated regimes. Field stars show substantially weaker fields ($573\pm272$ G) and consistently occupy the unsaturated regime. Using the three samples, we derive the relationship between small-scale magnetic field strength and Rossby number, identifying saturation limits for the Rossby number ($\mathrm{Ro_{SAT}}=0.145$) and mean magnetic field ($\langle\mathrm{B}\rangle_{\rm SAT}=2452$ G). Within the Hyades sample, we find that, at a given age, cooler stars tend to have stronger magnetic fields. This trend is less apparent in the other samples, due to the broader age distribution of the field stars and magnetic saturation among the Pleiades stars. Comparisons with isochrones indicate positive correlations between mean magnetic field strength and both stellar radius inflation and photospheric spot coverage. We also find positive correlations between magnetic field strength and chromospheric and coronal activity, with stronger fields associated with larger H$\alpha$ equivalent width excess and higher X-ray-to-bolometric luminosity ratios.

papers.title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
papers.abstract: Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $\gamma \ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.

papers.title: Swarm Choreography Made Simple: Superposed Guiding Vector Fields for Rigid Formation Path Following
papers.abstract: This paper presents a decentralized guiding vector field framework for rigid formation path following in multi- UAV systems based on the superposition of simple rule-driven vector fields. Each control objective is encoded as a dedicated vector-field component: a normalized tangential term to ensure progression along a prescribed geometric path at a desired speed, a convergence term driving the formation toward the path, a local coordination term that preserves the desired formation shape through a pseudo-path parameter, and a local separation term for inter-agent collision avoidance. The coordination mechanism requires the exchange of only a single scalar per agent, resulting in low communication bandwidth. Partial theoretical results establish convergence of the swarm to the desired path and formation in the absence of the sepa- ration term, while collision avoidance is formally guaranteed. The approach is experimentally validated using a swarm of five quadrotors executing two 3D choreographies. The first experiment involves tracking a helical path while maintaining a rigid V-shaped formation. The second demonstrates a spiral- like motion obtained by a rotating circular formation tracking a vertical line. The experimental results support the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Improved regret bounds in tabular RL under local differential privacy
papers.abstract: We study regret minimization for time-homogeneous episodic tabular reinforcement learning with $S$ states and $A$ actions under non-interactive $\epsilon$-local differential privacy (LDP). In each episode $k \in [K]$, the decision-maker sends a policy to a user, the user executes the policy for $H$ steps, and sends an $\epsilon$-locally differentially private message back to the decision-maker. When $H=1$, the problem reduces to an LDP contextual bandit with $S$ contexts, $A$ arms and horizon $K$. We prove that the minimax regret is $\min\bigg(K, \frac{ \sqrt{\max( S, \exp(\epsilon) + 1) S A K (\exp(\epsilon) + 1)}}{\exp(\epsilon) - 1}\bigg)$, up to constants and a $\sqrt{\log(A)}$ factor. The upper bound is achieved by an adaptation of EXP3 and a unary encoding mechanism. When $H > 1$, and for small $\epsilon$, we show a lower bound in $\Omega(HS\frac{\sqrt{A K}}{\epsilon})$ and an upper bound in $\tilde{O}(H^2 S^2 \frac{\sqrt{ AK}}{\epsilon})$. The upper bound is achieved by an algorithm based on UCBVI and a unary encoding mechanism. For small $\epsilon$, these bounds improve the previously known lower bound by a factor $\sqrt{S}$ and the previously known upper bound by a factor of $H \sqrt{A}$.

authors.name: Hugo Richard
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

papers.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation Under Capacity Constraints: A Regime-Switching Value-Investing Game
papers.abstract: Edge computing service deployment requires the Network Operator (NO) and Service Providers (SPs) to coordinate investment and resource allocation under uncertain demand. This paper develops an audit-based service management framework for daily coalition formation with fixed capacity and service-level agreement (SLA) reservations. A two-stage coalitional game separates infrastructure investment from operational participation. Demand follows a Geometric Random Walk (GRW), and SPs apply an ordered admission and suspension rule using reported marginal contributions. With the NO held fixed, the operational coalition value is submodular; mandatory reservations can produce negative Shapley payoffs. We derive a separable benchmark, compute operational Shapley allocations, and give a sufficient condition for convergence to an individual equilibrium. A probabilistic audit mechanism provides a conditional daily truthfulness guarantee under verified settlement and enforceable penalties. For five service classes over three years, the reference run gains 12.4% over static grand-coalition membership and recovers 94.6% of the full-information optimum. Across 30 runs, the median gain is 13.3%. Sensitivity tests examine policy parameters, capacity and alternative demand models. The gain depends on capacity and update order; abundant capacity can make the admission rule underperform static membership.

authors.name: Rosario Patane
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Density and Current Fluctuations for Run-and-Tumble Particles With and Without Interactions
papers.abstract: We study density and current fluctuations in a one-dimensional gas of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs), whose intrinsic velocities switch between two opposite values at a constant rate. We consider particles with and without pair interactions, including regularized Riesz gases, and also obtain corresponding results for Brownian particles. By linearizing the Dean-Kawasaki (DK) equations around a homogeneous stationary state, we compute density correlations and the variance of the integrated current through the origin. For repulsive Riesz interactions decaying as $1/|x|^s$ with $s>0$, this variance grows at long times as $t^{1/2}$ for $s>1$, but as $t^{s/(1+s)}$ for $0<s<1$. Starting from the same DK description, but retaining the Poisson statistics of direction reversals, we derive a macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) for RTPs with smooth pair interaction potential, which allows to compute the large time large deviation of the time integrated current. We show that, in the absence of interactions, the MFT saddle point equations can be solved explicitly using a generalized Cole-Hopf transform. This allows to recover and generalize previous results for the current distribution obtained by microscopic calculations, for RTPs with annealed or quenched step initial conditions. Beyond these distributions, MFT allows to compute the optimal density histories producing a prescribed current through the origin. We find that these density profiles, for both RTPs and Brownian particles, exhibit a nontrivial space-time structure. We also study stationary current fluctuations on an interval connected to reservoirs. Finally, we analyze the MFT equations perturbatively in the interaction. In both the infinite-line and reservoir geometries, we obtain explicit first-order corrections to the current generating functions for short-range interacting RTPs and Brownian particles.

papers.title: CFD-driven symbolic regression of RANS transition models
papers.abstract: Laminar-turbulent transition governs skin friction, heat transfer and losses in turbomachinery, yet Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) transition models rely on empirical correlations and hand-calibrated activation functions whose structural deficiencies cannot be resolved by recalibration. We propose a CFD-driven sparse symbolic regression framework to learn interpretable, closed-form corrections to the production and destruction activation functions in the intermittency equation of the local, Galilean-invariant $k$-$\omega$-$\gamma$ model of Ge et al. Each correction combines a polynomial of a local pressure-gradient parameter, controlling amplitude and sign, with a bounded exponential of local flow features, controlling spatial support. This construction bounds the corrections without ad hoc limiters. Coefficients are identified by gradient-free optimization with the RANS solver in the loop, accelerated by POD-Kriging field surrogates, using mean-velocity data from wall-resolved large-eddy simulations (LES) of the ERCOFTAC T3 flat-plate cases. Elastic-net hyperparameters are selected automatically through bi-level optimization with leave-one-case-out cross-validation. The resulting model retains 11 of 21 candidate terms, compared with 20 under conventional grid-search tuning, while achieving comparable or slightly better accuracy on training and unseen cases. Both approaches recover the same leading-order correction. Applied without retraining to the transonic LS89 turbine cascade, far beyond the training envelope, the augmented model remains numerically robust and improves heat-transfer predictions at all four operating points, reducing errors by up to 70% where the baseline predicts premature transition under high freestream turbulence. Residual errors in transition onset and length highlight the limits of training on flat-plate data alone.

papers.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality
papers.abstract:
We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets.
  As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $\tau = \min\{\lambda,1-\lambda\}$ in the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}.
  Finally, in the same fashion as Krist\'aly and P\^irvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$

papers.title: Can We Stop the Backtest Yet? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Adaptive Financial Research Agents
papers.abstract: Financial research agents can generate and monitor trading rules faster than a human can document the resulting selection process. Candidates appear at data-dependent times, weak rules are abandoned, and promising ones are watched until they cross a reporting threshold. We introduce PROMOTE, a protocol that assigns every candidate predictable testing wealth at birth and accumulates a cost-aware e-process only from subsequent returns. If lifetime allocations sum to at most one, a weighted Ville argument bounds the probability of ever promoting a rule whose declared bounded net score has always had nonpositive conditional mean. The result permits dependent candidates, adaptive births, and indefinite monitoring. We audit the implementation in two settings. A retrospective pseudo-out-of-sample replay contains 24 panel--rule hypotheses, 3,000 shared-sign null paths, injected alternatives, and public ETF and industry data. Repeated unadjusted tests produce a family crossing in 94.5% of null paths, versus 0.0% for PROMOTE; at a 15-bp aligned ETF-component perturbation, PROMOTE has 70.1% target power and median crossing session 2,327. A separate exact mean-zero experiment lets an agent select candidate identities and birth times from past scores; the funded gate has 1.77% false-family crossings across 3,000 programs. The market replay produces zero promotions after costs. The certificate controls historical false promotion under the declared null; it is not a certificate that an earlier edge remains profitable at deployment. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks.

papers.title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
papers.abstract:
During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems:
  1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1).
  2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2).
  3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3).
  4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4).
  5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).

authors.name: Yana Teplitskaya
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line
papers.abstract: Propagating spin waves have emerged as promising candidates for signal processing and information transmission. We present a theoretical investigation of the generation, propagation and collection of spin-wave wave packets in micrometer-wide magnetic conduits, highlighting their potential for analogue frequency demultiplexing in space and time. We clarify the roles of the excitation duration and of the spin wave dispersion relation, as well as the influence of the spin-wave linewidth in setting the spatio-temporal evolution of propagating spin-wave wavepackets excited by Gaussian field pulses. We issue rules for the spatio-temporal separation of wavepackets that carry different frequencies. We finally propose an amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line of 60x5 $\mu$m$^2$ footprint.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Penalize the Common Trade: A Collision-Aware Layer for Learned Portfolios
papers.abstract: Different learning systems can make nearly the same trade when they share data, objectives, or representations. The market then sees decision concentration even if the models look diverse. We call exposure to this shared direction a signal collision. A linear-impact game shows the basic externality: each allocator chooses too much common exposure because it does not bear the full price effect imposed on others. An overlap-dependent toll recovers the social choice, and a feedback model gives the exact gain at which return-responsive allocation becomes unstable. We also state the restrictive spectral conditions under which a leading eigenportfolio can reveal the collision direction. These results motivate a simple post-model layer: subtract a penalty for loading on the recent common return mode before forming the portfolio. In a frozen panel of ten liquid cross-asset ETFs, 760 completed weeks from January 2012 through July 2026, and exact self-financing costs of 10 basis points per dollar traded, this layer changes maximum drawdown from 23.6% to 14.1%, volatility from 12.6% to 10.7%, and excess-return Sharpe from 0.664 to 0.667. A volatility-matched momentum diagnostic still draws down 19.9%. Paired stationary-bootstrap uncertainty is wide: the 95% interval for drawdown improvement is $[-3.3,18.4]$ percentage points and includes zero. The result establishes a reproducible risk-control association and specifies the holdings-and-flow validation needed to attribute the common direction to AI crowding. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks.

papers.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
papers.abstract: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). Two popular paradigms for improving the stability of learned dynamics are to train on interpolated or noisy samples or to regularize the Jacobian of the learned representation. In this work, we demonstrate that these paradigms can be understood under a common lens and that they both correspond to an approximation of the gradients obtained in an unrolled learning strategy. Building on this understanding, we derive a principled and complete approach to regularize training and demonstrate its impact on the stability of learned dynamical systems.

authors.name: Etienne Meunier
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: High-order in-cell discontinuous reconstruction path-conservative methods for conservative systems in primitive variables
papers.abstract: We present a path-conservative methodology for the numerical approximation of conservative systems formulated exclusively in primitive variables, the most physically relevant set of variables. The approach is designed to preserve the correct weak solution while avoiding the spurious oscillations near contact discontinuities that may arise in conservative formulations. Nonconservative products are treated through the selection of a suitable family of paths combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction strategy, which is locally activated near shocks. To choose the path we introduce a compatibility condition between the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions of the non-conservative form, with the exact ones, assumed to be known. In smooth regions and across contact discontinuities, a standard path-conservative scheme is employed. The method is further extended to achieve high-order accuracy. Numerical results for the Euler multimaterial and shear interface model demonstrates correct shock-capturing property, suppression of spurious oscillations due to contact discontinuities, and convergence without using hybrid formulations.

authors.name: Mario Ricchiuto
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The effects of an alternating bias on a single orbital spin impurity
papers.abstract: Electron spin resonance with the scanning tunneling microscope (ESR-STM) enables coherent manipulation and detection of individual atomic spins with atomic-scale spatial resolution, yet the microscopic mechanism by which the radiofrequency (RF) bias drives the spin remains under debate. We study this problem using a Redfield quantum-master-equation framework in which the oscillating bias enters explicitly through the electronic reservoirs rather than through an effective time-dependent tunneling amplitude. In the semiclassical limit, the RF voltage periodically sweeps the system through its static transport landscape, so that the transport regime depends jointly on the DC bias and RF amplitude. When the RF trajectory approaches or crosses a charge transition, the damping-like torque (DLT) associated with spin-polarized charge transfer is strongly enhanced. By contrast, the field-like torque (FLT) induced by the exchange field remains finite deeper in the Coulomb-blockade (CB) regime because it originates from virtual charge fluctuations. The RF trajectory also averages strongly bias-dependent static quantities over a finite voltage range, smoothing features such as the Lamb shift near the charge thresholds. These results establish the RF amplitude as a control parameter not only for the strength of the ESR drive, but also for the transport regime and the ratio between FLT and DLT.

authors.name: Jose Reina-Galvez
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: EmbryoProfiler: A Visual Clinical Decision Support System for IVF
papers.abstract: In-vitro fertilization (IVF) has become standard practice to address infertility, which affects more than one in ten couples in the US. However, current protocols yield relatively low success rates of about 20% per treatment cycle. A critical but complex and time-consuming step is the grading and selection of embryos for implantation. Although incubators with time-lapse microscopy have enabled computational analysis of embryo development, existing automated approaches either require extensive manual annotations or use opaque deep learning models that are hard for clinicians to validate and trust. We present EmbryoProfiler, a visual analytics system collaboratively developed with embryologists, biologists, and machine learning researchers to support clinicians in visually assessing embryo viability from time-lapse microscopy imagery. Our system incorporates a deep learning pipeline that automatically annotates microscopy images and extracts clinically interpretable features relevant for embryo grading. Our contributions include: (1) a semi-automatic, visualization-based workflow that guides clinicians through fertilization assessment, developmental timing evaluation, morphological inspection, and comparative analysis of embryos; (2) innovative interactive visualizations, such as cell-shape plots, designed to facilitate efficient analysis of morphological and developmental characteristics; and (3) an integrated, explainable machine learning classifier offering transparent, clinically-informed embryo viability scoring to predict live birth outcomes. Quantitative evaluation of our classifier and qualitative case studies conducted with practitioners demonstrate that EmbryoProfiler enables clinicians to make better-informed embryo selection decisions, potentially leading to improved clinical outcomes in IVF treatments.

papers.title: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
papers.abstract: Computing molecular free-energy landscapes over collective variables (CVs) is central to understanding molecular mechanisms, but poses a difficult learning problem without training data available a priori. Samples of the marginal CV distribution must be generated by molecular dynamics (MD), whose trajectories can remain trapped in metastable states and rarely cross the free-energy barriers governing conformational changes or chemical reactions. We introduce VESPER, which couples the generation of these samples to neural-network-driven free-energy learning: MD supplies configurations for learning, while the evolving model biases the MD to accelerate exploration and generate further training data. VESPER minimizes a single variational objective that is convex in the free energy and can combine several tempering levels, each flattening the free-energy landscape to promote barrier crossing. Every level has the same physical free energy as its minimizer, allowing data from all levels to train one shared model without reweighting. Learning uses the difference in mean parameter gradients between biased MD configurations and auxiliary walkers that explore the flattened model in CV space. We prove conditional convergence of the coupled overdamped population dynamics without replica exchange under log-Sobolev and Polyak-Lojasiewicz assumptions. VESPER matches or improves on established enhanced-sampling methods on alanine dipeptide and yields self-consistent free-energy reconstructions from three to six CVs on alanine tetrapeptide. For methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511) with a machine-learned interatomic potential, it recovers two-CV Boltzmann marginals and a reactant-to-saddle free-energy difference along a three-CV path, both qualitatively consistent with the lower-dimensional reference. It also samples RMSD-defined folded and unfolded regions of chignolin while biasing seventeen CVs.

papers.title: Scalaris: A Scalable Enterprise Memory Architecture for Conversational AI Assistants
papers.abstract: Enterprise conversational systems require memory to personalize interactions, retain information across sessions, and maintain conversational coherence. At enterprise scale, however, memory must not only retrieve relevant information accurately but also provide it efficiently to the answer-generation model. Existing memory systems face a trade-off between retrieval accuracy and context efficiency. Retrieving more context can improve recall but increases inference cost and latency. We present Scalaris, a scalable enterprise memory architecture that addresses this trade-off through a unified long-term and short-term memory design. We propose that user interactions and assistant responses possess distinct characteristics and roles in a conversation: user interactions capture evolving knowledge about the user and provide value across sessions, whereas assistant responses must be stored efficiently so that only information relevant to the current query is retrieved. We therefore treat them separately and support each with specialized representations and ingestion/retrieval pipelines. Scalaris reaches 92.2 % accuracy on LongMemEval-S and 90.77 % on LoCoMo using Qwen3-32B, state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks, while supplying the answer-generation model with approximately 10 times fewer retrieved context tokens than Hindsight, a leading memory system for conversational AI. When integrated with our proprietary closed-source AI assistants, Scalaris improved overall response quality by 36 %. Together, these results establish Scalaris as a cost-effective framework for building scalable, personalized conversational AI systems.

authors.name: Sarthak Pawar
authors.institution: MIT Art, Design and Technology University

papers.title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
papers.abstract: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance. Explicit graph filtrations illustrate the groupoid-valued construction, and so we suggest a new approach to interpret persistence diagrams and large data sets in topological data analysis, based on recent works of A-homotopy theory of the last years.

authors.name: Francesco G. Russo
authors.institution: École Nationale Supérieure de Techniques Avancées

papers.title: Likelihood-Free Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Sampling for Bayesian Inference with Fixed-Proposal Reuse
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian posterior sampling when the likelihood is an expectation that is costly to evaluate. We construct a likelihood-free Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer sampler whose drift is written as a ratio of expectations over Gaussian variables and simulator outputs and is estimated directly from joint draws of the two. Importance sampling with a fixed proposal allows the simulator outputs to be generated once and reused across all time steps and trajectories. For the likelihood-free Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer sampler, which draws new Monte Carlo samples at each step, we bound the terminal Wasserstein error under regularity and moment assumptions, separating time-discretization and integration errors. For the likelihood-free Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer sampler with sample reuse, we prove that the output converges to the posterior in the Wasserstein distance, assuming only a finite posterior second moment. Numerical experiments illustrate the reduction in simulator calls and the benefits of randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for drift estimation.

papers.title: Instance-Specific Sharp Convergence Rate of the Add-$\lambda$ Estimator via Feature Space Decomposition
papers.abstract: Using the Feature Space Decomposition framework, we establish non-asymptotic matching upper and lower bounds for the expected Kullback-Leibler estimation error of the Add-$\lambda$ estimator of a discrete probability distribution, for any signal, any dimension, any sample size, and any $\lambda>0$.

authors.name: Zong Shang
authors.institution: Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique

papers.title: Systematic Derivation of Leakage in Massey Secret Sharing Schemes
papers.abstract: Leakage attacks on secret sharing schemes can be based on the exploitation of partial information about individual shares to recover the underlying secret. In coding theory, linear exact repair schemes (LERSs) allow the recovery of a codeword symbol from limited information obtained from the remaining symbols. When applied to code-based secret sharing schemes, such repair schemes can be interpreted as recovering the secret from partial information about the shares, expressed in terms of subfield symbols. Guruswami and Wootters introduced the first explicit constructions of LERSs for low-rate Reed--Solomon codes that is optimal in terms of bandwidth. In this work, we first investigate the construction and algebraic properties of LERSs, building on the Guruswami-Wootters construction. We derive new explicit repair schemes from their construction and establish structural properties of the resulting schemes. Second, we further develop a systematic computational approach based on a Gr{\"o}bner bases approach to identify leakage functions associated with LERSs for arbitrary linear codes. This approach enables us to investigate the existence and structural properties of LERSs across different code families and parameter ranges. We first applied our method to Reed-Solomon codes, which gave as further insights into the algebraic structure of LERSs. Moreover, by applying our method to generalized Reed-Muller and Tamo-Barg codes, we identify several LERSs that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been described in the literature.

papers.title: FastAgent: A Physics-Aware FastFluent-to-Fluent Workflow for Rapid CFD Screening and Industrial Steam Dewaxing Design
papers.abstract: Industrial computational fluid dynamics (CFD) becomes costly when complex geometries, long transients and coupled physics must be evaluated across large design spaces. We introduce FastAgent, a physics-aware campaign controller built around FastFluent, a lightweight numerical engine for rapid physical screening. FastFluent supplies stage-specific fields and diagnostics; FastAgent allocates physical models, numerical resolution and simulation horizons by the active quantities of interest (QoIs), while returned Fluent discrepancies update subsequent decisions. Across six public CFD benchmark campaigns, the framework reduces normalised worst-QoI error by 5.68-99.14% and accelerates decision-relevant computation by factors of 1.53-15.36 relative to a matched Generic Agent control. Applied to high-pressure steam dewaxing in investment casting, FastAgent identifies nonuniform condensation heating as the dominant startup mechanism and separates rapid risk-window localisation from high-fidelity melt-completion confirmation. The rapid route requires 81.39% fewer cell-time updates than a fine-grid, small-time-step reference. Structural analysis localises fracture at the observed blade edge. Screening 131,072 outlet layouts and selectively evaluating candidates with Fluent and Abaqus identifies Sparse-6, which reduces simulated crack opening by 96.0% and connected crack extent by 66.7% relative to the Original design. These results demonstrate how rapid numerical evidence and adaptive fidelity control connect large CFD search spaces to mechanism-guided industrial design.

authors.name: Yuan Man
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique des 2 Infinis Irène Joliot-Curie

authors.name: Wu Lin
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Technology and Education

papers.title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
papers.abstract:
Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem.
  We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.

authors.name: Yi Yu
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique des 2 Infinis Irène Joliot-Curie

papers.title: Isogeny rigidity under algebraic group actions and finite translation orbits
papers.abstract: We study finite orbits generated by fibrewise translations on varieties carrying two abelian fibrations. Under natural dominance and generation hypotheses, non-isotriviality of the first family forces points with finite orbit to lie over proper closed subsets of both bases. This extends results of Corvaja, Tsimerman and Zannier to complex families of arbitrary, possibly different relative dimensions, including torsors. The proof combines relative Manin-Mumford with a general isogeny rigidity theorem for algebraic group actions.

papers.title: From Single-Shot QA to Continuous Perception: Revisiting the Energy Composition and Optimization Boundary of Edge VLMs
papers.abstract: Visual-prefill energy conclusions for edge vision-language models (VLMs) are commonly drawn under single-shot workloads; we revisit them under continuous perception. Profiling nine VLMs across three architecture families on Jetson AGX Thor and Orin (4,508 records, calibrated with a pure-text task), we find two mutually independent energy laws: the per-output-token decode cost grows monotonically with model scale, whereas the visual-prefill (image-encoding) cost is dominated by visual-encoder architectural efficiency, not scale. Under continuous perception ($N{=}10$) with sparse output, visual-prefill energy reaches 92--97\% of total. We derive optimization strategies---visual frame reuse, adaptive output truncation, task-aware routing, and encoder throughput optimization---for edge VLM deployment.

authors.name: Bo Peng
authors.institution: National Engineering Research Center of Electromagnetic Radiation Control Materials

papers.title: DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas
papers.abstract: Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at https://github.com/xinyuehuo/DramaVQA

papers.title: An all-weather microwave-based AI retrieval of pan-Arctic melt pond fraction
papers.abstract: Melt pond fraction (MPF) is a key variable governing Arctic sea ice albedo and seasonal sea ice predictability, yet existing pan-Arctic MPF products rely almost exclusively on optical sensors, limiting availability under cloud cover and seasonal darkness. This study presents PRISM-MPF, the first pan-Arctic, multi-year, all-weather MPF dataset, derived from PRISM (Polar Retrievals through Intelligent Sensor Merging), a machine learning framework fusing multi-source microwave observations with auxiliary thermal and spatiotemporal information to complement optical products. An XGBoost model was trained on eight melt seasons (2017-2025, excluding 2019) using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter, AMSR2 brightness temperatures and sea ice concentration, NOAA OISST sea surface temperature, and spatiotemporal descriptors (date and grid position). Three experiments assessed baseline skill and feature importance, independent sensor-group contributions (including CryoSat-2 radar freeboard), and regional specialisation, all under Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) cross-validation on unseen melt seasons. The baseline retrieval achieved a per-season mean R2=0.468 and RMSE=0.080 (pooled over 1,066,808 pixels: R2=0.532, RMSE=0.077), comparable to prior regional microwave-based studies, now at pan-Arctic, multi-year scale. Removing spatiotemporal features or C-band SAR reduced skill comparably (Delta R2=+0.089 and +0.085), whereas physical sensors alone outperformed spatiotemporal features alone (R2=0.375 vs 0.261), showing the two groups are complementary. Regional specialisation offered no advantage over a single pan-Arctic retrieval. This framework establishes a reproducible foundation for all-weather Arctic MPF monitoring, extensible to new sensors, longer records, and reference products.

papers.title: The upper main sequence in h and chi Persei
papers.abstract: Binary interactions play a crucial role in the evolution and eventual outcomes of massive stars. Rich young open clusters provide large coeval populations to constrain the effects of binary evolution. The Double Cluster, with a turn-off mass well above the threshold for core-collapse supernovae, is an excellent test bed for these processes. We used h and chi Persei, together with NGC 663, to constrain the evolutionary pathways of massive stars, particularly the role of binary interaction. We present spectroscopy of around 80 stars to obtain spectral types and derive stellar parameters. We combined this dataset with Gaia astrometry to evaluate their evolutionary status and possible evolutionary paths. We derived atmospheric parameters for almost 60 stars in the upper main sequence (B2V and earlier) and found broad agreement between two independent fully automated procedures. We identified the cluster turn-offs between B1 V and B1.5-2IV and differentiated this feature from the vicinity of theTAMS, where we found a population of B1-B1.5 giants, with a high fraction of Be stars. The bulk of the population in all of the massive clusters studied in the Perseus arm is consistent with single-star evolutionary models at a given age, but some B-type supergiants are much more luminous than any other cluster star. Their typical cluster kinematics and stellar parameters suggest a merger origin. Other lower-luminosity B-type supergiants seem consistent with the rest of the population. Kinematic analysis has indicated that most Be stars have not been dynamically perturbed by a supernova explosion. Those below the turn-off are likely to have been formed via case A mass transfer. The more massive Be stars above the turn-off do not display any other characteristic indicating a distinct evolutionary population (abridged)

papers.title: EEG-HealthLLM: Hierarchical Adaptation of Large Language Models for Unified Heterogeneous EEG Health Assessment
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive means for neurological and mental health assessment, yet existing EEG models are typically developed for individual tasks and are difficult to unify across heterogeneous signal configurations and assessment objectives. Large language models (LLMs) offer a common interface for multiple tasks, but adapting heterogeneous EEG signals to a shared LLM raises a key challenge: how to preserve task-specific signal characteristics while enabling effective language-side parameter sharing. To address this problem, we propose EEG-HealthLLM, a unified and parameter-efficient framework for heterogeneous EEG health assessment. We introduce an Asymmetric Hierarchical Adaptation Strategy: task-specific EEG adapters preserve heterogeneous spatio-temporal dynamics, while a unified shared LoRA is injected into the LLM backbone (e.g., Phi-3) to capture shared high-level assessment semantics across tasks.
