papers.title: How tightly can PBH abundance information constrain scalar-induced gravitational waves?
papers.abstract: Primordial black hole (PBH) abundances and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) probe the same primordial fluctuations through different physical weights. We examine the predictive power of precise synthetic information on absolute PBH abundances over a finite stellar-mass interval, together with an exact total abundance and external population bounds. For Gaussian perturbations under a fixed quantum chromodynamics (QCD) formation prescription, two smooth, symmetric lognormal spectra satisfy the same abundance conditions while producing nonproportional leading-order SIGW spectra. The two spectra differ by about 20% when averaged over the lower of two adjacent nanohertz windows but by nearly a factor of 60 in the higher-frequency window, so the difference cannot be represented by a single rescaling of the gravitational-wave background. Peak position and width compensate with amplitude in the abundance calculation, while the higher-frequency window draws almost all its energy from scalar-mode pairs with both wavenumbers above the primordial peak. Under the principal abundance benchmark, local finite-width components yield larger contrasts at a fixed nanohertz frequency through distinct mode couplings under both the QCD and stochastic peak-curvature formation prescriptions. For a separately generated population, extending mass information over most of its abundance restricts the lognormal peak-position and width compensation and reduces the higher-window contrast, while the unequal window responses persist. These results show why joint PBH-SIGW inference must propagate primordial shapes compatible with the PBH abundance information rather than assign one tensor template to a single abundance fit.

authors.name: Ruixin Zhou
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Materials Processing and Die & Mould Technology

papers.title: Microphone Geometry Aware Regional Target Speaker Extraction
papers.abstract: Regional target speaker extraction (RSE) aims to extract speech originating from a specified angular region, relaxing the requirement for precise target speaker location when performing location based speech extraction. However, existing RSE methods typically assume a fixed microphone array configuration and microphone number, limiting their applicability to unseen microphone geometries and varying numbers of microphones. In this work, we propose a geometry-aware RSE framework capable of extract with varying microphone array geometry and microphone numbers. Specifically, we introduce an attention-based multichannel front-end to encode inter-microphone phase information, together with a spatial audio reconstruction-based auxiliary objective to improve the front-end spatial representations quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves SI-SDRi by 5.1 dB over geometry-aware baselines across microphone arrays with four-microphones, while maintaining a performance gap of less than 0.6 dB compared with a tetrahedral geometry-specific baseline when evaluated on the tetrahedral microphone array.

papers.title: Unlikely likelihoods: likelihood analysis for the triangular and random histogram models
papers.abstract: This paper concerns certain parametric models for densities on the unit interval which lead to nonsmooth and nonregular likelihood functions. (i) The first is the simple triangular model on the unit interval, characterised by a density linearly increasing from zero to the mode position $\theta$ and then linearly decreasing to zero from the mode to one. With data from this model the likelihood function is a sum of individually log-convex terms, and with the derivative having discontinuities at each data point. (ii) The second is the one-parameter two-box density which is flat on $[0,\theta]$ and $(\theta,1]$, with $\theta$ the median. The likelihood has jumps at each datapoint. Here the maximum likelihood estimator is sharper than usual, with convergence in distribution of $n(\hat\theta-\theta)$ to a nonnormal limit. We also study the $k$-box extension of this model, with density being flat on $k$ boxes determined by $k$ quantiles. (iii) This second model is extended to the two-parameter two-box model, with areas $\gamma$ and $1-\gamma$ for boxes $[0,\theta]$ and $(\theta,1]$. Again the likelihood is nonregular, and the maximum likelihood estimators exhibit different rates of convergence for the breakpoints and the density values. The model generalises to the $2(k-1)$ parameter density piecewise flat over $k$ boxes. For each of these models we tend to the delicate task of sorting out the large-sample behaviour of the log-likelihoods, then leading to precise and partly nonstandard limit distributions for the maximum likelihood and Bayes estimators.

papers.title: Rapid microscopic decorrelation precedes sustained collective ordering in quenched two-dimensional colloids
papers.abstract: Independent Brownian noise can rapidly separate trajectories launched from the same microscopic configuration, but configuration-space distance need not reveal their later assembly outcomes. We studied this distinction in 480 two-dimensional Brownian-dynamics trajectories generated as three independent-noise replicas of 40 parent configurations under four finite-duration quenches. Ninety-two of 160 replica sets sharing one parent and one protocol reached both ordered and non-ordered terminal outcomes. A relative-diffusion calculation relates the free-particle mean-squared replica separation to the time-integrated diffusivity. The measured mean-squared separation remained about one-sixth of the free-particle reference, while its scaling was indistinguishable for replica pairs with the same and different outcomes. In contrast, outcome-resolved global sixfold order, ordered-particle population and coherence, and reciprocal-space translational order separated progressively after quench completion. With quench durations weighted equally, global order, the state score combining global and population order, coherence, and translational order remained informative 0.50 reduced time units before terminal assessment. This result persisted after either changing the terminal window or reducing the integration timestep. Transient threshold crossings were common, and 94.5\% of non-ordered crossings subsequently lost the required ordered-particle population. An independent $N=128$ ensemble showed state-score discrimination at temperatures for which both terminal classes occurred. The assembly dynamics therefore separate generic microscopic decorrelation from the later emergence and finite-window persistence of collective order associated with terminal structure.

authors.name: Ruixin Zhou
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Materials Processing and Die & Mould Technology

papers.title: Does Random Search Discover Task Experts? Revisiting Neural Thickets
papers.abstract: Pretrained models are typically viewed as generalists, requiring bespoke post-training to achieve task-specific expertise. Gan & Isola (2026) recently proposed a striking alternative: that pretrained models lie in a dense neural thicket of task specialists, which can be surfaced with simple Gaussian weight perturbations. We examine this neural thicket of task-specific experts and identify several key findings that question this perspective. First, we find that the apparent lift of the best-of-N selected perturbation decays quickly with selection-set size m, strongly suggesting overfitting to the selection questions. In fact, for 10 of the 12 model-task pairs we study, a simple null model of pure selection noise predicts more than 75 percent of the top expert's reward lift. Second, the top experts' advantage often vanishes on held-out questions or remains within the run-to-run variability of the unperturbed pretrained model. Third, we find that majority voting over the top-K selected perturbations, termed RandOpt(N, K) by Gan & Isola (2026), is often matched or outperformed by majority voting over K samples from the base model. Overall, our results suggest that random weight perturbations may be ineffective at uncovering task experts around pretrained models, and that task adaptation requires more sophistication than random search. Code and artifacts are available at github.com/asil012/RevisitingNeuralThickets.

papers.title: FiDeR: Denoising Astronomical Images at the Observational Resolution
papers.abstract: We present Finite-iteration Deconvolution--Reconvolution Denoising (FiDeR), a method for reducing noise in astronomical images while retaining approximately the input point-spread function (PSF). We first apply a finite number of Richardson--Lucy (RL) iterations to the nonnegative source-plus-background image. We then measure the response of a calibration point source processed with the same settings and derive a reconvolution kernel matched to the observational PSF. The calibration includes the background-to-source flux ratio. We compare FiDeR with six denoisers using simulated point-source and mixed stellar--galaxy fields, and observations from the James Webb Space Telescope Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) and Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI). In the stellar tests, bright-source widths remain close to the input widths; faint sources show small residual offsets. For the mixed field, FiDeR reaches peak signal-to-noise ratios of 46.701 and 44.850 dB at backgrounds of 10 and 20 counts per pixel, with wing errors of 0.657 and 0.858 counts. It also gives small aperture-flux and shape errors, although block-matching and three-dimensional filtering (BM3D) gives higher structural similarity. The NIRCam data show lower core and combined-region errors, while the three-exposure MIRI test gives benefits mainly in the stellar aperture and photometry. These results support substantial noise reduction with little change in the measured PSF within the tested regimes. The denoised images can provide inputs for further reconstruction and measurement; their uncertainties must account for residual noise correlations.

authors.name: Bin Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Aperture Photometric Accuracy of Point-spread-function-deconvolved Astronomical Images
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an improved Richardson--Lucy (RL) framework utilizing negative backfilling (NB) and the novel filtered image deconvolution and noise backfilling (FiDNoBa) algorithm. By integrating a low-pass prefiltering stage---specifically employing a Kalman filter---with the reintegration of filtered-out noise components after RL iterations, we effectively suppress noise artifacts while maintaining rigorous flux integrity. We extensively evaluate our Kalman + RL + NB approach using both numerical simulations and real observational data. Simulations across three regimes demonstrate superior photometric accuracy, reducing the relative mean deviation (RMD) to below 1\% for isolated sources, maintaining high fidelity (RMD $\sim$0.37\%) for blended S\'{e}rsic galaxies, and achieving $\sim$5\% RMD in crowded stellar fields while significantly increasing source recovery rates compared to traditional point-spread function photometry. Crucially, we validate the practical efficacy of FiDNoBa on real space-based (JWST/NIRCam) and ground-based (Very Large Telescope Survey Telescope OmegaCAM) images. The results confirm that our method reliably handles complex instrumental signatures, such as the extended wings of the STPSF, mitigating the severe ringing artifacts typical of traditional RL deconvolution while ensuring highly stable aperture photometry in practical survey processing.

authors.name: Fengshan Liu
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Large Geometry Models Are Priors For Fast Physics Pretraining
papers.abstract: Language and vision models became data-efficient by pretraining on plentiful unlabelled data; physical field models have such data, over ten million 3D shapes, but geometry pretraining designs its targets rather than deriving them from the physics. Euler-Lagrange geometry pretraining derives them: for attached flow, a shape enters the flow's Euler-Lagrange equation only through coefficients that distance and normal line (the normal up to sign) fix to first order. Their reconstruction error therefore bounds what a representation loses about any field, and fine-tuning on costly simulations need only assemble the global field. We realise it in AREALS, a masked surface autoencoder whose areal tokens carry position, normal and area, pretrained self-supervised and sign-free on 61,822 raw meshes. Because the operating condition enters only through the far field, sensors can supply it: AREALS completes a hidden field in one forward pass without condition labels. It matches the accuracy of the same architecture trained from scratch with half the simulations on DrivAerML and DrivAerNet++ and about a quarter on WindsorML. On DoubleDelta wings, 20 sensors give $3.9\times$ and $4.0\times$ lower field and force error than GABI, a Bayesian inversion method with a learned prior, and beyond the training angles pretraining halves the error.

papers.title: Solving the Mystery of the Electron Radiation Belt at Uranus: Leveraging Knowledge of Earth's Radiation Belts in a Re-Examination of Voyager 2 Observations
papers.abstract: Voyager 2 provided the only direct measurement of the radiation environment at Uranus and established the well-accepted characterization of a system with a weaker ion radiation belt and surprisingly intense electron radiation belt. Recent re-analysis of the flyby, however, suggests that these observations were not taken during normal solar wind conditions, and instead occurred while a large solar wind transient, a corotating interaction region, was passing over the system. With this context, this study compares the Voyager 2 observations to a similar event observed at Earth. This comparative approach, along with an expanded contextual interpretation of the Voyager 2 flyby, suggests that solar wind-magnetospheric interactions at Uranus may have driven enhanced lower band chorus wave emissions capable of accelerating electrons to relativistic energies. This motivates new, more expansive questions to be explored at Uranus and highlights the need for a Uranus orbiter mission.

authors.name: G. C. Ho
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Accessed, never disclosed: Silent access to protected health information by medical artificial intelligence agents
papers.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence agents should retrieve patient identifiers only when a task requires them, the data-minimization principle behind the HIPAA minimum necessary standard for protected health information (PHI). An agent can retrieve identifiers without revealing them. Such silent access remains invisible to evaluations that inspect only the output. We embedded canaries in synthetic patient records and linked each tool invocation to canary exposure in the final answers across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames for identifier-free clinical tasks. Three models invoked the PHI tools unnecessarily, whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 did not. Stronger boundaries reduced this access, and the residual access under the strictest policy was confined to frames in which the user overrode the policy or asserted approval. A pre-execution gate given the task-necessity criterion nearly eliminated this access. Output-only evaluation cannot verify minimum-necessary access; boundaries, gates, and access-log audits are required together.

papers.title: DexArena: A Unified Benchmark for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior.

papers.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
papers.abstract: Progress in AI is often measured by what a single model can do on its own. Yet teams of AI agents are starting to make breakthroughs and discoveries in science, medicine, mathematics and software engineering. As AI begins to work in teams of agents and people, the ability to collaborate becomes a core part of their intelligence. Research on human teams has measured this ability for decades. Inspired by this, we introduce the Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark, which measures how well an AI agent works as a teammate. It contains 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork, from refusing an unsafe shortcut to checking the work that a weaker model leaves behind. Each task comes from a real record or an existing benchmark, from aviation accident reports and clinical cases to coding tasks and negotiations, and has a programmatically verifiable outcome. To isolate teamwork from individual capability, models are scored only on tasks that they can solve by themselves when they have full information. We evaluate 18 closed- and open-weight models and find that every model, across sizes and families, has clear weaknesses as a teammate, with the best model scoring only 82.2 out of 100. Frontier models almost always refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct, yet they cave under interpersonal pressure, reaching the best overall deal in only 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate drops from 97% to 81% when they take over a task in which a weaker model has cheated. Crucially, general capability does not guarantee good teamwork, as models with nearly the same capability score differ by up to 11 points as teammates. The benchmark includes 160 public tasks with code and data, along with 80 held-out tasks for evaluation. As AI agents increasingly work alongside other agents and people, the ability to collaborate effectively is becoming a crucial capability to measure and develop.

papers.title: Does the Judge See What the Evaluation Requires? Input Assurance for LLM Agent Evaluation
papers.abstract: An LLM judge assesses agent steps from text packets. A renderer converts recorded runs into these packets, while software checkers test records and packets against requirements. We ask what evidence shows a packet is what the evaluation requires and propose four input-assurance obligations: required content survives rendering, checkers cover their requirements, a failed check stops later use and the judge reads the bytes last checked. In one pipeline with 30 trajectories, matching hashes, passing checkers and successful staging (copying packets for the judge) coexisted with violations of all four obligations, the last two in integration tests. The renderer omitted every structured tool call, leaving 53 of 60 judged steps blank despite matching hashes. For one judge configuration, later context raised error flags by 13 more on error than on correct steps. Restoring every call reduced this contrast to 2, a reduction of 11 (0.37 per trajectory, 95% cluster-bootstrap interval 0.17 to 0.53). In packets ending at the judged step, that configuration abstained at least once on every blank step, while the other four sometimes abstained but also flagged blank error and correct steps. Both separately written checkers accepted an unmatched tool result. In integration tests, a stub replacing the judge read a failed build's packet and a copy changed after staging. Three added controls stopped 18 of 19 constructed fault cases before the stub read any packet. The remaining stale script never ran. We turn the obligations into four tests and plan to evaluate their transfer to independent pipelines.

authors.name: Qinghua Lu
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

authors.name: Liming Zhu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: An Information Hierarchy of Privacy Filters and Odometers
papers.abstract:
In sequential data analysis, privacy loss accumulates over time, and privacy filters and odometers are used to control and track this cumulative cost. We study how the information used by differential privacy filters and odometers fundamentally limits what they can achieve. We formalise three levels of information: spec-level information, fixed prior to the interaction; mechanism-level information, which includes the mechanisms instantiated during the interaction; and realisation-level information, which further includes the realised interaction. We classify privacy filters and odometers by the least informative level sufficient to determine their behaviour.
  Our main results establish strict and arbitrarily large separations in achievable performance across this information hierarchy. For privacy filters, moving up the hierarchy can yield an unbounded utility advantage, quantified by a clipped measure of the number of allowed releases. For privacy odometers, it can yield an arbitrarily large improvement in precision, quantified by the expected peak excess of the reported bound over the realised privacy loss. Further, although the information classes are distinct, we show that moving to a richer class need incur essentially no loss in performance.
  Finally, we show that randomisation provides a resource orthogonal to information: at every information level, it can yield an arbitrarily large utility improvement over deterministic filters. Thus, information access and randomisation can be viewed as fundamental resources governing privacy procedures in adaptive interactions.

papers.title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers largely relies on a costly premise: preventing catastrophic forgetting requires either spawning a dedicated LoRA branch per session---causing adapter parameters to scale linearly with task horizon---or applying sparse Mixture-of-Experts gating symmetrically to both forward and backward passes, which sacrifices representational rank at test time. We argue that reading consolidated knowledge and writing new task credit are fundamentally asymmetric operations. Because visual features in a shared low-rank space distribute across rank-1 atoms rather than localizing in disjoint task silos, forward inference should read all atoms at full rank capacity, whereas backward optimization should restrict plasticity to a sparse subset of input-aligned channels. We introduce RASP (Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity LoRA), which adapts a single stationary-size adapter across sequential tasks. At each step, a scene-modulated cosine router selects the top-$q$ unlocked atoms to receive gradients, blocks updates on the remaining $r-q$ channels, and penalizes Frobenius Gram coherence between active and non-updated output directions. Across sessions, the router's empirical activation trace and each atom's exact spectral norm form a zero-overhead geometric consolidation index $\omega_j = \sqrt{\tilde{c}_j \tilde{\sigma}_j}$ that drives Cauchy step attenuation and boundary anchor locking. Across CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A, RASP matches or surpasses branch-expanding LoRA learners under a strictly constant parameter footprint.

papers.title: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition
papers.abstract: We introduce CoLa3D, a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition that, given a single whole-scene latent from either a single image or an existing scene mesh as input, directly outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be assembled back into a coherent scene. CoLa3D introduces a novel paradigm for 3D scene decomposition within a shared whole-scene latent, unlike alternatives that perform per-object generation in canonical spaces and then glue the objects back together with fragile pose and scale estimation. The network is a lightweight, flexible, and scalable query-based transformer that accepts various types of queries, including 2D masks, 3D points, and learnable queries, and learns to decompose the scene into objects in a compact latent space. On both synthetic and real-world datasets, CoLa3D achieves state-of-the-art performance on composable 3D scene decomposition, substantially improving global scene-level consistency and object-level quality while running 2 times faster and using less than 1% of SAM 3D's training data. Visible depth on par with MoGe2 further confirms that latent decomposition preserves accurate visible scene geometry while producing physically complete, decomposable object meshes.

papers.title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Exemplar-free continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers increasingly relies on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), yet prevailing methods govern the low-rank update space through strict subspace isolation. By projecting each incoming task into the approximate null space of historical token activations, isolation-based learners equate any cross-task feature overlap with catastrophic interference. We show that this orthogonality premise induces a structural bottleneck we term \emph{spectral starvation}: when down-projection bases are locked before task optimization, the gradient norm reaching the trainable up-projection is upper-bounded by the energy of current-task features captured by the chosen basis. Because natural visual tasks share low- and mid-level covariance structure, historical null tails contain barely $5.5\%$ of incoming task variance, starving new-class plasticity while blocking positive consolidation along shared directions. We propose BISECT (Bilevel Spectral Decomposition), a continual LoRA framework that partitions a fixed rank-$r$ budget into two orthogonal functional blocks: an invariant carrier spanned by the dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix, and a novelty complement extracted via generalized Rayleigh whitening followed by orthogonal complement projection. After single-task training, BISECT folds both blocks back into the frozen backbone using a closed-form precision gate that scales each rank-1 invariant atom by its current-to-joint Rayleigh ratio while preserving novelty atoms at unit gain. Across eight incremental settings on ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and DomainNet, BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines with zero extra inference parameters or FLOPs, and remains complementary to sparse analytic expansion.

papers.title: Inferring geometric structure from eigenfunction triple products
papers.abstract: This article presents two converses to well-known observations regarding products of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on a closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. First, if $(M,g)$ is real-analytic, the coefficients in the eigenfunction expansion of a product of eigenfunctions decay exponentially. We show that such exponential decay in fact implies that $g$ is real-analytic. Second, it is clear that if $(M,g)$ is flat, there exists an eigenbasis for which the product of any two of its elements lies in the span of at most $N = N(M,g)$ elements. We prove that any manifold with such an eigenbasis must be flat. We then construct metrics on $\mathbb{S}^7$ that share an eigenbasis with the standard metric yet are not locally homogeneous, from which we deduce that homogeneity cannot be characterized solely in terms of the multiplicative structure of eigenfunctions.

papers.title: CNN-Based Retinal OCT Classification: Research Gap Analysis and a From-Scratch Baseline, ED126-A
papers.abstract: Automated classification of retinal pathologies from Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images remains challenging because diagnostically relevant morphological patterns may exhibit substantial inter-class similarity. Although high classification accuracies have been reported on benchmark OCT datasets, cross-study comparison is limited by heterogeneous evaluation protocols and by the limited characterization of compact convolutional neural network (CNN) baselines trained from random initialization. This study addresses this gap through two contributions. First, it provides a focused review of CNN-based retinal OCT classification and identifies methodological considerations relevant to controlled benchmarking. Second, it presents ED126-A, a purpose-built four-class CNN baseline trained from scratch under a documented experimental protocol on the Kermany labeled OCT dataset. The model contains 1,241,380 total parameters, including 1,239,460 trainable parameters, and is evaluated using training-dynamics analysis, class-wise performance metrics, confusion-matrix analysis, confidence analysis, t-SNE representation-space visualization, Grad-CAM, hierarchical feature-map analysis, and one-vs-rest ROC/Precision-Recall analysis. On the image-level held-out test set, ED126-A achieved 95.03% accuracy, with a macro-F1 of 0.9205 and a weighted-F1 of 0.9521. The principal class-conditional limitation occurred for Drusen, which attained a recall of 0.9605 but a precision of 0.7493 and an F1-score of 0.8419. The confusion matrix identified Normal to Drusen and CNV to Drusen as major error channels. These results support the use of ED126-A as a documented from-scratch reference baseline and provide an empirical basis for controlled evaluation of transfer learning, increased depth, attention, multi-scale feature fusion, and calibration in subsequent studies.

papers.title: Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: Embodied agents are usually organized around individual tasks, yet the physical world keeps changing between tasks and during execution. We introduce LIFE (Lifelong Intelligence from Experience), a framework in which a robot observes continuously, remembers selectively, and turns experience into new capabilities. RoboBeats, a family of lightweight streaming gates, tracks conditions set by the agent and discovers new events, deciding when an observation warrants a response or a memory write. Selected observations enter Plastic Memory, a flat store of images and structured records that keeps the source evidence, so new fields and indexes can be added when later questions need them. When existing tools fall short, Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM) turns solutions found during problem solving into validated, reusable tools and skills. Under matched protocols, RoboBeats substantially improves condition tracking over its base models and, at the same writing budget, retains more useful evidence for memory question answering than uniform sampling. A case study of limited scale, replaying 24 hours of continuous video recorded by a real robot, illustrates how the integrated system builds memory from a day of experience and uses it to answer everyday questions. LIFE takes a step toward robots that become more familiar with their surroundings and more capable through experience: learning not only to complete tasks, but to live in the world.

authors.name: Yimeng Su
authors.institution: State Grid Shanxi Electric Power Company (China)

papers.title: Supervised Autonomous Bimanual Suction and Cauterization for Bleeding Control in Low Grade Splenic Trauma
papers.abstract: Uncontrolled hemorrhage remains a leading cause of preventable trauma mortality. Timely intervention is not always available, making autonomous systems that can aid in bleeding control a promising alternative. Given the safety-critical nature of the task, supervised autonomy, in which the system executes the technical steps while a human retains oversight, represents a necessary intermediate step toward this goal. In this work, we present a supervised autonomous bimanual robotic framework for injury cauterization (eletrosurgical coagulation) in low-grade splenic trauma. The system integrates real-time bleeding segmentation, markerless tool keypoint tracking, and deep tool-tissue contact detection to coordinate two robotic arms for synchronized suction and cauterization. Evaluated on a novel, cannulated ex vivo splenic hemorrhage model, the system achieved an average bleeding surface cauterization coverage of 82.9% across seven distinct injuries. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using a supervised autonomous bimanual system to deliver targeted coagulation across an injury site.

authors.name: Jiawei Ge
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: TME-ContextNet: Class-Conditioned Spatial Supervision and Grouped Decoding for Joint Nuclei Instance Segmentation and Classification
papers.abstract: Joint nuclei instance segmentation and classification requires precise boundaries and neighborhood information that helps distinguish morphologically similar cell types. We present TME-ContextNet, a multi-task framework that learns class-conditioned spatial context from existing nuclear annotations and organizes decoding into geometry-related and semantic task groups. Class-conditioned spatial supervision extends nuclear labels into a dense target using Euclidean distance transforms, requiring no additional tissue-region annotation. We derive its nearest-region interpretation and characterize its stability to small annotation perturbations. A local--global context module combines dilated convolution and self-attention, while a grouped task decoder reduces redundant computation. The spatial head supplies training supervision and is omitted during inference. Experiments on PanMix, CoNSeP, and PanNuke yield Dice scores of 80.23%, 65.32%, and 79.13%, and mean multi-class panoptic quality (mPQ+) scores of 67.62%, 35.50%, and 43.74%, respectively. PanNuke results are averaged across three test folds. Target and decoder controls support the combination of distance-based supervision and grouped decoding while identifying their dependence on task configuration. The framework uses 36.40 million parameters, compared with 54.74 million for HoVer-Net. These findings support a compact, context-aware formulation for joint nuclei analysis in computational pathology.

authors.name: Rukang Ma
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Bingxue Wang
authors.institution: Institute of Environment and Sustainable Development in Agriculture

authors.name: Luying Gui
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Tropical Cyclone Wind Field Diagnosis with Image-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel application of image-to-image generative adversarial networks (GANs) to produce a complete tropical cyclone (TC) surface wind field diagnosis from a single frame of satellite infrared brightness temperature (IR). Because TC surface wind fields are infrequently observed, we train on two data sets. The first contains 3,323 image pairs of IR and wind fields from Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF) simulations (WRF2WRF). The second contains 11,886 real IR satellite images paired with parametric wind fields built on the extended best-track data set (IBTrACS) of TC intensities and wind radii (GOES2PARA). Both models, conditioned on storm intensity, motion, and latitude, transform single-channel IR into wind fields over 6$^{\circ} \times$ 6$^{\circ}$ (WRF2WRF) and 7$^{\circ} \times$ 7$^{\circ}$ (GOES2PARA) domains, at 256 $\times$ 256 pixel resolution. GOES2PARA captures outer wind field asymmetries, enabling diagnosis of 64, 50, and 34-knot wind radii (R64, R50, R34) in each quadrant. WRF2WRF also produces detailed rainbands and eyewall asymmetries. Pixel-wise RMSE against held out truth demonstrates realistic wind field generation with mean RMSE of 6.4 knots (GOES2PARA) and 7.2 knots (WRF2WRF). Compared against IBTrACS, WRF2WRF achieved mean absolute errors (MAE) of 14.8 nautical miles (NM) for radius of maximum wind (RMW) and 25.9 NM for R34. GOES2PARA achieved 10.0 NM MAE for RMW and 25.9 NM for R34. Against Synthetic Aperture Radar wind fields GOES2PARA yielded a lower mean pixel-wise error (RMSE 12.1 kt, MAE 9.5 kt) than WRF2WRF (RMSE 13.9 kt, MAE 11.3 kt). Unlike many existing operational surface wind speed algorithms, our image-to-image models provide updated wind fields with every new satellite image.

papers.title: Finite Global $H_{\infty}$ Optimization of the $Q$-Filter Time Constant for Nominal-Response Recovery in SISO Disturbance Observers under Parametric Plant Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This paper develops a finite real-algebraic procedure for global H-infinity optimization of the time constant of a fixed-shape Q-filter in a single-input/single-output (SISO) disturbance observer (DOB) under affine parametric plant uncertainty. Robust internal stability defines a possibly disconnected feasible domain, and the objective is the worst-case weighted mismatch between the uncertain DOB reference response and the nominal closed-loop response. A recovery-error factorization preserves affine dependence of the performance numerator and denominator on the same uncertainty vector. Phase lifting and a complex-polynomial Edge theorem reduce the uncertainty box to finitely many polynomial edges, while quadratic dependence of the squared frequency-domain inequality on the edge coordinate permits analytic elimination of that coordinate. The resulting semialgebraic formulation has only the squared frequency as a universally quantified variable. It determines the global infimum, decides whether it is attained, and constructs the complete optimizer set over the full robust-stability domain. A DOB case study with a plant family containing non-minimum-phase members yields a unique optimal time constant of approximately 0.0364075 and a worst-case norm of approximately 2.29975. The optimizer lies strictly inside the first robust-stability component, and every smaller feasible time constant in that component has a larger worst-case norm. Finite algebraic certificates establish robust stability, performance feasibility, and strict global optimality.

papers.title: AnchorKV: Lossless Key-Value Cache Reconstruction from Layer-Sparse Residual Anchors
papers.abstract: Residual-stream caching can reconstruct transformer key-value (KV) caches losslessly, but its memory advantage depends on architecture. We present AnchorKV, a storage-replay spectrum connecting per-layer residual caching and full recomputation through configurable residual anchors. An architecture-dependent break-even rule identifies the first storage-saving spacing, while deployment selects an operating point from the spectrum and cascade replay reduces reconstruction from O(Ls) to O(L), with L the model depth and s the anchor spacing. For interleaved sliding-window architectures, exact dynamic programming places anchors under non-uniform reconstruction demand. Across CPU, CUDA, and Ascend NPU backends, six architecture families, and fp32/bf16 arithmetic, evaluations verify bit-exact KV reconstruction and unchanged continuation logits and tokens. At 4k context, cascade reconstruction is up to 16.3 times faster than naive replay; across eight applicable global-attention checkpoints at 32k context, deepest spacing yields 5.78-54.0 times full-KV reactivatable session capacity. Compared with seven external cache methods on a common model, AnchorKV preserves full-cache retrieval and question-answering scores, whereas lossy methods change output fidelity and task scores. The break-even spacing is computable from a model's configuration file alone.

papers.title: MemRole: From Memories to Decisions for Long-Horizon Reasoning in Role-Playing Agents
papers.abstract: LLM-based role-playing agents are fluent at imitating a character's style, yet struggle to make role-consistent decisions over long narrative horizons. Such decisions are shaped by experiences spanning many prior scenes, which are often partial and may point in different directions. Existing methods inject cross-scene memories as context, but do not reason about how past events shape a character's current motivations and behavior. We propose MemRole, a framework that makes this memory-to-decision process explicit. It introduces Long-Horizon Memory Thinking (LHMT), a reasoning schema that decomposes hidden reasoning into context understanding, memory activation, and response strategy planning, trained on a novel-derived dataset whose character-grounded, timeline-constrained memory pools limit each character to what it could plausibly know at the current narrative point. Beyond supervised fine-tuning, we propose Self-Refining On-Policy Self-Distillation (SR-OPSD): the model critiques its own rollouts against the reference under a data-driven rubric, and a critique-conditioned teacher view of the same model distills token-level guidance back into the policy. MemRole-32B improves over its backbone by 15.2 points on memory-grounded role-playing, performs on par with frontier LLMs such as GPT-5.4, and achieves the best character-motivation recognition accuracy on CroSS-MR.

papers.title: EvoRec: A Unified Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender with Dynamic Reflection Trees
papers.abstract: Conventional recommender systems rely on fixed cascaded pipelines, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving user needs and feedback. Existing agentic recommenders introduce reasoning and tool use but often lack end-to-end decision control and systematic failure reflection. We propose EvoRec, a unified agentic recommendation framework that combines autonomous decision-making with reflection-driven self-evolution. A Need Agent infers user needs from long-term, short-term, and working memory. A Planning Agent adaptively allocates retrieval budgets between Behavior Continuation and Need Satisfaction, selects retrieval tools, and sets ranking-fusion weights. An Acting Executor executes the plan and records decision traces. Following user feedback, a Dynamic Reflection Tree identifies failures in need inference, planning, or previous repairs, proposes personalized corrections, and validates them through replay. Verified repairs update working memory and are distilled into reusable cross-user strategies, enabling continual improvement without parameter updates. Experiments on a Kuaishou local-services advertising dataset show a 15.7% Hit@50 improvement over the strongest baseline. Hierarchical reflection further improves Hit@50 by 13.1% among users with prior repairs. In a seven-day online A/B test, nearline EvoRec increases advertising revenue by 4.6% and CTCVR by 3.5%, with a 14.5% revenue gain for high-intent users. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of reflection-driven self-evolution in industrial-scale recommendation.

papers.title: On the probability that the integer parts of polynomials are coprime
papers.abstract:
We prove that for any $s\ge 2$ and polynomials $f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{s-1}(x)\in \mathbb{R}[x]$ satisfying a certain equidistribution condition, the natural density of the numbers $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $n,\lfloor f_{1}(n)\rfloor,\dots,\lfloor f_{s-1}(n)\rfloor$ are mutually coprime is $1/\zeta(s)$.
  This generalises a recent result of Champagne, in which this was proven under the assumption that $f_{1}$ is linear.

papers.title: Decomposition Atlases of Brains and Kidneys from Postmortem CT: Shape and Topological Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Forensic assessments of postmortem decomposition often rely on external, whole-body signs, yet structural changes within organs remain largely unquantified. Using whole-body computed tomography scans of 59 decedents from the New Mexico Decedent Image Database, we conduct an organ-level statistical shape analysis of decomposing brains and kidneys, representing each organ as a three-dimensional point cloud of its outer surface and internal cavity boundaries. Decomposition creates voids, fragmentation, and structural heterogeneity, complicating point correspondence. Registration-based principal component analysis and principal nested cones yield interpretable orderings for brains only. We therefore construct a registration-free pipeline using persistent homology and a fusion of complementary topological distances selected through simulations of cavity formation and growth. Clustering identifies broad patterns of internal decay, and seriation produces organ-specific decomposition atlases. The brain atlas combines geometric and topological rankings; the kidney atlas uses topology alone. Rank agreement is higher between paired kidneys (Kendall's $\tau = 0.59$) than between brains and kidneys ($\tau = 0.34$ to $0.39$), indicating asynchronous decompositions within a body. Whole-body stages agree more closely with brain than with kidney rankings. These findings support quantitative forensic taphonomy by complementing whole-body staging with organ-level, interior-based measurements. We release the organ point clouds and analysis code to support research on organ decomposition and shape analysis without reliable correspondence.

papers.title: Spontaneous Chirality and Collective Chern Bands in a Dipole-Conserving Bose System
papers.abstract: We demonstrate spontaneous chiral dipole order and an isolated collective Chern band in a time-reversal-symmetric microscopic bosonic lattice model with exact dipole-moment conservation. In a controlled large-occupation limit at zero temperature, frustrated dipole exchange and three-particle conversion stabilize two time-reversed chiral condensates. The two dipole Goldstone modes remain gapless, while a separate finite-frequency band carries Chern numbers $-1$ and $+1$ in the opposite domains. We trace this topology to complex mode couplings in the chiral background that gap finite-frequency Dirac crossings. Site-resolved density drives preserve dipole-moment conservation and reconstruct the band Chern number from band-resolved absorption spectra in the quadratic theory.

papers.title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
papers.abstract: The cuscuton is a scalar field that obeys a constraint rather than an evolution equation, so it modifies gravity without adding a propagating scalar degree of freedom. We study the cosmology of effective cuscuton theory when matter is minimally coupled in the Jordan frame, and therefore conformally coupled to the cuscuton in the Einstein-frame. We derive the background and linear perturbation equations and show that the algebraic cuscuton response mediates a fifth force even though the scalar itself does not propagate. The same conformal factor also changes Einstein-frame particle masses and the friction of matter perturbations, tying the strength and sign of the force to the background evolution rather than to an independent coupling. We study a power-law family of models which contain both tracking solutions and sign-switching solutions; in the latter the effective cuscuton density runs from negative during matter domination to a positive, cosmological-constant-like value today. Using a modified version of CLASS, including the induced particle-mass dependence of recombination, we illustrate the corresponding changes to CMB temperature and linear matter power spectra for benchmark models, without fitting to data. In the strongest benchmarks the fifth force changes the effective gravitational coupling on sub-horizon scales by about one percent, smaller than the accompanying changes to the matter power spectrum and the acoustic scale. For the sign-switching solutions this change is negative over most of cosmic history, so a non-propagating field can weaken rather than strengthen gravitational attraction.

papers.title: Revisiting LLM Homogeneity Through a Multidimensional Lens
papers.abstract: Concerns about LLM homogeneity are typically quantified with embedding similarity, which reduces two texts to a single score. We revisit homogeneity with 25 interpretable metrics spanning five dimensions: semantic, lexical, syntactic, structural, and stylistic & presentational. A human study shows that perceived similarity depends on both content (what responses say) and form (how they say it), yet embedding similarity correlates less with human meaning judgments than sentence-level matching ($\rho=0.417$ vs. $0.606$) and not significantly with form judgments ($\rho=0.140$). Across 18 contemporary LLMs, models say similar things in different words: they share global semantics and broad linguistic profiles but remain distinct in lexical characteristics, structural patterns, and interactional conventions. Across releases from 2024 to 2026, models become more like themselves but not more like one another: among significantly changing metrics, intra-model distances decrease for 17 of 22, and inter-model distances increase for 14 of 21. Across two post-training pipelines, model-specific conventions emerge during SFT and are selectively reshaped by preference optimization. These results suggest that homogeneity is multidimensional and evolving, and that embedding similarity alone can overstate cross-model homogeneity while concealing diverging intra- and inter-model trends.

papers.title: HQNN-CL: Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Neural Network with Continual Learning for Financial Forecasting
papers.abstract: Financial time-series forecasting is still difficult owing to the non-stationary nature of the market, regime changes, and catastrophic forgetting, which makes conventional deep learning models hard to adapt in the long term. To achieve uncertainty-aware robust financial forecasting in the face of changing market conditions, this study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Continual Learning (HQNN-CL). The proposed framework combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) based regime detection, BiLSTM temporal encoding, adaptive-depth parameterized quantum circuits, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), experience replay, and probabilistic forecasting in a single architecture. The framework was tested on four real-time stock datasets: Microsoft, Systems Limited, Teradata and Tata Consultancy Services, and compared with seven state-of-the-art forecasting models, including recurrent and Transformer-based models. The experimental results show that HQNN-CL has outperformed other methods on the Systems Limited (RMSE = 3.0149) and Teradata (RMSE = 0.8909) datasets and is within 0.32% and 0.40% of the best baseline method for Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services, respectively. The proposed framework also generates well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts within the range of 89.5% to 96.5% empirical coverage rate, has zero catastrophic forgetting (BWT = 0.0000) for all sequential learning tasks, and consistently shows positive forward transfer. Ablation and statistical significance analyses also validate the performance of adaptive quantum feature learning and continual adaptation under heterogeneous market conditions, regime-wise.

papers.title: StateFence: Task-State Protection Against Evidence-Chain Contamination in Blue-Team LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Indirect prompt injection creates a distinctive risk for blue-team Large Language Model (LLM) agents in Security Operations Centers (SOCs). Malicious instructions can be embedded in telemetry, tickets, retrieval results, or memory and then propagate through alert triage, incident summarization, response recommendation, and Indicator of Compromise (IOC) extraction as locally plausible intermediate decisions. We characterize this failure mode as evidence-chain contamination of protected task state. The main challenge is task dependent: a suspicious string may be malicious control text for summarization but essential evidence for IOC extraction. To address this challenge, we propose StateFence, a task-aware evaluation and defense framework that treats severity labels, incident narratives, response policies, and IOC sets as protected states. StateFence maps indirect prompt-injection attacks into explicit, stealth, multi-hop, and persistent SOC evidence attacks, records observable propagation traces, and routes defenses according to the attacked state. Across controlled SOC cases and public-SOC validation cases, StateFence lowers attack success and reduces failures that appear only after evidence is poisoned, while preserving task utility and avoiding the indicator loss caused by task-mismatched filtering. Our findings indicate that robust blue-team LLM agents require mechanisms that preserve task-critical state under untrusted evidence.

papers.title: Integrating Domain Adaptation and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Saline-Alkali Land Reclamation Planning
papers.abstract: Reclamation of saline-alkali land requires management plans that account for soil and water conditions, treatment evidence, and financial constraints. This study develops Wenyao, an agricultural decision-support system integrating domain adaptation with retrieval-augmented generation. A bilingual corpus of 8,664 research papers was processed using a 110-indicator schema to construct SA-Bench, comprising 4,860 paper-level planning instances. A QwQ-32B model was adapted through low-rank supervised fine-tuning and combined with case retrieval for budget-conditioned planning. Evidence extraction achieved an F1-score of 0.83 on 300 expert-annotated papers. Without retrieval, Wenyao achieved 95.83% accuracy on 936 source-disjoint multiple-choice questions, compared with 87.93% for the strongest general-purpose baseline; removing explanatory supervision reduced accuracy to 89.42%. Matched-evidence comparisons across 69 region-budget cases supported complementary contributions from adaptation and retrieval. In a blind assessment by 31 experts, Wenyao with retrieval obtained the highest mean scores for objectives and projected outcomes, whereas GPT-5 scored highest for cost estimates. These findings support literature-informed reclamation planning with professional review, while ongoing field monitoring will assess soil and crop responses.

papers.title: A conditional generative model for T2-weighted prostate MRI with downstream evaluation in clinically significant cancer classificatio
papers.abstract: Scarce and unrepresentative training data limit the performance of prostate MRI prediction models. Synthetic T2-weighted (T2W) MRI may augment training data containing clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) and transition zone (TZ) lesions. In this retrospective, single-center, ethics-committee-approved study, we developed a conditional generative model for T2W prostate MRI extending MAISI-v2 with csPCa class, zonal, and lesion-mask-guided conditioning, incorporating a relative advantage weighted loss fine-tuned on 1,303 patients (1,654 lesions). Fidelity was assessed by incremental ablation, and downstream utility was evaluated with T2W-based csPCa classifiers across five simulated training-data scenarios, each testing 18 synthetic-data configurations. The proposed model reduced Fr\'echet inception distance (FID) from 13.28 (pretrained MAISI-v2) to $2.04 \pm 0.06$ internally (PI-CAI: $3.83 \pm 0.51$). Synthetic augmentation significantly increased AUC in all five scenarios (+0.027 to +0.088; adjusted $p = 0.016$--$0.043$), though cross-institutional augmentation of PI-CAI yielded a non-significant gain (+0.013; $p = 0.397$). Overall, our model improved T2W MRI fidelity, and synthetic images improved csPCa classification under simulated data constraints, although benefit did not transfer significantly across institutions.

papers.title: Persistence of $C^2$ regularity for aggregation patches
papers.abstract: We prove persistence of $C^2$ boundary regularity for patch solutions of the two-dimensional aggregation transport equation, in contrast with the known $C^2$ ill-posedness of Euler vortex patches. More generally, we consider transport equations with kernels of the form $L(\nabla N)$, where $N$ is the fundamental solution of the Laplacian and $L$ is a linear map. We show that $C^2$ regularity persists for every $C^2$ initial patch if and only if $L$ is a scalar multiple of the identity. Our approach builds on the curvature formulation introduced by Kiselev and Luo.

papers.title: ROSE: Deep Learning exchange-correlation functional from reduced density-matrix representations
papers.abstract: We introduce ROSE, a deep-learning exchange--correlation energy functional built from the occupied-state density matrix. On GMTKN55 and on additional external benchmarks considered in this work, ROSE improves over modern neural network functionals trained under matched protocols and is on average more accurate than, or on par with, most hybrid and range-separated hybrid functionals considered here. On the experimental benchmarks considered here it has leading accuracy across hybrids, range separated hybrids, and neural functionals. These results motivate nonlocal density-matrix representations as a route to systematic improvement of learned XC functionals with low computational cost.

papers.title: Episodic Protostellar Outflows: A Proper Motion Study in Serpens South
papers.abstract: Serpens South is a notable protostellar cluster with signatures of recent star formation, including a high protostellar fraction. Within the region, several protostars provide important mechanical feedback via outflows. We investigate the molecular outflow driven by the Class 0 protostar known as CARMA-7, which is located in the central hub of Serpens South. Two epochs of observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) with sub-arcsecond resolution capture the well-collimated, episodic outflow with distinct ejecta knots. This outflow, traced with 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7, appears to be mostly blueshifted to the south and redshifted to the north, with radial velocities up to at least 25 km/s. We present the first proper motion study of this outflow by comparing observations taken in 2017 and 2021. The measured proper motions trace the ejection history and refine the inferred outflow morphology. We find that proper motions of the 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7 knots range between 10 - 40 mas/yr, corresponding to 30-90 km/s. Using radial velocities and proper motions, we determined that the inclinations of the outflow lobes are ~60 -80 degrees relative to the line of sight. Finally, we measure ejection timescales as recent as ~10 to ~120 years, and we discuss this in the context of other known protostars with recent ejecta events.

papers.title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
papers.abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $\pi$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $\pi((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-\kappa}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $\kappa>0$ solves $p^\kappa+p\kappa=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.

authors.name: Grigory Terlov
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Multiplicity and Uniqueness of Stationary Expected Payoffs in Coalitional Bargaining
papers.abstract: I study uniqueness of stationary expected payoffs in random-proposer coalitional bargaining with transferable utility. Proposer independence of coalition surplus does not guarantee uniqueness, even when the surplus is strictly monotone and every equilibrium features immediate agreement. For $M^\natural$-concave characteristic functions, including non-monotone ones, I show that stationary expected payoffs are unique and continuous in the primitives, provided that every equilibrium features immediate agreement. To prove uniqueness, I identify an equitable grouping property of maximizing coalitions and show that $M^\natural$-concavity implies it at every no-delay candidate payoff vector. Using equitable grouping, I show that every no-delay equilibrium payoff vector is isolated and has positive local index. For parameter changes that preserve immediate agreement in every equilibrium, a uniform increase in a player's contribution to every coalition containing her strictly increases her expected payoff, while an increase in her discount factor weakly increases it. I apply these results to joint ventures with coordination costs and government formation with ministerial expertise.

papers.title: Extremal permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with many good slopes and applications to quantum Latin squares
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We prove the sharp upper bound $\varphi(n)$ on the number of good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. We classify and count the equality cases for prime powers and products of two distinct odd primes. Non-affine equality cases exist for every composite $n\ge6$. We also prove the sharp bound $p_0-1$ for the size of a set of good slopes with invertible differences between distinct elements, where $p_0$ is the least prime divisor of $n$. Finally, we establish gap results below $\varphi(n)$ and apply our bounds to a construction of quantum Latin squares due to Ball and Simoens.

papers.title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
papers.abstract: Convection-diffusion equations are fundamental models for transport phenomena, but their numerical solution becomes challenging in convection-dominated regimes due to steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. This motivates the development of accurate approaches capable of effectively resolving such features while avoiding costly iterative optimization. In this study, a modified ELM framework based on shifted Legendre polynomials is developed for convection-diffusion equations in steady-state, continuous-time, and discrete-time formulations. The proposed approach is evaluated on steady and unsteady benchmark problems with relatively high Peclet numbers, including continuous and discontinuous boundary conditions. Finite element method solutions are used as independent solution references. By exploiting the linearity of the governing equations, MELM determines the output weights through a single least-squares solve, avoiding the iterative gradient-based training required by PINNs. The shifted Legendre polynomial basis provides an effective spectral representation for resolving steep gradients and sharp boundary layers. For the DT-MELM formulation, the coefficient matrix remains unchanged across successive time levels, allowing its LU or QR factorization to be computed once and reused. A systematic comparison with PINNs that incorporate advanced training strategies demonstrates that MELM provides higher accuracy and shorter solution times for steady-state and DT-MELM formulations across the benchmark problems considered. In contrast, CT-MELM exhibits scalability limitations as the size of the space--time basis increases. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of MELM for steady-state and discrete-time convection--diffusion problems, while also showing that PINNs provide better scalability for large space--time formulations where global CT-MELM becomes computationally demanding.

authors.name: Ramon Codina
authors.institution: International Center for Numerical Methods in Engineering

papers.title: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration
papers.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$. Prior FPGA works follow two approaches: accelerating entire FHE schemes, which yields significant speedups but ties them to specific parameters and algorithms, or accelerating only the NTT, which applies across schemes, algorithms, and libraries. Most FPGA NTT designs require interconnects that grow with parallelism and utilize significant resources, which complicates routing on multi-die FPGAs. Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, end-to-end NTT acceleration within an FHE context has so far been left unexplored. We design a fully unrolled, delay-commutator streaming NTT/INTT kernel, and floorplan it across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80. At 400 MHz, the kernel transforms a polynomial of $2^{16}$ coefficients every 5.12 $\mu$s, the highest throughput among FPGA designs at this size. Offloaded end to end, it is up to 22x faster than the CPU per transform. We integrate the kernel into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluate it end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, it accelerates core FHE operations, such as key switching and bootstrapping, by 1.8-2.2x, and neural network inference by 1.8-2.1x.

papers.title: Stability of least-energy solutions of the harmonic map flow from the plane into the 2-sphere
papers.abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of the least-energy harmonic map $W:\mathbb R^2\to S^2$ for the harmonic map flow under small, sufficiently decaying, non-symmetric perturbations. Solutions exist globally and are asymptotically described by a modulation of $W$ plus a remainder that converges to zero as $t\to\infty$. The modulation parameters associated with scaling, rotation, and translation remain close to their initial values and converge to finite limits. The proof relies on an inner-outer gluing decomposition and the analysis of a non-local equation governing the modulation parameters.

papers.title: Magnetoelectric Wireless Power Transfer Receivers for Sub-Millimeter Scale Implantable Bioelectronics
papers.abstract: Implanted biomedical devices for continuous physiological monitoring require reliable wireless power delivery to anatomically constrained and sensitive sites where batteries are impractical or hazardous. Existing wireless power transfer (WPT) modalities, including inductive coils and ultrasonic transducers suffer from performance degradation as receiver dimensions are miniaturized, limiting their application for space-limited locations such as fingertips, the ocular cavity, and intracranial sites. We present a microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) magnetoelectric WPT receiver integrating piezoelectric aluminum scandium nitride and magnetostrictive iron-cobalt/silver multilayer thin-films, microfabricated within a footprint of 770 x 360 x 2.25 micrometers. The receiver operates at its 100 kHz flexural-mode resonance with a quality factor of 1180 and delivers 1.0 microwatt to a matched 10 kohm load under a standard-compliant 205 micro-Tesla RMS excitation field. This device exhibits a magnetoelectric coefficient of 1274 V cm-1 Oe-1 and a power figure of merit (FOMP) of 4.05 x 10-3 mW cm-3 Oe-2 Hz-1, both the highest reported values of comparable magnetoelectric WPT receivers. The FOM is 20-fold higher than the next best comparable-frequency device. These miniaturized devices establish MEMS magnetoelectric transduction as a scalable platform for battery-free wireless powering of microwatt-class implants in the most anatomically demanding regions of the body.

papers.title: Can Agentic AI Undermine Its Own Assurance Loop? Closed-Loop Dependency Assurance for Cognitive Network Digital Twins
papers.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Network Digital Twins (NDTs) are increasingly combined to form Cognitive Digital Twins (CDTs) that translate operational intents into network changes and support closed-loop management. However, a network change may achieve its intended objective while disrupting the monitoring or recovery mechanisms needed for subsequent decisions. For example, a service may be rerouted while its latency-monitoring traffic continues along the original path, producing measurements that no longer reflect the service's performance. We propose Closed-Loop Dependency Assurance (CLDA), an assurance mechanism that augments agentic AI-enabled NDTs with dependency-aware validation. In our framework, an agentic AI planner generates and refines network plans, while the NDT evaluates the projected network outcomes of these plans. CLDA extends this analysis using a Loop Dependency Graph (LDG) that connects service requirements to monitoring mechanisms, forwarding paths, failure domains, and recovery prerequisites. CLDA projects candidate actions onto these dependencies, checks intermediate states of multistep plans, and supports deterministic make-before-break repairs using temporary monitoring mechanisms. Unlike the Large Language Model (LLM)-based planner, CLDA uses explicit, deterministic rules for assurance decisions and repair. We evaluate CLDA through controlled reconfigurations, a 240-trial LLM-based planning campaign, and live network execution. A separate synthetic study examines deterministic assurance scalability across network models representing up to 1,024 routers.

papers.title: Equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for amenable actions
papers.abstract:
We prove that every amenable action of a countable discrete group on a separable, simple, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra absorbs the trivial action on $\mathcal{Z}$ up to cocycle conjugacy. The group may be nonamenable, as in Suzuki's recent examples, and no assumptions on outerness or on the tracial state space are needed. This extends OpenAI's result for amenable groups to amenable actions. Amenability of the action cannot be omitted in general, as examples of the author and Lupini show. More generally, we show that every tracially amenable action on a separable, unital, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra with traces admits invariant central copies of all matrix algebras, without simplicity or nuclearity. For amenable actions on simple nuclear algebras, equivariant property (SI) allows one to deduce $\mathcal{Z}$-stability from this. As applications, we obtain absorption of $\mathcal{Z}$ for intermediate subalgebras in the crossed product, and also pure infiniteness for outer amenable actions of nonamenable groups.
  The basic techniques involving Gaussian variables originate in OpenAI's preprint, and are also the main new tool in its proposed solution to the Toms--Winter conjecture. We extend these techniques in order to deal with the weight functions coming from amenability, and one of the main new ingredients is the fact that one can replace an amenable action by an auxiliary one for which the amenability weights are central.
  In order to make the probabilistic tools accessible to the community beyond what is used here, we include an appendix where the theory is developed assuming only an elementary background, and where the relevant estimates are proved in detail.

papers.title: LoRAForge: Co-Designing Post-Hoc Compression and Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
papers.abstract: Multi-LoRA serving allows many task-specific adapters to share a common base model, but scaling to large adapter fleets introduces substantial storage, loading, and execution overheads. Post-hoc compression can reduce the memory footprint of trained LoRA adapters, yet smaller ranks do not automatically translate into faster serving. For instance, padding, factor access, and generic kernels can obscure the retained low-rank structure, while independently recompressing thousands of modules also incurs significant preparation overhead. We present LoRAForge, a system connecting batched factor construction to rank-specialized execution through an explicit retained-rank representation. It supports two allocation policies: uniform retention ratios (LoRAForge-U) and spectral-energy budget allocation (LoRAForge-S). Both share FlashTSQR factor construction and the same serving backend. FlashTSQR exploits parallelism across modules and row tiles, accelerating factor construction by up to $2.28\times$ over matched library QR. In a fixed-work Qwen control, the shared runtime adds $1.17$--$1.22\times$ throughput across both compressed policies, with negligible gains on original adapters. Across 85 trained open-weighted Qwen and Llama adapters, the spectral policy's floored quality configuration retains about 7.7% of adapter parameters with fleet-average score drops of at most 1.2 points on a 0--100 scale. The same rank-floored $1/12$ spectral exports achieve substantial token-throughput gains on both AMD and NVIDIA GPUs.

papers.title: Generic point processes are intermittently hyperuniform and maximally rigid
papers.abstract: We study the prevalence of hyperuniformity and spatial rigidity among translation- invariant ergodic simple point processes of fixed intensity, in a topology controlling local second moments. Hyperuniform processes are dense but meagre. We prove that intermittent hyperuniformity is residual: the number variance exhibits hyperuniform behavior along some sequences of radii and hyperfluctuating behavior along others. Maximal rigidity is also residual. Thus generic processes are maximally rigid but not hyperuniform. A local-to-global principle reduces the proofs to cross-section constructions for an arbitrary fixed essentially free ergodic $\mathbb{R}^d$-action. We also prove that processes admitting revival sequences form a residual set and exhibit near-quadratic variance along suitable van Hove sequences.

papers.title: When Does Adaptive Halting Win? Selection Rules Matter in Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped language models can stop iterating early, and recent work shows that post-hoc readouts of the loop trajectory often rival the learned exit gate of the looped model Ouro. Such comparisons reduce each method to one operating point chosen by a selection rule. We ask whether that rule decides the outcome. On a frozen Ouro-1.4B with four loops, we compared a trained stability probe ($\pi_1$-x) with Ouro's native gate, adapted to a per-question stopping decision, in pre-registered studies; the confirmatory study was designed after an exploratory finding on development data and evaluated once on a sealed test set of 8,517 questions. In the pre-registered confirmatory comparison, which selected operating points with a bootstrap-screened 1 pp accuracy-loss rule, the probe saved more of the four-loop budget than the native gate (+0.053 gross macro saving over three benchmarks, 95% CI [+0.049, +0.057]), mostly from CommonsenseQA, where the probe's test upper bound on accuracy loss exceeded 1 pp. Under a point-only rule, a pre-specified secondary analysis on the same test set reversed the preference (-0.022 [-0.026, -0.018]), with operating points that exceeded the budget. In pre-specified secondary comparisons, the probe showed no demonstrated advantage over an untrained KL divergence between successive loops (+0.00125 [-0.0041, +0.0065]); we emphasise this result post hoc and claim no equivalence. The probe also broke its budget on one of two out-of-distribution benchmarks (3.26 pp loss on Social IQa). Savings are estimated from stored full-depth traces, not measured inference time, and our screen carries no formal risk-control guarantee. We conclude that halting methods should be compared as signals together with selection procedures, with strong untrained baselines and out-of-distribution checks.

papers.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recommending creators that a user does not yet follow is a cold-start problem: from hundreds of thousands of popular creators and only a short trail of prior engagements, the system must predict the next creator worth surfacing. The prevailing generative recommendation recipe tokenizes each creator into a \emph{Semantic ID} (SID) by quantizing a frozen embedding and trains a language model to generate SIDs. We show that this SID layer, not the language model, is the binding constraint. The creator-to-SID map is many-to-one, so colliding creators must be resolved by a popularity tie-break that caps creator-level recall and favors already-popular creators, and the frozen quantizer stops the training gradient from reaching the creator representation. We propose Atomic Creator Token (ACT), which gives every creator its own vocabulary token trained end-to-end. The map is bijective, so collisions are impossible and inference is a direct top-$k$ over creator logits. In a controlled comparison on production data in which the token layer is the only variable, ACT improves creator-level Recall@15 by 19.8 points ($1.84\times$) over a matched SID baseline, still leads when the SID codebook is enlarged $64\times$, and serves at ${\sim}2.7\times$ lower per-user latency. The advantage carries over to the public KuaiRand dataset, where ACT is the only method that beats a global-popularity baseline, provided each creator token sees enough training examples. In a live A/B test, ACT is directionally positive on every reported metric against both the SID-enhanced and the classic production rankers.

papers.title: Transient subtraction method: An alternative approach for variance reduction in dissipative particle dynamics
papers.abstract: The efficient and accurate computation of transport coefficients remains a numerical challenge in dissipative particle dynamics (DPD), which can require substantial sampling to control statistical uncertainty.
