papers.title: Parameter Bounds and Inverse Approximation for Linearized ReLU$^k$ Networks on the Sphere
papers.abstract: We study direct and inverse approximation for linearized shallow ReLU$^k$ networks on $\mathbb S^d$ with quasi-uniform hidden parameters. For $0<\alpha<\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}$, under the coefficient growth condition $\bigl(n\sum_{j=1}^na_{j,n}^2\bigr)^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq n^\alpha M$, we prove that approximation at the order $n^{-\frac{d+2k+1}{2d}+\alpha}$ is equivalent to membership in the parity-compatible Besov space $\mathcal B_{2,\infty,*}^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}-\alpha d}(\mathbb S^d)$. Mere convergence under the same coefficient budget does not imply this regularity. For unconstrained approximation along a nested parameter sequence, a single ridge function gives a counterexample when $\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$, whereas for $\alpha>\frac{1}{2}$ the endpoint Besov inverse conclusion follows from a Bernstein inequality under antipodal quasi-uniformity. The inverse conclusion is also recovered when the prescribed rate holds for two quasi-uniform parameter sequences whose union is antipodally separated.

papers.title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.

papers.title: Task-driven sparse-view planar X-ray computed tomography for axial metrology
papers.abstract: Computational imaging can reduce the acquisition burden when the system is designed around task-relevant information rather than complete image recovery. We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. Numerical experiments show that, under a fixed total photon budget, task-driven metrology changes little over 12-64 views, while reconstruction-driven metrology is strongly view-dependent with much larger errors. The direct estimator also follows the expected photon-limited scaling. These results demonstrate a computational sensing strategy in which XCT acquisition, physical modeling, and inference are evaluated according to the quantitative information required by the task rather than for general-purpose volumetric image fidelity.

papers.title: Convergence Guarantees for the Broximal Point Method under Perturbations
papers.abstract: The Broximal Point Method (BPM) of Gruntkowska et al. (2025) comes with strong guarantees for convex optimization: under convexity alone, it terminates after finitely many steps and converges linearly in function value, with bounds that do not depend on the condition number or on any other regularity property of the objective. Each iteration, however, requires the exact minimization of the objective over a ball, which is generally intractable. As a first step toward implementable variants, we study the method when these subproblems are solved only approximately. We introduce and analyze Inexact BPM, which replaces the exact broximal point by an approximation and makes no assumption on how this approximation is obtained. Under summable or sufficiently small errors, we bound the number of iterations needed to reach a neighborhood of the set of minimizers, and these bounds remain independent of the regularity of the objective. Under the weaker requirement that the errors stay below the ball radius, we prove sublinear convergence in function value for the exact broximal points underlying the perturbed iterates, valid until the target neighborhood is reached, and we recover linear rates under bounded sublevel sets or strong convexity.

papers.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
papers.abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.

papers.title: A Distributed Microphone Network for Real-Time Gunshot Detection and Localization in GNSS-Challenged Large Areas
papers.abstract:
This paper presents a scalable distributed acoustic surveillance system for real-time gunshot detection and localiza tion in large-area, GNSS-challenged environments. The system consists of multiple low-cost MEMS microphone array units (MAUs) deployed as distributed anchors. Each MAU performs edge-level sound-event detection using a lightweight Sound De tection and Echo Suppression (SDES) algorithm, followed by a TinyML-based classifier for gunshot identification. For detected gunshots, an enhanced Generalized Cross-Correlation (eGCC) al gorithm estimates intra-array time differences of arrival (TDoAs)
  with improved robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio and re verberant conditions. Angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimates obtained from individual MAUs are fused through a modified SCO-EV localization framework to determine the gunshot position in a global coordinate system. A misplacement calibration (MC)
  algorithm compensates for platform orientation errors, improv ing angular consistency and localization accuracy in practical field conditions. Extensive experiments conducted over coverage areas ranging from 4,985 m2 to 49,063 m2 demonstrate reliable operation across varying spatial scales. The proposed framework achieves a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.70 for gunshot recognition and average localization errors below 6.5 m over 25,000 m2 , while maintaining errors under 15 m at larger scales. The results demonstrate the practical potential of the proposed system for distributed gunshot surveillance in GNSS challenged large areas.

papers.title: Frank-Wolfe is Approximate Broximal Gradient Descent
papers.abstract:
We show that the Frank-Wolfe method is an approximation of Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), and hence of the ball-proximal method. For constrained minimization, the ball-proximal method minimizes the objective over the intersection of the feasible set with a ball around the current iterate. Linearizing the objective gives BroxGD, but the intersection can remain difficult to handle even when linear minimization over the feasible set alone is cheap. We therefore replace the intersection by a smaller copy of the feasible set, obtained by shrinking it toward the current iterate so that it lies inside the ball. Minimizing the linear model over this smaller set gives exactly Frank-Wolfe, with the shrinking factor as its step size.
  We examine what this approximation preserves and what it can lose. For smooth convex objectives on compact convex sets, Frank-Wolfe retains a linear-model decrease guarantee that gives it and BroxGD a common convergence proof, recovering the classical $O(1/k)$ bound. Among compact convex regions inside the ball chosen before the gradient is known, the smaller copy is the smallest that preserves the same linear-model decrease guarantee. Nevertheless, Frank-Wolfe can achieve much less linear-model decrease than BroxGD at the same radius. A simplex example illustrates the sparsity gained by restricting the region, while a family of triangles shows how Frank-Wolfe can lose the distance decrease guaranteed by BroxGD. We also give a computable test for recovering the distance guarantee and a refinement procedure that terminates after finitely many oracle calls on polytopes.

papers.title: KAUSTics-Net: Diffusion-Based Through-Water UAV Restoration with a Semi-Synthetic Dataset
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of shallow-water environments using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is challenged by water-induced distortions, including refraction, caustics, and wavelength-dependent attenuation. The scarcity of paired distorted and reference imagery further limits the development of supervised restoration methods. To address this challenge, we introduce KAUSTics, a semi-synthetic dataset combining 1,280 reference patches derived from 32 high-resolution UAV images with 12,800 degraded observations generated through Blender-based water-surface rendering and empirical color and blur augmentations. We further propose KAUSTics-Net, a pixel-space conditional diffusion framework integrating a multi-scale conditional encoder, feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), cross-attention, and a composite reconstruction objective to restore shallow-water imagery. We evaluated the framework against eight image-restoration methods, complemented by architectural ablations and cross-dataset experiments. On KAUSTics, KAUSTics-Net achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 31.715 +/- 0.439 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.849 +/- 0.002, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.145 +/- 0.007 across three training seeds. On the independent Sea-Undistort dataset, sampler-aware fine-tuning improved restoration fidelity, reaching 19.469 +/- 0.332 dB PSNR and 0.554 +/- 0.005 SSIM under combined water-surface distortions, although perceptual trade-offs remained. Additional experiments on real UAV imagery examined feature preservation and segmentation behavior. These findings demonstrate the potential of semi-synthetic training and conditional diffusion for shallow-water image restoration while highlighting the importance of evaluating both reconstruction fidelity and downstream remote-sensing utility.

papers.title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
papers.abstract: LLM agents are judged by what they deliver, and in professional work what gets delivered is a project, not a task. A project pays off only if the whole package holds, and one weak part can limit the value of the rest. Yet existing benchmarks mostly test agents on one task at a time, leaving a gap between the capability we measure and the outcome that makes agents useful. To address this gap, we introduce DeliverBench, which tests whether agents can carry a project from brief to final delivery. Its 11 projects, spanning financial due diligence, legal contract drafting, and drug safety reporting, are reconstructed with 13 domain experts from real materials and chain 150 subtasks through 2-15 rounds of new materials and client feedback. Because no reference outputs are injected, agents inherit their own errors from one task to the next. Expert rubrics then score every checkpoint as well as the final package. Across seven model-harness systems, even the best system scores only 65.0 out of 100 on final delivery and passes 50.0% of subtasks at a 90-point threshold. The failures are often failures of carrying work forward: in one audit project, all seven systems addressed the review findings, but only one preserved traceability. Together, these results suggest that task-level capability does not simply compose into delivery, which also depends on keeping the work coherent as it evolves.

papers.title: A hyperbolic nonlinear Schr\"odinger system in multiple spatial dimensions: structure, convergence, and numerical discretization
papers.abstract: We propose and study a first-order hyperbolic approximation of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in $N$ spatial dimensions. This is an extension of the recently-proposed 1D hyperbolic NLS model. We study the structure and properties of the hyperbolic approximation and their relation to those of the original system. We show that the N-dimensional hyperbolic system exactly conserves analogs of the mass, energy, and momentum, and that it possesses stationary solutions that are closely related to those of NLS. The hyperbolic system is also shown to admit plane-wave solutions that share some stability properties with those of NLS, and that relaxation can shrink the focusing low-wavenumber modulational instability band as well as introduce a high-wavenumber instability band not present in NLS. We also show that solutions of the hyperbolic system converge to solutions of NLS in the relaxation limit. We present an adaptive-mesh finite volume discretization of the hyperbolic system and demonstrate its effectiveness in handling simulations, including those with geometric obstacles or non-periodic boundary conditions. The effectiveness of the numerical scheme is demonstrated through examples including a Bose-Einstein condensate, line soliton instability, and superflow past a cylinder.

papers.title: Local superderivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract: We prove that every even or odd local superderivation of the Block Lie superalgebra $S(q)$ is a superderivation for every $q\in\mathbb{C}$, with both basis indices ranging over $\mathbb{Z}$. The superderivations used in the local condition have the same parity as the map. The proofs use the known description of homogeneous superderivations, bracket computations, and coefficient comparisons.

papers.title: Dynamic Modeling of Transmission Networks, Grid-Following Inverters, and UPS-Based AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: This document presents dynamic models of a transmission network and average models of power-electronic devices and loads in the synchronous $dq$ frame. We model the network in the positive sequence and its synchronous generators with the classical swing equation and a first-order turbine governor. The power-electronic models cover grid-following inverters and AI data centers. Each inverter has a phase-locked loop, a power controller, and a current controller. Each data center connects to the grid through two step-down transformers. Its low-voltage bus feeds an IT load, an induction-motor cooling load, and a constant-impedance load. A double-conversion uninterruptible power supply (UPS) serves the IT load. We model its rectifier, grid-forming output inverter, battery, and bidirectional DC-DC converter. A measured GPU power trace drives the IT demand. We replace every non-smooth operation with a smooth surrogate. This keeps the discretized model continuously differentiable for the nonlinear solver. We also show how we initialize each model at its power-flow operating point.

papers.title: Brain-Behavior Modeling from Multimodal MRI using Opportunistic Pretraining and Common-Cohort Adaptation
papers.abstract: Incomplete imaging coverage limits sample sizes for multimodal cognitive prediction. We evaluated a two-stage opportunistic deep ensemble using baseline Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study data to predict fluid, crystallized, and total cognition. Separate neural models processed structural/diffusion, resting-state, and task-based MRI data with covariates. Models were pretrained on eligible modality cohorts (up to 9,686 participants), adapted to common training cohorts, and fused via Ridge regression (trimodal cohort: 4,216 participants). Five-fold family-aware cross-validation compared this approach against constituent and covariate-only models. Two-stage training increased mean test coefficient of determination (R^2) in 24 of 27 comparisons (median gain: 0.0081). Fusion increased mean R^2 by 0.0051-0.0333 over the strongest constituent and reduced mean absolute error by 0.0067-0.0976. Task-plus-resting-state and trimodal ensembles reduced absolute error across all targets (nominal p <= 0.0108). Task-plus-resting-state fusion achieved the highest mean R^2 for fluid (0.2222) and total cognition (0.3665), while structural-plus-resting-state led for crystallized cognition (0.3706), yielding R^2 gains of 0.0805, 0.1180, and 0.0890 over covariate-only references. Ablations showed expanded pretraining drove most improvements. Gradient-based attribution identified target-dependent input patterns. These findings support using partially observed cohorts for model development to achieve modest fusion gains. Pending external validation, this approach may support MRI-informed cognitive phenotyping.

papers.title: Latent Spectral Prompting for Multimodal Hyperspectral Object Tracking
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral videos provide rich spectral signatures for robust tracking under challenging conditions such as camouflage and low illumination. However, limited hyperspectral annotations and the large RGB-hyperspectral domain gap hinder the direct use of modern temporally pretrained RGB trackers. We propose SProTrack, a multimodal framework that transfers temporal knowledge from pretrained RGB trackers to the hyperspectral domain through latent spectral prompting. The key idea is to decouple temporal modeling from spectral adaptation, allowing temporal dynamics to be inherited from RGB foundation models while hyperspectral information is learned from unlabeled data in a self-supervised manner. Unlike band-selection methods that discard most spectral information or prompt-based approaches that rely on local-search crops, SProTrack learns a global, scene-level spectral representation from the full hyperspectral frame using an autoencoder. This latent representation is used to guide spectral prompt extraction while a pretrained RGB tracker preserves strong temporal modeling on RGB-compatible inputs. By encoding spectral-spatial structure into compact latent prompts, SProTrack bridges the RGB-hyperspectral modality gap without extensive retraining or dense supervision. Experiments on HOT2020 and HOT2023 demonstrate that SProTrack achieves the best overall performance, with strong results across all spectral domains.

papers.title: PlagiaCorpus: A Bilingual, Adversarial, and Cross-Lingual Dataset for Forensic Plagiarism Detection
papers.abstract: PlagiaCorpus is a bilingual Arabic-English dataset for benchmarking plagiarism and text-reuse detection, including reuse produced by large language models (LLMs) and reuse across languages. It contains 198,643 text records: a source corpus of 34,885 passages drawn from English and Arabic Wikipedia and two openly licensed book collections, and 163,758 queries (147,381 for training and 16,377 for testing). The queries cover five reuse classes of increasing difficulty, namely verbatim copying, character-level obfuscation, same-language paraphrasing by two different LLMs, and English--Arabic translation with structural paraphrasing, together with a Safe class of non-reused passages. Every positive query is linked to its source passage, and the train/test split is grouped by source passage so that no passage contributes queries to both splits. The release was curated through language identification, removal of LLM generation artefacts, and exact and cross-lingual de-duplication. Technical validation reports per-class length statistics, automatic checks of the train/test split, and inter-annotator agreement on a manually rated sample. The dataset is distributed in JSON and Parquet formats under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

papers.title: ArabGeoText: Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Models for Arabic Geospatial Text Spotting
papers.abstract: Geospatial text spotting involves locating and transcribing geographic labels, such as road names, district names, and landmarks, in raster maps. These labels are often small, densely arranged, and arbitrarily oriented. Although Arabic text recognition has been studied extensively in documents and natural scenes, Arabic geospatial text spotting remains underexplored. We introduce ARABGEOTEXT, an Arabic-centric benchmark covering 970 geographic locations in Riyadh and Jeddah, with 17,875 manually annotated text instances per view type. For each location, we pair an OpenStreetMap (OSM) rendering with a composite created by overlaying that rendering on the corresponding remote sensing (RS) imagery. The paired views preserve label content and pixel geometry, allowing evaluation across different backgrounds. Geographic partitions support in-city and city-disjoint evaluation of detection, recognition, and end-to-end spotting. Experiments with direct Qwen3.5-4B spotting show difficulties in recovering all labels within a tile. We therefore propose a tool-augmented vision-language framework that combines YOLO26 localization and crop rectification with Qwen3.5-4B recognition adapted through low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The framework outperforms direct LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-4B spotting across both image views and test cities. With localization held fixed, reader adaptation further improves recognition over the pretrained zero-shot reader. The dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yakoubbazi/ArabGeoText.

papers.title: Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.

papers.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -\Delta u+u=\lambda u\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<\lambda<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.

papers.title: Vision-language classification of Torsades de Pointes risk from pseudo-coloured ECG images: do T-wave morphology and colour context help or hinder?
papers.abstract: Contextual prompting is widely presented as a cheap route to better performance from vision models, but the evidence comes largely from benchmarks in which an attribute named in a prompt is also present in the image, confounding the two channels. We investigate the significance of context for a semantically complex biomedical signal classification task using a domain-adapted vision-language model, BiomedCLIP. Building on our previous work that renders electrocardiogram (ECG) signals as colour-enhanced images to flag Torsades de Pointes risk using the QT-nomogram and pseudo-colouring technique, we cross four context strategies with four T-wave morphology label sets, evaluated zero-shot and with a class-balanced linear probe, under five-fold stratified cross-validation on 9,789 images. Zero-shot inference is unusable. Once trained, the colour-enhanced images outperform the colourless ones on every metric: balanced accuracy 0.903 versus 0.825, sensitivity 0.914 versus 0.827, specificity 0.892 versus 0.823, ROC-AUC 0.955 versus 0.888 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) 0.437 versus 0.311. Crossing colour-in-image with colour-in-prompt separates the confounded channels: the image contributes +0.126 MCC (+0.078 balanced accuracy, +0.067 ROC-AUC) whether or not the prompt names colour, whereas naming it changes nothing under any metric. Context is two-sided: the best prompt set gains 0.008 MCC where colour is present and 0.016 where it is not, while the worst loses 0.017 and 0.013. For a signal rendered as an image, the leverage lies in how the signal is drawn rather than in how it is described - and where the endpoint is an interval measurement, prompts naming T-wave morphology describe the wrong quantity.

papers.title: Impact of Surface Preparation on the Propulsion of Catalytic Janus Colloids and Implications for Reproducibility
papers.abstract: Platinum-coated polystyrene (PS) Janus particles (JPs) propelled by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are a widely used model system for active matter, yet reported speeds for similar particles and fuel concentrations differ by more than an order of magnitude. Broad adoption of these materials requires increasing consistency in the preparation and achieving improved repeatability in their behavior. Herein, we focused on two routine, but rarely reported, preparation steps that we found to alter the particle speed. First, we found that pre-exposing the platinum cap to H2O2 before cell assembly increased the mean speed by a factor of 2.4. The size of this effect depended on batch history, where an aged batch responded strongly, while a freshly prepared batch sped up by only 16%. Second, we found that plasma cleaning of the glass substrate decreased the speed 2.7 times. In a 120 $\mu$m cell the suppression was the same at both walls even when only one wall was treated. The suppression grew with the treated glass area per unit fluid volume, which pointed to species released into the bulk solution rather than to a change at the wall. Plasma-cleaned glass released more ions into water than untreated glass, and XPS detected an ionic metal fluoride on the plasma-cleaned surface. A model in which the released ions lower the speed through the solution conductivity reproduced the measured speeds in all four cell geometries. Of the 17 published studies compared here, pre-activation is reported in only four studies and substrate cleaning in only six studies. We propose a minimum reporting standard for the preparation and associated speed measurements of catalytic Janus particles.

papers.title: Differentiable Iterative Learning Control for Black-Box Position-Commanded Manipulators
papers.abstract: High-accuracy repetitive tracking is challenging for position-commanded manipulators whose low-level controllers are inaccessible, while constrained model-based iterative learning control (ILC) can require substantial manual parameter tuning. We present Differentiable Iterative Learning Control (Diff-ILC), an online bilevel framework that adapts the parameters of a constrained ILC update between physical robot executions. A closed-loop differential model is identified once from paired smooth perturbations and subsequently kept fixed. At each trial, a constrained quadratic program computes a feasible command correction, while a real-anchored next-trial prediction defines a task-level objective. Hypergradients are obtained by implicitly differentiating the locally active KKT system, enabling multiple computational parameter updates without additional robot executions. Experiments on a 6-DoF DOBOT CR3 across unseen planar and three-dimensional trajectories show substantially faster physical-trial convergence than fixed-parameter model-based ILC. Across the four primary trajectories, after only two trial-to-trial updates, Diff-ILC achieves 78.8% and 76.4% lower mean joint-vector and Cartesian RMSE, respectively, than fixed-parameter model-based ILC.

papers.title: DINOFAS: Bonafide-Centric Representation Learning for Face Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: Face anti-spoofing (FAS) models often learn attack- and dataset-specific cues that degrade performance under unseen acquisition conditions and presentation attacks. We present DINOFAS, a DINOv3-based framework that formulates FAS as bonafide-centric representation learning. The proposed framework combines parameter-efficient DINOv3 adaptation using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), an attention style-content disentanglement (ASCD) module for reducing domain-specific appearance variations, and a dual-branch architecture that separates prototype-based liveness learning from attack-semantic supervision. The model is jointly optimized using a bonafide-centric prototype objective, an attack-semantic classification loss applied to detached features, and orthogonality regularization. DINOFAS achieves an average HTER of 9.09\% under the standard OCIM leave-one-domain-out protocol, where training is performed on three source datasets and evaluation is conducted on the held-out unseen domain. We further evaluate synthetic-to-real generalization by training exclusively on SynthASpoof and testing on four unseen real-world datasets, where DINOFAS achieves the lowest average HTER of 21.41\% and the highest average AUC of 86.14\% among the compared methods. Evaluations on OULU-NPU and SiW-Mv2 additionally demonstrate robustness to variations in acquisition conditions, devices, and unseen presentation attacks.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications
papers.abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) extend conventional diagonal RISs by allowing controllable coupling among reflecting elements. This flexibility is attractive for aerial networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face rapidly varying channels and strict power limits. In this paper, we study a hybrid BD-RIS-assisted multi-UAV rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlink, in which UAVs within favourable BD-RIS coverage use both direct and BD-RIS-aided links, whereas the remaining UAVs are served through direct links only. We formulate a network sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, RSMA common-rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS scattering matrices, and UAV-BD-RIS association. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by using deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, equipped with a constraint-preserving action layer that generates reciprocal and lossless BD-RIS responses in closed form and handles the binary association inside the environment transition. Simulation results, averaged over three training seeds under a physically consistent channel model with blocked direct links near the BD-RISs, show that the proposed design attains a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient ( TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and deep Q-network (DQN), exceeds per-slot alternating optimization with fixed trajectories at about 1/65 of its per-slot runtime, and benefits mainly from RSMA, while the additional BD-RIS gain is modest.

papers.title: Magnetized Accretion Flows with Low Angular Momentum Around Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the global structure of slowly rotating accretion flows around black holes in the presence of large-scale magnetic fields. Using a steady, height-integrated transonic model with radial mass loss, we examine how magnetic pressure, tension, and torque modify the dynamics of Bondi-like and disk-like accretion. Adopting a radial magnetic-field prescription based on results from previous numerical simulations, we compare hydrodynamical and magnetized solutions across a range of plasma-$\rm \beta$ values, from weak to strong field regimes. We find that magnetic stresses substantially alter the sonic radius and change the angular momentum and mass accretion rate reaching the black hole. For sufficiently strong fields, the inner flow becomes highly sub-Keplerian and magnetically dominated ($ \beta= P_{\mathrm{gas}}/ P_{\mathrm{mag}}<1$), and magnetic stresses can drive transitions to lower angular momentum. We also show that outflows in this magnetized accretion flow can significantly alter the structure of disk-like accretion. We further perform 2D simulations of magnetized Bondi accretion and torus accretion and find that the radial structure and magnetically dominated, sub-Keplerian character of our semi-analytical solutions are qualitatively reproduced.

papers.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
papers.abstract:
Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ \kappa_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known.
  Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was instrumental in explaining the geometry of the $841$-point kissing arrangement in ${\mathbb R}^{12}$.
  We give a simple generalization of quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$ obtained from record configurations. They are parameterized by three Latin cubes of order $4$, six permutations of $3$-element set, and are all infinitesimally jammed. Computer-aided counting shows that there are $4\,072\,728\,621$ isometry classes in this family of $4320$-point kissing arrangements.

papers.title: Steering with Multilingual Lexicons for Sentiment Control in Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: Activation steering offers a lightweight mechanism for controlling model behavior, but existing methods depend on sentence-level contrastive data that is unavailable for most of the world's languages. We show that multilingual sentiment lexicons are a viable substitute across three model families: aggregated multilingual lexicons outperform English-derived steering vectors for mid- and low-resource languages, while monolingual lexicons remain stronger for languages a model has specialized in during pre-training. The steering efficacy is mechanistically dictated by both representational density and pre-training priors. Large-magnitude English vectors overwhelm the compact representations of low-resource languages, causing "linguistic collapse." This fragility is mitigated by the norm-dampening of multilingual aggregation. Architectural biases, including bilingual specialization penalty and latent numerical rigidity, also heavily constrain cross-lingual steering responsiveness. Ultimately, our work establishes lexicons as a practical steering signal and offers a comprehensive mechanistic account of cross-lingual steering dynamics.

authors.name: Muhammad Dehan Al Kautsar
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Angle-dependent emission from evolving accretion layers
papers.abstract: Photon propagation through an evolving atmosphere can change the angular distribution of emerging radiation even when its integrated optical column remains constant. We quantify this effect in an irradiated, internally heated, expanding plane-parallel layer using grey, special-relativistic similarity solutions. The full angular radiation field determines both the source function and the acceleration of a pressureless flow in prompt radiative balance. We compare each evolving solution with two frozen transport calculations on the same density and velocity profiles, holding the source fixed in one and allowing it to relax in the other. Heating produces the familiar transition from limb darkening to limb brightening, while the temporal correction to the angular contrast changes sign with optical column. For an upper boundary moving at $0.04c$, an injection speed of $0.06c$, and heating four times the reference incident flux, the intensity ratio between direction cosines $0.1$ and $1$ exceeds the frozen, fixed-source result by $18.8$ per cent at column $\tau_0=0.15$, but is smaller by $2.53$ per cent at $\tau_0=0.55$. Source relaxation preserves this reversal. The corresponding direct photon flight times are one third and three per cent of the flow age in the oblique and normal directions, respectively. These solutions provide a controlled local benchmark for temporal angular transfer in evolving disc atmospheres and reprocessing layers; application to a specific accreting system requires thermal, spectral, and geometrical physics beyond the present model.

papers.title: "I Wrote, I Paused, I Rewrote": A Mixed-Methods Study of Learner Perceptions of Process-Aware LLM Feedback
papers.abstract:
Large language models increasingly provide formative writing feedback, but most systems evaluate only the submitted text. Process-aware systems can additionally incorporate intermediate drafts and interaction records, yet access to these traces does not establish whether learners perceive the resulting feedback as useful, fair, or aligned with their own revision experience. We conducted a convergent mixed-method post-task evaluation with 43 undergraduate English-language learners. Participants completed a timed essay, received LLM-generated feedback based on the final essay, intermediate snapshots, and keystroke-derived records, and then answered six five-point Likert items and four open-ended questions.
  Ratings were concentrated above the neutral midpoint across all six items. Between 74.4% and 95.3% of participants selected ratings of 4 or 5, and all six one-sided exact sign tests remained significant after Holm correction. Perceived correspondence between the revision analysis and the participant's reported thought process was positively associated with overall perceived usefulness, Spearman's $\rho_s=.327$, 95% bootstrap CI $[.009,.609]$, $p=.032$, $n=43$.
  Qualitative responses were analysed through an LLM-assisted codebook development procedure followed by independent human coding of 14 binary codes. Participants frequently described the product feedback and revision rationale as accurate, while a smaller set reported misinterpretation of surface corrections, time constraints, or rhetorical intention. The findings distinguish perceived detection of revision activity from perceived interpretation of why revision occurred.

papers.title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives. On the Euclidean motion group, where the Stockwell transform reduces to a windowed Hankel transform, this gives boundedness and continuity as soon as the smoothness exceeds half the dimension, which is the classical threshold for Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: PACT: Defending Recommendation against Promotional News Rewriting via Attack-Diverse Score Consistency
papers.abstract: Personalized news recommenders are increasingly vulnerable to LLM-powered promotional attacks, where content providers rephrase headlines to manipulate rankings without altering underlying facts. Defending against such manipulation requires covering a wide spectrum of LLM generators and optimization strategies--ranging from stylistic prompting to reinforcement feedback--without incurring prohibitive training or inference costs. In this work, we present PACT (Pooled Attack Consistency Training), a model-agnostic defense that decouples relevance estimation from superficial rhetorical variations. PACT integrates three synergistic operations: it pools offline, fact-checked rewrites from multi-generator and multi-strategy attack sources; samples a constant number of variants at each training visit to yield an unbiased estimator of the pool-wide consistency objective under a fixed compute budget; and aligns original and rewritten ranking scores within the same user context jointly with click supervision. Requiring no architectural modifications or test-time filtering, PACT deploys the trained recommender with zero extra latency. Across nine experimental settings spanning three recommendation backbones and three unseen-generator attacks, PACT consistently achieves the lowest promotion rate and target exposure, outperforming the strongest defense baseline by up to 3.0 percentage points in promotion reduction under LANCE. Further evaluations verify that PACT's superiority holds robustly under unseen attack-strategy holdouts and adaptive white-box retraining, while keeping clean recommendation utility virtually intact.

papers.title: Graceful supertrees with at most $2m-\mathrm{diam}(T)$ edges
papers.abstract: A graceful labeling of a tree with $m$ edges is a bijection from its vertices to $\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$ whose edge differences are pairwise distinct. The Graceful Tree Conjecture asserts that every tree admits such a labeling; equivalently, the smallest graceful tree containing a given $m$-edge tree has $m$ edges. For this embedding problem, Sethuraman, Ragukumar and Slater proved that fewer than $4m$ edges suffice, while Sethuraman and Ragukumar observed that in practice fewer than $2m$ appear to suffice. We prove the latter bound for every tree. For any root of height $h$ with $t_h$ vertices at maximum distance, we construct a graceful tree containing the original tree with exactly $M=2m-h-t_h+1$ edges; in particular, $2m-\operatorname{diam}(T)$ edges suffice. The construction completes a cyclic reflection of van Bussel's level labeling without increasing its span; each original edge difference $d$ is replaced by $M+1-d$. Unused vertex labels and missing edge differences are indexed by the same intermediate-level positions, allowing an explicit attachment rule that preserves the tree property. The best root for this construction is computable in linear time. Because every graceful supertree labeling restricts to a range-relaxed labeling, a uniform supertree bound of $(2-\varepsilon)m+O(1)$ would imply such a range-relaxed bound for all trees.

papers.title: Sharper Bounds for Graphical Two-Choice Allocation
papers.abstract: In graphical two-choice allocation, vertices are bins, and each arriving ball must be placed irrevocably at one endpoint of a uniformly random edge. The objective is to keep the maximum-minus-minimum load gap small at every time. On cycles, endpoint-local monotone rules incur polynomial gaps at long time horizons, whereas global rules can achieve polylogarithmic gaps. We prove a joint exponential-moment inequality for the orthogonal contrasts of a binary partition tree, controlling all contrasts along a root-to-leaf path simultaneously. Applied to the Bansal--Feldheim strategy, it improves the gap on every $\kappa$-edge-connected $d$-regular graph from $O((d/\kappa)\log^4 n\log\log n)$ to $O((d/\kappa)\log^3 n\log\log n)$. We give an explicit strategy on the $n$-cycle with expected gap $O(\log^2 n)$ uniformly over deterministic times and exponential tails at each such time. An Euler-tour projection yields $O(\bar d\log^2(2M))$ for every connected graph with $M$ edges and degree-proportional capacities. For lower bounds, we introduce a stochastic cut workload: the expected largest normalized overload forced by the requests, plus an indivisibility term. For every online integral strategy, the supremum over time of the expected gap is at least one sixth of this benchmark. Regular rings of cliques attain $\Omega((d/\kappa)\log n)$ along an explicit family, improving the prior additive lower bound. With unequal capacities, the workload need not control the gap: one family has constant relative cut slack, bounded workload and gap $\Omega(\log\log n)$; another has workload at most $20$ but forces gap $\Omega(\log n)$ even for clairvoyant fractional allocations that remain irrevocable.

papers.title: Whitened Advantage Summation Policy Optimization: Correlation-Aware Aggregation for Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for language models often combines several rewards by normalizing each one and adding them with fixed weights. When the rewards are correlated, the variation they share is counted once for every reward that carries it. In terms of the ZCA-decorrelated components of the reward signal, the weighted sum applies weights $\Sigma^{1/2} w$ rather than the chosen weights $w$, where $\Sigma$ is the reward correlation matrix. We study WAS-PO, which whitens the normalized advantages with $\Sigma^{-1/2}$ before adding them, so that the chosen weights apply to those components. We derive the scalarized objective whose gradient it follows when normalization statistics are held fixed, show that its weights on the raw rewards can be negative, give an exact two-reward condition under which the lighter-weighted reward is reversed, and give a loose bound on the error from estimating $\Sigma$ during training. On tool calling with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, WAS-PO reached a higher mean training reward than GDPO in all seven seeds with three rewards (3.8% higher) and all three seeds with four (3.9% higher). WAS-PO also replaces GDPO's per-prompt normalization with batch-level normalization, and we did not separate the two changes with three or four rewards. The training-reward gains did not carry over to held-out accuracy, which was slightly lower than GDPO's with three rewards (not significant) and 0.03 lower in absolute terms with four (two seeds evaluated). With two rewards, WAS-PO trailed GDPO in training reward, and a three-seed control weakly suggests that the gap comes from batch-level normalization rather than whitening. In a math setting where the two rewards were nearly identical by construction, WAS-PO drove down the lighter-weighted reward, as the sign condition predicts.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Detecting Building Setback Rule Violations in Urban Planning: A Case Study on Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Dhaka's rapid urban growth has made building setback violations common, narrowing footpaths and blocking emergency access. RAJUK, responsible for building control in the Dhaka Metropolitan Area, enforces setback rules mainly through manual field inspection, which scales poorly. We present a systematic comparison of four machine learning approaches for classifying building setback conditions from street-level photographs: negative (compliant), moderate (borderline), and positive (violation). We built a labeled dataset of 372 geo-tagged images from sixteen Dhaka neighborhoods and expanded it with 5,968 augmented copies for training. We trained and evaluated a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), a Random Forest ensemble on frozen ResNet50 embeddings, a support vector machine on frozen ResNet18 embeddings, and a fine-tuned ResNet18 CNN. On a 1,275-image test set, the fine-tuned CNN achieved 65.4% accuracy (macro-F1 0.50), followed by Random Forest at 59.9% (macro-F1 0.44) and SVM at 58.2% (macro-F1 0.45). All models classify the compliant class reliably but struggle with the borderline moderate class due to visual ambiguity. These results establish reference performance levels for automated setback-compliance screening in a South Asian regulatory setting.

papers.title: Pano2BIM: A Geometry-Constrained Vision-Language Agent for As-Built BIM Generation from a Floor Plan and a Single 360$^\circ$ Image
papers.abstract: Digital twins require accurate, up-to-date building information models (BIM) that reflect physical conditions, yet generating and maintaining as-built models remains costly and labor-intensive. Emerging image-based methods can capture visual appearance without inherently producing structured BIM information, while vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with reliable metric object placement. This paper presents Pano2BIM, a geometry-constrained VLM agent that generates approximate IFC4 models at Level of Development (LOD) 200 from a floor plan with known room dimensions and a single 360-degree photograph. The VLM identifies landmarks and objects, while deterministic tools estimate camera pose, compute metric positions through ray casting, and check spatial constraints. An optional second stage enriches the presentation model through render-and-compare feedback without modifying the primary furniture geometry. In a preliminary evaluation on one laboratory, the proposed Measure workflow achieved a mean furniture-footprint intersection over union (IoU) of 0.53, compared with 0.44 for a single-response baseline using identical modeling instructions, and matched an average of 4.0 versus 2.3 of seven fixed furniture elements across three runs. Centroid disagreements were similar for the four elements consistently identified by both approaches. The measurement stage averaged 3.8 minutes and USD 1.63 in API costs per run, while the complete demonstrated workflow required approximately 42 minutes and USD 11. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of rapid, low-cost as-built BIM generation, with potential applications in maintaining digital twins that reflect changing physical conditions.

papers.title: From Lookups to Lessons: Turning Retrieved Knowledge into Parametric Memory
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) helps large language models (LLMs) answer factual questions beyond their training data, but it adds storage and inference costs. Distilling previously retrieved information into parametric memories enables reuse without online retrieval. However, training the memory to mimic a retriever rewards accurate independent predictions, which do not necessarily improve the final output quality when combined with the LLM's existing predictions. To address this, we introduce ResMem, in which the LLM reads retrieved text offline to generate teacher targets. This design avoids storing massive token representations, unlike existing parametric memory approaches such as MLP Memory, which relies on k-nearest neighbor (kNN) datastores. Furthermore, by using the LLM as an offline teacher that reads privileged retrieved evidence alongside the input, we train a parametric memory to learn an additive logit residual. This residual aligns the predictions of a student sharing the same backbone with the teacher distribution, while self-distillation updates remain confined to the parametric memory. On a Wikipedia subset, ResMem reduces the storage retained for teacher construction by 94.7% compared with the evaluated kNN pipeline. Across five question answering datasets, ResMem raises mean token F1 from 32.83% for the frozen LLM to 34.48%. It also breaks 21% fewer of the LLM's correct answers than a kNN-trained memory. These findings validate our motivation of treating retrieval as a learning resource, with parametric memory shaped by how retrieved knowledge is used to inform the model's future predictions. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/SSRand/From-Lookups-to-Lessons and https://huggingface.co/RandHan/ResMem-Mistral-7B-v0.3.

papers.title: Ripple: Deadline-Aware CPU-GPU Sharing for Embodied Inference
papers.abstract: Unified-memory edge devices increasingly run LLM/VLM inference alongside time-critical CPU tasks for perception and control. GPU memory traffic can overwhelm these tasks, yet platforms such as DGX Spark expose neither bandwidth counters nor direct bandwidth regulation. We present Ripple, a CPU-GPU co-scheduler that combines model-derived GPU memory volumes with CPU completion feedback to regulate interference. Ripple divides inference into pausable, layer-based units and translates each CPU job's deadline slack into a GPU-byte budget, admitting work within the budgets of all overlapping jobs. Online updates track changing interference, while deadline-aware pacing and judicious SM footprint narrowing preserve inference progress. Implemented with SGLang engine hooks and a central scheduler, we evaluate Ripple on DGX Spark with four robotic CPU task mixes and LLM/VLM inference. It is the only evaluated approach that consistently meets the 2% CPU deadline-miss target and VLM deadlines across the tested deadline settings while retaining best-effort LLM throughput.

papers.title: EZ-Ar-VC: Robust Arabic Voice Anonymization with Generalization across Dialects and Code-Switching
papers.abstract: Voice conversion (VC) models can be used to anonymize speech data while preserving naturalness. Existing models, however, are mainly optimized for English and other high-resource languages, and they fail to generalize well to Arabic due to its distinct phonology. In this work, we comprehensively evaluate existing zero-shot VC systems for Arabic speech, identifying limitations in pronunciation preservation. We then train an Arabic-centric model based on EZ-VC on diverse Arabic speech, and demonstrate strong performance in intelligibility, naturalness, and pronunciation preservation, while maintaining high speaker dissimilarity. Through subjective evaluation, we further demonstrate its robustness to code-switching and cross-dialectal conversion, as well as its generalization to Arabic dialects with limited representation in the training data. Our findings highlight the limitations of zero-shot VC and the importance of target-language adaptation for robust voice anonymization.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability
papers.abstract: A common assumption in chain-of-thought (CoT) oversight is that a visible reasoning trace makes model behavior easier to monitor. We argue that this assumption can conflate distinct properties along a chain linking a model's internal computation, reasoning artifacts, outputs, and monitor judgments. We identify four properties along this chain: reasoning visibility (whether a trace is accessible), mechanistic faithfulness (whether a trace reflects internal computation), mechanistic localizability (whether a compact causal mechanism can be isolated), and behavioral monitorability (whether a monitor can detect the target behavior). Two complementary case studies across three open-weight reasoning models show why these distinctions matter. In the security vulnerability reasoning study, probes and activation ablations provide evidence of internal representation and causal influence, but a monitor with access to the reference answer does not outperform the majority-class baseline in a held-out test. In authority-hint factual reasoning study, a monitor correctly distinguishes changed from unchanged answers, but seven mechanistic analyses do not isolate a compact causal mechanism. These results show that evidence for one claim does not establish the others. We therefore propose an evidential-chain reporting standard. Each claim carries a licensing statement that specifies its target property, access tier, and artifact, and labels each required link as supported, unsupported, or assumed. These assessments determine whether the conclusion is licensed, conditionally licensed, or not licensed.

papers.title: Tracing How Language Models Integrate Temporal Anchors into Factual Recall
papers.abstract: Factual recall in language models is typically framed as retrieving a factual association: a subject--relation pair maps to a single object. However, many facts are context-dependent: the same pair maps to different objects depending on a condition such as time. We introduce anchored factual recall, in which the model receives an explicit conditioning expression, an anchor, and must select the object valid under it. This raises questions that single-object recall does not: where the anchor enters the computation, what it changes, and how that change selects the answer. Focusing on temporal anchors, we answer them with causal interventions on four open-weight models on English prompts and identify two routes. In a subject-mediated route, the anchor resolves the final subject-token representation to the queried year, and the relation redistributes the readout of this state across attention heads. In a direct route] the final position attends to the anchor, and upper-layer MLPs turn this signal into a preference for the time-appropriate object. The two routes are parallel channels: their contributions add up, most queries use both, and their balance depends on the query, e.g., on the relation, consistently across models. This reframes mechanistic accounts of factual recall from retrieving a single stored object to selecting among context-dependent alternatives.

papers.title: MedPsy: State-of-the-Art Small Medical Language Models for Efficient Edge Deployment
papers.abstract: Medical language models promise expert clinical support, but the strongest open-source LLMs remain too large for private edge-device deployment, while compact medical models still trail substantially on knowledge-intensive and real-world healthcare tasks. Reasoning models that fit edge memory budgets can produce long reasoning traces, increasing sequential decoding, end-to-end latency, energy consumption, and KV-cache memory pressure. We present MedPsy, a family of text-only 1.7B and 4B medical language models designed for edge deployment, targeting this accuracy-generation-efficiency trade-off. Our recipe combines a synthetic medical data pipeline over biology, medicine, and health seeds with chain-of-thought targets from a 235B medical-focused LLM teacher; a four-stage post-training curriculum comprising two SFT stages followed by two RL stages with hard-sample mining; and an edge deployment evaluation spanning multiple GGUF quantization variants and real-device inference on laptop and smartphone hardware. On seven closed-ended medical benchmarks, MedPsy-4B surpasses MedGemma-1.5-4B by 19.34 points and matches MedGemma-27B while being 6.75x smaller; MedPsy-1.7B outperforms MedGemma-1.5-4B by 11.42 points despite being less than half its size. On HealthBench-Hard, MedPsy-4B surpasses MedGemma-27B by 15.33 points, while MedPsy-1.7B surpasses it by 11.66 points despite being ~16x smaller. Beyond accuracy, MedPsy reduces average response length by 1.7x (1.7B) and 3.2x (4B) versus its Qwen3 backbones, while Q4_K_M quantization preserves the aggregate score within 1 point of BF16 with ~69% lower disk footprint. In real-device inference, MedPsy-4B's shorter generations translate into 75% lower median end-to-end latency and estimated energy per answer than its Qwen3 backbone at matched quantization, while peak RAM remains below 5 GB across our tested laptop and smartphone configurations.

papers.title: VerdictAD: Few-Shot Anomaly Detection via Decision-Guided Refinement
papers.abstract: Detecting defects in real-world industrial inspection often requires learning from only a few normal images per category. Recent few-shot anomaly detection methods have achieved strong performance by measuring feature differences between query images and normal references. However, visual differences do not always indicate genuine defects, as normal appearance variations can also produce high anomaly scores. Conversely, structural or logical anomalies may not produce strong local feature differences, making them difficult to detect. To address this limitation, we introduce VerdictAD, a training-free framework that refines existing anomaly detectors through visual decisions. Rather than replacing existing detectors, VerdictAD adopts a typed decision model to assess the query image and its local regions against a few normal references. By directly producing structured decision probabilities without text generation, the model provides complementary evidence for refining anomaly responses at different spatial scales. Building on this capability, we introduce two modules: Global Verdict Refinement (GVR) uses image-level decisions to refine the overall anomaly score, while Local Verdict Refinement (LVR) aggregates regional decisions to refine the anomaly map. Combined with a simple DINOv2-based detector, VerdictAD achieves competitive performance in one-shot and few-shot anomaly detection. More importantly, as a plug-and-play framework, it consistently improves existing anomaly detectors across MVTec AD, VisA, and MVTec LOCO AD, achieving strong results across one-shot and few-shot settings. Our code and experimental logs are publicly available at https://github.com/sgstq0811/VerdictAD-Jev-AD.

authors.name: Shijian Lu

papers.title: Auditing Representation-Space Fraud Detection: A Bayesian IRL Framework for Calibrated Uncertainty and Its Limits
papers.abstract: Shilling detectors for recommender systems are almost always evaluated by one number, detection AUROC, with no account of when it can be trusted. We audit representation-space detection with VEIL (Variational Evaluation via Inverse-reinforcement Learning), a pairwise (Bradley-Terry) Bayesian reward-inference framework over frozen encoder embeddings, following the Bayesian auditing paradigm for LLM alignment [1]: (A) a base posterior; (B) a hierarchical ARD extension with learned confidence; and (C) a label-routed organic/attacker mixture used as an evidence-accumulation check.We prove (Proposition 1) that no detector built on a representation invariant to a transformation of user profiles can outperform chance against an attack that is indistinguishable from organic profiles under that invariance.Detection is near-perfect against synthetic-structure attacks (AUROC 0.936-1.000) but collapses under donor-mimicry, which clones a real user's item set and splices in 1-3 target items. Performance falls to chance on MovieLens-1M (0.48-0.51), partially degrades on Amazon Musical Instruments, and degrades least on CiaoDVD.Donor-mimicry is not undetectable: a non-learned baseline, based on each profile's maximum raw item-set Jaccard similarity to any other profile, reaches AUROC 0.92-0.97 (average precision 0.50-0.57) on all four donor-mimicry configurations, including ML-1M, where every embedding-based score is at chance.The signal is present in the raw profiles, but LightGCN's representation discards it, placing injected profiles closer to their true donor than its zero-propagation MF reduction does (distance 1.98 vs. 3.09). Severity varies by dataset, encoder, and detection method, with no single axis predicting the others. The limit lies in the representation, not the attack, and raw-similarity checks are a necessary complement to any learned detector.

papers.title: Voice-Native LLMs Hear Frustration but Do Not Listen to It
papers.abstract: Users convey frustration in what they say and in how they say it, and voice-native models, which hear speech instead of an ASR transcript, can register both. Existing evaluations read unchanged performance as robustness without checking perception. Following Brunswik's lens model, we measure on identical audio whether frustration is expressed, perceived, and utilized. We cross frustrated wording with frustrated voice in a within-item 2x2 design over 353 tasks and release the 1,412 clips as VoxAffect. Across 8 models, outputs look robust, with no detectable vocal effect on accuracy for 7. With neutral wording, all 8 label the frustrated voice frustrated in at most 3.1% of clips, although 7 of them detect acted anger in 73-100% of clips and human listeners classify the voice correctly in 65.3% of judgments. Yet linear probes decode the frustrated voice from the audio encoders of the 2 open-weight models, with paired accuracy 0.67 and 0.69, and in proprietary models too the voice raises perceived frustration once the words agree. The models thus hear the frustrated voice but do not listen to it, whereas their invariance to frustrated wording, perceived in 40-75% of clips, is genuine robustness. Our work is openly accessible at https://github.com/Astarojth/hear-not-listen.

papers.title: PRIME: Predictive Routing of Interventions by Modeling Effects for Scientific Ideation
papers.abstract: Feedback-driven iteration is widely used to improve LLM-generated scientific ideas, but existing systems either leave revision decisions implicit in generation, align revisions with feedback-localized weaknesses, or restrict action selection to system-specific operations. This is problematic because problems, hypotheses, and solutions are interdependent: the location where a weakness manifests does not itself determine the revision scope that will produce a better successor. We term this phenomenon diagnosis-intervention mismatch. We introduce Predictive Routing of Interventions by Modeling Effects (PRIME), a plug-and-play feedback-to-revision decision layer for existing scientific ideators. PRIME operates in three stages: (1) Structural Attribution interprets feedback over the problem-hypothesis-solution structure without fixing a revision target; (2) Counterfactual Routing constructs alternative scope-conditioned interventions and compares their projected successor utility and risks through lightweight rollouts; and (3) Intervention Execution compiles the selected intervention into an ordered generator-facing plan with semantic actions, preservation constraints, and dependency requirements for successor generation. We validate diagnosis intervention mismatch on 112 human-annotated idea-feedback pairs. Across four benchmarks, two ideators, and fixed- and open-problem settings, PRIME improves successor quality and routing reliability over strong baselines; removing counterfactual routing reduces quality from 3.463 to 1.960 and increases route regret from 0.426 to 1.929, confirming cross-scope effect modeling as the primary source of its gains.

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
papers.abstract:
We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $\chi'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star). Two natural lower bounds are the maximum weighted degree $\Delta_w(G)$ and the maximum local bin-packing number $\mathrm{bp}(G)$: the maximum, over vertices, of the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the incident weights. We have $\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil\le\mathrm{bp}(G)\le\chi'_w(G)$. How closely these local lower bounds approximate the global optimum is a longstanding open problem.
  Our main result establishes an asymptotic weighted analogue of Vizing's theorem: every simple graph admits a coloring using at most $(1+o(1))\mathrm{bp}(G)$ colors. Thus local bin packings can be made globally consistent with asymptotically vanishing relative loss, even in nonbipartite graphs. Our local-to-global rounding framework coordinates feasible local packing distributions into a partial coloring, leaving only $o(\mathrm{bp}(G))$ uncolored weight at every vertex.
  For bipartite multigraphs, we prove $\chi'_w(G)\le(2+o(1))\Delta_w(G)$, establishing the Chung--Ross conjecture [SICOMP'91] asymptotically. For loopless multigraphs, we obtain the exact bound $\chi'_w(G)\le3\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil$. Both leading coefficients are optimal, giving weighted analogues of the classical K\H{o}nig--Shannon bounds.
  Further upper and lower bounds show that the classical factor-$3/2$ separation does not persist with the local bin-packing benchmark. We also disprove the exact weighted-degree conjecture of Feige and Singh [ESA'08]. Our upper bounds have polynomial-time algorithms, and their existence statements are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Forecasting How RLHF Responds to Reward-Model Edits Before Training
papers.abstract: Responses with headers, lists and greater length receive high scores from reward models (RMs), and RLHF policies learn to produce these features even when true quality does not improve. Practitioners therefore edit their RMs, but they learn whether an edit works only after an RL run. We show that the response of a policy to an RM edit can be forecast before training, from samples of the current policy and the scores of the old and new RM. If we read the RM as a set of prices, the first-order theory of KL-regularized RL implies that each feature moves in proportion to its within-prompt covariance with the change in reward. We implant controlled price changes into retrained RMs under a 2^(4-1) fractional factorial design with a self-distilled placebo, run 54 RL runs from six parent policies, and fix every forecast before the runs. With the covariance predictor, we predict the direction of all 20 changes in supply whose forecast has the same sign at every parent and explain 82% of the standardized change. With counterfactual prices, the classical alternative, we explain 50%. The forecast also holds under GRPO and for real RM upgrades, where we explain 66% out of sample with a coefficient frozen from the factorial runs. For rent, the gap between the proxy reward and a gold reward from stronger judges, we rank RM edits correctly with the same covariance over the first 30 steps (Spearman 0.94). This measures the horizon of the forecast: by step 200, the ranking of the factorial edits reverses under both RLOO and GRPO, while the real upgrades keep their order. When we vary the KL coefficient beta, the initial response does not depend on beta, and the response saturates below the KL equilibrium. In one experiment, the long-run response to a price rise is consistent with an additional implicit regularizer beta_0 of about 0.003 to 0.007.

papers.title: Multi-User Precoding with Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces via Neural Reparameterization
papers.abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) enable wave-domain signal processing, and provide a promising architecture for enhancing spectral efficiency in multi-user wireless communication systems. However, jointly optimizing transmit power and multi-layer phase shifts in SIM-assisted wireless systems under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints results in a large-scale nonconvex problem, for which conventional numerical optimization-based methods, such as alternating optimization (AO), suffer from high computational burden and limited scalability. In this paper, we develop a QoS constraint-aware neural reparameterization framework for SIM-assisted downlink precoding. By embedding the cascaded wave-propagation structure of the SIM into a model-based differentiable architecture, both the phase shift configuration and transmit power allocation are reparameterized as parameters of a structured neural model that inherently satisfies feasibility constraints of the original problem. The resulting formulation enables efficient optimization that does not rely on a channel-to-precoding mapping learned through offline training. Instead, it directly updates the reparameterized optimization variables to realize real-time precoding for any channel realization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior sum rate performance under QoS constraints, while significantly improving computational efficiency compared with conventional numerical optimization approaches.

papers.title: Now You See Them, Now You Dont FusionGhost Gait for Occlusion-Robust Gait Recognition with ArabGait dataset
papers.abstract: Skeleton-based gait recognition is generally more robust to appearance changes than pixel-based methods, but this robustness depends on stable pose extraction. Clothing variation in gait recognition includes changes in garments, silhouette, and carried items; under Gulf clothing (Kandoora/Abaya), the dominant failure mode shifts from appearance change to lower-limb pose degradation caused by severe occlusion. To study this regime, we introduce ArabGait, a 45-subject indoor multi-view dataset with four walking conditions across three viewpoints, and show that Gulf clothing lowers mean lower-limb confidence from 0.811 to 0.683 and raises lower-limb failure rate from 7.98% to 17.82%, with ankles most affected. We propose FusionGhost-Gait, a fused spatiotemporal architecture that integrates spatial graph blocks and temporal modeling in one residual unit, removes redundant channel projections, and uses compact temporal Ghost kernels as a lightweight regularization mechanism for pose-noisy trajectories while preserving efficient temporal downsampling. On ArabGait cross-clothing evaluation, including Protocol A and Protocol B, FusionGhost-Gait reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1 while remaining compact (108,970- 133,674 parameters and 0.035-0.052 billion floating-point operations (GFLOPs)), achieving more than 65% fewer parameters and 75% lower FLOPs than existing baselines. These results indicate that the proposed model generalizes effectively to challenging Gulf-clothing conditions while remaining lightweight and deployable for surveillance and access-control biometric systems.

papers.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
papers.abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.
