papers.abstract: Recursively self-improving (RSI) systems are increasingly viewed as a promising means of accelerating progress toward artificial general intelligence. They aim to autonomously improve their capabilities by refining their working pipelines and recursively improving the strategies that guide subsequent refinements, with gains generalizing to unseen scenarios.However, existing evaluations lack reliable metrics to distinguish capability gains from scenario fitting, sustainable and extensible protocols for unseen tasks and difficulties, and fine-grained attribution of improvement to evolution traces. To this end, we propose SelfImprove-Bench,an RSI evaluation framework that organizes tasks into three primary capabilities (i.e., Exploring, Planning, Reasoning) as scenarios for guiding model evolution. We instantiated the tasks on games for controllability and reproducibility, and pairs them with scalable generation and orchestration driven by task templates and difficulty coefficients. Beyond task-level scores, SelfImprove-Bench organizes evaluation into generalization ladder levels G0 to G4 that measure how far gains transfer from training conditions. Experiments reveal that the evolutionary gains of existing RSI methods are inconsistent across generalization levels.

papers.title: Predictive Safety Guardrails Do Not Always Make LLM Agents Safer
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly take consequential actions in digital and physical environments, where safety risks may emerge only after multiple interaction steps. This has motivated world-model-driven predictive safety guardrails, which anticipate future consequences before execution. However, existing evaluations largely focus on end-to-end safety outcomes, leaving unclear whether safety gains arise from reliable prediction and faithful use of predicted risks. In this work, we systematically diagnose the prediction-to-action pipeline along three dimensions: how world-model predictions are integrated into decision making, whether the predictions themselves are reliable, and whether their content is faithfully used. Across seven policy models and two safety environments, we find that stronger prediction involvement does not yield monotonic safety gains and can reduce task completion while substantially increasing inference cost. We further find that world-model predictions remain insufficiently reliable, especially over longer horizons, where safety prediction degrades substantially relative to near-term forecasting. Finally, we find that safety gains can persist even under corrupted predictions, while locally verified predictions still leave subsequent safety violations, showing that predictive content is not faithfully incorporated into the decision process. Together, these findings expose a fundamental prediction-to-action gap in current predictive guardrails: producing more or seemingly accurate foresight is insufficient unless that foresight is both reliable and faithfully translated into safer decisions.

papers.title: Unlocking the Potential of Contrastive Regularization for Diffusion Transformer Training
papers.abstract: Representation regularization has emerged as an effective way to improve diffusion transformer training. Yet one of the most canonical regularizers--InfoNCE-style contrastive learning--remains largely underexplored in this setting. We naturally ask a question: can standard contrastive learning serve as an effective regularizer for diffusion transformers? Surprisingly, we find that naive InfoNCE regularization brings only marginal gains. Our analysis reveals that the objective is easily dominated by a shortcut: near-orthogonal noise components in diffusion inputs provide a bypass for enlarging negative-pair distances while weakening positive-pair alignment, especially at high noise levels. To unlock the benefit of contrastive regularization, we propose Clean Representation-ANchored Contrastive (CRAN) regularization. Specifically, CRAN anchors contrastive dispersion with clean-sample representation distances, transferring clean relational semantic structure to noisy diffusion representations to suppress the noise shortcut. Extensive experiments on ImageNet show that CRAN consistently improves diffusion transformer training across model scales and training budgets, outperforming internal feature-alignment and dispersive regularization baselines while matching external DINO-guided REPA. These results re-establish InfoNCE-based contrastive learning as an effective regularizer for diffusion training, once its noise-driven over-dispersion is properly constrained.

authors.name: Yi Tan
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: RouteREPA: Routed Representation Alignment for Just Image Transformers
papers.abstract: Representation alignment (REPA) is widely used to accelerate the training of latent-space diffusion transformers (DiTs). However, applying it to pixel-space models such as Just Image Transformers (JiT) is challenging. Our analysis reveals a pronounced representation conflict between discriminative alignment and pixel-space generation. Compared with its latent counterpart, JiT learns representations that are substantially less aligned with DINOv2. Applying REPA to JiT consistently reduces the reconstructability of its intermediate representations, whereas this effect is not observed in Latent JiT. We attribute this conflict to JiT directly reconstructing pixels, which requires its representations to hierarchically encode discriminative semantics and reconstruction-relevant visual information across network depths. To address these challenges, we propose Routed Representation Alignment (RouteREPA), which uses lightweight, representation-dependent routers to adaptively route task-oriented representations for alignment and generation. We further apply routing across multiple network depths to accommodate their depth-dependent representation requirements. Extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K at 256x256 resolution show that RouteREPA consistently improves JiT across model scales and training budgets, outperforming standard REPA. On JiT-H/16, RouteREPA further surpasses PixelREPA using only one-third of its training epochs without classifier-free guidance.

authors.name: Yi Tan
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Zhenshan Tan
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Strong Borel-Cantelli laws and clusters of visits for random intermittent maps
papers.abstract: Near the neutral fixed point of an intermittent map, a single entrance into a small target can be followed by a long run of consecutive visits, so the number of visits need not follow its mean. We study targets $[0,u_n]$ for iid random compositions of Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps with a bounded parameter law that is regularly varying at its minimum $\alpha\in(0,1)$; this includes a single map. For $u_n=cn^{-g}L(n)$, where $c>0$, $0<g\leq1$ and $L$ is slowly varying, the visit count is almost surely asymptotic to its mean if and only if $\sum_n n^{-1}(nu_n)^{-(1-\alpha)/\alpha}<\infty$. Under the stationary law, the count divided by its mean converges to one in $L^1$ exactly when $nu_n\to\infty$. Thus clusters of visits separate these two modes of convergence.

papers.title: VizDAGuide: Misleading Chart Question Answering in Compact Vision Language Models via DAG-Structured Supervision
papers.abstract: Misleading charts can lead vision-language models to conclusions that conflict with underlying data. Existing work focuses on inference-time strategies, while training-time supervision remains less explored. We present VizDAGuide, a DAG-structured supervision method for misleading-chart question answering. The method represents intermediate reasoning states and their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph, assigns supervision weights according to their roles, and serializes the graph into a unified training target for open-ended and multiple-choice QA with single-pass inference. Experiments on two benchmarks across Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 models show improvements over a content- and weight-matched Linear CoT-SFT baseline on both answer formats. Process-level evaluation shows gains in grounding and operation execution, while ablations indicate that dependency structure and weighted supervision are most effective when combined. These results support DAG-structured weighted supervision for misleading-chart question answering.

authors.name: Changbo Wang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: Perturbation Analysis of Gravitational Collapse of Gaseous Stars in the Pressureless Euler-Poisson System
papers.abstract: The compressible Euler-Poisson system describes the full evolutionary processes of inviscid compressible gases, including compression, expansion, fluid motion, equilibrium states and gravitational collapse, under the combined effects of self-gravitation, pressure and inertial forces. It constitutes the fundamental macroscopic mathematical model for describing stellar structures, nebular evolution and gravitational collapse of gaseous celestial bodies. The system comprises mass conservation, momentum conservation, energy conservation laws coupled with the Poisson equation. Following the research in \cite{huang2022}, this paper investigates the quantitative relations among the relative perturbation amplitude of initial velocity, critical time and collapse time for gaseous stars undergoing gravitational collapse within the framework of the pressureless Euler-Poisson system. The closed-form formulas are verified against direct numerical integration, the accuracy of the asymptotic power law is quantified, and the relation between the two time scales is examined.

papers.title: VL-Dedup: Graded Multimodal Entity Resolution for Image-Text Data Deduplication
papers.abstract: Image-text corpora contain copies of one image, captions that describe one image in different ways, captions reused for different images, and captions that do not match their images. Each case calls for a different curation action. Deduplication and multimodal entity resolution (ER) only decide whether records are the same, and they are evaluated on labeled pairs. Yet pair scores do not tell which records end up in the same cluster or which useful captions get deleted. We therefore formulate image-text deduplication as graded multimodal ER, which decides visual identity, caption handling, and mismatches for each pair, and we evaluate it at three levels: pairs, clusters, and the retained set. Our method, VL-Dedup, groups records of the same visual entity into clusters and caps the size of each cluster. Within each cluster, a vision-language model (VLM) and CLIPScore decide which captions to keep and which to flag. We also build VL-DedupBench, with 50,000 COCO and SOP records and 66,788 labeled pairs. On it, a classifier that selects no false edge among the labeled pairs still joins millions of record pairs from different entities. Spending VLM calls on the pairs inside clusters, rather than on pairs with uncertain scores, gives better caption decisions from the same model. Even when almost all clusters are correct, keeping one record per cluster loses facts in many deletions, while the deletions of VL-Dedup lose much less information.

authors.name: Ke Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether vision-language models (VLMs) can enable page-native deep research: directly retrieving and reasoning over rendered document page images. We introduce DR Pixel, the first open-source end-to-end multimodal DR agent that uses rendered page images as its sole retrieval and reasoning unit, operating over a corpus of 1.06M pages. To evaluate this setting, we construct DRPixelBench, a benchmark on scientific papers requiring reasoning over text, figures, tables, and equations. Surprisingly, page-native DR already works well without training, outperforming OCR-based baselines across state-of-the-art models like GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B, while requiring fewer tool calls. We next turn to DR training. A key challenge is that teacher trajectories for agentic supervised finetuning are noisy, mixing critical reasoning and action steps with redundant or failed attempts. To address this, we introduce counterfactual credit reweighting, a fine-grained credit assignment method that weights individual reasoning and action steps by their counterfactual contribution to the final answer. Our training improves retrieval recall by about 15 points and final accuracy by over 10 points on DRPixelBench, and likewise outperforms the untrained baseline on four existing benchmarks. On out-of-distribution ViDoRe-V3, DR Pixel comes within 1.8 points of an oracle that is given the gold pages directly. Our results suggest that the conventional OCR-then-retrieve pipeline is not only unnecessary but suboptimal: directly retrieving and reasoning over visual document pages makes complex DR both more effective and more efficient.

papers.title: FineCraft: Enhancing VLA Models for Fine-Grained Manipulation
papers.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation couples instruction grounding, local visual precision, and sustained execution. We present FineCraft, a framework that adapts pretrained models for fine-grained manipulation in the MetaFine Challenge. A task-routed mixture of policies selects independently adapted DINOv2-DiT or pretrained $\pi_{0.5}$ policies through a common observation-action interface. Local visual features help identify the instructed object parts, demonstrations and expert continuations teach the required actions, and new observations guide replanning during execution. FineCraft ranks fourth with an overall score of $0.878$, exceeding the published reference on all five tasks. Official results and local diagnostics characterize performance across visual perturbations, instruction changes, and multi-stage manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/eqcy/FineCraft

papers.title: ACTOR: Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents
papers.abstract: Large language agents for literary role-playing are typically modeled around dialogue generation, leaving characters' non-dialogue behaviors and their dynamic evolution over story time underrepresented. In this paper, we propose ACTOR (Action-Centered Temporal Organization for Literary Role-Playing Agents), an automated framework for constructing such behavior trajectories from raw novel texts. ACTOR extracts dialogue and persona-relevant non-dialogue behaviors, represents each behavior using a Thought-Action-Observation structure, and organizes behavior trajectories according to the internal temporal order of the story. We build a behavior dataset from 143 diverse literary works. For each source behavior, we generate counterfactual behaviors that are contextually plausible yet inconsistent with the character's persona. We find that existing models struggle to reliably infer character-consistent actions from historical behaviors and evolving character states. Using these behavior pairs, we train models with Regularized Preference Optimization (RPO), which augments DPO with a negative log-likelihood loss on the source behavior to jointly optimize behavior preference and generation. We further design a four-way next-behavior selection task to evaluate the model's ability to faithfully mimic character actions. Across 17,560 evaluation instances, the model trained on ACTOR's preference pairs achieves substantially improved accuracy. This result demonstrates that structured, temporally organized supervision enables models to leverage character profiles and prior behaviors to infer subsequent actions, greatly advancing literary role-playing beyond mere dialogue imitation. Code and data are available at https://github.com/SilentStar233/ACTOR.

authors.name: Zheng Wu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges. First, node identities are graph-specific, and similar interaction patterns can appear at different temporal and activity scales, making histories difficult to represent consistently across networks. Second, the predictive roles of historical patterns vary across interaction dynamics, limiting transfer from a narrow range of training processes. In this paper, we show that a common interaction language, combined with learning across diverse interaction processes, offers a basis for dynamic graph foundation modeling. We propose CL-DGFM, a Common Language Dynamic Graph Foundation Model for temporal link prediction. Its Dynamic Interaction Tokenizer encodes interaction memory, historical connectivity, and ordered destination transitions into calibrated tabular inputs, making dynamic histories accessible to existing predictors without an additional trainable graph encoder. Its Dynamic Interaction Prior trains a pretrained tabular foundation predictor across diverse synthetic dynamics. Labeled historical context guides prediction, with a Contextual Value Adapter modulating attention values. The model transfers to real graphs without target-graph parameter updates. Experiments on TGB and TGB-Seq demonstrate competitive performance. Further comparisons show that the common language supports basic machine learning and neural models, and enables direct use of frozen tabular foundation models on dynamic graphs.

authors.name: Xin He
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: ForceLDM: A Force-aware Latent Dynamics Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires fine-grained control and complex physical interactions with the environment, posing significant challenges for robot policy learning. Vision-only policies struggle with such tasks, as contact states and interaction forces are difficult to infer from visual observations alone. Existing methods mitigate this issue by incorporating force or tactile sensing. However, they often treat these signals as auxiliary observations without fully exploiting their role in modeling future interaction dynamics. To address this, we propose ForceLDM, a force-aware latent dynamics model that learns future contact and motion dynamics to guide action generation. Rather than directly predicting future observations, which can entangle task-relevant dynamics with irrelevant sensory details, ForceLDM learns a compact representation of future dynamics through knowledge distillation. Specifically, a teacher network with privileged future force/torque and optical flow signals extracts future dynamic features, which are then distilled into a student network trained only on current observations. This enables the student model to reason about upcoming contacts and physical dynamics without relying on future sensory inputs at deployment. To improve robustness and generalization, we further introduce a curriculum-based progressive noise injection strategy to mitigate over-reliance on future features. Experiments on five real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks demonstrate that ForceLDM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, generalizes effectively to novel objects, and remains robust to environmental perturbations. Project page and code are available at https://tpy001.github.io/ForceLDM/.

authors.name: Yanyong Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zijiang Yang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
papers.abstract: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.

authors.name: Shanshan Zhong
authors.institution: First Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: Toward Uncertainty-Aware, Physics-Grounded Human World Models
papers.abstract: A robot that acts around people needs a world model of the human: a belief over the person's body state and a dynamics model that predicts where that state goes next. This abstract argues that two published components form exactly these two halves, and specifies how to couple them. KNOWN [1] reconstructs the 3D human body while estimating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in real time (11.6 ms per frame); its aleatoric term identifies unreliable observations, its epistemic term identifies inputs from low-density regions of the training data, and refinement driven by the epistemic term reduces the error on such inputs from 81.3 to 70.3 mm. PhysMoP [2] predicts future body configuration by solving the Euler-Lagrange equations of the body with learned dynamics terms, reducing the 80 ms prediction error from 9.6 to 2.1 mm on Human3.6M and from 12.1 to 0.7 mm on 3DPW. We define the interface between the two, propose three mechanisms by which KNOWN's uncertainty enters PhysMoP, and specify an evaluation protocol on in-the-wild video. No new experimental results are reported here.

papers.title: Subpolynomial-Query Proximal Sampling Beyond Log-Concavity
papers.abstract:
We study the gradient query complexity of sampling from a density $\pi(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ has a $ eta$-Lipschitz gradient but need not be convex. Our approach uses the proximal sampler, which alternates Gaussian perturbation with sampling a position conditional on the noisy observation. We implement its observation chain using the high-order noisy conditional sampler of [OpenAI 2026], obtaining improved dimension dependence under functional inequalities. If $\pi$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality (LSI) with constant $\alpha$, then for every fixed $
u>0$, there is a finite constant $C_
u$ depending only on $
u$ such that the algorithm returns a sample within total-variation distance $\varepsilon$ using at most $C_
u\kappa(d+\kappa+\varepsilon^{-1}+\|
abla V(x_0)\|^2/ eta)^
u$ queries, where $\kappa= eta/\alpha$ and $x_0$ is an arbitrary reference point for initialization. The analysis controls center-dependent local errors along exact proximal histories and removes the final observation noise by conditional decoding. Under a Poincar'e inequality (PI), we obtain a corresponding guarantee from a warm start with a known bound on its R'enyi divergence. An oracle lower bound shows that a stationary point alone, which suffices under LSI, is insufficient under PI.

authors.name: Wei Guo
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mechanical Structure Mechanics and Control

papers.title: LODox: A Web-Based Platform for Cultural Heritage Linked Data Discovery
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models have transformed how data can be linked, discovered, and enhanced. LODox, Linked Open Data at Oxford, is an evolving web-based platform that embraces this transformation for cultural heritage Linked Open Data. LODox features a novel interface with intuitive card-based data presentation and visualization in a semantic portal. It represents an evolving approach to explore heterogeneous cultural heritage data across multiple sources through a unified interface. In this paper, we will briefly describe the LODox architecture, its implementation, and future development plan, particularly its alignment and integration with Solid.

papers.title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
papers.abstract: We give a proof of a folklore conjecture that a compact K\"ahler manifold with the same scalar Laplace spectrum as complex projective space equipped with the Fubini--Study metric is holomorphically isometric to it. More generally, we prove that the spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree $p$ determines $\CP^n$ up to holomorphic isometry among compact connected K\"ahler manifolds, for every fixed pair of integers $(p,n)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$. Equality of a single Hodge spectrum first forces periodic geodesic flow and the integral cohomology ring of complex projective space. The ordinary first heat coefficient then identifies the total scalar curvature except on a Pell sequence of pairs. For those pairs, a clean wave-trace argument, a Krawtchouk estimate, and a mod-two projective-bundle obstruction determine the geodesic return holonomy. A canonical K\"ahler involution recovers a weighted first heat coefficient which is nonzero throughout the exceptional sequence. The Kobayashi--Ochiai theorem and a fixed-class second-heat-coefficient calculation complete the argument.

papers.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. PlantVLM-Edge combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface, allowing growers to ask open-ended questions and receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. The framework is backbone-agnostic: we validate it with two different VLM types with varying scale and architecture (Qwen3-VL-2B and LLaVA-1.5-7B), four quantization schemes, and two diagnostic domains (plant diseases and insect pests), and we deploy all variants on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Eight-bit quantization affects answer quality minimally relative to the full-precision model, and 4-bit activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality on both domains while reducing the weight memory of the 2B backbone by 49%. In its most compact form, PlantVLM-Edge requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory, returns its first token in about 0.12 s, and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 s. These results demonstrate that timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is practical on edge devices, providing a foundation for next-generation crop monitoring and decision support systems.

papers.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. I
papers.abstract:
Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove \[ \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{1\leqslant n\leqslant X}\lambda\left(n\right)\mathrm{e}\left(n\alpha\right)\right|
  \mathrm{d}\alpha
  \gg X^{\frac{1}{4}}. \] This removes the $X^\varepsilon$ loss in the previous result of Pandey and Radziwi\l\l~\cite{PandeyRadziwill2026}. In the second paper in this series, we will prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)} {\log X} \geqslant\frac{1}{3}. \]

papers.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
papers.abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. We study dynamic-boundary 4D CFD prediction for articulated moving geometries and introduce RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved robotic CFD benchmark spanning diverse morphologies and flow conditions. To address the computational and autoregressive challenges of this setting, we propose DynaSolver, a neural operator that explicitly conditions on boundary evolution and causal flow history. DynaSolver employs an efficient physical-token formulation that amortizes point-to-token projection across the operator stack, substantially reducing repeated point-space spatio-temporal computation while retaining accurate point-level reconstruction. We further introduce Replay-Augmented Parallel Training, which exposes the model to autoregressively generated histories while preserving parallel dense supervision, narrowing the gap between ground-truth-conditioned training and autoregressive rollout. Experiments on RoboCFD-4D show that DynaSolver achieves the best full-rollout accuracy among a broad range of learned CFD surrogates, with its advantage increasing as rollout proceeds, indicating substantially reduced autoregressive error accumulation. Project page: https://made-gpt.github.io/DynaSolver-ProjectPage.

authors.name: Junhao Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Cross-Prompt Reuse of Entity-Replacement Responses
papers.abstract: With model weights fixed, we measure how much of an entity-replacement response transfers between English factual questions, beyond whether answers change. We add the hidden-state change from two source questions to a target question about the same entity, comparing the predicted log-probability shift between two relations' published answers, given known answer prefixes, with the measured one. Hidden reuse injects the aligned change at 50% depth before the target's remaining layers; direct reuse adds source output-score changes. With other-relation sources, hidden reuse removes 45% and 49% of no-change error on 0.5-1B Qwen and Llama. Gemma-2-2B removes 22% and passes one of three comparisons in plain text without its default beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token. A later protocol restoring it yields 58-68%, passing every comparison on three cohorts. Larger checkpoints, chat format and new entities show replication and format- or cohort-dependent failures. On small plain-format checkpoints, other-relation hidden reuse mainly reproduces the shift both relations' questions share, without reliably lowering relation-selective error. With target-relation sources, hidden reuse's post hoc advantage over direct reuse is 0.2-0.9 nats outside chat format, unconfirmed and not replacement-specific. The same relation-neutral change at both questions' entity tokens lowers relation-selective error more than random or other-replacement changes, indicating receiving-question dependence.

papers.title: Structural and Optical Properties of PVP-Modified ZnS Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
papers.abstract: Pristine and PVP-modified ZnS nanoparticles were investigated to examine how PVP addition affects structural, surface, optical, and methylene blue (MB) decolorization properties. X-ray diffraction confirmed cubic zinc-blende ZnS in all samples, with apparent Scherrer coherent-domain sizes of 3.10-3.31 nm. Electron microscopy revealed agglomeration, while HRTEM and electron diffraction confirmed locally crystalline regions in S1 and S4. The estimated direct Tauc gap decreased from 3.69 eV for S1 to 3.58 eV for S4. Between 100 and 300 K, the principal TO-like Raman band softened on heating, while visible photoluminescence changed predominantly within the overlapping green-yellow region. After 210 min under 254 nm irradiation, MB-band losses near 664 nm reached 19.33%, 58.18%, 70.00%, and 94.42% for S1-S4, compared with 6.58% for the catalyst-free control. PVP modification therefore alters optical and dye-decolorization responses while preserving the principal ZnS phase; however, dye-band attenuation alone does not establish complete mineralization.

authors.name: Dushyant Singh
authors.institution: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar

papers.title: Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes
papers.abstract: Land-cover maps classified from wide-area hyperspectral surveys are least reliable along class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, so their errors are spatially structured. We study how this structure can direct a limited verification budget: when a low-altitude UAV or a ground crew can visit only a handful of sites, where it should go depends on how classifier uncertainty is arranged across the scene and how a fixed sensor footprint tiles that arrangement. We estimate a per-pixel uncertainty surface from the disagreement of an ensemble of spectral classifiers and select sites by greedy, field-of-view-aware coverage of the uncertainty mass. On seven benchmark scenes, the highest-uncertainty decile of pixels is 2.6 to 7.9 times richer in errors than the scene as a whole, and the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of the classifier's errors with 15 sites, 1.7 to 18 times as many as uncertainty-agnostic sampling of the same labelled region. A non-overlapping selection of the footprints richest in uncertainty does equally well, so the gain comes from scoring whole footprints by uncertainty mass. The advantage persists under spatially blocked evaluation and with a spectral-spatial classifier, although disagreement then ranks errors less well. It requires restricting the surface to labelled land cover: over the whole scene, disagreement peaks on unlabelled ground, where inspections cannot be scored. The best policy for covering connected high-uncertainty regions depends on the scene and on the threshold that defines them, and Gaussian-process selection covers less uncertainty than the coverage greedy on every scene. The pipeline runs on commodity CPUs.

papers.title: Robust Pixel-wise Digital Image Correlation under Large Motions and Illumination Variations via a Global-to-Local Hybrid Neural Field
papers.abstract: Digital image correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact technique for full-field displacement measurement. Data-driven deep-learning DIC offers rapid inference but may generalize poorly to unseen speckle patterns, deformation modes, noise levels, and illumination conditions. Classical optimization-based DIC and recent image-constrained neural formulations avoid labeled displacement data, yet their convergence and accuracy remain vulnerable to initialization, large rigid-body motion, fine non-uniform deformation, and gray-value disturbances. This paper presents a global-to-local hybrid neural DIC framework for robust pixelwise measurement. Stage 1 estimates a dominant in-plane rigid transformation through coarse rotation search, phase correlation, and masked refinement, providing a reliable initialization under large translation and rotation. Stage 2 represents the residual displacement with a hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), and optimizes it using a valid-overlap, illumination-robust structural loss. The local gray-value model explicitly accommodates multiplicative and additive intensity changes. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate accurate and stable displacement recovery under noise, non-uniform deformation, large rotation, illumination variation, and degraded imaging conditions.

authors.name: Xianglong Guo
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Meromorphic functions together with their partial derivatives sharing zeros and poles in $\mathbb{C}^m$
papers.abstract: In the paper, using Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$, we study the problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be two finite order non-constant meromorphic functions in $\mathbb{C}^m$ such that $f$ and $g$ share $0$ and $\infty$ CM. If $\partial_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM and if for one $n>1$, $\partial^n_{z_i}(f)$ and $\partial^n_{z_i}(g)$ share $0$ CM, where $i=1,2,\ldots,m$, then $f$ and $g$ have special presentations. Our finding extends the result of K\"{o}hler (Meromorphic functions sharing zeros and poles and also some of their derivatives sharing zeros, Complex Var., 11 (1989), 39-48) into higher dimensions. Moreover, we show by an example that the restriction on the growth of $f$ and $g$ is necessary.

authors.name: Hong Yan Xu
authors.institution: Tumor Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: Molecular conical intersections with odd electron number are realizations of the topological Yang monopole
papers.abstract: The two-level conical intersection of a molecule with odd electron number in the absence of magnetic field obeys time-reversal symmetry $T^{2}=-1$ (referred to as the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection), and has a five-dimensional branching space due to the Kramer degeneracy. Similar to how the conical intersection of a molecule in a magnetic field ($T^{2}=0$) behaves as the Dirac monopole, the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection behaves as the Yang monopole, an mathematical generalization of Dirac monopole with SU(2) gauge field and SO(5) symmetry. This implies that we can study topological properties of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersections in chemistry based on what is known about Yang monopole in high energy physics. In this work, we present a few mathematical tools to study this connection. First, we show that geometric algebra and quaternion numbers together provides a natural way to utilize the $T^{2}=-1$ time reversal symmetry and the SO(5) symmetry in scaled coordinates, making it simple to derive eigenfunctions, Berry connection and Berry curvature of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection. In particular, this approach provides a simple proof that when viewed from the upper or lower states, the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection behaves as the self-dual or self-antidual Yang monopole with second Chern number $C_{2}=+\frac{1}{4}$ or $-\frac{1}{4}$ respectively. In addition, we propose a visualization method for the SU(2) Berry connection of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection. This is achieved by showing that the nonzero part of the Berry connection induces Hopf-fibration on the $S^{3}$ longitude space, and is further visualized through stereographic projection.

authors.name: Chenchen Song
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinxiang Medical University

papers.title: Simple algorithm for evaluating SU(2) non-abelian geometric phase in the vicinity of molecular conical intersection of odd electron number
papers.abstract: Molecular conical intersection of odd-electron number are known to give arise to non-abelian geometric phases. In this work, we present a simple algorithm for evaluating the SU(2) geometric phases given a trajectory represented as a discrete set of coordinates in the 5-dimensional branching space. Motivated by the special property that such conical intersection behaves as abelian ones in 3-dimensional subspace, we take two steps to establish the algorithm. We first prove that it is possible to construct an augmented trajectory consisting of spherical triangles that has the same geometric phases as the original trajectory. We then prove that the geometric phase contribution from each spherical triangle can be evaluated from its properties using Stokes' theorem in a way that closely resembles abelian conical intersections. The total geometric phases are thus evaluated by path-ordered products of contributions from each spherical triangle. Based on the augmented trajectory, we further show that the geometric phases of the upper and lower states will switch under inversion transformation of the trajectory. This relation is further generalized to show that the Wilson loop, defined as the trace of the geometric phases, will switch between the two states under any 5-dimensional improper isometric transformation. Example calculations of geometric phases for trajectories generated on 5-dimensional polytopes are also presented and discussed.

authors.name: Chenchen Song
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinxiang Medical University

papers.title: Do Orthogonality Constraints Help Language-Model Training Beyond Sphere Optimization?
papers.abstract: A growing body of work reports benefits from orthogonality constraints in fine-tuning large language models (LLMs). These results raise an open question: do orthogonality constraints also help LLM pre-training? We conduct a systematic empirical study of decoder-only LLM pre-training with models ranging from 360M to 3.1B parameters, trained on nearly 200B tokens. We examine fourteen variants of orthogonality training: some constrain the weight matrix itself, while others use orthogonal factors to reparameterize it. Because a strictly orthogonal square matrix loses half of its degrees of freedom, we also study block-wise orthogonality, where every $d$ rows form a row-orthonormal (Stiefel) matrix and the block size $d$ is a hyperparameter. Among block sizes ranging from 1 to the shorter side of the matrix, no $d>1$ used throughout the network reliably outperforms $d=1$, and large blocks are clearly worse; the one placement that helps, symmetric positive-definite factors on the query and key projections, loses its small gain as models grow. At $d=1$, the constraint reduces to sphere optimization, with each row direction on its own unit sphere, which by itself already improves on tuned Muon. The same two findings hold for a diffusion transformer trained on ImageNet, and after fine-tuning, downstream accuracy does not separate the parameterizations. Our conclusion is that, across the realizations we tried, orthogonality between rows does not help language-model pre-training beyond sphere optimization. Since this appears to conflict with several prior results, we re-examine five prior methods in pre-training and fine-tuning that report orthogonality improvements. In each case the reported gain is attributable to numerical precision, training horizon, optimizer realization, or per-row norm control rather than to the orthogonality the methods impose.

authors.name: Li Zhang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: $TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering
papers.abstract: Tactile sensing plays a crucial role in everyday human interaction. Consider inserting a plug into a tight socket, vision alone provides limited guidance during the final insertion stage, and we instead rely on both anticipated contact and realized tactile feedback to ajust the insertion motion. The same capability is equally important for robots, particularly in dexterous manipulation tasks. Yet many contemporary robot policies remain vision-dominant. This visual bias, compounded by limited tactile data and sparse contact events, can cause directly incorporated tactile signals to be ignored or even compromise the policy's pretrained capabilities, yielding degrading performance as observed in our experiments. We present $TF^2$-Steering, which refines actions via learned residual steering of the flow-matching action expert's velocity field, using a tactile mixture-of-experts architecture to integrate both tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback. Together with specific designed three stages training recipe, $TF^2$-Steering enables tactile signals to correct and, when necessary, redirect the flow-matching action-generation process, while building on the strong action-generation capacity of the vision-based foundation policy. Extensive experiments across six simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of $TF^2$-Steering. It outperforms the strongest evaluated baselines by 10.7 percentage points in average simulation success rate and 9.1 percentage points in average real-world progress success rate. Project page: https://yiming-cc.github.io/tf2-steering/.

authors.name: Yiming Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Li Zhang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: A GeV PWN Candidate in the PSR J1135--6055/G293.8+0.6 Field
papers.abstract: We present a \textit{Fermi} Large Area Telescope (LAT) study of PSR~J1135--6055 and the composite supernova remnant (SNR) G293.8+0.6. MeerKAT radio observations reveal a bright central plerion within the faint SNR shell, while Chandra observations detect a compact nebula around the pulsar. Together, these observations establish the presence of a PWN within G293.8+0.6. Our analysis of the 20~GeV--1~TeV LAT data yields a point-like excess with $\mathrm{TS}=26.30$ and photon index $\Gamma=1.63\pm0.33$. Its best-fit position is consistent with the pulsar within the 95\% statistical localization region, and neither the uniform-disk nor Gaussian model is favored, providing no evidence for significant extension. A one-zone leptonic model, together with an independent jet component, reproduces the multiwavelength observations. In this model, the GeV photons are produced mainly by inverse-Compton scattering from relativistic electrons and positrons. Given its positional agreement with the pulsar/PWN and broadband interpretation, we regard the LAT point source as a GeV PWN candidate.

authors.name: Li Zhang
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: Private Uniform Language Generation
papers.abstract: We study uniform language generation under approximate differential privacy. Given a uniformly bounded number of distinct examples from an unknown target language, a generator must produce infinitely many new examples from that language with probability one while protecting the privacy of its input. We introduce a new combinatorial dimension termed the nested branching dimension and prove that a language class is privately uniformly generatable if and only if both its closure dimension and nested branching dimension are finite. Previous work characterizes non-private uniform generation by the finiteness of the closure dimension alone. Our results therefore identify an additional combinatorial obstruction imposed by privacy.

authors.name: Peng Ye
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Finite-Sample Calibration and Power Benchmarks in Two-Sample Random-Integration Tests
papers.abstract: In high-dimensional two-group studies, a supplied variable set can be used directly or to learn a projection. We study how much attainable power these choices retain at fixed observation and calibration budgets. For complete unbiased random-integration statistics under Gaussian common shape, a fixed-spectrum comparison orders direction-wise power and gives an explicit criterion balancing an oracle advantage against learning loss. Joint regeneration controls level for a specified learner with unknown diagonal shape. A paired construction permits observation reuse and finite-reference calibration of fitted scores and menus. In the paired diagonal experiment, an invariant sparse likelihood-ratio benchmark provides an attainable efficiency target. Finite-amplitude bounds connect a classical bounded quadratic to this target; conditioning on the coordinate maximum yields informative complementary bounds at moderate and strong signals. Both comparisons include finite reference budgets, and null-only simulations certify local comparisons with specified fitted rules. Equal-budget experiments and a leukemia application compare aggregation, projection and fitted quadratic scores. For correlated paired data, classical sign randomization supplies a separate calibration under central symmetry. The efficiency guarantees apply to the stated experiments and signal classes; general small-budget shape efficiency and adaptation to unknown signal allocation remain open.

papers.title: Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD
papers.abstract: We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions generate a spin-nematic squeezed state in the $m_F=\pm1$ modes. The resulting pair-correlated state has a rank-one quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for the two mode phases relative to the $m_F=0$ mode and therefore cannot resolve them independently. Nevertheless, we find that a parameter-independent passive three-mode transformation lifts this rank deficiency and enables joint estimation of both phases. In the undepleted-pump regime, we derive expressions for the QFIM, optimize the equal-weight multiparameter quantum Cram\'er-Rao bound, and obtain a full-rank probe with squeezing-enhanced sensitivity below the matched fixed-total-number standard quantum limit (SQL). These analytical predictions are confirmed by exact-diagonalization calculations. We further construct a parameter-independent readout that maps the phase combinations onto displacement channels accessible through atomic homodyne or parity measurements. Our results provide a route from spin-mixing-generated quantum correlations to two-phase estimation in spinor condensates.

authors.name: Dong E. Liu
authors.institution: Frontier Science Center for Quantum Information of the Ministry of Education of China

papers.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
papers.abstract:
We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h,
  \qquad
  \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$
  The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks. A positional encoding of the finite-field moment curve has $q$ elements in an interval of length $O_h(q^h)$, while, for each $1\leq r<h$, sums arising from distinct $r$-element multisets are separated by more than $q$. This separation allows whole blocks to be appended to a prescribed finite set without a further dilation. In particular, our result gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Szemer\'edi \cite{szemeredi}.

papers.title: Quadratic bounds for intersecting hypergraphs: An affirmative answer to a question of Duke and Erd\H{o}s
papers.abstract: Let $m(k,b)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an intersecting $k$-uniform hypergraph in which every $(k-1)$-set of vertices is disjoint from at least $b$ edges, with $m(k,b)=+\infty$ if no such hypergraph exists. Duke and Erd\H{o}s [Congressus Numerantium (1980)] asked whether $m(k,k)=o(k^4)$ is possible. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively and determine the order of growth of $m(k,k)$ by proving that $k^2+1\leq m(k,k)\leq Ck^2$ for all sufficiently large $k$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. More generally, we show that $m(k,b)=\Theta(kb)$ for all sufficiently large odd $k$ and every integer $b$ with $k\leq b\leq (k-1)(k-3)/2$, where the implied constants are independent of $k$ and $b$.

authors.name: Linlin Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The equality $s(G)=\eta(G)+\exp(G)-1$ fails for $G=C_2^7\oplus C_6$
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. The Erd\H{o}s-Ginzburg-Ziv constant $\mathsf{s}(G)$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $\exp(G)$. The short zero-sum constant $\eta(G)$ is defined similarly, with the requirement that the zero-sum subsequence is nonempty and has length at most $\exp(G)$. It is known that $\mathsf{s}(G)\ge \eta(G)+\exp(G)-1.$ A conjecture proposed by W. Gao in 2003, which has been widely studied in zero-sum theory, predicts that $$ \mathsf{s}(G)=\eta(G)+\exp(G)-1 $$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. In this paper, we prove that this conjecture fails for the group $C_2^7\oplus C_6$.

papers.title: Extremal zero-sum sequences without elements of maximal order
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group $G$, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $G$. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured that every minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)$~\cite[Conjecture~6.1]{GG99} and every zero-sumfree sequence of length $\mathsf D(G)-1$~\cite[Conjecture~4.1]{GG06} contains an element of order $\exp(G)$. We disprove both conjectures by proving a density-one theorem: for every fixed finite abelian group $H$ of exponent $M=2^ap^b$, where $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, and $p$ is an odd prime, the set of integers $r\ge0$ for which $G_r=C_2^r\oplus H$ admits a minimal zero-sum sequence of length $\mathsf D(G_r)$ with no term of order $M$ has natural density one.

papers.title: Chiral phonon magnetism from localized Raman excitation
papers.abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal {\alpha}-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.

papers.title: Extensions at Nonzero p-Characters for Cartan-Type Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: For restricted simple Cartan-type Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, the reduced enveloping algebra at every nonzero $p$-character is a matrix algebra over a terminal symmetric corner, and this corner determines the extensions. Central-socle traces recover its radical and its simple factors, and the first radical layer determines the degree-one extensions. For the Witt algebra $W(1;1)$, at even height $2\le h\le p-3$, the unique simple module has self-extension dimension $\min\{p-h-2,h+2\}$. At height two in characteristic seven, we present the Yoneda algebra as an eight-dimensional symmetric algebra tensored with a polynomial algebra on three central degree-two classes. An equivariant Tate resolution and cocycle identities prove the presentation in all degrees.

papers.title: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Long-lived agents rely on persistent memory of users, tasks and decisions, and this memory must stay consistent with a world that keeps changing. When an upstream fact changes, however, memory systems can revise the contradicted memory itself while the beliefs, plans and actions derived from it remain accepted, even though they have lost their support. We therefore formulate dependency-aware state revision, which asks not only what changed but also which dependent states should no longer be trusted. To address it, StateGraph maintains an evolving state dependency graph whose edges are recovered from interaction histories. Its core design is counterfactual verification: each candidate edge is tested by asking whether the dependent state would survive the loss of its premise, which separates support dependence from semantic relatedness, and revision then invalidates a dependent state only when a strict dependency fails and no independent support path survives. To test this design, we introduce StateChangeBench, a controlled benchmark of 50 author-constructed cases annotated with cascade depth, hard negatives and action consequences. On it, StateGraph's Impact-F1 margin over a CUPMem reimplementation is 6.9 percentage points at depth 1 and 26.0 at depth 3+. On public long-term memory benchmarks, its point estimates are comparable to or higher than those of the evaluated baselines on most datasets. These results provide initial evidence that explicit dependency tracking can improve selective memory revision under changing conditions.

authors.name: Jiaqi Zhang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Automobile Materials, Ministry of Education, Jilin University

authors.name: Mingkai Zheng
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: Flat Features, Detailed Images? Simple Detail Control for Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Prompt engineering is commonly used to encourage text-to-image models to generate more detailed images. However, it does not provide reliable, continuous, or disentangled control. We analyze feature tokens produced with and without detail-enhancing prompts across six diffusion transformers and observe a common pattern: these prompts tend to increase the entropy of each token's energy distribution while largely preserving its ordering. That is, flattening the distribution increases the level of detail. Motivated by this counter-intuitive finding, we introduce a simple training-free approach that continuously adjusts the level of detail according to a scalar. Specifically, it shifts the squared channel magnitudes of each token toward a higher entropy distribution with a time-aware scheduler to concentrate the intervention at intermediate sampling steps. Across extensive experiments on different types of diffusion transformers, we show that our approach provides continuous control over detail metrics while largely preserving image quality and semantic structure. It requires only a few lines of code and adds negligible inference time overhead.

authors.name: Jiyang Zheng
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: Ask More, Hear Less: How a Review Prompt Changes What Online Ratings Show
papers.abstract: Platforms ask customers for online reviews to reduce self-selection, but theory conflicts on whether review solicitation makes online ratings more or less informative. Selection theory implies that asking helps, voice theory that it dilutes the news, and research on rating inflation that compression destroys information. We reconcile these views with signal detection theory, which separates what a rating knows (its sensitivity) from what it shows (its criterion). We test the framework on Steam, a leading PC video game store, whose client began in October 2019 to prompt players for a review after about three hours of play. Using a difference-in-discontinuities design at that inferred threshold in 21.6 million Steam reviews of 315 games, we find that review counts just above the threshold become 4.25 times those just below, and the jump in the positive share grows by 6.6 percentage points. Agreement with critics changes little near launch and erodes later. The rating's movement changes far more: pass-through from reviews written in the first two hours falls from 0.73 to 0.18 just above the threshold, against 0.81 to 0.64 just below, and a fixed rating tier responds to 12% of downturns in those reviews above the threshold, down from 42%, against 41% and 47% below it. What the stream knows changes less. At equal review counts its sensitivity falls more above the threshold, because added reviews respond about half as much and scores near the ceiling are noisier per review, but at natural counts added volume offsets this loss, leaving a change of -0.03 relative to the stream below (95% CI -0.13 to 0.06). Failures that developers acknowledge, which run through complaints, still move the score after launch. Review prompts therefore mainly change how a rating must be read, and platforms that solicit reviews should recalibrate their rating labels.

papers.title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
papers.abstract: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37\%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86\% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15\% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.

authors.name: Liujiang Zhou
authors.institution: National Engineering Research Center of Electromagnetic Radiation Control Materials

papers.title: Symmetry, uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions of the Choquard equation
papers.abstract:
We study positive solutions \(Q\in H^1(\mathbb R^N)\) of \[-\Delta Q+Q=(I_\alpha*Q^p)Q^{p-1},\] where \(I_\alpha\) is the Riesz potential of order \(\alpha\), \(N\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<N\), \(p>1+\alpha/N\), and \((N-2)p<N+\alpha\). We prove that every such solution is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing about some point. For \(p\ge2\), we establish uniqueness up to translations and show that the real linearized operator has Morse index one and kernel spanned by \(\partial_1Q,\ldots,\partial_NQ\).
  The symmetry proof uses the method of moving planes. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy and compactness through a continuation argument.

authors.name: Jianjun Zhang
authors.institution: People's Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

papers.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
papers.abstract: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. The second stage extends these capabilities to tool-dependent reasoning through a scalable pipeline for constructing diverse and automatically verifiable tasks grounded in real-world data sources and deterministic computation. Finally, reinforcement learning further strengthens long-horizon reasoning and interaction with external tools and environments. Despite this compact training recipe, Axion 1.0 achieves strong performance across a broad suite of agentic benchmarks and is competitive with leading commercial models on several of them. Equally importantly, Axion 1.0 is open beyond model weights: we release the complete recipe, including data construction, generation, filtering, verification, prompts, and training code, enabling the entire development process to be reproduced and extended. Axion 1.0 demonstrates that strong agent foundation models can be both open and simple, offering a practical and reproducible path toward advancing open agentic intelligence.

authors.name: Yunjie Tian
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
papers.abstract: Robust 3D point-cloud recognition is critical for robotics, mapping, and urban sensing, yet point-cloud classifiers often suffer performance drops under domain shifts caused by sensor changes, environmental variation, and acquisition artifacts. Many existing adaptation methods are difficult to deploy in practice because they require access to source data or the internal parameters of the source model, which may be restricted by privacy, licensing, or security constraints. We present 3D-BBDA, a backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation framework that adapts a source-trained predictor to unlabeled target data using only black-box outputs. Our method performs pseudo-label guided prototype-based alignment and employs a weighted prediction module to fuse source logits with alignment logits, reducing sensitivity to noisy pseudo-labels. To stabilize prototype memory when pseudo-label coverage is incomplete, we construct a Gaussian-perturbed prototype prior from unlabeled target predictions and use it as a fallback for missing or unreliable class prototypes during alignment. Experiments on four corrupted 3D benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines. On ModelNet-40C, 3D-BBDA achieves mean errors of 32.08% (PointNet) and 29.62% (GDANet), outperforming Source-only (35.88% / 34.03%) and BFTT3D (33.78% / 32.36%). 3D-BBDA requires only a single forward pass with no gradient updates making it suitable for real-time, privacy-preserving deployment in transferable 3D recognition pipelines. Project page is available at https://visdomlab.github.io/3D_BBDA

authors.name: Kunal Jangid
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

authors.name: Vinod K Kurmi
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

papers.title: BGD-SF PolySegNet: boundary-guided dynamic selective fusion network for robust polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images
papers.abstract: Effective polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images is crucial for early detection of colorectal cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. While current deep learning models perform well on traditional Dice benchmarks, border segmentation remains difficult. Most methods use boundary information only as an additional loss signal during training, which prevents the network from explicitly learning border-guided feature selection or mask refinement. This paper introduces BGD-SF PolySegNet, a boundary-guided encoder-decoder architecture that controls three phases of the segmentation pipeline: dynamic multi-scale context aggregation, selective skip-feature fusion, and final mask refinement. The architecture comprises a pretrained EfficientNet-B4 backbone and three proposed modules: Boundary-Guided Dynamic Cascaded Multi-Scale Context Aggregation (BGD-CMSCA), Boundary-Guided Selective Attention Fusion (BG-SAGF), and a Multi-Level Boundary Guidance Head (MBGH). The model is trained on 3,535 annotated images from Kvasir-SEG, BKAI-IGH NeoPolyp-Small, and PolypGen, and evaluated on four held-out benchmark datasets. On the internal test set, BGD-SF achieves a Dice of 0.887, IoU of 0.839, mask-derived Boundary F1 of 0.531, HD95 of 30.32, and ASSD of 18.10, improving Boundary F1, HD95, and ASSD by 15.7%, 27.5%, and 34.6% over the strongest CNN baselines. External validation on CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-ColonDB, ETIS-Larib, and CVC-300 yielded Dice scores of 0.891, 0.776, 0.863, and 0.885, respectively. The model runs at 35 FPS with 22.51M parameters. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirm statistically significant mask-derived Boundary F1 improvements over six of seven ablation variants (p < 0.001; small-to-moderate effect sizes, r = 0.215-0.434), demonstrating that integrating boundary guidance as an active architectural component measurably advances polyp boundary delineation.

papers.title: Modern Software Engineering with Verification Agents: A Spec-First Architecture for Autonomous Synthesis, Verification IRs, and Organizational Scale
papers.abstract: When autonomous coding agents synthesize implementation code, formal specifications, and mechanical proofs simultaneously, the software engineering hierarchy inverts: the formal specification becomes the primary human-reviewed artifact, while source code and proof scripts become disposable build outputs. This paper presents an end-to-end architecture for agent-authored, formally verified software engineering. First, we establish a logic-agnostic foundation combining a spec-first stack inversion, a zero-code-review workflow gated by automated continuous integration (CI) checks, and a minimal Verification Intermediate Representation (VIR) lowered via a thin, verified translator. Second, we pair an extensional Computational Type Theory (CTT) specification layer with Higher-Order Abstract Syntax (HOAS) and linear resource typing in the VIR--eliminating rewrite friction for synthesis agents while defining an experiment, its protocol frozen before the first reader, to measure whether removing boundary coercions improves human specification readability. Third, we scale collaboration across multi-team organizations using Personal Spec-Copilots and a Shared Synthesis Fleet that detects cross-team Semantic Merge Conflicts and fuses modular contracts into zero-copy binaries. We illustrate this architecture on a zero-copy authenticated message router and distinguish our existing empirical baselines (salt, SaltBench, x86lean, and MetaPRL) from newly proposed components.

papers.title: Improving Financial Cybersecurity Through Fraud Transaction Detection with Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Financial fraud detection remains a critical challenge in cybersecurity, with traditional rule-based systems struggling to keep pace with evolving attack patterns. This paper presents a deep learning approach for fraud transaction detection, leveraging neural network architectures to identify anomalous financial behaviors with high accuracy. We evaluate multiple deep learning models including LSTM, CNN, and hybrid architectures on real-world financial transaction datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over conventional machine learning baselines. Our approach achieves robust performance in detecting fraudulent transactions while minimizing false positives, providing a scalable solution for enterprise financial cybersecurity systems

papers.title: Inhalation-exhalation asymmetry in pressure-driven airflow through a population-derived median unilateral human nasal cavity
papers.abstract: This study investigates inhalation-exhalation asymmetry in population-derived median unilateral human nasal cavity under pressure-driven breathing using time-resolved computational fluid dynamics (CFD). A standardized geometry reconstructed from averaged CT data of 30 adults was subjected to a sinusoidal nasopharyngeal pressure waveform over a complete breathing cycle. Low, intermediate, and high pressure amplitudes were considered to quantify breathing-phase-dependent changes in flow rate, Reynolds number, wall shear stress, nasal resistance, and olfactory-region airflow. For identical imposed pressure magnitudes, inhalation produced a consistently larger flow rate and lower aerodynamic resistance than exhalation, demonstrating a direction-dependent pressure-flow response. Increasing breathing intensity increased Reynolds number and nasal resistance while largely preserving the spatial pattern of the flow. During inhalation, stronger airflow penetrated further into the superior nasal cavity and produced higher and more localized wall shear stress, whereas exhalation exhibited smoother airflow redistribution. The breathing-phase asymmetry also affected regional ventilation: the fraction of total airflow reaching the olfactory region increased with inspiratory intensity and reached approximately 6% under the high-pressure condition, while the expiratory fraction remained comparatively insensitive to breathing intensity. These results demonstrate that pressure-driven transient simulations naturally capture geometry-dependent inhalation-exhalation differences that are suppressed when identical flow rates are prescribed for the two breathing phases, with consequences for both global nasal resistance and regional airflow delivery.

papers.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
papers.abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.

papers.title: DiA: Directional Adapter
papers.abstract: Fine-grained action recognition often depends on how an action unfolds over time rather than on appearance alone. Visually similar classes may differ in preparation, execution, or completion phases, making uniformly aggregated temporal context suboptimal. We study this problem under a practical objective: i) improving recognition performance with few tunable parameters, ii) being compute efficient, and iii) using only the readily available video modality. Motivated by this missing temporal observation and the accuracy--compute efficiency--unimodality objective, we propose Directional Adapter (DiA), a parameter-efficient adapter on top of CLIP. DiA formulates temporal specialization into causal and anti-causal directions, allowing past-to-present and future-to-present cues to be modeled differently. To keep this directional modeling parameter- and compute-efficient, both directions use depth-wise temporal convolutions in a compact bottleneck space and are combined through a learnable fusion. DiA achieves state-of-the-art performance among methods using a single video input modality across seven public benchmarks, with only $\sim$3.6M tunable parameters, while also delivering higher throughput and lower inference latency than prior methods. Code is available at https://github.com/prakashchhipa/DiA-Directional-Adapter.
