We investigated zero-shot classification, a feature-based ensemble, and a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST). The fine-tuned AST achieved 89.36% accuracy, 85.98% precision, 89.24% recall, and 87.58% F1 on held-out test data for binary classification of Person talking. Because this result remained below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous annotation, model predictions were used as suggestions and subjected to human verification. Of the 5,026 initially unlabeled recordings, 2,337 were routed to a speech-verification queue and 2,689 remained for ordinary manual annotation. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and detected zero false positives, yielding 100% verification accuracy. The observed average verification time was approximately 4.2 seconds per file. At an average rate of 35 seconds per file for manual annotation, the hybrid workflow reduced work on the remaining queue from approximately 48.9 to 28.9 person-hours, saving about 20.0 hours (41%). The study documents the model-selection process, provenance-aware file organization, verification procedure, observed errors, practical limitations, and opportunities for extending AI assistance beyond one category.

papers.title: Joint Transmit Power and Reflection Coefficient Optimization for Underlay Cognitive Radio Ambient Backscatter Communication
papers.abstract: The integration of cognitive radio (CR) technology with backscatter communication offers a promising solution for developing spectrum-efficient and low-power wireless networks. In this paper, we investigate the performance of an underlay cognitive radio ambient backscatter communication (CR-AmBC) system operating under primary network (PN) interference constraints. The objective is to maximize the performance of the CR-AmBC system while protecting the PN from interference. Differing from prior work, our formulation jointly accounts for: (i) interference from the PN on the CR receivers, (ii) interference from the backscatter device (BD) on the PN receiver, and (iii) imperfect successive interference cancellation (i-SIC) at the secondary destination. We propose a joint transmit power and reflection coefficient optimization framework that incorporates the minimum data rate requirements, the PN interference constraint, and i-SIC for decoding the BD signal. The nonconvex problem is decomposed into two subproblems solved via alternating optimization: (a) a closed-form expression for the feasible transmit power given a fixed reflection coefficient, and (b) an efficient one-dimensional search for the reflection coefficient. We prove that the power update is optimal, reducing the joint problem to a one-dimensional search, with monotone convergence and $\mathcal{O}(KN_\beta)$ complexity for $K$ iterations and $N_\beta$ search points. We present a comprehensive simulation-based performance evaluation and the results demonstrate that the proposed joint transmission power and reflection coefficient optimization provides an effective strategy to maximize the performance of the CR-AmBC system without violating the PN protection constraints.

papers.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_{\theta} = \smash{[ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]}$, for every fixed $\theta > 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $\sigma - 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + \theta})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(\sigma + \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Heirloom: Carrying a Phone's Personalization Across Base-Model Generations
papers.abstract: On-device language models can learn a user's preferences through adapters trained on private data. However, a base-model upgrade may change the layers or vocabulary, leaving the personal adapter incompatible. Replacing it with a non-personal adapter loses much of the personalization, while retraining requires retaining the user's labeled history. We present Heirloom, a system that transfers a personal adapter to a new base model on the phone without retaining labels. Heirloom uses the old personal model as a teacher, collecting its predictions on stored unlabeled inputs, vendor-provided prompts, or prompts generated by the new base. It then unloads the old base and trains an adapter for the new model to match those predictions, keeping only one base model in memory at a time. We evaluate Heirloom across three generation upgrades from two model families, an architecture-preserving refresh, and three personalization tasks. On movie tagging, migration from stored inputs maintains pre-upgrade accuracy and differs from labeled retraining by at most 1.7 percentage points across the three upgrades. On a phone's neural processing unit (NPU), a fixed-length migration for the 4B upgrade takes 38 minutes and consumes 20% of the battery end to end, making the stored-input setting feasible during overnight charging.

authors.name: Qingkai Dong
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
papers.abstract: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

authors.name: Ankit Arora
authors.institution: Manubhai Patel Dental College and Hospital

papers.title: A Symbolic-Neural Framework for Context-Aware Evidence Extraction from Mobile SQLite Databases
papers.abstract: Reliable forensic evidence extraction from mobile SQLite databases is challenging because application schemas are undocumented, evolve across releases, and differ across operating systems, making schema-specific methods brittle and difficult to maintain. We present SNEEF, a symbolic-neural framework for context-aware evidence extraction that encodes each SQLite row as context-value pairs with standardized provenance metadata and column labels, uses a language model to recognize nine forensic entity types, and binds each accepted entity to its source table and row through the PA-EEP provenance protocol. We evaluate SNEEF against examiner-verified ground truth from five corpora built from public Android and iOS device images, spanning multiple application versions. SNEEF achieves an F1 score of 0.967 for evidence entities extracted from SQLite row content, excluding application names, compared with 0.728 for a context-free configuration, with consistent gains across all corpora. We also introduce an Evidence Failure Mode taxonomy to characterize why extraction errors occur.

authors.name: Divyangkumar Patel
authors.institution: Shroff S.R. Rotary Institute of Chemical Technology

papers.title: Composable CAD: Sketch-to-CAD Program Synthesis in Parts
papers.abstract: Designers often build CAD models part by part, and may iterate on individual components throughout the design process. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can synthesize CAD programs from sketches, but generating parts independently does not ensure that they are composable: components may lose the intended proportions and alignments or fail to join correctly where they meet. We present Composable CAD, a framework that uses off-the-shelf VLMs to synthesize a design space of independently sampled, interchangeable component programs, where any selection composes into a coherent CAD model. We recover design constraints from the sketch and use them to construct a coarse proxy that establishes how the components are sized, aligned, and attached. We then generate each component independently from its proxy and apply a deterministic rewrite to ensure that neighboring components meet at their prescribed interfaces. We evaluate Composable CAD across a range of objects and sketch styles and conduct two user studies. Compared to VLM-only baselines, our method produces more detailed, composable designs.

authors.name: Yuanbo Li
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

authors.name: Sean Liu
authors.institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

papers.title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
papers.abstract: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious. An analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning while extracting the specification can do worse than no intervention, and instructing it to ignore them did not close the gap, so we exclude assistant turns structurally. On Lost in Conversation (replaying difficulty-selected instances), where AO is an oracle by construction, AC3 closes 55-84% of the gap between full context and AO on three of four tasks and exceeds AO on the fourth, and an LLM that faithfully summarizes the history does not reproduce the gain even with more compute. On real WildChat conversations, a GPT-5-mini judge prefers AC3's next turn over both full context and AO in every configuration of our main table, though this preference depends on the judge; on CollabLLM results are mixed. In stateful tool use (tau2-bench), AO collapses to 0% on every model; AC3 does not collapse, though it falls slightly behind full context. Detector studies show that Reset removes injected pollution but is not span-selective: the gain comes from rebuilding the specification.

papers.title: Precedent Labels and Facts Shift LLM Approval Decisions in Opposite Directions
papers.abstract: When a language model decides refund or claim requests under written policies, the system can show it similar past cases. Each past case has two parts: its facts and the decision recorded for it. We separate the two. A model sees a policy, a request and three past cases, and we change either the recorded decisions or the facts, keeping the request fixed. We select requests that are close calls: deciding without past cases, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash approved each in some of four tries and denied it in others. When the past cases are near-copies of the request (its facts with a few details changed), switching their recorded decisions from DENY to APPROVE raises approval by about 30 to 55 percentage points in DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on policies written for the study, and DeepSeek and Luna show the same on nine public policies paraphrased from real ones. The facts push the other way: shown without their recorded decisions, past cases whose facts support approval make these two models approve less often than past cases whose facts support denial. One reading is that the request looks weaker next to them. This push is not just a correction toward the right answer: in an additional DeepSeek analysis, it was of similar estimated size on requests that human annotators judged approvable and on those they judged deniable. In a separate DeepSeek run on the public policies, when the past cases are near-copies of a different request, switching their decisions moves approval by 9 points instead of 43, while facts that support approval still lower it by 22 points against facts that support denial. Systems that retrieve past decisions should test the two parts separately.

papers.title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
papers.abstract: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Geographic Multicast Routing in Cognitive Wireless Sensor Networks
papers.abstract: Energy consumption is a major design concern in wireless sensor networks. Cognitive radio provides opportunistic access to licensed spectrum, while multicast routing allows several destinations to share forwarding paths. In this paper, we propose two geographic multicast routing protocols for cognitive wireless sensor networks, CCast and PCast. CCast combines multicast-tree construction with a latency-oriented spectrum-selection metric. PCast uses a normalized link-power cost to select routes and can avoid regions where primary users occupy lower-frequency bands. Both protocols use local neighbor information and destination coordinates, without requiring a complete network-topology map. Simulations compare the proposed protocols with geographic multicast routing (GMP) and multiple unicast routing. In simulations, CCast and PCast reduce energy consumption by 21\% and 26\% relative to GMP, at the cost of longer per-destination routes and higher delivery delay.

papers.title: Model-Based Co-Clustering for Censored Data
papers.abstract: Co-clustering jointly partitions the rows and columns of a data matrix. Standard co-clustering methods for continuous data typically assume that entries are observed exactly. Matrices with censored entries, such as assay measurements below a detection limit, are therefore commonly completed by substitution or imputation before co-clustering. Since the completed values are treated as exact, the estimated block means and partitions depend on the completion rule. We propose the censored Gaussian latent block model (CGLBM), in which each censored entry contributes the probability of its reported interval. We establish identifiability under a known Type I censoring design. Approximate standard errors for the block means follow from the Fisher information under censoring. CGLBM is fitted by a generalized expectation--maximization algorithm, and its row and column class numbers are selected by a BIC approximation to the integrated classification likelihood. In simulation studies, boundary substitution and truncated normal imputation attenuate the contrasts between block means, whereas the partition recovery of multiple imputation drops the most under heavy censoring. CGLBM preserves the contrasts, and its partition recovery drops the least. The method is implemented in the R package CGLBM.

authors.name: Mincen Liu
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Adaptive Preference Elicitation in Preference Robust CPT-Based Shortfall
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the cumulative prospect theory (CPT)-based shortfall risk measure where the value (utility) function and the distortion (probability weighting) functions are ambiguous. We propose a worst-case CPT-based shortfall risk measure where the capital requirement is based on the worst-case value function and distortion functions from an ambiguity set constructed with user-specific information (e.g., preference between risky and certain lotteries) and well-known general information such as the S-shape of the value functions. When the underlying random loss is discretely distributed and parameters in pairs of lotteries remain undetermined, we demonstrate that the worst-case value function and the distortion functions have a piecewise linear structure. Based on this observation, we develop an adaptive preference elicitation approach extended from the well-known polyhedral method to simultaneously elicit the distortion functions and the positive and negative parts of the value function by solving a sequence of mixed-integer linear programs. Based on the elicited distortions, we design new queries to construct a feasible set of the holistic value functions. The proposed framework iteratively shrinks the ambiguity set through designed queries, yielding a computationally implementable robust CPT-based shortfall risk measure. To examine the in-sample and out-of-sample performance of the elicited CPT-based preference functions and the resulting preference robust shortfall risk measure, we conduct numerical experiments under an S-shaped value function and inverse S-shaped distortion functions and report the corresponding results.

papers.title: Reduced Cost Influence Functions for Predict-then-Optimize under Noisy Data
papers.abstract: Machine learning models deployed in decision-making pipelines, from vehicle routing to dynamic pricing to clinical decision support, must remain reliable in the face of low-quality training data. We study a predict-then-optimize setting in which an upstream model predicts the cost vector of a downstream linear program, with a large pool of noisy training data supplemented by a small curated set of clean data. We introduce Reduced Cost Influence Functions (RCIFs), which combine influence functions from robust statistics with the geometry of linear optimization to estimate how each training point shifts downstream decisions. Building on this, we propose a reweighting algorithm that uses RCIFs to downweight harmful training points and reduce downstream regret. Experiments on random linear programs and shortest-path problems show that our approach reduces regret, and accompanying theory characterizes properties of RCIFs and identifies regimes favorable to our method relative to baselines.

papers.title: Ranked but Not Stopped: Detecting Prompt-Injection Hijacks from Typed Decision Models' Output Probabilities
papers.abstract: Programs that use a language model as a classifier act on its most probable label. Text injected into the input can move that label to one the attacker chooses, a hijack. A monitor that does not know the attacker's label can read the model's own confidence and raise an alarm when the top probability is low. We test this monitor on AG News topic classification with five systems, three of them served through a provider's API. Pooled over five families of injected text, low confidence ranks hijacked answers above clean ones on four of the five systems (AUROC 0.86-0.90). Ranking them does not stop many of them. A threshold set so that at most 5% of clean answers to separate calibration articles alarm falls among the least confident clean answers, and every more confident hijack passes. In our main gate run on the three API-served systems, the monitor misses 51-70% of the hijacks caused by a plain injected note (per-system point estimates). When the note adds one handwritten sentence that calls the target certain and asks for full probability, the monitor misses 99-100% of the hijacks, although low confidence still ranks them at AUROC 0.70-0.79. Confidence monitors should be tested at their operating alarm rate, against attackers who claim certainty.

papers.title: When Neither Side Confirms: Destructive Tool Approval Across MCP Servers and Hosts
papers.abstract: LLM agents call tools that delete data or move money through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The specification asks for a human who can deny tool calls but splits the mechanism between the server, which can annotate a tool or ask the user through the host (elicitation), and the host application, which decides whether to prompt. We measure both sides from source code. In a 1,000-repository sample of the official MCP registry, an estimated 90% of destructive tools (95% CI 82-95) have no server-side confirmation, and most servers that elicit proceed, or fall back to a flag the model can set, when the host cannot relay the question. Of 41 popular open-source hosts and agent SDKs, 32 have no approval step by default, including 16 of 25 applications. Pairing sampled destructive tools flagged by a rule-based extractor with these applications, 60.7% of pairs have no enforced human approval by default. Through four agent SDKs, four of five low-cost models executed an injected deletion in 479 of 960 runs. If hosts prompted for every tool not annotated read-only or non-destructive, the unapproved share of these pairs would fall to 5.4%; universal elicitation support would leave 56.7%. Applications should therefore configure approval.

papers.title: Where Is a Prediction Model Miscalibrated, and for Whom? Local Audits in Outcome-Learned Pockets
papers.abstract: Overall and group-level averages, and ranking metrics such as the AUC, can hide sets of observations for which a prediction model systematically over- or under-predicts. We present an audit that asks where a model is miscalibrated (in which sets of similar observations it over- or under-predicts on average) and for whom (whether its average prediction error differs between demographic groups, such as by race or sex, within the same set). It groups observations into pockets using random-forest similarity, which weighs each feature by its importance for predicting the outcome, with a ridge-regression grouping alongside. Pockets are learned on one sample and tested on another, with simultaneous confidence intervals that allow for correlation within units such as hospitals; the audit needs only features, outcomes and fixed predictions. In 17 simulation scenarios with an error planted for one group, the combined audit located it better than the strongest alternative grouping in 15, with false-alarm rates near or below 5%; with a local error planted for everyone, it won in 12 of 15 scenarios at the smaller error size and lost when the error was unrelated to the outcome. In public synthetic data from the care-management algorithm studied by Obermeyer et al., it found no detectable overall error but under-prediction of illness in the sickest pockets and over-prediction elsewhere, and distinguished Black patients' concentration where the score under-predicted for everyone from a Black-White gap within pockets. For APACHE IVa, an exploratory analysis located its previously reported over-prediction of ICU mortality in a mostly ventilated pocket and a low-risk pocket, with none detected in a moderate-risk one. Two chest X-ray classifiers showed offsetting local errors behind no detectable overall error. Code: https://github.com/modenesi/pocket-audit

papers.title: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion at Test Time
papers.abstract: Pose-driven human video diffusion animates a person from a single reference image and a target pose sequence, yet it struggles to preserve identity, rendering the face and garments unfaithfully as the pose departs from it. Personalization is the standard remedy, but its supervision is missing: one image fixes identity at a single pose, while a multi-pose subject video cannot be assumed in practice. Instead, we synthesize the missing supervision. A domain-tuned, pose-conditioned generator produces pseudo-ground-truth frames at selected key poses. An inference-time reference-only sampler steers these candidates toward the subject and keeps the most identity-consistent. A per-subject low-rank adapter then trains on static clips of them, configured from the reference alone, with no subject video, ground truth, or labels. Although lower in fidelity, these synthetic frames supervise more effectively than real ones. Real frames as captured carry motion that erodes the temporal prior, while a static clip conveys appearance alone. On TikTok and UBC Fashion, the adapted model improves the base on every metric, inverts the identity-versus-motion trade-off, and matches or surpasses adaptation on five real frames despite using none. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/SadmanPinon/one-image-is-enough.

papers.title: Nested MCMC for Uncertainty Propagation in Spatial Modeling of Temporal Long-Memory in Resting-State fMRI
papers.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) signals exhibit long-range temporal dependence, characterized by a slow power-law decay of autocorrelation. This scale-free temporal structure, quantified by the long-memory (LM) parameter, has been associated with brain function and age-related changes in neural dynamics. Investigating spatial variation in cortical LM and its association with demographic and clinical covariates requires methods that account for spatial dependence and propagate uncertainty in LM estimation into population-level inference. We develop a two-stage spatial Bayesian framework that incorporates a conditional autoregressive (CAR) prior to model dependence among neighbouring cortical vertices and a nested Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) strategy to propagate uncertainty from subject-specific LM estimation into regression inference. A composite-basis representation enables computationally feasible population-level inference over the high-dimensional cortical surface. In simulation studies, the CAR prior substantially improved subject-level LM estimation accuracy, while CAR-based approaches reduced population-level estimation error and generally improved detection of localized group effects relative to independent estimation. Nested MCMC produced posterior mean estimates comparable to those of CAR plug-in, while yielding slightly wider credible intervals that account for uncertainty in subject-level LM estimation. Application to HCP-Aging resting-state fMRI data identified significant negative associations between age and LM in localized cortical regions, particularly in frontal and precentral areas. These findings demonstrate the benefits of spatial modeling for cortical LM estimation and uncertainty propagation for population-level Bayesian inference.

papers.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
papers.abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

papers.title: A nearly tight bound on the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate
papers.abstract: A graph is even-degenerate if we can order its vertices as $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that the number of edges from $v_i$ to $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$ is even for all $i>2$. We show that the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate is $e^{-\Omega(n/\log\log n)}$, which is only a factor of $\log\log n$ away, in the exponent, from the trivial lower bound $2^{-O(n)}$.

papers.title: Tilted Convexity and an Exact Offline-Online Separation
papers.abstract:
Convexity has three equivalent descriptions: support by affine functions, monotonicity of the subdifferential, and increasing secant slopes. We weaken all three by one distortion with parameter $\gamma\in(0,1]$, which multiplies positive changes by $\gamma$ and divides negative ones by $\gamma$. The resulting classes are the convex functions at $\gamma=1$ and, for $\gamma<1$, are distinct and nested, with the parameter dropping by at most a square along the chain. For proper lower semicontinuous functions in these classes, the effective domain is convex, local minimizers are global, and the function is locally Lipschitz on the relative interior of its domain.
  The classes separate offline from online optimization over compact convex sets with efficient projection, with access to function values and bounded support vectors. A smooth member of any class can be minimized to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$ with $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ first-order queries and projections. Online, with nonpositive losses and $\alpha$-regret measured against $\alpha$ times the best fixed point, a polynomial-time algorithm achieves $\gamma$-regret $O(\sqrt T)$ on the largest class. For every fixed, effectively specified $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and every $\alpha\in(\gamma,1]$, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm has sublinear expected $\alpha$-regret unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, already for smooth concave polynomial losses in the smallest class, each minimized by one linear optimization. Thus, unless $\mathbf{NP}=\mathbf{RP}$, $\gamma$ is the exact online coefficient of each class, while the offline coefficient is one.

papers.title: Spatial structure promotes coexistence, resilience, and synergy in microbial communities
papers.abstract: Microbial communities are highly complex systems with a tremendous number of interactions. They thrive in vastly different environments, from the human body to soil and marine ecosystems, and show remarkable properties such as coexistence, diversity, and resilience. Additionally, they are almost always spatially structured. However, the role of space in shaping microbial communities remains poorly understood, in part because explicitly modeling space substantially increases model complexity and limits further exploration of its effects across different settings. Here, we present a minimal theoretical model that incorporates spatial structure into a consumer-resource framework through local and global nutrient consumption. Using this model, we explore the effect of spatial structure on several important properties of microbial communities. We find that spatial structure promotes coexistence under nutrient limitation, increases community resilience to environmental fluctuations, and allows communities to benefit synergistically from poor nutrients. We then extend the model to make spatial structure adaptive, allowing species to become more isolated when competition threatens their presence. Our results show that moderate spatial adaptation promotes coexistence, while weak and strong adaptation do not. Interestingly, strong spatial adaptation can substantially increase community coexistence under environmental fluctuations, while not necessarily promoting coexistence in the absence of fluctuations. Together, our results provide a simple framework for exploring how spatial structure shapes microbial community assembly, dynamics, and response to fluctuating environments.

papers.title: What Does a Safety Label Measure? Auditing Situational-Safety Benchmarks for Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: Situational-safety benchmarks label each scene SAFE or UNSAFE and score a multimodal large language model (MLLM) against that label, usually by judging its free-form answer, and these scores guide deployment. We ask what such a label measures. A label score can come from the scene, the request or the benchmark's own files. We propose the Benchmark Card, seven measured fields that tell them apart, and fill it for six benchmarks. Only MSSBench chat leaks the label through its image files: image size alone reaches 82.3% accuracy, matching or beating six of seven commercial models. Elsewhere the signal outside the scene comes from design. In MOSSBench the item partition fixes the label, and on HoliSafe the request alone ranks pairs about as well as the scene. On our corrected chat split, the size rule falls to chance. We then introduce the Spot-Stop decomposition, which compares ranking with labelling on pairs of a safe and an unsafe scene. It splits the gap above a label-swap null into three parts: a threshold part, overlap between safe and unsafe scores, and order that holds only within a pair. Most of fourteen open MLLMs rank better than they label, beyond what their AUROC predicts. On chat, one shared threshold repairs a third to a half of the excess, and label-free recentering recovers it on balanced batches. Recentering on unlabelled scenes of the same situation improves ranking on VSCBench for 13 of 14 models.

papers.title: From Radiotherapy Dataset to Cherenkov Dose Map: A Digital Linac Monte Carlo Simulation Pipeline
papers.abstract: Background: Cherenkov-based radiotherapy monitoring depends on the relationship between dose and locally generated Cherenkov photons, before optical transport and detection. Purpose: To develop a DICOM RT-driven Geant4 digital linac Monte Carlo framework that scores dose and Cherenkov creation together and to evaluate their spatial correspondence. Methods: The framework converts DICOM CT, structure, plan, and dose objects into beam-delivery states and scores energy deposition and Cherenkov photon creation on a common 2.5-mm isotropic grid in a water-equivalent phantom. Static fields, different beam qualities, and a two-arc VMAT plan were tested. Monte Carlo dose was compared with TPS RTDOSE from Acuros XB and AAA; dose-Cherenkov associations and spatial agreement were assessed at voxel, plane, and profile levels. Results: Full-volume 3D dose gamma passing rates (3%/3 mm, 10% threshold) were 97.05%-98.86% for Acuros XB-referenced field-size and beam-quality cases (97.47% with AAA) and 97.84% for VMAT. Cherenkov creation correlated strongly with dose, with voxel $r^2 \geq 0.9890$ and projection/profile $r^2 \geq 0.9942$ in all cases. Dose-Cherenkov 3D gamma passing rates were 97.97%-99.16% for $10\times10$ 6X, 10X, and 15X fields and 96.59% for VMAT, but fell to 71.22% for $5\times5$ fields and 32.82% for 6FFF. Deviations were most apparent near small-field edges and along depth for 6FFF. Conclusions: In a homogeneous water phantom, local Cherenkov creation broadly tracks local dose but shows systematic differences at beam edges and with FFF beam quality. This framework supports future studies of optical transport and surface-based Cherenkov dosimetry.

papers.title: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. At student-generated prefixes, we form a four-observation matrix by treating the student and teacher as both candidate sources and evaluators. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/OC-OPD.

papers.title: Better Answers, Weaker Evidence Control: Evidence Bypass in On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) can improve answer accuracy while weakening responsiveness to supporting evidence. We investigate this separation in scientific-document question answering through matched document interventions that change the supported answer while preserving the question and unrelated context. We identify evidence bypass: a student retains an originally correct answer after the document changes to support a different one. On QASPER with a Qwen3-4B student, standard OPD raises original-document accuracy by 3.4 percentage points, lowers counterfactual accuracy by 5.3 points, and increases bypass by 15.7 points; the same directional pattern appears on PeerQA. Controlled perturbations localize the shift to answer-critical evidence, and bypass grows with the student's pre-distillation closed-book preference for the original answer. A factorized study of teacher targets, privileged information, divergence, and supervision density finds that explicitly supplying the teacher with annotated answer-critical spans yields the largest joint improvement in evidence response and claim support. These findings motivate Evidence-Paired OPD (EP-OPD), which combines on-policy supervision on matched documents supporting different answers to the same question with an answer-level margin that favors each document's supported answer over its paired alternative. Across both datasets and two student sizes, EP-OPD recovers 54-66% of standard OPD's counterfactual-accuracy loss while preserving 80-85% of its original-document accuracy gain. Our results establish evidence responsiveness as a distinct training and evaluation target alongside answer accuracy. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/RuoranXu/EP-OPD.

papers.title: Scaling Makes It Possible: How Large Models Master Impossible Languages
papers.abstract: While language models (LMs) excel in natural language tasks, their ability to learn impossible languages--those that violate the structural, cognitive, or logical constraints that make human languages learnable and functional--remains debatable. This controversy is further fueled by a divide between linguistic theorists and empirical researchers working with small-scale LMs. To address this controversy, we introduce semantic coherence. This concept measures how effectively semantic information is expressed in language structures and examines the learning capabilities of LMs across multiple scales. By fine-tuning billion-parameter LMs on impossible language samples, we demonstrate that larger LMs achieve similar performance on impossible and possible languages, whereas million-parameter LMs exhibit significant degradation when trained on impossible languages. This performance gap widens as semantic complexity increases. We further show that scaling up the LM size fundamentally shifts the learning focus from grammatical rules to semantic understanding, with billion-scale LMs exhibiting a threefold reduction in sensitivity to low-level linguistic perturbations while maintaining stable performance under high-level semantic perturbations.

papers.title: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, and recent methods incorporate curvature-aware strategies. However, in the high-dimensional parameter space of LLMs, these methods inherently suffer from exploding gradient variance and prohibitive costs. Conversely, confining updates to a low-dimensional subspace reduces variance but discards critical high-dimensional information, degrading performance. This creates a fundamental dilemma: full-space optimization is informative but has high variance, while subspace optimization has low variance but loses information. To break this trade-off, we propose ENGINE (Endogenous Variational MultiScale). Inspired by computational mechanics, we adapt static Variational MultiScale (VMS) theory to dynamic optimization, treating low- and high-dimensional spaces as resolved coarse and unresolved fine scales. Through a multigrid-style V-cycle, ENGINE alternates between spaces, dynamically probing fine-grained information in the high-dimensional space and injecting it to correct the efficient low-dimensional sampling process. Under appropriate assumptions, statistical analysis characterizes variance reduction and correction of curvature-induced bias, and convergence analysis establishes a stationarity bound for the corrected coarse updates. Evaluations on standard LLM benchmarks show that ENGINE achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, achieving up to a $2.61\times$ speed-up in forward passes with zero additional peak memory overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/AI4Science-WestlakeU/ENGINE.

papers.title: ElectroChemLLM: A Multimodal LLM Pipeline for High-Fidelity Electrochemical Informatics
papers.abstract: Electrochemistry is central to solving many modern-day challenges, including energy storage systems for a sustainable future, and its advancement relies heavily on the data from past findings. Existing automated pipelines are limited by text-only architectures, context fragmentation, and numerical hallucinations - collectively preventing accurate, large-scale curation of property databases. We introduce ElectrochemLLM, a multimodal information extraction pipeline that jointly identifies structured electrochemical records encompassing electrolyte compositions, electrode materials, cell configurations, and their measured physicochemical properties from unstructured scientific PDFs at scale. By combining hybrid document parsing with vision-capable LLM orchestration, the pipeline extracts verifiable, structured data across text, tables, and figures. Evaluated on the battery-electrolyte subset of our manually annotated benchmark of 232 papers, ElectrochemLLM achieves an F-1 score of 0.97, and has been applied to curate ElectroChemDB, a structured database spanning 15,000 electrochemical research articles. We demonstrate the utility of this resource by training machine learning models for electrolyte property prediction, illustrating a complete pathway from unstructured literature to predictive materials discovery.

papers.title: An Incidence-Based Edge-Averaged Method for Convection-Diffusion Problems on Polytopal Meshes
papers.abstract: We develop an incidence-based edge-averaged method for scalar convection-diffusion problems on convex polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimensions. The proposed method extends the classical edge-averaged finite-element scheme through a graph-theoretic formulation based on vertex-edge incidence matrices. We first establish this formulation on simplices in arbitrary dimensions and then extend it to convex polytopes by introducing complementary edges and generalized barycentric coordinates. A key ingredient is a matrix identity that relates the generalized Whitney edge mass matrix to a diagonal representation of the Poisson stiffness matrix, enabling an exponentially-fitted discretization expressed entirely in terms of nodal values and edge weights. We prove that the resulting stiffness matrix is a nonsingular $M$-matrix under suitable positivity and connectivity conditions, ensuring monotonicity and the discrete maximum principle. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional simplicial and nonsimplicial meshes demonstrate first-order convergence in the $H^1$ semi-norm and stable, nonoscillatory solutions in convection-dominated regimes.

papers.title: Generative Modeling with Continuous Flows: Sample Complexity of Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion-based generative modeling, offering a continuous-time ordinary differential equation formulation with fast sampling and a simple regression-based training objective. Despite its empirical success, some theoretical analyses idealize the learning procedure by assuming that the velocity field is obtained by exact empirical risk minimization. This assumption does not reflect the practical finite-dataset setting, where the empirical flow-matching loss is only approximately minimized by a finite number of stochastic-gradient updates. We develop an empirical-risk-minimizer-free analysis for flow matching that explicitly accounts for both finite-sample statistical error and finite-time empirical optimization error. Our analysis considers a finite dataset of \(N\) flow-matching samples and a learned parameter \(\theta_T\) obtained after \(T\) stochastic gradient updates on the empirical objective. Under regularity assumptions on the interpolation path, sub-exponential source and target distributions, approximation by a bounded-parameter smooth neural velocity class, empirical-loss optimization, and uniform flow stability, we prove a guarantee that holds with high probability over the finite training dataset and in expectation over the stochastic-gradient randomness. The resulting bound separates approximation error, statistical error from the finite dataset, tail error from unbounded source and target distributions, and empirical optimization error from approximate minimization of the finite-sample objective.

papers.title: Dependable Agents Need Hard and Fuzzy Rules
papers.abstract: Language models let software read requests in ordinary language, but they keep rules as people do: usually, and less so under pressure. Conventional code keeps rules exactly, but it cannot read a request. We argue that dependable agents need both, because the two kinds of rule cover overlapping and unequal regions of what an agent might do. Code holds the limits that can be stated exactly. Learned fuzzy rules cover the judgment that cannot. We test the hard layer in three domains, purchasing, delegation of authority and data access, on 1,340 episodes written by authors outside our team. Models left to decide for themselves executed unauthorized actions in up to 151 of 340 purchasing episodes and 269 of 470 delegation episodes, and the strongest model breached in every condition. A hard guard between proposal and action executed none, and an exhaustive search of 183,204 proposals agreed. In a further test, where an outsider wrote the owner's rules and a program mapped them to the guard, two episodes breached at a boundary we had written down in advance. We then test the pair. Concept Programming instills a named rule in a model and measures its errors on wording it never saw. A small model taught four judgment rules this way flagged 95 of 96 rule-breaking purchases that no exact rule can see, and 4 of 108 legitimate requests. Placed in front of the guard, it left 1 of 192 rule-breaking requests unstopped, where the guard alone left 77 and 70, and the guard still held every exact limit. A prompted frontier model did about as well, so the claim is that a small taught rule can do the job, not that it does it better.

papers.title: Compliance-Shifting Elastogranular Shells
papers.abstract: Shells and grains separately exhibit complex nonlinear behavior when confined - shells buckle and snap, while grains transition from fluid-like to solid-like. When coupled, elastogranular structures have the ability to display a remarkable variety of mechanical behaviors. Gere we created an elastogranular shell where spherical grains are sandwiched between two thin, elastic shells. By evacuating the air enclosed by the two layers, we can tune the stiffness of the elastogranular shell and alter its critical buckling load. Introducing controlled vacancy defects in the arrangement of the grains allows us to more finely tune critical buckling parameters, as the shell must balance the combined effects of defect size and resultant granular packing density. Defects in the jammed granular layer have a counterintuitive effect on the shell's buckling load, as they can stiffen the shell away from the defect. With an empirically determined scaling model, we established how the shell and grains distribute load and create a compliance-shifting structure with a tunable buckling load.

papers.title: Uniqueness of SRB measures for stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: For a dissipation stochastic differential equation (abbreviated as SDE), exponential ergodicity has been investigated a lot in a wide range of settings. In this paper, we prove that the Markovian measure $\mu$ determined by the unique stationary measure is also the unique invariant measure which satisfies the entropy formula. Consequently, the existence of an SRB measure is completely determined by the sign of the sample top Lyapunov exponent of $\mu$: if $\chi_\mu^1>0$, then $\mu$ is the unique SRB measure, whereas if $\chi_\mu^1\leq0$, then the SDE admits no SRB measure. As an application, we establish a dichotomy of SRB measures for the 2D additive-noise stochastic Hopf normal form within a shear parameter domain.

papers.title: The Brin-Katok local entropy formula for non-compact random dynamical systems and an application
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for $C^1$ random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for $C^2$ random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. Furthermore, we also construct a counterexample showing that the integrability condition above cannot in general be omitted.

papers.title: ECGJev: Question-Conditioned Option Scoring for 12-Lead ECG Interpretation
papers.abstract: Clinical interpretation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) often requires answering targeted diagnostic questions with clear, quantifiable decisions. We introduce ECGJev, the first ECG framework built on a decision decoder, a pretrained language model trained to return a probability for every listed option. A question-conditioned bridge compresses frozen waveform and spectrogram features into 16 ECG tokens, and a two-stage procedure adapts the bridge and low-rank adapters on the decoder's native option readout using diagnostic labels alone, scoring all options for a question in one forward pass. Evaluated across four ECG benchmarks, ECGJev achieves the highest macro-F1 on CPSC2018 (80.46%), PTB-XL (71.68%) and Chapman (96.86%), and generalizes competitively to the small-sample PTB cohort. Concept probes and perturbation analyses further show that its predictions rely directly on the ECG input, remain stable under option-order and wording variations, and transfer zero-shot to unseen waveform concepts. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhuoyuanli-lab/ECGJev.

papers.title: Primary components and large prime factors of cyclotomic values
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi_r(a,b)$ denote the homogeneous cyclotomic value. For sufficiently large $A$, uniformly for $1/2\leq B\leq A$, $r\geq3$ and $Z\geq2$, the number of coprime pairs in $(A,2A]\times(B,2B]$ whose greatest prime factor $P(\Phi_r(a,b))$ is at most $Z$ is $O(AB/\varphi(r)+\sqrt{r/\varphi(r)}\,\pi(Z;r,1))$, where $\pi(Z;r,1)$ counts primes at most $Z$ congruent to $1$ modulo $r$. If $n=n(A)\to\infty$ through positive integers and $1\leq H(A)=o(\log A)$, then $P(a^{2^n}+1)>2^nAH(A)$ for almost all $a\in(A,2A]$, and $P(a^{2^n}+b^{2^n})>2^nA^2H(A)$ for almost all coprime pairs in $(A,2A]^2$, with no further restriction on $n$. For every fixed $\alpha>0$ and every $r\geq A^\alpha$, pairwise distinct primitive prime divisors of $\Phi_r(a)$ can be selected for all but $O_\alpha(A^{1-c_\alpha})$ bases in $(A,2A]$, where $c_\alpha>0$. For coprime positive integers $a,b$ with $\max(a,b)\geq2$ and $r\geq3$, put $C=\Phi_r(a,b)$ and $S=\varphi(r)^2\log\max(a,b)$. Uniformly as $S\to\infty$, $\max_{p\mid C}p^{v_p(C)}\geq(5/16-o(1))S$. For every positive function $h(S)\to\infty$, $\sum_{p\mid C,\;p^{v_p(C)}>S/h(S)}v_p(C)\log p =(1-o(1))\log C$ uniformly in the same limit.

papers.title: Complete Bernstein functions and real powers of P-matrices
papers.abstract: We classify the nonzero complete Bernstein functions whose matrix functions preserve every real P-matrix in every order. They are precisely $f(z)=a+bz$, with $a,b\ge0$ and $a+b>0$, and $f(z)=a+cz/(z+s)$, with $a\ge0$ and $c,s>0$. For each fixed order $n\ge4$, the preservers vanishing at zero are exactly $cz$ and $cz/(z+s)$; every other such function admits a strictly totally positive counterexample. For a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $(0,\infty)$, put $g(z)=\int z/(z+s)\,\mu(ds)$ and $M_t=\int s^t\,\mu(ds)$. In every fixed order $n\ge4$, a finite constant shift restores preservation on all real P-matrices if and only if $M_{r_n}$ and $M_{-r_n}$ are finite, where $r_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$. Every $a>c_n\sqrt{M_{r_n}M_{-r_n}}$ is sufficient, with $c_n$ depending only on $n$. A complete Bernstein function vanishing at zero admits a possibly different repairing constant in every order exactly when it is linear, or is a pure kernel mixture with all positive and negative integer moments finite. For principal real powers, the preserving exponents are $\mathbb R$ in order one, $[-1,1]$ in orders two and three, and $\{-1,0,1\}$ in every higher order. An explicit rational determinant-one totally positive family gives negative principal minors uniformly on prescribed compact subsets of $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$.

papers.title: Toward Contrast-Free Breast MRI: Improving Cancer Detection With Virtual Contrast Enhanced Imaging
papers.abstract: Although contrast-enhanced (CE) breast MRI is an important tool for cancer detection, intravenous gadolinium administration introduces additional considerations for patients and clinical workflows. AI based virtual contrast enhanced (VCE) MRI could help identify patients for whom acquired CE imaging may be avoidable without compromising diagnostic performance. We developed a framework that combines non contrast (NC) and VCE MRI predictions for cancer detection. On the held-out test set, cancer detection using NC MRI alone achieved an AUROC of 0.865. Combining the predictions from NC and VCE MRI improved AUROC to 0.901. Building on this complementary predictive value, we evaluated patient-level routing to progressively replace acquired CE examinations with the NC plus VCE pathway, prioritizing patients with the most confident NC predictions. This simulation suggests that diagnostic performance can be largely preserved while limiting acquired CE imaging to approximately 40% of patients. Together, these findings demonstrate the complementary value of VCE MRI and suggest its potential to support selective contrast use in breast cancer screening.

papers.title: CAPER: Circuit-Aware Parameter-Efficient Reasoning in LLMs for Analog Verification
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate analog circuits, yet every netlist must also be verified. We propose LLMs as verification assistants for analog circuits that flag unmet specifications and reliability issues that appear under process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variation. These issues emerge from how circuit stages combine, a structure that generic parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods such as LoRA do not capture. To this end, we introduce CAPER, a circuit-aware PEFT method that adds a small branch alongside LoRA to read each stage's properties from the LLM and combine them from the relevant stages. In deciding whether a feedback loop is negative, LoRA and a high-rank adapter stay at chance, whereas CAPER answers every test case correctly. For comparator latches, where 11 of 90 LLM-written designs that work under nominal conditions fail under PVT variation, CAPER likewise learns to flag such latent failures, while generic adapters stay near chance. These results show that adding circuit knowledge to PEFT makes such analog verification checks learnable through fine-tuning.

papers.title: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
papers.abstract: Existing Graphical User Interface (GUI) benchmarks predominantly rely on precise and stateless user instructions. In everyday usage, however, instructions are often \emph{vague and history-dependent}: users omit the exact details of their past operations because they no longer remember them, leaving the agent to recover the missing context from long and noisy interaction histories. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce \textbf{MemU-Bench}, a mobile benchmark of \textbf{118 vague tasks} grounded in 29 long-horizon user trajectories, where agents must distill raw interaction streams into memory and retrieve the missing context on demand, with task outcomes verified against serialized application databases. Alongside Success Rate, we incorporate Interaction Efficiency (IE) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) to expose agents that succeed by exhaustively searching across different applications rather than by \emph{genuinely recalling} the history. Evaluations show that without user history, state-of-the-art systems struggle under such ambiguity: the best-performing Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves an SPL of only 16.4\%, and end-to-end GUI agents fall below 5\%. To address this, we further propose \textbf{AppMem}, a training-free framework that distills user history into a \emph{structured, app-centric} memory bank, tracks interrupted intents across application switches, and selectively retrieves relevant memories via target-app inference. AppMem raises the SPL of GPT-5.5 from 15.7\% to 66.9\% (\textbf{+51.2\%}), outperforms a naive summary baseline by 9.3\%, and delivers consistent gains across evaluated backbones.

papers.title: TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) accelerators for edge inference must meet tight energy, latency, and area (EDP) constraints, and their optimal hardware architecture and dataflow configuration is typically identified through design space exploration (DSE). However, on-chip memory technology including cell type, bank organization, and process node, is rarely treated as a first-class citizen in DSE. For example, increasing memory capacity can reduce memory accesses through greater data reuse, but at the cost of higher area and access energy, thereby limiting the compute units budget. Consequently, memory technology can fundamentally shift the optimal accelerator architecture for a given area and EDP budget. Existing machine learning (ML)-based DSE methods require repeating simulation, data generation, and model training for each new memory technology. We present TADA, a memory technology-aware DNN accelerator performance and energy estimator that predicts system latency and energy for a given workload, hardware configuration, and memory technology. TADA is trained on a synthetic dataset that generalizes across memory technologies. The dataset spans current and future technology trends while enforcing physics-based guardrails to preserve realistic area-energy trade-offs. Each memory technology is represented by a technology signature, a vector of read energy, write energy, and storage capacity across a range of areas, provided as input alongside the workload and hardware configuration. Across 21 unseen technology curves spanning SRAM, STTRAM, ReRAM, PCM, FeFET, eDRAM, and CTT, TADA predicts system energy and latency with 1.5-4.4% and 0.7-1.2% mean absolute percentage error, respectively. In three pairwise case studies, it matches the simulator-selected memory technology at 98.7-100% of area budgets, with a mean EDP loss of at most 0.21%, while achieving over 10^4x higher evaluation throughput.

papers.title: Unpacking the process of watching a 360-degree video: How physiological responses and head rotation relate to affective and cognitive outcomes
papers.abstract: A defining feature of 360-degree video is that the perceptual experience is actively constructed. As viewers turn their heads, shift their gaze, and encounter changing visuals, their perceptual experience is not predetermined, but rather emerges through ongoing exploration. Yet, it is unclear how the process of watching immersive videos unfolds, and how it is related to psychological and physiological outcomes. We present a large-scale study (N=200) in which participants experienced one of 10 pieces of 360-degree videos in virtual reality. Results showed that greater head rotation was associated with greater valence, higher attention focus, longer length of subjective review, and lower simulator sickness; greater pupil dilation was associated with lower valence, lower review ratings, and greater use of negative tone in written reviews. A mediation analysis revealed that participants who rotated their heads more experienced greater frame-to-frame pixel-level perceptual changes in their field of view, which in turn resulted in greater valence and lower simulator sickness. Moreover, participants tended to rotate their heads toward field of view regions with greater perceptual movement, while directing their eye gaze toward less perceptually dynamic areas within that view. We outline theoretical and practical contributions for designing 360-degree content and predicting experiential outcomes.

papers.title: OmniMechanism Design for Human-AI Collaboration with Impressionable Minds
papers.abstract: As AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, effectively integrating human expertise with AI outputs is critical for reliable decision-making. A substantial body of theoretical work studies optimal mechanisms for human-AI collaboration (HAC), focusing on when to involve humans and how to combine their expertise with AI predictions. However, these approaches largely overlook a key factor highlighted by empirical evidence: human judgments are impressionable and can vary depending on how AI outputs are presented. For example, when AI systems defer decisions to humans, revealing or withholding the AI prediction can significantly influence human judgments. Moreover, existing work neglects deployment-time variability, where conditions, particularly the cost of eliciting human input, may differ substantially from those observed during training. To address these challenges, we introduce a rigorous and theoretically grounded framework for human-AI collaboration, termed collaborative omnimechanism design, based on a novel and computationally efficient contextual bandit variant of boosting for outcome indistinguishability. In particular, we reduce a calibration-type outcome indistinguishability condition to weighted calibration, providing a novel time-efficiency result, bypassing the high-dimension curse induced by complicated collaboration methods and outcome space. Our framework provides a principled characterization of human impressionability and introduces a unified optimization scheme that enables robust and adaptable decision-making across diverse query costs and evaluation objectives without retraining. We evaluate the framework in three HAC settings, examining adaptation to query costs and prediction objectives without retraining, and show that its induced policies perform comparably to or better than the evaluated baselines.

papers.title: Time-Specific Multinomial Logistic Regression for Competing Risks
papers.abstract: Motivated by the project on premature menopause among childhood cancer survivors in the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (CCSS), we develop methods for estimating time-specific factor effects using doubly censored event time data with competing risks. We begin with fitting separate binary logistic regression models for different causes. However, the approach does not ensure the sum of the resulting estimated cumulative incidence rates remains bounded by one. To overcome this limitation, we consider a multinomial logistic regression formulation to jointly model all cause-specific risks. Two inverse-probability-of-censoring-weight (IPCW) based estimating functions are proposed accordingly. To handle the estimation instability caused by data separation, we incorporate the Firth-type penalization in those estimating functions to obtain more stable coefficient estimators. The sandwich variance estimator is applied to estimate the standard errors. A weighted quasi-likelihood information criterion, paired with a backward elimination, is further adapted to the proposed estimating functions for selecting covariates at a given age. Simulation studies are conducted to examine the proposed approaches regarding consistency, efficiency, and robustness of the estimators. The Firth correction substantially reduces the bias induced by separation and provides valid standard error estimation. We illustrate the proposed approach with the CCSS data viewing premature ovarian insufficiency and surgical premature menopause as the two potential causes of the primary event, premature menopause. The data analysis reveals that the effects of the cancer treatment-related covariates are significant on premature ovarian insufficiency but not on surgical premature menopause. The variable selection procedure, illustrated on an extended covariate set, yields estimated risks close to those under the full model.

papers.title: Movement based social interactions with label uncertainty
papers.abstract: Drone-based imagery provides high resolution data for tracking wildlife populations. However, monitoring marine mammals like cetaceans is challenging because individuals frequently submerge into water or move out of the drone's field of view, resulting in disconnected trajectories due to uncertain identities. Existing social movement models assume individual identities are known, which is often only true when data come from physical tracking devices like GPS collars. To address this limitation, we propose a Bayesian hierarchical state-space model that treats the identities associated with observed locations as unknown random variables. This allows us to jointly estimate individual movement parameters while propagating the uncertainty about identity. We apply our framework to drone-measured movement data from Risso's dolphins (Grampus griseus) to estimate the effects of sonar exposure on the dolphins' movement behavior. Our proposed method offers a solution for analyzing collective animal behavior when continuous tracking of every individual is challenging.

papers.title: The First-Order Value of Free Covariates in Budgeted Risk Monitoring
papers.abstract: A deployed model sees its inputs for free, but checking whether its risk has risen requires costly labels. We study how to spend a label budget so that a risk increase is detected quickly while false alarms stay controlled, including under input shifts that keep the risk below a safety threshold $\tau$. Let $A$ be the false-alarm control scale and $h(r)=\mathrm{kl}(r,\tau)$ the Bernoulli KL divergence between the changed risk $r$ and $\tau$. At label rate $b=c/\log A$, we prove that every rule that chooses requests from its own label history has worst-case (Lorden) delay at least $(1/h(r)+1/c)\log A$ to first order: besides collecting evidence, it must wait for its next label. The bound needs only a label budget on one finite stretch of safe source data and false-alarm control over an initial window; a bound on the average time to false alarm does not suffice. When a harmful change also shifts the inputs, a rule that lets the inputs trigger labeling attains delay $\log A/h(r)$ to first order on a fixed Gaussian model, so free covariates save at least $1/b$ rounds. A hybrid rule adds a label-history fallback for risk changes that leave the inputs unchanged. Synthetic experiments and two ACS tasks, with strengthened label-only baselines, show the predicted pattern. The covariate trigger has a cost: because its budget is calibrated on the source, a benign input shift can make it request nearly every label.

papers.title: Price is Only the Symptom: Understanding and Analyzing Economic-State Manipulation Vulnerabilities in DeFi
papers.abstract: Economic-state manipulation has emerged as a significant security threat to decentralized finance (DeFi), causing substantial financial losses. Existing studies predominantly characterize these attacks as price manipulation, focusing on observable price distortions while overlooking underlying violations of economic-state integrity. We conduct a comprehensive empirical study of Economic-State Manipulation (ESM) vulnerabilities in DeFi. We first curate a diverse dataset comprising 276 real-world attacks and 91 Code4rena audit findings. Based on these cases, we develop a cause-oriented taxonomy comprising four primary categories and eleven subcategories. Our analysis reveals that ESM vulnerabilities extend beyond conventional price manipulation, frequently involving violations of protocol-internal accounting, AMM state consistency, and execution-time constraints. We further investigate the evaluation datasets of six existing studies and find that, although they cover 6-10 vulnerability subcategories, their distributions remain dominated by limited manipulation mechanisms. Furthermore, we systematically evaluate seven representative detection approaches on our dataset. Our results reveal limited coverage, with the best-performing approach identifying only 50.4% of real-world attacks. Through an analysis of false negatives and false positives, we identify fundamental limitations arising from reliance on predefined attack patterns, insufficient reasoning about economic-state semantics, and incomplete exploitability validation. These findings provide empirical insights for developing more generalizable ESM vulnerability detection techniques.

papers.title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
papers.abstract: Existing studies of vulnerable pre-installed Android apps identify dangerous behavior by checking whether an app invokes an API from a predefined set of security-sensitive APIs. These sets usually exclude generic APIs to avoid false positives; unfortunately, this misses a class of vulnerabilities in which a generic API, such as a database read, appears benign in general but becomes security-sensitive when operating on protected data, yet is left without sufficient access control. While this class of vulnerabilities appears addressable via access control analysis, existing studies focus only on the presence of checks, not on whether those checks enforce sufficient protection for the operation at a given callsite. In this work, we propose Callix, which first assesses callsite sensitivity by jointly analyzing the invoked API functionality and the data involved in the operation, then recovers each security check on the execution path as an explicit security property, and finally introduces the notion of restriction context to decide whether these checks are sufficient for the identified sensitive operation. We evaluated Callix on 1,750 distinct pre-installed apps from the 10 top-tier Android vendors as of 2025. In total, Callix discovered 819 vulnerable paths across these vendors, 42.1% of which allow reading or modifying private user data through generic database operations. Manual validation of a random 60% sample shows a precision of 95.1%. Many of our findings have been confirmed and rewarded through vendor bug bounty programs.
