papers.title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
papers.abstract:
We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=\lambda\Psi_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(\Psi_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(\lambda\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_\delta(\lambda+W/\lambda)\leq T\leq \lambda^{1+\kappa_d^{\rm BA}-\delta}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(\kappa_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(\lambda^3+\lambda W)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asymp\lambda^2\) between \(\lambda^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda WT}\).
  The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.

papers.title: Semantic Interoperability in Federated Digital Twin Systems: A Systematic Review Through the Levels of Conceptual Interoperability Model
papers.abstract: When two companies connect their digital twins, software models of their plants kept up to date with live data, each twin must translate the other's data into its own terms, and that translation rule, called a mapping, can stop being correct when one company changes the meaning of its data without telling the other. This PRISMA 2020 systematic review screened 5,833 records and read 119 full texts to determine whether any published system detects such a broken mapping and repairs it while the twins operate. In all 32 included studies the mapping is fixed before operation, and the two ingredients of run-time repair appear only separately: cross-company matching without any check that the match still holds, and detection and repair of changed meaning within a single company. The review turns this gap into six requirements, each illustrated on one running example, that a system claiming run-time semantic interoperability between independently owned twins should meet.

papers.title: Stacked-bases Properties, maximal ideals and polynomial closures of Rings of Integer-Valued Polynomials
papers.abstract: We study the integer-valued polynomial ring with the stacked-bases property, maximal ideals above valuation ideals, and the polynomial closure of matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomials. A content argument gives stacked-bases properties for integer-valued polynomial rings over number-field integer rings. The construction of Hagg and Mortberg provides a Bezout domain without this property. For rank-one valuation domains, maximal ideals are described by evaluations and pseudo-convergent sequences. For matrices, we give congruence-ideal and companion-lattice criteria, together with finite-level tests to characterize the polynomial closures.

papers.title: The precision of fractional factorial designs under randomization
papers.abstract: A regular fraction of a two-level factorial design runs fewer treatment combinations (cells), with more units in each. With the number of units fixed, more units per cell do not by themselves reduce the variance. Averaged over the fractions of one defining contrast subgroup, a fraction's variance is smaller than the full design's by the unit-to-unit variation of the aliased effects, a gain the usual variance estimator misses. Assuming the aliased effects are zero, we propose a full-design estimator that weights the fractions' contrasts by inverse variance. Its estimated variance never exceeds the saturated estimator's. In large samples, it is proportional to the harmonic mean of the fractions' average cell variances, and a fraction's, on average, to the arithmetic mean. We test this assumption, but choosing between the two estimators by the test can lose coverage. The results extend to unequal allocations, and the large-sample results to covariate adjustment.

papers.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.

papers.title: Studentized inference in randomized experiments when a few units dominate the outcome variation
papers.abstract: In completely randomized experiments with heavy-tailed outcomes, a few units can carry a share of the residual variation that does not vanish as the number of units grows. We study the studentized difference in means and Lin's regression-adjusted estimator, with covariates whose leverage vanishes, when the finite population is fixed, and the treatment assignment is the only source of randomness. The studentized statistic then has a nonnormal limit in general. Populations with the same marginal distributions of potential outcomes can have different limits, as the limit depends on the unobserved pairing mechanism of the two potential outcomes of each dominant unit. When the outcome errors are drawn from a heavy-tailed law, the limit is random and, outside a degenerate case, varies with the population. Under balanced allocation, the conventional Wald interval has an explicit asymptotic coverage floor. At the nominal level $0.95$, the floor is about $0.42$ for every population and about $0.84$ when the two potential residuals of each unit are equal. Both floors are close to the best possible, and without balanced allocation, the coverage can fall to the smaller of the proportions of treated and control units.

papers.title: Control Foundation Models across Changing Block Diagrams: Generalizing Time-Series Prediction to Dynamic Graphs
papers.abstract: In the prediction and control of physical systems, combining records from different experiments and operations is expected to supply information that no single experiment provides on its own. Time-series foundation models, which learn a shared predictor from diverse time series, offer a framework for treating such records as a common training resource. Moreover, query-based prediction models, which switch between known and target signals within the same time series, make it possible to handle response prediction and control-input generation in a unified manner. However, in control-experiment data, the connections between signals change with the experimental stage, such as system identification, filtering, and feedback control, which calls for a formulation that handles signal values and connection structures dynamically and in a unified way. We formulate a control foundation model that defines a data space of dynamic graphs containing connections, signal values, and missing values, together with an operation on this space that specifies the known signals and the prediction targets. This allows response prediction and control-input generation to be described as a common masked prediction problem, even for experimental data with different connections and recorded signals. The Block Diagram Transformer (BDT), which implements this formulation, combines attention along the time axis with a graph neural network that follows the block-diagram connections, and can be initialized with the pretrained parameters of existing time-series foundation models. Trained on control-experiment data that mix multiple experimental settings, the proposed model stabilized an unstable system through feedback control, which is difficult to achieve by fine-tuning existing time-series foundation models. Ongoing work applying this approach to a wide range of target systems is also yielding promising results.

papers.title: Transformer-guided Variable Projection for Phasor and Fault-Time Estimation Under DDC Offset
papers.abstract: Decaying DC (DDC) offsets introduce substantial phasor estimation errors during the first post-fault cycle. Recent approaches have sought interpretable waveform representations, but identifying analytical expressions can incur substantial computational costs. This paper proposes a transformer-guided variable-projection estimator that extracts the fundamental phasor, DDC parameters, and fault inception time from point-on-wave (POW) samples as an interpretable analytical expression. An offline-trained transformer provides the signal structure and decay rate, while variable projection refines the parameters and handles windows containing the fault without knowledge of time of fault. Across single- and dual-DDC scenarios with time constants of 2.5--400~ms, the mean maximum overshoot (MO) is at most 2.7% on post-fault windows and 2.2% during online operation, where the DFT reaches 10--14%. The post-fault phasor settles within 5% approximately 12.5~ms after inception. Circuit-level validation on a 230-kV two-source system yields 1.6% mean MO, compared with 9.5% for the DFT.

papers.title: Grid-Mode-Aware AI Data Center Power Smoothing via Bayesian-Optimized Hybrid Energy Storage System
papers.abstract: AI data centers exhibit highly stochastic, volatile power demands from intensive workloads and synchronized GPU training cycles, which can excite grid natural frequencies and threaten system stability. This paper proposes a real-time, forecasting-independent control framework utilizing a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) that coordinates a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and a supercapacitor (SC). Employing a parameterized frequency-decoupling and active modal-damping policy, the framework mitigates critical oscillatory load components while smoothing overall power fluctuations. To bypass the heavy computational burden of online receding-horizon optimization, this work introduces an offline Bayesian Optimization (BO) approach to optimally tune real-time control parameters, minimizing a multi-objective cost function that balances grid compliance penalties and storage degradation. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method ensures grid stability and strong target envelope adherence. Specifically, it reshapes extreme 75-160 MW raw demand fluctuations to largely fit within a tight 10 MW target band, with only brief transient excursions, while attenuating the critical 20 MW oscillatory component below 1 MW to suppress resonant excitation.

papers.title: von Neumann-Morgenstern stable sets in job matching problems
papers.abstract: We show that a von Neumann-Morgenstern (vNM) stable set generically exists in the many-to-one job-matching model. Unlike the core, which can be empty in this model, a vNM stable set exists whenever there is a unique efficient matching: the set of all individually rational (IR) and efficient outcomes form a vNM stable set. If an economy has multiple efficient matchings, a vNM stable set may not exist. If the vNM stable sets are required to be rich in a certain sense, then such a rich vNM stable set exists if and only if the set of efficient matchings is essentially unique, and the set of all efficient and IR outcomes forms the unique rich vNM stable set.

authors.name: Debasis Mishra
authors.institution: Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology

papers.title: Answer Correction with Verifiable Rewards: A Gemma-Family Study of Multi-View Driving QA
papers.abstract: Multi-camera driving question answering provides a discrete test of vision-language models, but post-training gains can reflect changed selected answers or improved answer extraction. We investigate this distinction within the Gemma model family using archived, task-linked WaymoQA evaluations. A zero-shot diagnostic on 5,519 test questions spans effective-small, mixture-of-experts, unified, and dense checkpoints, with serving differences disclosed rather than interpreted as architecture effects. The strongest controlled evidence is a matched-harness Gemma-4-12B base/GRPO pair: accuracy rises from 73.78% to 75.43%, a gain of 1.65 percentage points with a scene-cluster bootstrap interval of [+0.84, +2.41]. There are 215 improvements and 124 regressions; 213 improvements start from an extractable but incorrect base answer, and only two recover previously unextractable responses. Crossing correctness with extraction state shows why correct noncompliant outputs cannot be counted as prediction errors. Category counts reveal a critical safety asymmetry: routine perception gains (+5.93 pp) mask a regression in safety-critical hazard prediction (-1.82 pp), demonstrating that unweighted outcome rewards can trade off rare edge cases for aggregate accuracy. Reward saturation describes sampled training dynamics rather than an architectural ceiling. A separate archived Gemma-31B thinking comparison yields no detected average improvement, with uncertainty that does not establish equivalence. These results support a modest answer-selection gain for the recorded tuning configuration and a reproducible diagnostic accounting, without attributing corrected labels to specific grounding mechanisms or claiming superiority over matched supervised tuning.

papers.title: Fewer Tokens, More Answers: Verifiable-Reward Tuning of an Ornith-Style VLM for Multi-View Driving QA
papers.abstract: Reasoning-enabled model derivatives must turn intermediate deliberation into a usable answer within a deployment budget. We study that transition in an Ornith checkpoint adapted to multi-camera driving question answering with verifiable rewards. Paired archived outputs show that, on a selected 400-question development screen with a 256-token cap, GRPO increases answer extraction from 78.25% to 90.25% and accuracy from 55.50% to 63.75%. Of 39 wrong-to-correct transitions, 33 begin with an unextractable base response. The base's 87 unextractable responses all reach the token cap. Checkpoint-verified reconstruction on those same questions gives a much smaller first-pass accuracy gain at 512 tokens: +0.75 percentage points, versus +8.25 at 256. A later answer-cued continuation is analyzed separately; it helps the base more and narrows the adapter difference. On the full 2,511-question development set, this recovery-enabled pipeline reduces mean generated tokens from 108.6 to 47.1, while the paired accuracy interval includes zero gain. We frame these findings as adaptation of answer delivery under finite budgets, with explicit selection and provenance limits. Ornith's self-scaffolding lineage and newer reasoning-enabled derivatives such as Bonsai motivate the problem, but our measured results concern Ornith alone and do not establish a shared architectural mechanism or cross-model transfer.

papers.title: Pressure-correlation phase diagram unraveling quantum phase transitions in altermagnetic $\epsilon$-FeOOH and realization of piezo-anomalous Hall effect
papers.abstract: We establish a pressure-correlation phase diagram that yields multiple pressure-tunable quantum phase transitions in iron oxyhydroxide ($\epsilon$-FeOOH) across three critical pressures, $P_{c1}>P_{c2}>P_{c3}$. The transitions arise from the competition among electron-correlation, crystal-field, and Hund's coupling. First-principles calculations reveal that the earlier reported high-spin (HS) to low-spin (LS) crossover at correlation-sensitive $P_{c1}$ is accompanied by a transition from charge-transfer to Mott insulating (CTI-MI) phase, and a change in the spin-quantization axis (SQA) from $\hat{y}$ to $\hat{x}$. The HS-LS crossover and CTI-MI transition is driven by the simultaneous increase in crystal-field splitting and decrease in Hund's coupling. The critical pressure $P_{c2}$ governing the structural transition from centrosymmetric $Pnnm$ phase to noncentrosymmetric $P2_1nm$ phase is found to be independent of electron-correlation. When correlation is strong, a third critical pressure ($P_{c3}$) emerges in the lower-pressure regime of the phase diagram. Validating the recent experimental observation, $P_{c3}$ is responsible for changing the SQA from $\hat{z}$ to $\hat{y}$. By exhibiting altermagnetism in both $P2_1nm$ and $Pnnm$ phases and possessing finite anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) only for SQA along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, $\epsilon$-FeOOH enables a unique piezo-anomalous Hall effect where one can switch on the AHC at a lower pressure and change its direction at a higher pressure.

papers.title: Label-Free Localization and Test-Time Suppression of CLIP's Typographic Circuits
papers.abstract: CLIP-based Vision-Language Models have become cornerstones of modern multimodal systems. The cross-modal contrastive objective equips the CLIP vision encoder to both see objects and read text. These two abilities induce an entanglement between the encoding of lexical and semantic shapes, creating a distinctive vulnerability to typographic attacks, in which rendered text overrides an image's semantic content with its literal meaning. The black-box nature of these encoders has prevented a mechanistic interpretation of such entanglement. We introduce a head-decomposed Sparse Dictionary Learning (SDL) architecture that, by design, decomposes individual attention heads into interpretable, head-specific latents. Based on this inductive disentanglement, we re-purpose Clarity Score and propose normalized Text Attribution Score, which are both label-free, to identify attention heads that carry typographic information. As a causal validation of successful circuit separation, we perform a mechanistic intervention that reweighs attention away from the patch tokens in the identified lexical heads at test-time. Experiments show that the intervention effectively recovers object classification under typographic attack and, across five CLIP variants and four typographic benchmarks, achieves up to 46.9% improvement while incurring up to 1% accuracy loss in general image perception, outperforming prior supervised and training-free methods. Expanding on the mechanistic intervention, we propose a test-time adaptive attention head routing to further reduce the impact on performance at matched robustness, pushing beyond the Pareto frontier of current robustness-perception tradeoff.

papers.title: Neural Integral Control Barrier Functions for Agile Collision Avoidance
papers.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) are a standard way to keep a planner inside a safe set, but they assume control affine dynamics, a barrier function given in closed form, and a known nominal controller. Integral control barrier functions (ICBFs) remove the first assumption and absorb input constraints, yet they still assume a given nominal controller and a barrier function. In this work, we present an approach to learn all three from data, using neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for the dynamics, imitation for the nominal controller, and supervised regression for the barrier function. The learned dynamics, nominal controller, and the barrier function are used to build the ICBF filter constraint analytically. Furthermore, the barrier is trained on viability rather than geometry, meaning that a state counts as safe only if some emergency maneuver can still avoid the constraint under the actuator limits, a correction that geometric labels miss entirely and that grows with speed. Actuator limits then enter the online program as hard bounds while the learned barrier rows may be relaxed, which keeps the program solvable at every state and the actuator limits exact, and we bound how far the input it returns can drift from the one the true models would give. On agile racing with a 6-D dynamic bicycle, the filter removes all 12 unsafe episodes from 200 held out layouts at an unchanged success rate and above 100 Hz on one CPU core, holds the input constraint on every episode of a benchmark where a jointly trained baseline holds it on 53.38%, and keeps that advantage under large errors in the plant friction.

authors.name: Efstathios Bakolas
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations. However, an agent may achieve a user's goal while causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files, weakening access controls, or corrupting data, in response to benign inputs without explicit jailbreaking. This failure mode is particularly important because apparent task success may reassure users that an agent behaved correctly, causing harmful side effects to go unnoticed. We call this harmful success: the agent successfully completes the intended benign task while simultaneously causing unintended harm. Despite its importance, harmful success is difficult to measure because conventional task-success metrics overlook harmful behaviors, while existing safety evaluations are often designed solely to assess harmful outcomes. We introduce VeriHarm, an automatic framework for constructing programmatically verifiable benchmarks that directly measure harmful success. VeriHarm minimally perturbs coding tasks to elicit unintended harmful behavior while maintaining the benignity of the task and preserving the original task objective. It then synthesizes executable harm tests that, together with the original task-correctness tests, evaluate both task accuracy and harmful outcomes. Frontier agents, including GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, achieve an average task accuracy of 95% on our curated VeriHarm-Bench, yet still struggle to complete tasks safely: their safe success rate, the fraction of tasks completed successfully without triggering the designated harm, averages only 37%. These results suggest that successful task completion can frequently coexist with unintended harm, and that task-success metrics alone may substantially understate the potential safety risks of coding agents.

papers.title: BanglishDepYT: Depression Detection in Native Bengali Social Media with Emotion-Preserving Preprocessing and Domain-Adaptive Pretraining
papers.abstract: Depression affects millions of Bengali speakers across South Asia, yet automated detection systems have relied almost entirely on datasets translated from English. Such datasets cannot capture the emoticons, romanized Bengali words, and elongated spellings that characterize real expressions of distress. We introduce BanglishDepYT, a Bengali depression dataset collected natively from YouTube, comprising 191,000 unlabeled comments and 1,000 samples verified through dual bilingual annotation. We propose EPH (Emotion-Preserving Hybrid preprocessing), which converts emoticons to semantic tags, preserves Banglish tokens, protects negation words, and normalizes emotional elongation. A key finding is that preprocessing choice substantially affects performance on informal text: standard cleaning reduces the Banglish Survival Rate to zero (SVM F1: 0.7062), while EPH preserves signals (CESS: 0.9996 vs. 0.6694) and raises SVM F1 to 0.8570, an improvement of 0.1508. We further apply domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT), continuing SahajBERT pretraining on unlabeled in-domain comments. DAPT-SahajBERT achieves the highest mean F1 (0.8161) and MCC (0.6272), significantly outperforming the baseline (F1: 0.7805, p = 0.0013, d = 1.450) and matching MuRIL (p = 0.589). These results suggest that targeted domain pretraining is a competitive alternative to large-scale multilingual pretraining. LLM-assisted annotation using Qwen2.5-7B achieves substantial human agreement (kappa = 0.611), enabling pseudo-labeling of 96,071 comments. Semi-supervised training improves AUC from 0.8499 to 0.8731 (p = 0.044), offering a scalable path to expanding annotation. All code, models, and datasets are publicly released to support reproducible research.

papers.title: Combinatorial Algorithms for Partial Inverse Min-Max Spanning Tree Problem under the Weighted Sum Hamming Distance
papers.abstract: Given a connected weighted graph G=(V, E, w) and a forest F of G, the goal of partial inverse min-max spanning tree problem is to change the weight function as little as possible, so that there is a min-max spanning tree with respect to the new weight function containing F. In this paper, we study this problem under the weighted sum Hamming distance. We take the alternative set of the maximum edge weight in F with respect to the optimal weight function as a key factor, and further consider the case of this problem under the restriction of this factor. On this basis, a polynomial time algorithm with time complexity O(|V|^4) is proposed to solve this problem.

papers.title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
papers.abstract: We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).

authors.name: Yifan Jiang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: $^{85}$Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ three-photon cascade schemes
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor. Using the cascade system $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ in $^{85}$Rb, we explore two collinear laser-beam configurations. The detunings of the upper two lasers of the cascade system are varied. In both configurations, the probe transmission maps contain rich sets of EIT/EIA features and substructures. To explain these, we utilize a dressed-atom and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. The latter includes 108 relevant fine- and hyperfine-structure levels and their magnetic substates, accounting for coherent optical drives, optical pumping, atom recycling, electromagnetic decays via the $5P_{J}$ levels, and velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions. We find quantum-trajectory solutions of the Lindblad master equation, which show good agreement with experimental data and aid in finding physical explanations for the observed spectra. To further explore collision-induced spectral features, collisional loss of EIT/EIA visibility, velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions, we acquire spectra in Rb cells with 50 and 500~mTorr of Ar gas. Our work is of interest to studies of multi-level EIT systems that underpin emerging quantum technologies, where accurate accounting of internal atomic structure, laser beam geometry, optical pumping, transit time, and collisional effects is critical.

papers.title: Few Trials, Many Metrics: Beta Mixtures for Low-Budget AI Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating a stochastic AI system often requires many repeated samples per instance, especially for metrics defined over long horizons. Recent work has shown that modeling instance-level success probabilities with a Beta distribution recovers Pass@$k$ from far fewer samples than direct estimation. We show that this framework supports a broader range of evaluation targets. We fit a mixture of Beta distributions by marginal maximum likelihood, with the number of components chosen by BIC. From that one fit, we compute Pass$^k$ and AUC@$k$ at any horizon in closed form. We also derive delta-method confidence intervals for these metrics and for Pass@$k$, which require no additional model calls. Treating configurations rather than tasks as instances extends the same model to sensitivity analysis. For repeated success metrics, we find that mixture priors yield more accurate estimators than naive estimation across competition mathematics and graduate-level science benchmarks when extrapolating beyond the observed number of trials, and the resulting intervals cover the full-data reference. When prompts are treated as instances, it estimates the distribution of prompt sensitivity more accurately than a comparable item-response baseline without external covariates. Direct estimators remain preferable once trials reach the target horizon.

papers.title: Quantum HHL Algorithm for Solving 1D Linear Advection Equation Using Explicit and Implicit Finite Difference Schemes
papers.abstract: This study develops and implements a Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) quantum algorithm for solving a one-dimensional linear advection equation with periodic boundary conditions. The governing equation is first discretized using a classical finite difference (FD) scheme to obtain a linear system suitable for quantum solution. We present a newly designed, circuit-level implementation of HHL assembled from Qiskit circuit components and exploit the circulant structure of the periodic discretization matrices through Fourier-based matrix evolution. The HHL algorithm is benchmarked with three explicit schemes and one implicit scheme. The implicit scheme requires a nontrivial linear solve arising from the discretized PDE on progressively finer grids, whereas the explicit schemes provide different input fields for testing state preparation and reconstruction with identity coefficient matrices. HHL solution states are validated against direct classical solves in noiseless simulation. For hardware execution, the periodic matrix structure permits a Fourier implementation that applies reciprocal eigenvalues without phase estimation. Results on the IBM Rensselaer Nighthawk processor are compared at a shared final time. Noiseless reconstructed fields approach the transported profile on resolved grids, while substantial hardware errors remain for both explicit and implicit schemes. Crank-Nicolson remains exceptionally well-conditioned and utilizes similar circuit re sources to the explicit controls, proving that hardware degradation in our tests was not driven by poor matrix conditioning. Ultimately, this study shows new means for HHL algorithms to study quantum CFD problems involving advection equations with implicit time integrations, while demonstrating how state preparation and measurement affect the practical performance of quantum solvers on current devices.

papers.title: Parameters and lim CM sequences: the Q-sequence conjecture and Lech's formula
papers.abstract: We prove that if a local ring has a weakly lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence of modules, then it satisfies the conjecture that every system of parameters is a Q-sequence. We also give a generalization of Lech's formula for the multiplicity of a local ring $(R,m)$ with respect to a system of parameters that allows a very large class of sequences of $m$-primary ideals generated by monomials in the parameters to be used in the calculation. The cases where the sequence of ideals consists of the powers of the ideal generated by parameters, or where the ideals in the sequence are generated by varying powers of the individual parameters all of which tend to infinity, which is Lech's original formula, are included.

papers.title: Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
papers.abstract: We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $\lambda$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-\lambda t$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.

papers.title: Abstention Spends Its Budget on Local Label Variance More Than on Novelty: Auditing Conformal Calibration and Selective Prediction under Molecular Scaffold Shift
papers.abstract: Selective prediction with split conformal calibration promises a post-hoc fix for molecular property prediction: abstain on the least reliable compounds, ideally out-of-distribution chemistry, and the retained set becomes trustworthy without retraining. We audit this recipe for a gradient-boosted fingerprint model on lipophilicity (regression) and BBBP (classification) under a Bemis-Murcko scaffold split, holding the fitted model and evaluation molecules fixed while varying only the calibration fold (18 replicates). (i) On lipophilicity, coverage depends on calibration provenance: calibrating on held-out training-scaffold molecules falls below nominal (PICP 0.841 at a 0.90 target), while novel-scaffold calibration recovers it (0.904); on BBBP, coverage stays above nominal in every regime. (ii) For split conformalized quantile regression (CQR) the conformal correction is a constant, so conformalization does not change what is abstained on. (iii) The abstention score (CQR width; effectively ensemble variance on BBBP) tracks local label variance more than chemical novelty: controlling for local label variance largely explains away the novelty association (partial Spearman 0.067 and 0.047). (iv) At a fixed assay budget, gating on interval width or ensemble variance never improves hit precision over ranking by point prediction, at the pre-specified operating point or across 20 exploratory settings; a plain novelty gate shows small, uncorrected gains at the smallest budgets. (v) In an exploratory analysis, exact conformal selection exceeds its false discovery rate target under training-scaffold calibration (0.303 at q=0.2) and is consistent with it under novel-scaffold calibration, contributing a data-driven batch size rather than a better ranking. Conformalization earns its keep through guarantees whose validity hinges on calibration provenance, not by choosing what to abstain on.

papers.title: Surrogate Losses for Fairness-Aware Classification: Fisher Consistency and Calibration
papers.abstract: Fairness-aware classification seeks to balance predictive accuracy and fairness across demographic groups. Although surrogate losses facilitate the optimization of fairness-aware objectives, it remains unclear when minimizing these losses yields optimal decisions under the original fairness-aware risk. This paper investigates the statistical validity of surrogate-based fairness-aware classification under demographic parity and equal opportunity, considering both attribute-blind and attribute-aware settings. We introduce fairness-aware Fisher consistency and characterize it through conditions on the derivatives of the surrogate losses. The characterization shows that consistency depends not only on the individual loss functions but also on their interaction within the fairness-regularized objective. We further establish a calibration inequality that relates the excess fairness-aware risk to the excess surrogate risk, providing a quantitative connection between surrogate optimization and the original classification objective. Numerical experiments illustrate how deviations from the consistency conditions affect fairness-aware excess risk and how the regularization parameter influences the well-posedness of surrogate optimization. An application to consumer credit default prediction demonstrates that appropriately calibrated fairness regularization can substantially reduce demographic disparities while maintaining predictive performance.

authors.name: Xiaoling Lu
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: EgoMo3R: Joint Egocentric Motion and Scene Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Understanding holistic 3D human motion and the surrounding environment from egocentric video is fundamental for applications in AR/VR and robotics. Although these tasks are inherently coupled, existing methods treat them separately. In particular, egocentric motion reconstruction methods typically assume access to metric, gravity-aligned camera trajectories from specialized inertial sensors. Recovering such trajectories from monocular egocentric video remains a significant challenge due to rapid head movements and motion blur. We present EgoMo3R, a joint optimization framework that simultaneously reconstructs 3D human motion and scene geometry from casual egocentric video. It leverages the robustness of low-level visuo-geometric primitives, including monocular depth, optical flow, and point tracks, integrated with a diffusion-based human motion prior via first-order optimization. We propose an alternating optimization scheme that establishes a synergistic feedback loop: scene reconstruction provides physical grounding and trajectory conditioning for the motion prior, while the motion prior regularizes the camera trajectory and anchors the scene in a metric, gravity-aligned world frame. We evaluate EgoMo3R on the highly dynamic sequences of the EgoExo4D and Nymeria datasets and show that it outperforms specialized baselines in both 3D scene reconstruction and egocentric motion estimation.

papers.title: Back to the Future: Predicting Long-Horizon Dynamics with Retrospective Correction for Disturbance-Aware Retrieval
papers.abstract: Retrieving objects from densely packed storage requires anticipating how contact disturbs surrounding objects when limited clearance prevents lifting the target over clutter. However, contact can propagate beyond the target's immediate neighbors, while accumulated prediction errors make learned dynamics unreliable over long planning horizons. We introduce DARE (Disturbance-Aware REtrieval), a geometry-aware relational dynamics framework that uses retrospective correction to improve long-horizon prediction for disturbance-aware retrieval. DARE encodes compact object descriptors and predicts action-conditioned disturbance propagation through object-level message passing. When a sparse observation becomes available, a learned corrector uses the prediction discrepancy to amend an earlier predicted state and reruns the intervening dynamics, propagating the correction through the predicted contact chain. These predictions guide a receding-horizon planner that balances retrieval progress against displacement and rotation of surrounding objects, permitting necessary contact while discouraging harmful disturbance. Experiments in planar and RoboCasa environments evaluate long-horizon prediction, generalization, and robustness for disturbance-aware retrieval in dense clutter. See our project website: https://the-back-to-the-future.github.io

authors.name: Jiwoong Choi
authors.institution: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Haoyu Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: When Delay Meets Drift: Physical Safety of Robot Foundation Models Is a Cross-Layer Problem
papers.abstract: Robot foundation models now act in a closed loop, yet their safety is evaluated one variation at a time: robustness benchmarks perturb the scene while assuming instantaneous inference, and real-time execution methods study inference delay in nominal scenes. We argue that physical safety is not a property of the model alone, but emerges from how variations in the physical environment, the model, the computing platform, and execution interact in closed loop. We formalize this as cross-layer variation propagation across these system layers and use an interaction contrast to measure when joint variation creates more risk than the sum of its parts. In 4,000 paired closed-loop episodes of the pi0.5 vision-language-action model on LIBERO, a 400 ms inference delay raises the safety-violation rate by 3.5 percentage points under the training viewpoint but by 37 percentage points under a 60-degree camera shift: 33.5 percentage points (95% CI: 25-43) more than the two effects combined. We close with a research agenda toward predictable physical intelligence: predicting when variation becomes risk, and adapting compute, power, and control accordingly.

papers.title: When to Probe and When to Act: Clarity-Aware Risk-Adaptive Control for Interactive Driving
papers.abstract: Safe navigation in interactive traffic requires autonomous vehicles to reason about unobservable human characteristics and the reciprocal nature of multi-agent interactions. Traditional architectures often decouple prediction from planning, leading to the "Frozen Robot Problem" or unsafe maneuvers under high ambiguity because they treat risk assessment and information acquisition as independent objectives. We argue that the notion of safety should not remain static but must instead dynamically co-evolve with the system's internal confidence: the robot should actively clarify ambiguity when necessary while also recognizing the diminishing returns of information, and naturally transition toward task execution. We introduce a unified belief-space Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that couples multistep information planning with a clarity-adaptive Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) barrier mechanism. By treating clarity, a scalar informational state, as an explicit planning variable, the controller co-designs its probing strategy with its safety specification, tightening conservatism under high ambiguity and relaxing constraints as confidence improves. We further provide a performance analysis showing that the cost of information seeking and the expected planning-cost gap to a controller that knows the true human characteristic are bounded by residual ambiguity and solver error. We evaluate the framework in lane-merging and unsignalized-intersection scenarios against representative interactive-planning baselines. Across 5,000 simulations, the proposed method achieves the highest success rates (94.6% and 93.2%) and the lowest collision rates (1.2% and 1.4%) among the compared methods, providing a principled foundation for robust decision-making in human-centric environments.

papers.title: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(\Phi_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\le\theta<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>\theta$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-\theta)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $\theta=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.

authors.name: Joseph M. Shunia
authors.institution: Ann Arbor Center for Independent Living

papers.title: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
papers.abstract: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.

papers.title: ReplayFactor: Replay-Aware Dual-Attribute Learning for Practical Speech Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Advances in synthesis techniques have made deepfake speech increasingly realistic, amplifying voice security threats, including unauthorized voice cloning and impersonation. Although existing deepfake detectors perform well on digitally generated speech, their performance often degrades on physically replayed deepfakes, which constitute a low-cost and practical threat to real-world systems. Existing research focuses primarily on dataset construction and evaluation, while available dataset diversity and replay-aware detector design remain limited. We propose ReplayFactor, a dual-attribute framework that enhances replay evidence by fusing self-supervised learning (SSL) representations with an acoustic prior, while leveraging multi-task learning and supervised contrastive learning to promote robust, generalizable representations. We also construct ReplayFake-CN, a large-scale, multi-device Chinese dataset comprising approximately 185k replayed synthetic utterances to complement public benchmarks. Our framework improves macro-F1 from 60.99% to 76.44% and reduces EER from 11.86% to 3.05% on the EchoFake open set over the baseline, demonstrating strong potential for practical replayed deepfake detection.

authors.name: Miao He
authors.institution: Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Peoples Hospital

authors.name: Jiayi Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Omni-Life: Benchmarking Omnimodal Real-Time AI Assistants in People's Daily Lives
papers.abstract: Real-time omnimodal assistants are expected to support people in everyday life, but audiovisual understanding alone does not establish whether they can provide timely and appropriate help. We introduce Omni-Life, a benchmark grounded in real-world user needs, deployment scenarios, and device-dependent observations. It combines controlled video synthesis for hazardous situations and edge cases with annotated real-world videos under a shared temporal protocol. The benchmark contains 400 videos: 290 requiring assistance, with 555 required intervention events, and 110 requiring silence throughout to test whether models can withhold unnecessary responses when no assistance is needed. We evaluate twelve configurations featuring mainstream real-time omnimodal models, jointly assessing event coverage, response content, timing, and unwanted output. At most 4.48% of videos requiring assistance are handled completely correctly. To examine practical deployment strategies, we study task reminders and response-latency tolerance. Reminders can improve recall by 17.12 percentage points but add approximately 4.6 unwanted responses per minute of reference silence. Increasing latency tolerance by 10s improves recall by at most 5.95 percentage points. These results show that existing models remain insufficient to deliver reliable assistance in real-life applications, calling for tailored model optimization in instruction following, timely proactive intervention, and withholding responses when assistance is not needed.

authors.name: Jia Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Di Jiang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: ILLRAW: Illumination-Aware RAW Object Detection
papers.abstract: Existing RAW-based detectors typically introduce learnable ISP modules to convert RAW inputs into sRGB-like formats to fit off-the-shelf detectors. However, this RAW-to-sRGB paradigm decouples representation learning from the downstream detection task. Crucially, it forces the network to inherit human-centric visual priors while discarding intrinsic RAW advantages, such as linear sensor responses and high-bit-depth, minimally processed scene cues. In this paper, we propose \textbf{ILLRAW}, an \textbf{ILL}umination-aware end-to-end \textbf{RAW} object detection framework. Instead of reconstructing visually plausible sRGB images, ILLRAW directly learns detection-oriented RAW features through a lightweight feature adapter inserted at the input stage of existing detectors. ILLRAW estimates an illumination mask and introduces channel-sensitive embeddings to model Bayer-channel responses. These features are fused by an illumination attention fusion module. Experiments show clear improvements on the diverse AODRaw benchmark and competitive performance on LOD and PascalRAW, with particularly strong results under dark exposure.

papers.title: Device Identification and Motion Classification of Passive Nonlinear RF Transponders Using Wi-Fi Channel State Information
papers.abstract: A method of joint device authentication and gesture classification using low-cost passive transponders and 802.11 signals of opportunity from commodity hardware is presented for tracking objects in cluttered environments. The approach detects nonlinear responses of diode-based radio-frequency (RF) transponders by estimating the mean time-varying phase across all subcarrier channel state information (CSI) obtained from standard preambles. These unique responses are enabled by passive transponders utilizing 2.4 GHz meander-line monopole antennas with capacitive top-hat loading and a low-barrier Schottky diode, allowing for low-power omnidirectional sensing and complex gesture recognition across multiple unique devices. The capture system uses a wireless access point to illuminate the transponder with a standard preamble. This signal is modulated by the diode's nonlinear response and transmitted to a single ESP32 receiver to calculate the channel response. Using the modulated CSI, device identification via RF fingerprinting achieves >95% accuracy in both static and dynamic conditions using simple machine learning models. For dynamically moving transponders, a time-varying velocity profile is calculated using a novel phase sanitation approach that significantly reduces the impacts of the non-cooperative network. This enables high-accuracy estimation of micro-motions on a single receiver, achieving a theoretical limit of 9.75 m/s using an amplitude-invariant binary comparator form of the sanitized waveform. The concept is experimentally validated using lightweight CNN-LSTM deep-learning models applied to a diverse dataset of five transponders and three motion profiles. This experimental validation demonstrated a classification accuracy of 98% in both gesture classification and device identification tasks.

papers.title: RadPose: ISAC-based RF 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Although mmWave radars provide robustness to illumination and occlusion, they rely on dedicated hardware and licensed spectrum, limiting scalability. In this paper, we present RadPose, a learning-based monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that enables mmWave communication devices to perform 3D human pose estimation. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. To address the sparsity and noise of RF observations, RadPose employs a cross-frame transformer-based pose inference network with semantic-guided spatial attention and target-driven temporal attention for robust spatio-temporal aggregation. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Extensive experiments demonstrate RadPose achieves competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art radar-based approaches while maintaining robust performance in unseen and occluded scenarios. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Geo-Chou/RadPose.

papers.title: RubricWorld: World Model-Guided Rubric Optimization for LLM Graders
papers.abstract: Rubric optimization improves LLM grading by revising scoring instructions while keeping the grader's parameters fixed. Existing optimizers often judge edits by aggregate validation performance, limiting the supervision they retain about which errors an edit corrects or introduces. Testing each candidate also requires rescoring validation answers, which limits how many edits can be explored within a fixed budget. We propose RubricWorld, a framework that learns from previous edit evaluations to guide further search. Its world model predicts an edit's correction and degradation rates at score boundaries, conditioned on the current rubric state. The training signal comes from paired grading results: scores for the same answers before and after an edit. Predictions select one candidate for direct evaluation, and held-out confidence bounds determine whether it corrects enough target errors while keeping new errors within prespecified limits. Measured effects update the model even when the edit is rejected. Across EIR (National), ASAP2.0, and ASAP-SAS with three frozen LLM graders, RubricWorld achieves the highest score in 20 of 27 metric comparisons. On ASAP2.0, it raises gpt-5-mini accuracy from 18.20% with the original rubric to 46.70%, exceeding the strongest baseline, APO, by 22.60 percentage points. code will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Hang Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
papers.abstract: For $0<\kappa<8$, we prove a uniform dimension transformation theorem for SLE in natural time: on a single probability-one event, Hausdorff and packing dimensions of every time set are multiplied by $d=1+\kappa/8$, and the same holds for lower and upper box dimensions of every bounded time set. The result applies to self-similar SLE with stationary increments, chordal SLE in the half-plane, and chordal SLE in bounded piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domains. In the last case, the box-dimension conclusion holds under a positive-angle endpoint hypothesis. We also establish boundary-inclusive local H\"older continuity of every order below $1/d$ for chordal SLE in natural time and identify the exact local dimension $d$ of the natural occupation measure on compact time intervals.

papers.title: OctEx: Billion-Scale Vector Search by Precomputed Lattice Neighbor Lists on GPUs
papers.abstract: Approximate nearest-neighbor search on GPUs serves retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation, and deduplication over datasets of up to billions of vectors. The fastest GPU indexes at high recall, such as CAGRA, walk proximity graphs in chained rounds, each of which waits for the distances of the previous one. High recall therefore costs many dependent rounds per query. Our insight is to spend the HBM of the GPUs on precomputed neighbor lists, so that a query reads its candidates in one parallel step instead of a chain of rounds. This paper turns the above insight into a GPU vector search system, namely OctEx, which holds hundreds of randomly projected copies of the dataset in GPU memory. Every copy rounds its vectors to the nearest points of a regular grid whose cells are nearly round and stores for every populated cell the list of vectors nearest to its center. A query reads the lists of its cells in all copies at once and then, in a fixed number of waves, the precomputed neighbor lists of its best hits. OctEx ranks the union of all hits by an int8 sketch before one exact rerank. OctEx runs the whole search of a batch as CUDA graphs over all GPUs of a server and places every part of its index in HBM or host memory by its access frequency. On four H100 GPUs at recall 0.95 to 0.995, OctEx outperforms CAGRA by 2.0x to 46.4x on seven datasets of up to one hundred million vectors, and by 1.46x to 2.05x on the one billion vectors of Deep1B and SIFT1B, whose indexes it builds in 44 to 47 minutes. OctEx also outperforms GGNN, PathWeaver, FlowANN, and the cuVS inverted file indexes IVF-PQ and IVF-RaBitQ by 5.4x to 343x.

papers.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
papers.abstract: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.

papers.title: Auditing GeoFM Evaluation for Field-Extent Segmentation: Label Proxies, Baselines, and When Frozen Features Match Fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Geospatial foundation-model (GeoFM) benchmarks for agricultural field-extent segmentation often rely on cropland land-cover proxies and compare against per-pixel spectral baselines. We measure how these choices affect conclusions using identical single-date Sentinel-2 pixels from six countries. Replacing polygon-derived field labels with ESA WorldCover cropland raises random-forest AUROC from 0.55-0.82 to 0.79-0.96, showing that the proxy creates a more spectrally separable task. On the actual field-extent labels, a from-scratch U-Net reaches 0.89-0.98 AUROC and has higher point AUROC than a Prithvi frozen linear probe in five of six regions. We then compare a frozen backbone and full fine-tuning using the same decoder for Prithvi and TerraMind, with ten matched seeds. At $\varepsilon=0.02$ AUROC, 9 of 12 region$\times$model cells are TOST-equivalent. Kenya is the common failure case: positives cover roughly 0.1% of pixels, and full fine-tuning performs better for both models. Cross-region results are less favorable to frozen models. On AUROC and average precision (AP), the U-Net leads the full 30-transfer matrix, while an exploratory analysis excluding Kenya finds that both frozen decoders outperform their fine-tuned counterparts; no AUROC difference is detected between frozen TerraMind and the U-Net in that subset. For Prithvi, a frozen decoder trains about $110\times$ fewer parameters than full fine-tuning. These results argue for auditing labels and baselines before interpreting GeoFM rankings, and for testing a frozen decoder before assuming that full fine-tuning will help. Our conclusions are limited to single-date, per-pixel field-extent segmentation, not parcel-boundary or instance delineation.

papers.title: The Kinetic Basis of the Genetic Code
papers.abstract: The origin of the genetic code is an enigma, requiring explanations for the emergence of degeneracy, the organizational structure of the code, and the correspondence between codons and amino acids. Here, we use the asymmetric cooperativity model to show that these features arise from asymmetric cooperativity in codon-anticodon association process. We first provide mechanistic and evolutionary accounts of wobble base pair degeneracy, without providing any preferential treatment to the third position. The model, with four tunable parameters, reproduces the organizational structure of the genetic code, and provides theoretical codon-anticodon association times. Although ribosomal kinetic data are not used in parameter estimation, these theoretical association times correlate with experimentally determined ribosomal residence times (r=0.73). The resulting timescales, extending over four decades, also exhibit correlations with diverse physicochemical properties of amino acids, at multiple timescales, motivating a nonequilibrium picture in which energy released during codon-anticodon association is transferred to its cognate amino acid to be dissipated into water. Finally, without incorporating information about aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases or further parameter adjustment, the model recovers the division of amino acids associated with the two aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase classes, with a combined segregation score of 0.92 ( p~10^{-8}). These results suggest that wobble degeneracy, genetic-code organization, translation kinetics, amino-acid physicochemistry, and the two-class organization of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases may reflect a common underlying kinetic constraint. We propose that non-equilibrium, asymmetrically cooperative kinetics, that possibly underlie DNA/RNA replication process, also provided a physical basis upon which the genetic code and its subsequent translation machinery evolved.

papers.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
papers.abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter $\alpha$ deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding $W_0(\alpha)=\pm1$, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases $\alpha$ where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.

papers.title: Unique Hahn-Banach extensions in Bochner $L^p$ spaces
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed subspace of a real Banach space $X$. Let $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a complete finite measure space and let $1<p<\infty$. We prove that $Y$ has property-$(U)$, property-$(SU)$, property-$(wU)$ in $X$ if and only if $L^p(\mu,Y)$ has the corresponding property in $L^p(\mu,X)$. No Radon-Nikod\'{y}m assumption on $X^*$ is required. The proofs use $w^*$-measurable representations of dual functionals and a simultaneous scalar-lifting construction. A norm-minimal representation for an element in $L^p(\mu,X)^*$ is found suitable in this case. We also study the point of continuity of the identity map under different topologies on the unit sphere of $L^p(\mu,X)^*$. For Bochner-integrable functionals, the pointwise $w^*-w$-continuity yields the uniqueness of the extension to $L^p(\mu,X^{**})$. Examples show why arbitrary $w^*$-measurable representatives cannot replace the norm-minimal representatives in this context.

papers.title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconducting 2D Hydrogenated Janus V2CSH and Nb2CSH MXenes
papers.abstract: Two dimensional hydrogenated Janus MXenes represent a new frontier in superconducting materials, where asymmetric surface terminations enable tunable electronic and vibrational properties. In this work, we present the first comparative study of hydrogen or sulfur terminated V2CSH and Nb2CSH monolayers using density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory. Both compounds are structurally and thermally stable, exhibiting isotropic in plane elasticity and nonmagnetic multiband metallic states dominated by transition metal d orbitals. The asymmetric S or H terminations generate nonequivalent surface potentials and intrinsic out of plane dipoles. Electron phonon coupling constants of 0.39 (V2CSH) and 0.53 (Nb2CSH) yield superconducting transition temperatures of 2.36 K and 5.27 K, respectively, within the Allen Dynes framework. Low energy lattice vibrations, primarily involving metal and sulfur atoms, account for 77% of the coupling in both MXenes. These findings establish metal substitution as a design principle for tuning superconductivity in Janus MXenes and highlight Nb2CSH as a promising candidate for low temperature superconducting applications.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
papers.abstract: A film-thickness error of 8 nm, within the tolerance of commercial thin-film lithium niobate wafers, shifts the group-velocity dispersion $\beta_2$ at 1550 nm by about 28 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. We study numerically whether a segmented, non-volatile phase-change cladding can correct this error after fabrication. In mode solves of 3012 geometries, Sb$_2$S$_3$ switches $\beta_2$ by a median of 181 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$ at a 40 nm strip thickness with no material absorption under the adopted optical constants, whereas Sb$_2$Se$_3$ reaches a comparable contrast at a median modal loss of 5.6 dB cm$^{-1}$. Because phase adds along the guide, four independently switched binary segments reach a two-dimensional region of the $(\beta_2,\beta_3)$ plane; eigenmode expansion supports this description at the junctions. Full-wave solves at 65 die geometries show that the segment states move with the die error, so the bit pattern is chosen from a per-die model: a spectral surrogate constrained by exact identities of the lossless Maxwell problem. Its accuracy within the training domain is similar to that of unconstrained baselines; it keeps $\beta_2$ and $\beta_3$ consistent, and its error at an unseen film thickness is 8.3 rather than 13.0 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. With a bare test ring and a second ring carrying a crystalline strip already on the mask, 96.8% of the dies are trimmed into $\pm25$ ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$, scored on full-wave solutions. A thermal model gives a candidate write window for a 532 nm beam.

authors.name: Shoumik Debnath
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Water electrolysis is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen (H$_2$) production. However, gas bubble formation significantly degrades the electrochemical surface area ($A_{\rm EC}$) and the electrocatalytic activity of microstructured electrodes in water electrolyzer cells. Existing theoretical models fail to connect computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and electrochemistry to analyze how bubble dynamics affect the performance of gas-evolving microstructured electrodes. This work develops a multiphysics-based theoretical model that couples two-phase CFD with Butler-Volmer and Faradaic kinetics, incorporating exchange current density, cell current, gravitational acceleration, surface tension, and fluid properties such as density and viscosity. The model quantifies essential electrochemical parameters, such as the enhancement in $A_{\rm EC}$ and the overpotential ($\eta$), which deviate by less than 7\% and 15\%, respectively, from the experimental results. Evaluations of the fabricated microstructured electrodes using polarization curves, cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and linear polarization resistance techniques demonstrate reduced $\eta$ by 2.49--21.39\% and 9.55--24.32\% for oxygen (O$_2$) and H$_2$ evolution, respectively. Furthermore, the model reveals the interplay between enhanced geometric surface area and bubble-transport limitations, facilitating the optimization and analysis of structural parameters. These findings establish a physics-informed roadmap for designing optimal, robust, and industry-scalable microstructured electrodes for efficient H$_2$ generation via water electrolysis.

papers.title: Constant Approximation of Fr\'echet Distance in Near-Linear Time
papers.abstract:
We present a deterministic algorithm that approximates the Fr\'echet distance between two polygonal curves in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $n$ and $m$ vertices within a constant factor in $O((m+n)^{1+\varepsilon})$ time, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and fixed dimension $d$. The approximation factor depends only on $\varepsilon$ and $d$. No assumption on the input curves is needed, and the algorithm also reports a matching certifying the approximation. The same result holds for the discrete Fr\'echet distance. Our result extends the line of work initiated by Cheng, Huang, and Zhang (2025), who gave the first constant-factor approximation in strongly subquadratic time, to near-linear time. For two $n$-vertex curves, the best previous running time was $\widetilde{O}(n^{5/3})$, due to van der Horst and Ophelders (2026).
  Our algorithm bootstraps between two primitives: a data structure that preprocesses a single curve for comparing any two of its subcurves, and a query procedure that compares subcurves of two different curves. Given the data structure for one curve, we compare it with another curve using a surrogate assembled from subcurves of the former. The surrogate is shared by all possible starting points of a matching. Conversely, faster queries make the next data structure cheaper to build. After a number of rounds that depends only on $\varepsilon$, both preprocessing and query time are $O((m+n)^{1+\varepsilon})$. To make each round's output reusable by the next, we compactly summarize how matchings can enter and leave a pair of subcurves. These summaries can be applied to different starting points and retain the information needed to report the matchings.

papers.title: Embodied AI for Radio Mapping: From Solo to Swarm
papers.abstract: Radio maps provide spatial knowledge of wireless environments to assess coverage, manage spectrum use, and support connectivity-aware mobility. Recent advances in embodied intelligence (EI) offer a promising approach to radio map reconstruction by enabling agents to perceive the environment and autonomously adjust their survey paths toward safe, reachable locations. However, a single agent remains constrained by limited endurance and onboard computing capacity, limiting measurement collection and reconstruction performance. Swarm cooperation can support more efficient radio mapping over larger areas by sharing observations and coordinating members' sampling. This article first explores the capabilities and applications of cooperative embodied agents. A cooperative radio map reconstruction framework is then presented, together with its key enabling techniques. Case study results illustrate how scene perception supports access to informative sampling locations and how air--ground cooperation improves reconstruction through complementary measurements and mobile support. The article concludes with open challenges and future research directions for reliable and efficient embodied cooperative radio mapping in complex environments.

authors.name: Shangjie Zhuang
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Maxima of the Q-index: Forbidden an odd wheel
papers.abstract: In 2013, Freitas, Nikiforov and Patuzzi (EJLA, 2013) proposed the problem of determining the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Recently, Yuan, Zhai and Zhang (LAA, 2026) determined the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs without wheels of sufficiently large order. In this paper, we consider the problem of forbidding a single wheel $W_{2k+1}=K_1\vee C_{2k}$. We show that, for every fixed integer $k\ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the unique extremal graph maximizing the signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $n$-vertex $W_{2k+1}$-free graphs is $K_k\vee(K_2\cup(n-k-2)K_1)$.

papers.title: Is That Clear? The Impacts of Clarifying Questions on Human-LLM Interaction
papers.abstract: LLM assistants increasingly ask clarifying questions (CQs) to elicit preferences and tailor recommendations. Although prior work emphasizes improvements in answer quality and user experience, how CQs shape users' subsequent engagement and reliance remains unclear. We conducted a controlled experiment (N=180) across six everyday decision scenarios, comparing human-LLM interaction with and without CQs. We further manipulated whether responses violated explicit constraints and whether violations occurred in the sub-decisions the CQs addressed, while preserving elicited preferences. CQs increased perceived understanding and satisfaction, yet participants spent less time reviewing and evaluating responses and accepted more responses unchanged, including erroneous ones. Within the CQ condition, participants more often accepted responses containing CQ-adjacent violations than nonadjacent violations. These findings demonstrate that LLM's proactive CQs shape subsequent engagement and reliance with preference elicitation. We discuss implications for designing and evaluating proactive assistants that support continued user scrutiny of answers alongside personalization.

papers.title: DyRadio: Spatiotemporal Diffusion for Dynamic Radio Map Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Accurate radio map (RM) reconstruction is essential for environment-aware wireless networks. Sampling-based methods, which infer radio conditions from sparse measurements, are widely adopted because they do not require explicit knowledge of transmitter configurations. However, in dynamic environments, time-varying propagation conditions cause RMs to evolve, complicating reconstruction from temporally distributed sparse observations. Although cross-frame observations provide complementary spatial information, their direct aggregation can introduce temporal state mismatch. Furthermore, unknown measurement noise adds to the reconstruction difficulties. To address these challenges, we propose DyRadio, a framework that integrates spatiotemporal RM reconstruction with unknown noise estimation. Specifically, a propagation-prior-guided, noise-conditioned spatiotemporal diffusion model (DM) jointly reconstructs consecutive RMs by capturing cross-frame dependencies, while adapting to measurement noise levels. To estimate the noise level, an iterative predictive likelihood method alternates between DM-based blind-area prediction and noise-level updates. The estimated noise level then conditions reconstruction of the complete RM sequence. Experimental results demonstrate superior reconstruction accuracy and robustness against measurement noise, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) improvements of 1.18-5.75 dB over the best-performing baseline across all evaluated settings.

papers.title: Seeing What Matters, Verifying What Pays: Load-Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates vision-language model (VLM) inference without altering the output distribution, yet two factors limit its gains. Existing drafters either lack the image evidence required for visually grounded tokens or pay to condition on every visual token, although a short draft block typically depends on only a few image regions.
