authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Interaction-Enabled Bulk-Boundary Correspondence without a Global Band Gap
papers.abstract: A challenge of growing interest is how to make topology observable when conventional gap-based frameworks no longer suffice. In bulk-edge correspondence, this challenge arises when the global band gap closes and localized boundary modes disappear, even though the bulk topology remains intact. Here we show that interactions unlock a novel emergent boundary response from this spectrally hidden topology without reopening the global band gap. These interaction-induced excitations originate from a bulk-band minimum, yet reconstruct the characteristic boundary channels of a gapped topological parent sharing the same Bloch eigenspaces. We establish this interaction-enabled bulk-boundary correspondence for first- and higher-order topology in one- and two-dimensional bosonic lattices, respectively, and identify a general compatibility principle governing its emergence. Our results extend bulk-boundary correspondence beyond its conventional spectral manifestation, with experimental prospects in cold-atom and photonic platforms.

authors.name: Zhifu Shi
authors.institution: PLA Rocket Force University of Engineering

authors.name: Yuqing Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ying Hu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Same Trajectory, Different Knowledge: Information-State-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Search Agents
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation trains search agents with teacher feedback on student-generated trajectories. Recent methods augment the teacher's context with supporting evidence, reference answers, or hindsight information. However, this privileged information may allow the teacher to rely on facts that the student cannot reliably recover from its current state. The resulting information-state mismatch can lead the teacher to undervalue retrieval that helps the student establish those facts. To address this mismatch, we introduce Information-State-Aware Distillation (ISA-Distill), which adapts teacher feedback to the student's factual recoverability. ISA-Distill estimates how reliably the student can recover action-relevant knowledge and derives teacher feedback for the same sampled action from two complementary views. The fact-use view supplies the teacher with the relevant fact, producing feedback that guides the student in using knowledge. The evidence-seeking view instead presents the information need, producing feedback that guides the student in acquiring supporting evidence. The two signals are weighted toward fact use when recoverability is high and toward evidence seeking when it is low, and the resulting feedback guides policy optimization. Experiments across diverse QA benchmarks and model scales demonstrate improved answer accuracy and retrieval efficiency. Our code and model checkpoints will be open-sourced.

authors.name: Zhijing Wu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
papers.abstract:
Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are promising for local inference because sparse routing allows the routed-expert pool to reside on SSD while DRAM caches recently used experts. However, under practical DRAM cache capacities, substantial SSD I/O remains on the critical path despite I/O-computation overlap. Token-level dynamic expert precision offers a natural way to reduce this data demand by allocating bits according to expert importance and quantization sensitivity. Nevertheless, treating each bit-width of the same expert as an independent object prevents cross-precision cache reuse, causing overlapping data to be fetched repeatedly.
  The key insight is that precision should instead denote the refinement depth of one shared expert state. Based on this insight, we present PagedMoE, which stores each expert once using a prefix-compatible tree codebook and bitplane layout. Lower-precision representations are valid prefixes of higher-precision ones, allowing cached data to be reused or extended by fetching only missing bitplanes. PagedMoE selects the required prefix length before I/O using current routing weights and offline expert-specific error profiles, and directly executes cached 1-8-bit prefixes without materializing full-precision experts.
  At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits, PagedMoE achieves quality close to GPTQ-INT4 on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and to MXFP4 on most evaluated GLM5.2 tasks. With a 24 GiB expert cache, it reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5, 1.33x the throughput of the same dynamic requests using independent precision objects and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution.

authors.name: Mingxing Zhang
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Constraint Dependency Graph Retrieval for Compliance Detection on Long SKILL Documents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents carry out business operations under enterprise documents we refer to as SKILL documents, which take the form of standard operating procedures (SOPs) that state the conditions to verify and the actions to take before an operation proceeds. Long, densely cross-referenced SKILL documents exceed the context budget of small deployed auditors. Similarity-based retrieval then brings in irrelevant rules while omitting mandatory prerequisites, and the two-stage audit policy provides no trainable signal for the retrieval stage. We present SkillCDG, a compliance detection framework that reformulates each SKILL document as a constraint dependency graph, shifting rule retrieval from similarity-based matching to closure-based selection under the deployment's context budget. Each atomic rule is anchored to its source text span as a graph node, and mandatory prerequisite relations form the sole edge type. Policy-generated retrieval keywords activate seed rules, whose dependency closure yields a compact and conditionally complete rule context within that budget. The same graph also supports a joint optimization scheme. The retrieval stage is trained with group-relative policy optimization using a verifiable reward that combines output-format validity with downstream verdict correctness, with closure non-emptiness serving as a validity gate, while selective on-policy distillation concentrates teacher supervision on high-entropy reasoning tokens, with verdict and termination tokens always included, to improve verdict accuracy. Experiments on three enterprise datasets and two public benchmarks show that SkillCDG improves accuracy and F1 over the full-document and retrieval-based baselines.

authors.name: Jiaye Lin
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
papers.abstract: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

authors.name: Yihan Fang
authors.institution: Anhui University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Zhanqi Zhang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Zhen Yang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Testing Exogeneity in Nonparametric Instrumental Variable Models
papers.abstract: We propose a test of mean exogeneity in nonparametric instrumental variable models. Under completeness, the null is equivalent to a conditional moment restriction involving the ordinary regression function, so the test avoids estimation of the structural function and its ill-posed inverse problem. We construct a residual-marked empirical process and analyze it through an auxiliary U-process of order two. We derive its limiting distributions under the null and Pitman-type local alternatives of order $n^{-1/2}$, and establish consistency against fixed global alternatives. The analysis reveals a nonparametric estimation effect that invalidates a direct multiplier bootstrap. We propose a computationally simple multiplier bootstrap with a tailor-made indicator correction to account for this effect, and establish its asymptotic validity. Simulations show good size control and power gains over existing methods in the nonparametric designs considered. An application to a wage equation provides evidence against the mean exogeneity of schooling.

papers.title: Experimental Realization of Higher-order Topological Water Wave Crystal
papers.abstract: Free-surface water waves provide a macroscopic platform in which topological localization can be measured through surface-elevation fields. Higher-order topological phases offer a route to localizing wave modes at structural corners, yet their experimental realization in water-wave systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a water-wave higher-order topological crystal, where surface waves are confined to structural corners and spectrally identified through measured free-surface responses. Bulk band analysis and finite-system simulations predict topological edge and corner states in the designed structure, while frequency-resolved surface-elevation measurements confirm the corresponding localized modes. The measured spectra and field distributions reveal pronounced in-gap corner localization consistent with the predicted higher-order topological modes. These results establish surface water waves as a directly measurable platform for higher-order topological physics, enabling spatial localization and spectral characterization of hydrodynamic wave modes.

authors.name: Qinhui Jiang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Infinitely many negative terms in two weighted partition sequences
papers.abstract: Recently, Andrews and El Bachraoui introduced partition-counting functions $a_2(n)$ and $b_2(n)$, together with their signed analogues $a'_2(n)$ and $b'_2(n)$, and proved that $a'_2(n), b'_2(n)>0$ for all $n\geq 3$. For $m\geq 2$, the latter functions extend naturally to $a'_m(n)$ and $b'_m(n)$, defined by \begin{align*} \sum_{n\geq 0} a'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q}{1-q} \frac{(q^m;q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{(1-q)^2},\\ \sum_{n\geq 0} b'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q(1-q^{m-1})}{1-q} \frac{(q^{2m};q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{1-q} \left( \frac{1}{1-q} -\frac{q^{m-1}}{1-q^{m+1}} \right). \end{align*} They asked whether there exists an integer $m>2$ for which $a'_m(n)$ is eventually positive, and posed the same question for $b'_m(n)$. In this paper, we resolve these two questions.

papers.title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
papers.abstract: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. Perhaps unexpectedly, preliminary evidence has recently shown that existing single-table FMs (aka TFMs), when combined with suitable parameter-free relational encoders, can be quite competitive in practice despite zero exposure to RDB pre-training or relational data of any kind. In this work we first empirically confirm this phenomenon with a more diverse array of experiments. We then turn to our main contribution, namely, surfacing multiple complementary explanations for why TFMs behave so effectively. These explanations ultimately hinge on innate synergies whereby parameter-free encoders map relational effects to fixed-length embeddings that loosely mimic distributions for which TFMs were originally designed; in so doing, desirable single-table properties transfer to relational settings (e.g., convergent posterior predictive distributions). Collectively, our analysis forges new pathways for improving RDB FMs, particularly when we prioritize interpretability and inevitable integration within agentic systems.

authors.name: Jixiang He
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Memory Admission and Result-Retention Sizing in an RV32IMC FPGA Soft Processor
papers.abstract: In FPGA soft processors with shared backing block RAM, memory admission can stall a multiplication after its product has been prepared. We study how admission timing changes result retention in PaceRV, our board-tested five-stage RV32IMC core, using fixed binaries and matched dynamic instructions. Offering data requests one edge earlier reduces geometric-mean Embench cycles by 18.2% and retention opportunities from 375,063 to 4,373. Admission and retention cycle gains are conditional and non-additive. Under slower reads, a 99% capture target selects an 18-edge validity window with registered requests and 28 edges with early requests, although no multiplication matched within both measurement intervals waits longer. A predeclared sizing rule predicts opportunity recovery exactly in all finite tests, including kernels excluded from model development. Independent timing analysis closely estimates execution-cycle savings. The results support choosing admission first, then deciding whether to extend validity and sizing it against an explicit capture or missed-opportunity objective.

papers.title: Quantiles, Not Points: Streaming Quantile Matching for Ordinal-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge scores are often distributionally shifted from human ratings on any given evaluation task, and post-hoc calibration (mapping LLM to human scores in a small labeled anchor set) has become a popular method to correct for this shift. In this paper we derive the calibration from two positions: that LLMaJ scores are ordinal ratings drawn from a distribution rather than isolated points. We present streaming quantile matching (SQM), a version of a classical method not previously bench marked for LLMaJ calibration, which is built on the two positions by computing the optimal-transport map between the LLM and human score distributions. We develop an evaluation framework and within it we show that unlike point-wise calibrations, SQM respects the ordinality of the human anchor set and achieves the best distributional fidelity and the top overall rank across models and data. We also show that in general, post-hoc calibration narrows the raw error gap between smaller and larger judge models, which opens the possibility of more efficient LLM judges.

papers.title: Efficient second-order physics-preserving schemes for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel second-order prediction--filter--projection framework for incompressible flows with variable density and viscosity. In this framework, a constrained $L^2$-projection is enforced to unconditionally preserve the prescribed density bounds and discrete mass conservation, while a generalized-Laplacian reformulation combined with the D-CSAV approach is used to discretize the variable-viscosity momentum equation. In particular, a density-weighted second-order time filter is proposed, which eliminates the additional uniform-in-time bound restriction imposed on the time difference quotient of the discrete density in existing stability analyses. The resulting scheme is shown to satisfy an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law, without the viscosity-related restrictions imposed in earlier work. Then, an additional scalar auxiliary variable and its compatible temporal discretization are introduced to construct a variable-step prediction--filter--projection scheme. This scheme is also bound-preserving and mass-conserving, and satisfies an unconditional modified-energy dissipation law. Moreover, the modified energy is much closer to the ``original'' kinetic energy, differing from it only through the auxiliary-variable corrections. Based on the variable-step scheme, a reliable energy-based adaptive time-stepping strategy is developed. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, physics-preserving properties, and efficiency of the proposed schemes.

papers.title: Step-Zero Attack: Agent Safety Before Observability
papers.abstract: Existing attacks and defenses for coding agents act once content enters the model context: injected text persuades the model, and guards inspect what the model reads. Yet to judge whether processing an unknown archive, network response, or image is safe, an agent often must process it first, and that step can do harm before any content reaches the model. We call this first processing Step Zero, and harm done by it a Step-Zero attack. Across seven harnesses and six models, each agent received only a path or URL to a crafted input, paired with a benign twin showing the same visible fields. Step Zero is where most agents are already unsafe: 32/42 harness-model pairs overran a 4 MiB disk budget, 26/42 before the model saw any member, and four of the six models did so in every round (84/84), so the damage precedes any model-side defense. Every twin stayed within budget, so the attacker's bytes alone cause the harm. On network and image inputs the risk moves to what the agent writes: agents stored the body under the name the input declared, letting the input decide what is written, and their checks faded once cues were removed. Model-free tests trace the harm to the processing primitive, so we defend it there: a gate that counts the bytes each call produces held every routed extraction within budget while agents completed 25/28 tasks. Vendors should pair such gates with safety-alignment training that teaches agents to inspect an input before processing it.

authors.name: Tian Qin
authors.institution: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

authors.name: Junzhe Chen
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical College

papers.title: Positive Safety Margins from Artificial Potential Field Reward Augmentation for Size-Robust Obstacle Avoidance under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: Collision-free reaching is central to manipulation, yet real cells often leave the size and exact position of an obstacle unobserved, which excludes reinforcement learning controllers that take obstacle geometry as input. A reward limited to a collision penalty does not depend on the clearance outside the obstacle, so under a step cost its learned policy skims the obstacle surface and fails once the obstacle radius exceeds its training value. We investigate whether a single analytic reward term can induce a safety margin without exposing the obstacle to the policy. We augment the reward of a simulated Franka Emika Panda reaching task with a horizontal artificial potential field that penalizes proximity within a safety margin around each of two pillars (fixed nominal layout, random drift). Under hidden observation, policies trained with this term maintain a safe success rate above 88% across a radius sweep from 0.03 m to 0.055 m (30 seeds), while policies without it fall below 10% at the maximum tested radius; the term induces a minimum clearance of 47.9 mm against 9.6 mm without it and eliminates training collisions at least eight times earlier (median steps). The advantage is statistically significant at all out-of-distribution radii and holds across three reinforcement learning solvers and under full observation. Its safe success rate is comparable to that of a classical potential-field planner given the pillar positions. The margin is a fixed buffer rather than an adaptation to the radius, and it lengthens the path by about 19%.

papers.title: Interval-valued circular time series: A cylindrical score-driven approach with an application to wind direction
papers.abstract: Interval-valued circular observations arise naturally in a wide range of environmental applications, particularly in wind direction monitoring, where directional measurements are observed by an interval of recorded directions over a period. An existing dynamic approach for interval-valued circular time series models the interval boundaries directly on the torus. While such an approach preserves the circular nature of the endpoints, an alternative approach is to consider the centre-range representation of circular intervals. This paper proposes a cylindrical score-driven framework for interval-valued circular time series by representing each interval through a circular centre and a bounded linear width. Dynamic conditional score recursions are developed for the centre and range processes, allowing circular-linear dependence to be captured jointly within a likelihood-based framework. To develop this model, various cylindrical distributions are introduced to accommodate bounded range values. The estimators are investigated through simulations, and the practical usefulness of the framework is illustrated using interval-valued wind direction data from South African and Brazilian wind farms. The proposed methodology provides an alternative approach for modelling the interval-valued circular processes using the directional location and dispersion in interval-valued circular observations.

papers.title: L2-contraction and Asymptotic Stability of Monotone Shock Waves for Cubic and Quartic KdV-Burgers Equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear stability of monotone traveling shock waves arising in the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation with a power-law flux, focusing on the cubic and quartic cases p=3 and p=4, respectively, in the presence of both dissipative and dispersive effects. Since shocks connecting distinct end states destroy the integrable structure of the equation, we introduce a slowly varying reference connection to establish global well-posedness for the Cauchy problem in an affine Sobolev space. A key ingredient in the stability analysis is to establish a new two-sided comparison estimate for the derivative of a monotone shock-wave profile. After a monotone coordinate transformation, this estimate allows the viscous dissipation to be compared with the natural vanishing weight arising in a shifted Poincare inequality. Together with an $L^\infty$ bootstrap controlling the higher-order relative-flux terms, this yields a global $L^2$-contraction property modulo a time-dependent shift for sufficiently small $H^1$ perturbations in the admissible parameter regimes. We obtain exponential decay of the shock profile and show asymptotic convergence to the shifted shock in $L^q(\R)$, $2<q\leq \infty$, with vanishing shift velocity.

papers.title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
papers.abstract: Uncertainties in weather, user behavior, and distributed energy production introduce significant variability into feeder power. Effective power system operations require both multi-horizon load forecasts and well-calibrated extreme quantiles for the forecast. Nevertheless, standard objectives that fit the full forecast distribution often underemphasize rare observations and extremes. Conversely, applying heavy tail-weighting in the distribution to capture these extremes can distort the underlying probability distribution. To address this issue, this paper proposes adaptive residual modeling for scenario learning (ARMSL), a two-stage framework. Particularly, Stage I in our framework sequentially models environmental response, history-dependent load patterns, persistent residual deviations, and the remaining innovations. Upon the modeling, we then generate joint active- and reactive-power scenarios with state-dependent dispersion. Stage II keeps the scenario model fixed and calibrates extreme marginal quantiles using a simple, channel-specific reference forecast (an anchor). Only outward deviations from this anchor are admitted, with their contribution determined by local calibration history and the current operating state. From our numerical simulations on FeederBW dataset, Stage I outperforms diffusion baselines in energy and variogram scores. Our complete framework achieves an active-power 0.99-quantile pinball loss of 0.1932 (a 30.08% to 85.33% reduction relative to three baselines) with 1.054% exceedance rate against a nominal 1%. From simulations on the Rolle dataset, we observe decreased losses by 5.39%--14.40% compared to the active-power-only anchor. Furthermore, the unchanged Stage I scenarios in the simulation yield a correlation of 0.953 between predicted and observed feeder event rates, with 90.0% of feeder errors falling within two percentage points.

authors.name: Jun Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
papers.abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.

authors.name: Hao Chang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
papers.abstract:
We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates.
  The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution.
  We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.

papers.title: Spatial degeneracy along weak geodesics in the space of K\"ahler potentials
papers.abstract: We study spatial Hessian degeneracy along weak K\"ahler geodesics. We construct examples in three settings: (1) On every compact K\"ahler manifold, the spatial form degenerates on a nonempty open set during an interior time interval, although both endpoints are smooth and strictly K\"ahler. (2) On ALE K\"ahler manifolds with a holomorphic quotient end and a decaying potential to the Euclidean metric, spatial degeneracy occurs on open regions arbitrarily far along an unbounded horn. (3) For cone and Poincar\'e endpoint metrics along a smooth divisor, normal spatial degeneracy occurs on open sets approaching the divisor. Both cone endpoints retain the prescribed angle. The first construction answers negatively the spatial-positivity question recorded in Darvas's survey. The ALE and divisor constructions show that weak geodesics need not preserve the asymptotic behavior of the endpoint metrics.

papers.title: Twisting-free converse theorems for $\Gamma_0(32)$ and $\Gamma_0(36)$
papers.abstract: We prove twisting-free converse theorems for $\Gamma_0(32)$ and $\Gamma_0(36)$ under the setting of Conrey--Farmer, namely assuming a single functional equation and a suitable Euler product, with particular shapes at ramified primes. The proofs make substantial use of the ramified primes, with methods somewhat different from the existing ones in the literature.

papers.title: What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generators produce long videos block by block, using historical context to maintain temporal consistency. After denoising, a committing pass encodes each clean block into keys and values (KV) that later blocks read, and the same clean block can be encoded into different KV depending on the history it reads. We therefore study historical context not only as a condition for denoising but also as an input to committing. Older historical context that supports denoising can harm subsequent generation when read during committing. At fixed context size and temporal positions, older historical context lowers mean clip-to-clip Subject Consistency. Across 5 generator configurations supporting longer contexts, consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines as committing context expands. Motivated by these findings, we propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. During committing, each block reads only the preceding block's stored KV, so older historical context reaches new entries only through the chain. We apply this rule to 6 pretrained generators. On 60-second VBench, Commit Forcing improves Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 Quality points and 1.10 Total points. Long-range consistency gains extend to 240-second videos. In a blinded comparison on 120-second LongLive videos, Commit Forcing achieves win rates of 83.5% for subject and scene consistency and 82.9% for overall preference against the base generator, excluding ties.

authors.name: Haofan Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting: A New Paradigm for Wireless Environment Representation
papers.abstract: Wireless channels are shaped by the surrounding propagation environment, making explicit environment representation an effective approach for characterizing channels. By combining explicit environment modeling with learnable radio frequency characteristics, 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) emerges as a new paradigm for wireless environment representation. This article establishes a systematic perspective on 3DGS-enabled wireless communications in terms of environment representation. We first clarify the rationale for extending 3DGS from visual scene modeling to wireless communications and formulate a unified framework for wireless environment representation. Building on this framework, we further investigate the applicability of 3DGS-based representations to a broad range of communication and sensing tasks, and characterize key considerations for practical deployment. Finally, emerging directions are highlighted, including cross-scene generalization, near-field channel modeling, real-world data collection, and lifecycle management.

papers.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Linear Programming
papers.abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman-Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale linear programming problems. We first introduce the semi-proximal HPR framework and summarize its convergence guarantees, together with its connections to Halpern PDHG and ergodic Peaceman-Rachford iterations. To improve practical performance, we develop adaptive restart and penalty parameter update strategies. We then describe several computational enhancements, including GPU-based preprocessing, diagonal scaling, reusable execution plans for sparse matrix-vector multiplication, and sieving techniques. We further discuss multi-GPU parallelization and lossless model storage and loading for handling large-scale instances. These developments form the foundation of HPR-LP, a GPU-accelerated solver for large-scale linear programming.

authors.name: Kaihuang Chen
authors.institution: Hsiuping University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yijia Liang
authors.institution: Jiangsu Center for Collaborative Innovation in Geographical Information Resource Development and Application

papers.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Convex Composite Quadratic Programming
papers.abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman--Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale convex composite quadratic programming problems. Within a unified HPR framework applied to the restricted Wolfe dual, we develop several algorithmic variants based on different choices of the semi-proximal operator $\mathcal{T}_1$ for the joint dual subproblem. Specifically, an sGS-based construction leads to a sequential $w$--$y$--$w$ update scheme, while a block-linearized construction eliminates cross-block coupling and enables parallel dual updates. To improve the latter, we further introduce a coupling-aware construction that exploits a second spectral moment to obtain a tighter row majorizer. We extend the framework to convex quadratically constrained quadratic programming through factor-based second-order cone reformulations. Additional computational enhancements include equality Gram scaling and asynchronous CPU polishing. We establish convergence results under fixed metrics and discuss practical adaptive strategies.

authors.name: Kaihuang Chen
authors.institution: Hsiuping University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
papers.abstract: The composition of X-ray burst ashes affects the thermal transport properties of the neutron star crust, as well as heating and cooling through weak interaction processes. Reaction-rate uncertainties can produce secondary peaks separated from the main peak in final abundance distributions. Using STARLIB reaction rates and their temperature-dependent uncertainties in the K04 one-zone post-processing model, we combine four sets of Monte Carlo calculations with XGBoost classification, SHAP analysis, and reaction-flow analysis to investigate the origins of these secondary peaks. We find that the competing $(p,\alpha)$ and $(p,\gamma)$ reaction pairs on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ are primarily responsible for secondary peaks outside the central 68\% confidence interval in all 44 isotopes examined. Fixing both pairs at their median rates reduces the fractions of samples in the secondary-peak regions by 96\%--100\%, while the bounds of the central 68\% interval remain largely unchanged for most mass numbers. The $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ pair has the larger effect. Enhanced recycling limits the supply of material to heavier isotopes and accelerates proton consumption, while earlier proton exhaustion further suppresses subsequent proton captures. These changes alter the balance between isotope production and destruction, leading to high- or low-abundance secondary peaks over a broad mass range beyond the Ni--Cu and Zn--Ga cycles. These results identify $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}(p,\gamma)^{60}\mathrm{Zn}$ and the two competing channels on $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ as priorities for further nuclear-physics constraints to improve XRB abundance predictions.

papers.title: Agent Memory as Rate-Limited Filtering: Explicit State Outlasts Long Context Beyond a Reader-Dependent Horizon
papers.abstract: Can a language model that reads the full history of an access log say whether a service may act now? On an executable benchmark of grants, withdrawals, reinstatements, expiries, groups and change windows under a known policy, scored on pairs of histories that differ only in the order or one field of the deciding events, open models of 7 to 32 billion parameters fall from 72 to 86 percent after eight or sixteen events to 48 to 55 percent after 256, while reasoning-trained 32B models reading the current state reach 96 and 98 percent. A reasoning model of 120 billion parameters trails the state by four and seven points at 256 and 512 events and by about ten at 1,024, so the length beyond which explicit state outlasts long context grows with the reader. We treat agent memory as recursive filtering. The decision depends on the history only through a state whose size is set by the number of tracked keys. A store holding fewer component records than the state forgets on a time scale set by its capacity, and a reader model predicts its accuracy within 0.02 on average in a registered test. Retaining log lines without regard to time order errs with probability approaching one half, a bound that is attained. A filter in which a model parses each line and an explicit rule applies the updates answers 80 to 89 percent at 256 events and beats relevance retrieval, model-kept ledgers, a reimplementation of StateMem and the Mem0 library. A retriever that selects at query time the lines the queried state depends on matches it at 256 events on the first domain, so what decides is selection by the state's dependencies, which the filter performs when writing, without the query. Applying parsed updates themselves, the models fall to 58 and 59 percent. A frozen replication on a second domain with fresh wording reproduces the horizon.

papers.title: RecGroupMemory: Feedback-Aware Cohort Memory for E-Commerce Recommendation
papers.abstract: Cohort memory can support LLM-based recommendation planning through group-level user profiles and advice. As outcome feedback becomes available, this guidance may need to be updated while preserving the underlying observations. We present RecGroupMemory, a workflow that provides this memory to an orchestration LLM and separates memory construction from feedback-based revision. It uses feedback from the previous day to revise decision guidance, while validation checks keep selected source values unchanged. Online comparisons were conducted among Taobao users with low purchasing power selected by the business team. Relative to a no-memory baseline, memory without feedback and memory with feedback showed increases of 1.58% and 1.78%, respectively, in the number of guided transaction users.

authors.name: Bin Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Subgradient Methods for Nonsmooth Sample Average Approximation
papers.abstract: We study direct subgradient methods for nonsmooth sample average approximation (SAA). Subgradient descent and Nesterov acceleration with constant step sizes attain polynomial and geometric rates matching their smooth counterparts. After $O(\log n)$ full-batch updates, where $n$ is the sample size, the computed solution has the same first-order expansion and limiting distribution as an SAA solution, even when the iterates do not converge. A bound on subgradient increments transfers population regularity to the sample objective, controls the algorithmic trajectory, and identifies the leading random term. The bound covers convex piecewise linear scenario costs, including two-stage stochastic linear programs with fixed recourse. Moreau smoothing displaces the population solution at first order and changes the limiting distribution of the computed solution. An explicit shift of the residual removes the first-order displacement and improves the expansion remainder. For sparse decisions, restricted increment bounds give convergence, support recovery, and expansions for proximal subgradient descent and iterative hard thresholding.

papers.title: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
papers.abstract: Complex video editing requires understanding complex instructions while jointly fulfilling multiple editing requests. Meeting these demands through dense model scaling substantially increases computational cost. We introduce VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing. Beyond sparse MLP-MoE layers, MoE-Attention expands attention capacity through routed key--value experts while preserving global interactions among video tokens. Initialized from a 5B video editing model, VideoEditor-MoE scales to 14B and 56B parameters, with approximately 8B parameters activated per token in both variants. Comparisons with existing methods and two complementary baselines, Explicit-MoE and MLP-MoE, assess its benefits over explicit expert guidance and MLP-only expert architectures. Further analyses demonstrate that all experts remain active and reveal that learned routing responds more strongly to sample content and diffusion noise levels than to human-defined editing categories. Spatial analysis further indicates sensitivity to object-level semantic features. We also identify decoupled weight decay as a strategy for stabilizing expert scaling.

papers.title: An Agentic OS Kernel for Flexible and Enhanced Semantics
papers.abstract:
Modern OS kernels expose general-purpose but rigid interfaces (e.g., syscalls) that are slow to evolve due to compatibility, performance, and security constraints, leaving apps to pay for mismatched semantics and legacy APIs. Existing kernel mechanism customization approaches (e.g., eBPF) improve flexibility but still face strict safety and performance restrictions and thus require substantial expertise. What's more, they targets customized kernel mechanisms rather than kernel abstractions.
  This paper presents agentic kernel, a new architecture that decomposes monolithic syscall functions into fine-grained, composable kernel-native micro-syscalls, and then enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to orchestrate them dynamically. Agentic kernel introduces a new entry, isyscall (intent syscall), which lets apps submit high-level intents describing their requirements. Then the kernel leverages LLMs to resolve each intent into composition plan of micro-syscalls to satisfy the user's goal. LLMs can further optimize the plan continuously at kernel runtime. To eliminate LLM inference costs on the critical path, agentic kernel caches and reuses verified plans to bypass LLM entirely. Crucially, agentic kernel's safety guarantees are independent of LLM correctness: micro-syscalls follows syscall-level security mechanisms, ensuring OS safety under arbitrary combinations and orchestration.
  We implement agentic kernel in Linux, called IntentOS, and evaluate it across four kernel versions and three application domains (about ten intents each). IntentOS outperforms baseline Linux in real-world applications, achieving up to 17.55% latency reduction for backend processes creation, 6.97% performance gain for multiple files operations, and 75.52% lower performance impact for frontend Nginx server during memory operations triggered by backend tasks.

authors.name: Haocheng Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic by Construction from Triangular Standard Contradictions
papers.abstract: Automated theorem generation (ATG) seeks to construct new theorems rather than merely prove given conjectures. Existing approaches typically generate candidate statements that require subsequent proof or formal verification. We propose a constructive framework for ATG in first-order logic based on triangular standard contradictions. The method constructs minimally unsatisfiable clause sets from selected first-order literals, then forms theorems by retaining some clauses as premises and taking the negation of one clause, or a conjunction of clauses, as the conclusion. Minimal unsatisfiability ensures that the remaining premises are satisfiable, avoiding trivial inference by explosion, while unsatisfiability of the full set guarantees the resulting entailment. Theorems are therefore correct by construction, without a separate proof procedure for each instance. Extending the previously developed $\Delta_1$ generator, we introduce seven methods, $\Delta_2$--$\Delta_8$, forming a unified family of eight theorem-generation methods. Four generators, $\Delta_1$--$\Delta_4$, have been implemented and released. We also formulate a general $\Delta$-class method encompassing the family. Combinatorial analysis demonstrates the capacity to generate large numbers of distinct theorems systematically. This framework offers a principled foundation for automated theorem discovery and the construction of logically guaranteed knowledge.

authors.name: Hailin Guo
authors.institution: Institute of Botany, Jiangsu Province and Chinese Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Jun Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Explicit Boundary-Entropy Deficits in the XX Spin Chain with arbitrary boundary fields
papers.abstract: The exact thermodynamics of the XX spin-1/2 chain with arbitrary Hermitian boundary fields is constructed via fusion techniques. The rigorous result shows that (1) each end with a nonzero transverse field contributes $+\frac12T\ln2$ to the low-temperature free energy, whereas strictly diagonal and free ends contribute no such linear term; (2) each nondiagonal end has a characteristic temperature $T_B$, which scales as $T_B\propto h_\perp^2/J$ in the weak-field regime. For $T\ll\min\{J,T_B\}$, the boundary entropy approaches a deficit of $\frac12\ln2$ relative to a diagonal end. As the transverse field tends to zero, the boundary crossover scale vanishes and the low-temperature expansion becomes nonuniform. The present result provides a clear benchmark not only for the boundary thermodynamics of open boundary quantum integrable systems, but also for dot defects in quantum critical systems.

authors.name: Yi Qiao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Digital Medical Engineering

papers.title: Ground state and excitations of the \(C_2^{(1)}\) spin chain with non-diagonal boundaries
papers.abstract: Understanding boundary effects in higher-rank integrable quantum spin chains requires connecting exact spectral relations with the root configurations underlying their energies and excitations. With non-diagonal boundaries, determining these configurations remains challenging even when an exact spectral solution is available, hindering the direct extraction of thermodynamic properties. We address this problem for the rational $C_2^{(1)}$ chain by combining DMRG in the tensor-network framework with the quantum inverse scattering method. The numerically determined zeros of the fundamental and fused transfer-matrix eigenvalues reveal three bulk-string distributions, labeled by $x$, $y$, and $w$, together with boundary strings and additional roots. Substituting these configurations into the operator identities relating the two transfer matrices yields the ground-state energy and the surface energy in the thermodynamic limit under non-diagonal boundary conditions. The analytical surface energy agrees with the numerical results up to $O(\tfrac1N)$ corrections. From the regularity conditions of the operator identities, we derive a boundary-string selection rule and numerically identify allowed configurations beyond the ground state. For excitations preserving the boundary-string configuration, we identify three elementary hole excitations, $X$, $Y$, and $W$, in the $x$-, $y$-, and $w$-string distributions, respectively, and derive their energies. Based on the symmetry of the zero roots, we also present a bulk-excitation selection rule governing the allowed combinations of these elementary excitations in physical eigenstates. The framework developed here can therefore be used to systematically analyze boundary effects, bulk excitations, and related physical properties in other high-rank integrable quantum models with non-diagonal boundary conditions.

authors.name: Yi Qiao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Digital Medical Engineering

papers.title: Counting Feedback Vertex Sets of All Sizes in Subexponential Time, Conditionally
papers.abstract: Assuming a Boolean tensor contraction hypothesis (Theorem D.1 of OpenAI's recent preprint refuting the Exponential Time Hypothesis), we study exact feedback vertex set counting in general graphs. For an $n$-vertex, $m$-edge simple graph, we compute the complete size distribution deterministically in $\mathrm{poly}(n+m)\,2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}$ time and polynomial working space. The algorithm combines a whole-edge forest identity, subset-index scalar networks, sparse parity filtering, and disjoint high-degree branching. A binomial inversion recovers the multiplicities introduced by exceptional-set guesses. The counting interface supports fixed vertices, minimum solutions, and unranking. Component markers yield induced-tree and induced-path counts within the same bound. Sparse Hamilton, forest, and Steiner edge-tree counting follow from the scalar encoding.

authors.name: Minghao Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Circuit Lower Bounds for Extended Gate Bases from Subexponential Counting
papers.abstract: We study circuit lower bounds for extended gate bases using exact CNF counting and an extension-ring form of the contraction theorem of OpenAI. The deterministic counting theorem of Claude (Anthropic) yields an $\mathsf{E}^{\mathsf{NP}}$ language requiring $\Omega(m\sqrt{\log m}/\log\log m)$ gates over unbounded AND/OR with binary XOR, infinitely often. Using that contraction theorem, a bounded binary base with a linear budget of arbitrary XOR and symmetric gates requires $\Omega(m\sqrt{\log m})$ gates infinitely often. These results extend the binary-gate lower bound of OpenAI. Signed long-clause selectors reduce the first counting problem to the difference of two ordinary 3-CNF counts. Affine characters and unit-separated interpolation give the second counting interface, with logarithmic cost per symmetric-gate arity. A quantitative local-reduction transfer accounts for auxiliary variables, branch counts, and integer recovery.

authors.name: Minghao Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learned Diffusion Channel Priors for Coded MIMO Turbo Receivers
papers.abstract: Iterative receivers for coded multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) links estimate the channel from pilots, decoded data, and a prior. In short packets with few pilots and at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the prior matters. An expectation propagation (EP) turbo receiver needs the channel's mean and covariance given an anisotropic Gaussian message from the pilots and decoder. A diffusion prior's denoiser, however, returns only a mean, and only for a channel in isotropic noise. We replace only the receiver's channel-prior module with a learned diffusion prior. At an isotropic query formed from the message, one network gives both moments: its output is the mean, its Jacobian the covariance. They form a matrix-valued EP site, the Gaussian factor representing the prior. We show why an indefinite Jacobian can make the receiver diverge, and we floor its eigenvalues. In coded block error rate (BLER), the diffusion prior fails less than a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) prior learned from the same channels. It does so on a controlled sparse specular model and a 3GPP model, at every tested receive-array and training-set size. On the former, scalar-site controls, with one variance instead of the covariance, keep this advantage, so the gain comes from the diffusion prior.

authors.name: Hyeji Kim
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Jeonghun Park
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
papers.abstract: Fourier phase retrieval reconstructs images from magnitude measurements without phase information, but noise and channel ambiguities make natural color-image recovery challenging. Although diffusion-prior methods provide strong image constraints, their recovery can deteriorate under stronger measurement noise, and repeated generative updates incur substantial computational cost. This paper proposes FlowFPR, which integrates a pretrained Flow Matching prior with relaxed averaged alternating reflections for oversampled Fourier phase retrieval. Each outer iteration obtains a clean image estimate through a single time-dependent Flow prediction, applies measurement-consistency correction, and reconstructs the next path state after fusing the two candidates. This process requires no backpropagation of measurement errors through the Flow network. To address ineffective or excessive correction caused by prescribed fusion weights and fixed inner depths, we introduce adaptive fusion based on residual improvement and a controlled inner search combining early stopping with best-so-far candidate selection. Their combination yields a joint variant alongside the basic method and the two independent improvements. Experiments on natural face images under a common ground-truth-assisted multiple-restart evaluation protocol show that the joint variant achieves the best mean quality among the evaluated methods at the two tested nonzero noise levels, while same-hardware timing demonstrates lower end-to-end runtime than the diffusion-based baselines.

papers.title: On-the-fly $\Delta$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly $\Delta$-machine learned force field ($\Delta$-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that $\Delta$-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm$^3$ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.

papers.title: Cross-Lingual Persona Effects in LLM Negotiation
papers.abstract: Tell an LLM negotiator to be "headstrong" and it should hold firm on price, but does that instruction retain the same behavior in every language? To test this, we use identical buyer and seller instances of Gemini 3.6 Flash to negotiate the same 12 CraigslistBargain scenarios in English and Korean. The pilot-scale 2 x 2 x 3 design crosses interaction language, seller urgency (none or strong), and buyer persona (cooperative, neutral, or headstrong), yielding 432 attempted negotiations. We call this property cross-lingual social-policy fidelity: whether a prompt-defined social policy produces the same behavioral effect regardless of interaction language. It often does not. Korean negotiations reached agreement far more often than English (77.3% vs. 52.5%, a 24.8-point gap, Holm-adjusted p = .0039), but only for neutral and headstrong buyers; cooperative buyers were already near-ceiling in both languages. Buyers' opening offers barely differed by language; the gap instead emerged later, through larger seller concessions and a smaller final gap in Korean, and agreed prices were also lower in Korean. Repeating the full design with Qwen3.7 Flash as both agents gives directional support: agreement was again higher in Korean (+13.9 points vs. Gemini's +24.8, with an interval whose lower bound is near zero), and sellers again conceded more. Pragmatic analysis reveals why: while both languages frequently featured face-threatening acts like rejections and counter-offers, Korean dialogue softened these threats with substantially more politeness mitigation, especially among sellers (11.7% vs. 3.6%). These results show that such a policy can produce different simulated negotiation behavior, not just different wording, when only the interaction language changes.

papers.title: Quantum Dipolar Magnon Drag in Conducting Magnetic Bilayers
papers.abstract: We predict electrical drag between two electrically isolated metallic ferromagnets mediated by quantum dipolar magnon coupling. A charge current in one layer generates a nonequilibrium magnon current whose momentum is transferred across an insulating spacer through interlayer dipolar interactions. The resulting magnon current in the passive layer produces a measurable voltage through electron-magnon scattering. We show the combination of resonant quantum momentum transfer and magnetic tunability through the control of magnetization configurations distinguish quantum dipolar drag from conventional drag mechanism.

papers.title: BEEF: A Hybrid Integrated Photonic Simulation Framework
papers.abstract: A Python framework is presented that retains first-principles electromagnetic modeling while extending simulation to devices whose length and geometric complexity place them beyond the practical reach of either method alone. The Bridged Engine for eigenmode expansion (EME) and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) (BEEF) partitions a device into sections which are simulated using either EME or FDTD independently developed Maxwell solvers depending on what best suits each section's geometry, and cascades the resulting responses. BEEF calibrates the EME propagation constants against FDTD-measured phase accumulation, providing a mode identity verification diagnostic across solver interfaces. For a 2x2 multimode-interference splitter, the hybrid result agrees with full-device FDTD to within 0.59% (bar) and 0.76% (cross) across the C-band; a tapered variant agrees to within 0.87% and 2.01%, respectively. For a directional coupler, effective-index calibration reduces cut-position dependence 167-fold. A circuit-level cascade reproduces the measured Fabry-Perot resonance lineshape and free spectral range while exploring the coupler-length and arm-length design plane through post-processing of four cached simulations. Finally, we use BEEF to simulate a 167.3 um-long 4x4 MMI-based 90-degree optical hybrid that is computationally impractical for full-device FDTD, with a reduced-length variant confirming close agreement in transmission and relative phase.

papers.title: A Parallel Adaptive Proximal ADMM for Linearly Constrained Separable Composite Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze an adaptive proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), based on Jacobi-type updates, for linearly constrained separable nonconvex composite optimization problems. The objective consists of two block-separable functions, one continuously differentiable and weakly convex, and the other convex and Lipschitz continuous. The proposed method is adaptive to all problem parameters and allows inexact solutions of the block proximal subproblems. At each iteration, we solve all block subproblems in parallel, then apply a novel test to decide whether to update the Lagrange multiplier and/or the penalty parameter. Without any rank assumptions on the constraint matrices, we establish an ${\cal O}(\epsilon^{-3})$ iteration-complexity bound for obtaining an approximate first-order stationary point. This matches the best-known complexity for cyclic proximal ADMM methods and improves the existing complexity of Jacobi-type schemes in this general nonconvex setting. Numerical experiments on a nonconvex quadratic program illustrate the proposed method's computational benefits.

papers.title: Evolving Scientific Intelligence: From Fragmented Evidence to Distributed Experimental Loops
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery advances when evidence from different investigations is brought into contact. Yet paper-centric communication leaves experimental results fragmented, delayed, or unreported, creating a "scientific memory wall" between growing computational capabilities and the evidence accessible to AI systems. We envision a different dynamic: in a network of intelligent laboratories, a failed or overlooked experiment in one domain could trigger a hypothesis in another, whose testing generates evidence that stimulates further investigations. Such chains of information collision and empirical validation could transform isolated discovery loops into a cumulative scientific process. We propose Evolving Scientific Intelligence (ESI), an architectural blueprint for enabling these evidence-driven chain reactions. ESI preserves experimental records in shared, computable scientific memory, where evidence from different domains can be recombined into testable hypotheses. It jointly selects candidates and evaluation methods according to scientific value, reliability, and cost, then coordinates physical tests across distributed experimental nodes. Their feedback revises hypotheses and evaluators, while slower meta-control reassesses research objectives and decision criteria to guard against self-reinforcing errors and misguided optimization. We call for an Information Manhattan Project to build the infrastructure for scientific intelligence that evolves through experimentally grounded chains of discovery.

papers.title: Editing the Goal: Per-Token SAE Steering and Its Depth Limits in $\pi_{0.5}$
papers.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have recovered interpretable, causally relevant features in robot foundation models (RFMs) such as $\pi_{0.5}$ (arXiv:2603.19183, arXiv:2603.19233). SAE features on individual instruction tokens are less interpretable than timestep-pooled ones (arXiv:2603.19183), and whether they can redirect a robot's goal remains untested. We show that replacing the SAE features of a single goal word with those of an alternative goal word, leaving the instruction text unchanged, steers $\pi_{0.5}$-LIBERO into completing the alternative task. At layer 0, BatchTopK feature swaps redirect behavior in up to 20/20 rollouts in a scene where random-feature swaps redirect none, with success varying across six scenes in two LIBERO suites and across layers. The effect depends on SAE architecture: word-selected Matryoshka edits largely do not outperform random ones. SAEs are also not required. Adding a fixed difference-in-means vector at twice its natural magnitude redirects 8-10/10 rollouts. Layer-wise activation patching shows that goal-word edits remain effective up to layer 6 for object location and layer 2 for object identity, and up to layer 13 in both cases when patching also covers camera tokens. These results are proof of existence in an RFM in simulation and an initial map of how deep goal-redirecting edits remain effective. Visit https://doubleblind-sae-pi05.github.io for video rollouts.

papers.title: SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?
papers.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.

papers.title: Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR's steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay's from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.

papers.title: Adaptive Optimizers Can Get a Policy Ranking Wrong: Momentum, Dependent Data, and a Two-Run Remedy
papers.abstract: Operators choosing among decision rules, such as when a battery charges or where an idle taxi goes, rank them by estimated long-run value. A standard estimator, linear temporal-difference (TD) learning, fits values from one stream of correlated observations. Large fits often use an adaptive optimizer, such as adaptive moment estimation (Adam), with fixed averaging rates. We show that these rates can change what is estimated, not just how fast: the same observations drive the updates and the optimizer's step-size scaling, moving the fit away from the intended TD value. The shift differs across rules, so it need not cancel in a comparison, and more data only makes a wrong ranking look more certain. Our remedy refits the same data at a second averaging rate that halves the effective gain, the number to which the leading shift is proportional. Twice the new fit minus the original removes that shift. In New York taxi and battery models calibrated to real data, common optimizer settings leave the selected rule unchanged but order close rules wrongly and misstate its value. Our remedy corrects nearly every wrong ordering, with one extra fit when the shift is moderate and two when it is larger.

papers.title: WFDB-x: Conformance-Tested Implementations of the WFDB Software Package in Seven Programming Languages
papers.abstract: The WFDB format is widely used to store and exchange physiological waveforms and annotations. However, existing software implementations are limited to C, Python, and MATLAB/Octave, can produce different results in corner cases and checksum calculations, and have defaults such as sampling frequency and gain, that can lead to silent misinterpretation of recordings. We developed WFDB-x, a cross-language, performance-optimized reimplementation of WFDB in seven programming languages, with extensive unit tests, to provide consistent WFDB processing across programming languages. We reimplemented the WFDB Software Package 10.7.0 natively in Python, C++, Rust, Julia, R, MATLAB/Octave, and Kotlin, using AI-assistance under human direction and review. Each implementation has library functions, a high-level interface, and command-line tools. We compared their outputs with those of the original C programs using 1098 conformance cases, 877 legacy-mode cases, unit tests, and differential fuzzing. Deliberate changes remove implicit waveform parameters, restrict file and network access, and prevent annotation loss. A legacy mode retains the original behavior. All seven implementations passed every conformance and legacy-mode case on the tested Linux platform, with matching outputs. The unit tests contain 9353 assertions. C++, Rust, and Julia read records 1.5-6.9 times faster than the original C library, while the Python implementation wrote records 9.2 times faster than the existing wfdb-python library in the benchmark. WFDB-x provides a tested, open-source basis for reading and writing physiological recordings consistently across seven languages, supporting reproducible research and software development without requiring a shared programming environment. We also share details of the AI-assisted development process and token utilization, which may be useful for other applications.

papers.title: Launder-Bench: Can Repository-Level Agentic Code Laundering Be Detected?
papers.abstract: Coding agents can now rewrite repository-scale codebases while preserving tested behavior, creating a new challenge for plagiarism detection, license auditing, and software provenance. We ask whether such rewrites can still be traced to their source. Existing clone benchmarks emphasize fragments and bounded edits, while repository-transformation benchmarks evaluate functional correctness rather than provenance. Moreover, ranking the most similar source does not establish derivation when independent implementations can be similarly close. We define repository-level agentic code laundering and introduce Launder-Bench, to our knowledge the first repository-level benchmark for provenance under agentic rewriting, constructed from 282 real-world repositories. A source-hidden reconstruction protocol decomposes source behavior, reconstructs modules and repository structure, and retains rewrites only after execution-based verification. We evaluate the same provenance problem in two complementary settings: Launder-Bench-Pair contains 1,128 pairwise instances asking whether two repositories share provenance, while Launder-Bench-Attr contains 229 source-attribution instances asking which candidate is the source, with abstention when evidence is insufficient. Measured same-domain independent repositories establish how much similarity can arise without shared provenance and provide detector-specific reference bands. Existing methods remain far from saturating Launder-Bench: the strongest static method reaches only 0.66 AUROC on pairwise detection, while repository encoders rank the true source first on up to 22% of attribution queries but earn calibrated attribution credit on only 1-2%. These results reveal a systematic gap between relative code similarity and source-specific provenance evidence, providing a reproducible target for provenance detection under agentic rewriting.

authors.name: Qiyue Li
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: User Engagement in Visualization: A Scoping Review of 243 Research Articles
papers.abstract: User engagement is well studied in other domains. Work to date has proposed conceptual models and definitions, approaches to measurement, and factors that influence engagement in digital interactions. However, of the articles in the visualization literature that refer to engagement, few of them make evidence-based, generalizable claims, and research that does is challenging to locate due to inconsistent reporting and often lacks connection to the broader engagement literature. To address these issues and promote the consideration of the broader engagement literature, we conduct a comprehensive scoping review of visualization literature and engagement. Using scoping review methodology, we identify and analyze 243 articles that make claims about engagement with visualizations. We coded the studies conducted, literature cited, definitions provided, and claims made in these articles and analyze the codes to evaluate the quality of the work in the field and to synthesize existing findings. We find that, despite frequent references to engagement and apparent interest in the topic, the overall quality of visualization engagement research is poor, often with weak evidence, inconsistent conceptualizations, and infrequent citation of existing models, methods, or claims. We report the evidence-based claims about what engages people with visualization, including the factors of animation, interaction, and immersion, additionally describing both corroboration and apparent contradictions between these claims. Finally, we propose the COMFI framework and mnemonic for reporting important information in future engagement studies.

papers.title: IMUdrape: Generating Garment-Mounted Virtual IMU Data from Text through Physics-Based Cloth Simulation
papers.abstract: Inertial sensors are moving into clothing, from sensorized sportswear to garments instrumented with hundreds of IMUs. Sewn into clothing, a sensor no longer moves rigidly with the body: loose fabric slides, twists and swings, so a garment-mounted sensor records the motion of the fabric as well as that of the body, and this extra motion differs from one garment to the next. Models for such sensors need training data recorded with the deployed garment, yet labeled data are scarce. Virtual IMU data generated from videos or text have eased this scarcity for body-attached sensors, but existing generators attach their virtual sensors rigidly to the body. We present IMUdrape, which generates garment-mounted virtual IMU data from text through physics-based cloth simulation. IMUdrape synthesizes motion from activity descriptions, reconstructs the target garment as a sewing pattern from photographs, places virtual IMUs at the deployment's real sensor positions, and simulates the garment with an intersection-free contact solver, so that every simulation yields paired garment and body signals. On four real datasets with clothing-mounted sensors, IMUdrape improves on existing virtual-data approaches for both activity recognition and full-body pose estimation. With one real subject, its data improve recognition macro-F1 by 7% to 46% over real data alone and by 2% to 11% over body-mounted virtual data from the same motion. When the garment is simulated on recorded motion, the pose error without any real training data falls by 30% to 33% relative to generated motion, and garment data remain 12% more accurate than body data. IMUdrape thus reduces the amount of real data that garment-mounted sensing requires.

papers.title: Beyond Answers, Traces, and Efficiency: Evidence for Adaptive Reasoning
papers.abstract: Current AI systems are evaluated as reasoners through final-answer accuracy, reasoning traces, process supervision, and computational or human-relative efficiency. Yet these measures do not establish whether reasoning adapts when tasks or evidence change. We distinguish across-task adaptivity, where acquired abstractions transfer or recombine across novel problems, fromwithin-task adaptivity, where hypotheses and actions are revised in response to new observations, feedback, or counterexamples. Using ARC-AGI as a diagnostic case study rather than an alignment benchmark, we examine what existing measures leave unresolved when test-time search, sampling, or adaptation affects performance. We propose intervention-oriented evaluation that tests abstraction transfer and hypothesis revision under controlled changes to tasks and evidence, with explicit reporting of test-time procedures and budgets. This perspective supports evaluating systems for robustness, responsiveness to corrective feedback, and auditability under changing conditions.

authors.name: Sundong Kim
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology
