Our demonstrations provide a basis for single-sided circularly polarized light sources and polarization-matched optical coupling.

papers.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
papers.abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

papers.title: Causal Optimal-Transport Attention: Positional Priors and Length Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Causal masking obstructs the column balancing used by optimal-transport (OT) attention. We study a prefix-consistent unbalanced operator and characterize the positional prior it induces. Under bounded scores, for any fixed balancing strength $\rho<1$, its fixed point dilutes attention: every fixed window receives a vanishing share as the context grows. For constant scores, we derive an exact scale-invariant prior. We then classify positional encodings by whether their distant attention mass remains bounded away from one. Discrete window-mass bounds quantify the finite-length dilution of summable log-distance priors near exponent one. Preregistered experiments with 25M- and 100M-parameter language models establish improved loss extrapolation over softmax; exploratory comparisons favor an explicit distance bias at a fraction of the cost. CABLE outperforms RoPE with evaluation-time YaRN on every seed at three training lengths. Changing only the bias beyond the training length moves long-context loss in the predicted direction on all 30 tested checkpoints. Even with exponents constrained above one, many heads approach the summability boundary during training. A margin selected by prior-only calculations for a specified window, length range and growth tolerance controls distant-mass growth in the tested setting. These results connect loss extrapolation to positional decay over the lengths actually evaluated.

authors.name: Ming Lian
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Polarization instability of unpolarized excited states in trapped two-component Bose--Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: A binary Bose--Einstein condensate in an elongated trap supports unpolarized excited states, in which both components share the same spatial profile. Within mean-field theory we show that the interspecies repulsion at which these states demix rises with the excitation level. Since each component keeps its atom number, the components separate by moving in opposite directions in the trap, and demixing sets in when the interaction energy released by the separation balances its cost in kinetic and trap energy. We show that the threshold also marks the onset of an exponential, non-oscillating growth of the separation, which divides the cloud into domains of opposite polarization, with walls at the density nodes and further walls interlaced with them. In the Thomas--Fermi regime of a quasi-one-dimensional condensate the rise of the threshold follows power laws in the ratio of the trap oscillator energy to the chemical potential. The trap raises the ground-state threshold, in units of the intraspecies repulsion, by 1.82 times the square of this ratio. Each density node of an excited state near the trap center raises the threshold further by 1.24 times the cube of this ratio. Because the steps between successive levels scale as the cube of this ratio, they fall as the inverse square of the atom number, and the dependence on the excitation level is a mesoscopic effect, appreciable only when the chemical potential is no more than a few times the oscillator energy. In a hyperfine mixture of $^{87}$Rb a Feshbach resonance tunes the interspecies repulsion across the thresholds of the lowest states.

papers.title: A Hybrid Anomaly Detection Method for Multivariate Time Series
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series are ubiquitous in monitoring smart systems such as power plants, smart houses, and servers. These systems use multiple sensors to collect the system's status over time. Those sensors represent the status of the whole system as one entity. Anomaly detection in such smart systems is of critical importance to prevent system failure and maintain functionality. But anomaly detection in such multivariate time series data is very challenging since this type of data includes both temporal and spatial information. Capturing both of these pieces of information is important to detect anomalies. In this paper, we propose a hybrid deep learning-based anomaly detection method, which captures both temporal and spatial information. We propose to take advantage of the feature extraction capabilities of 2d convolutional network in a variational autoencoder, alongside a prediction-based deep neural network of 2d convolutional networks and a gated recurrent unit network to capture both spatial and temporal information. Experiments on public data against state-of-the-art show the potential of our method.

papers.title: RSI-Env: An Open-Ended Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agents
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) envisions agent systems that autonomously improve their own models and harnesses, with each updated system continuing to improve itself. Existing approaches typically restrict optimization objectives, editable components, or evaluation procedures, limiting open-ended exploration and continuity across generations. We introduce RSI-Env, a persistent environment for coordinated model-harness improvement, supporting autonomous training, harness modification, and retention of research state. An independent Host Controller manages services, evaluation, and versioning. Under Self, each accepted model-harness version takes over the next improvement round. We define three settings that vary goal specificity and access to benchmark feedback: Open-General, Capability-Directed, and Benchmark-Guided. Across these three settings, we compare Self with two fixed external Teachers on seven tasks, starting from Qwen3.8-27B with a minimal harness. Without benchmark feedback, Open-General Self raises GPQA Diamond accuracy from 65.2% to 73.2% and AIME 2026 accuracy from 53.3% to 56.7%. All three Capability-Directed Self runs achieve target-aligned gains. Knowledge Self demonstrates continued improvement across system updates, with SimpleQA accuracy rising from 82.0% to 85.0% and then 88.0%. Benchmark guidance and Teacher benefits vary by task. These results demonstrate RSI-Env's support for open-ended exploration and sustained recursive improvement within the studied runs, while highlighting challenges in preserving gains across capabilities.

authors.name: Jiang Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ReWY: Faster Gradient Computation for Delta-Rule Attention Family
papers.abstract:
Delta-rule linear attention underlies language models such as Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next. Chunkwise implementations expose matrix parallelism, but their backward passes compute unnecessary auxiliary adjoints. We present ReWY, an algebraic reformulation that reduces this work before optimizing accelerator execution. Differentiating the chunk correction as one triangular residual system eliminates the inverse adjoint and reduces seven local WY matrix products to three. Two complementary transformations expose further reuse: centered matrix contractions replace pairwise vector-gate processing, and scalar-gate reductions reuse key-gradient products instead of forming a key Gram matrix. These identities simplify backward computation for DeltaNet, GDN, KDA, and GDN2 while preserving the recurrence and gradients in exact arithmetic, without changing the architecture or training objective.
  We implement the reduced graph on GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Under matched recomputation and full-saving policies, precision-qualified six-shape comparisons with frozen FLA references yield 1.15-1.81$\times$ geometric-mean complete low-level backward speedups on NVIDIA GPUs. All four operators achieve 1.18-1.70$\times$ on H100 and H200 while retaining original FP32 working matrices. A separate public-autograd evaluation on Ascend 950DT, including gradient conversions, yields 1.09-2.89$\times$ under available matched policies. Paired ablations establish further ReWY gains after optimizing the complementary contractions. Complete-gradient checks validate the recorded operator cases; supplementary full-model backward measurements assess integration into community FLA models and a GDN2 layer port. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/flashserve/ReWY.

authors.name: Zhixin Zhao
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Construction of stability conditions on some Kuznetsov components
papers.abstract: We construct Bridgeland stability conditions on the Kuznetsov components of smooth Fano hypersurfaces of degrees three, four, and six and dimension at least three, smooth quartic double fivefolds, and smooth Fano complete intersections of three quadrics. For odd-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces and quartic double fivefolds, every connected component of the numerical stability manifold is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C\times\mathbb H$. For general cubic sevenfolds and quartic double fivefolds, spherical twists produce infinitely many distinct connected components.

papers.title: Experimental realization of loss-induced quadrupole topology from a gapped trivial insulator in RLC circuits
papers.abstract: Non-Hermitian topological transitions offer a route to controlling topology through dissipation, but their experimental signatures depend on how loss modifies the system's response. Here, we experimentally realize loss-induced quadrupole topology in a square-octagon RLC circuit whose ideal Hermitian limit is a gapped trivial insulator. Patterned grounding resistors introduce on-site loss while the conservative couplings remain fixed. Band spectra and biorthogonal nested Wilson loops identify a loss-driven topological transition accompanied by closure and reopening of the real line gap. Impedance spectroscopy and spatial maps reveal corner-localized responses consistent with the predicted quadrupole phase. Comparing two finite-loss configurations, we observe enhanced corner contrast at stronger patterned loss within the same predicted phase. These results connect dissipation-driven topology to observable boundary responses in RLC circuits.

authors.name: Chen Wang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: MetaPOCS: Meta-Learned Multi-Exit Unfolding for Budget-Aware Seismic Data Interpolation
papers.abstract: Seismic data interpolation must reconcile reconstruction fidelity with the computational budgets of acquisition quality control and subsequent imaging. Fixed-depth unfolding networks are optimized for a single operating point, whereas their intermediate estimates may be insufficiently trained for early deployment. We present MetaPOCS, a meta-learned multi-exit unfolding framework for budget-aware seismic interpolation. Building on a spatial--spectral POCS reconstruction backbone, MetaPOCS supervises intermediate stages and preserves the acquired traces at every exit. A Meta-GF-based optimization procedure constructs exit-oriented parameter displacements from a common initialization and learns their fusion weights through an equal-exit outer objective. The weights vary across parameter tensors and respect the nested support of the reconstruction stages. We derive the resulting fusion hypergradient to characterize how the outer objective reallocates competing updates, and distinguish this mechanism from scalar loss reweighting. At inference, one checkpoint provides a set of reconstruction budgets through a latency-calibrated exit policy. The evaluation framework couples matched-cost interpolation comparisons with finite-update diagnostics and a fixed reverse-time-migration operator, connecting multi-exit optimization to waveform and imaging fidelity. MetaPOCS thus provides a unified formulation for studying the reconstruction--computation trade-off of seismic unfolding across deployment budgets.

authors.name: Nanqi Zhao
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: Hereditary lowerability of diagonal entropy scales
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a continuous self-map of a compact metric space. For each integer $p\geq2$, we consider the upper capacity entropy scale obtained by dividing the $p$-fold logarithm of an orbit covering number by the $(p-1)$-fold logarithm of time. We prove that every nonempty compact set contains a compact subset realizing any value between zero and its own scale entropy. Every strictly intermediate value is realized by a countable compact set with exactly one accumulation point. The proof combines localization at a fixed spatial resolution, a finite-tree selection lemma, and refinements of orbit covers at dyadic times. An example shows that the assertion about one accumulation point does not extend to the upper endpoint. On the product-diagonal construction used in classical entropy lowerability, the diagonal scales preserve the values of the base subsets, although classical upper capacity entropy takes only zero or infinity.

papers.title: Recast: Refinement-Centered Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Optimized for Storage
papers.abstract: Large-scale ANNS systems often exploit storage in addition to DRAM for supporting vector search. The central question is how to divide the work between memory and storage for achieving both high query throughput-recall and good index maintenance performance. Existing storage-optimized ANNS paradigms fall short of providing a complete answer: disk-resident graph indexes have difficulty in supporting efficient vector deletions, while posting-list systems often incur more disk I/Os for queries. In this paper, we introduce a refinement-centered paradigm for storage-optimized ANNS systems. We propose Recast as a concrete design of this paradigm. Recast stores raw vectors on disk and keeps an IVF index with our RecastQ quantization encoding in memory. For an ANNS query, Recast selects nprobe inverted lists and performs SIMD-based FastScan on their RecastQ codes to identify refinement candidates in memory. It then retrieves candidate vectors from disk, computes exact distances, and refines the top-K result. To reduce disk I/Os, RecastQ computes uncertainty intervals containing true distances with high probability. Our QUIC policy selects a minimal refinement set based on these intervals, minimizing candidate-retrieval I/Os. Both the on-disk raw vectors and the in-memory IVF structure support insertions and deletions. Experiments on real-world data sets show that Recast processes batched insertions and deletions 3.10-37.27x faster than SPFresh and OdinANN, while its QPS at 0.99 recall changes by at most 6.9% after updating 50% of the corpus. For static queries at 0.99 recall, Recast achieves 1.56-2.01x the QPS of the strongest baseline with the matched memory budget on each data set, while requiring 1.22-6.75x less external storage than the evaluated systems. At matched in-memory space, RecastQ also provides a better Recall-refinement frontier than RaBitQ.

authors.name: Wenzhuo Dong
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

papers.title: Task Adaptation Through Guidance in Frozen Feature Upsampling
papers.abstract: Adapting features before upsampling can improve dense prediction, but the gains may arise from changes in feature values, spatial aggregation, or both. We investigate this ambiguity by comparing matched residual adapters before and after a frozen JAFAR upsampler under a shared parent. We construct a readout-null intervention that preserves a frozen linear classifier's coarse logits while allowing spatial attention weights to adapt. Guidance/value exchanges on trained models and retrained fixed-guidance controls test the utility of this adaptation route. In three-seed experiments on PASCAL Visual Object Classes (VOC) and Cityscapes, adaptation before upsampling improves mean intersection over union (mIoU) by 0.807 and 1.413 percentage points, respectively, over adaptation after upsampling. Across both datasets and the JAFAR and AnyUp upsamplers, readout-null adaptation produces mean gains of 1.379-1.987 points over the corresponding frozen linear baselines. Retrained controls further support the benefit of adaptive spatial guidance. These findings explain how dense predictions can improve despite unchanged coarse classifier outputs and identify spatial guidance as a useful target when adapting frozen feature upsampling systems.

papers.title: Stability and exact extremal colourings for the Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz bound
papers.abstract: The Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz theorem states that every $q$-colouring of the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic matching of size $\lfloor(n+q-1)/(r+q-1)\rfloor$. For fixed uniformity $r$ and number of colours $q$, we prove a stability theorem: every colouring whose largest monochromatic matching has size at most $n/(r+q-1)+o(n)$ differs from a threshold extremal colouring on only $o(n^r)$ edges. We also give a necessary and sufficient structural characterization of all extremal colourings for sufficiently large $n$. The proofs combine rigidity of fractional covering weights with an extension argument for prescribed matchings. These results answer, for sufficiently large orders, the stability and extremal-colouring questions posed by Gishboliner, Glock, Michaeli and Sgueglia.

papers.title: Representations of Bound Quivers over $\mathbb{F}_1$ and Hall Algebras
papers.abstract: Representations of quivers over the virtual field $\mathbb{F}_1$ can be naturally extended to bound quivers with monomial and commutativity relations. In this paper, we introduce and study the Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ for a bound quiver $(Q,I)$ equipped with such relations. As in the quiver setting, $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ is a graded, connected, and cocommutative bialgebra, and the free subgroup generated by all indecomposable representations forms a Lie subalgebra. We study $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ in detail for two special classes of bound quivers: Nakayama bound quivers and gentle one-cycle bound quivers. In both cases, we prove that for any triple $L, M, N$ of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations over $(Q,I)$, the Hall number $g_{N,L}^M$ coincides with the evaluation of the corresponding Hall polynomial $\phi_{N,L}^M(t)$ at $t=1$. Consequently, there exists a canonical isomorphism between $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ and the degenerate Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_1(Q,I)$, justifying Tits's $\mathbb{F}_1$-philosophy in these settings.

authors.name: Xuelian Xiao
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: Efficient Numerical Evaluation of Arbitrary High-order Partial Derivatives via Algebraic Decomposition
papers.abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives of multivariate functions is often computationally and memory intensive. This paper addresses this problem via an algebraic approach. High-order partial derivatives of a multivariate function are expressed as linear combinations of univariate directional derivatives, which are computationally friendly. The coefficients and direction vectors are determined by the Waring decomposition of monomials, so that the number of univariate directional derivatives in the representation is minimized. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: Cyber-JEV: Matched Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Language Models for Fast Source-Code Vulnerability Triage
papers.abstract: Single-pass scoring models such as Jev give each code function a vulnerability probability, so that security teams can rank many functions for review without generating written explanations. Training an open-weight model for this task is limited by data. Benchmarks with both vulnerable and non-vulnerable labels keep few vulnerable functions once examples related to the test data are removed, while larger public vulnerability records mostly contain vulnerable functions only. Mixing the two lets the data source predict the label, and training on the labeled data alone leaves a model that often scores a fixed function above its vulnerable original. We present Cyber-JEV, a fine-tuning method that uses fix commits to turn these records into comparison groups. Each group holds a vulnerable function, its patched version and up to two unchanged functions from the same file, so the model sees the change that removed a recorded defect. One shared model learns two tasks: classifying functions from the labeled reference data, and ranking the vulnerable function above the other members of its group. At test time the input is one function and the output is a vulnerability score. On a test benchmark of 7,270 functions, an ensemble of five fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B models reaches an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.814, compared with 0.743 for Jev 1.13. With the 4,031 alerts of Jev as the review budget, it misses 16 of 322 vulnerable functions instead of 39. Compared with training on the reference data alone, it ranks the vulnerable version above the patched version 14.8 to 29.2 percentage points more often on three sets of real fixes. Such scores can order the changed functions of a pull request or a release for review under a fixed budget.

authors.name: Kang Wei
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Fischer-Burmeister-based Multiplier Dynamics in Inequality-Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: We study proportional-integral multiplier feedback for inequality-constrained optimization using the Fischer-Burmeister complementarity residual. We construct explicit dynamics and characterize gain-dependent stability and convergence rates. For a single active constraint, we derive exact local stability and decay-rate conditions, including a tradeoff between continuous-time convergence and discretization costs. For strongly convex objectives with affine constraints, we establish global convergence and characterize geometric conditions for uniform exponential stability. Numerical experiments compare feedback structures and computational costs.

papers.title: BLPO: Beyond-Local Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon tasks require large language model (LLM) agents to coordinate interdependent actions, a capability central to automating complex workflows. Stepwise group-based reinforcement learning provides finer credit than trajectory-level supervision, but reliable comparisons must account for differences in interaction history. Enforcing this consistency within the limited rollouts of each task can leave insufficient support for estimating action preferences. We propose Beyond-Local Policy Optimization (BLPO), which estimates task-progress advantages from experience shared across tasks and training updates. We summarize trajectory prefixes into task-progress states and abstract actions by their function, allowing corresponding decisions from different tasks to contribute to shared estimates. To control bias and noise from heterogeneous tasks, we accumulate context-relative returns in a global memory with balanced aggregation and reliability weighting. These global advantages complement local comparisons over normalized actions and trajectory-level credit without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with 1.5B and 7B policies show improved task success over the evaluated baselines under matched training budgets. Further analyses show faster learning and shorter trajectories with little computational overhead.

papers.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

authors.name: Jun Huo
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

authors.name: Haifeng Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cold-Start Pricing of LLM Services under Two-Sided Learning
papers.abstract:
Online large language model (LLM) services face a pricing cold start: providers initially lack the historical data and user information needed for precise pricing, while users' willingness to pay evolves with repeated use. We formulate this challenge as a \emph{two-sided learning} problem between a provider and a user. The user learns from private usage experience, whereas the provider incurs a serving cost and dynamically adapts prices using only purchase decisions to maximize cumulative profit. The provider's central challenge is to learn to price against an evolving willingness to pay without observing the private experiences driving that evolution.
  We establish matching upper and lower bounds on the minimax regret over horizon $T$, identifying two cost-dependent regimes. When serving costs are sufficiently low, our Calibration-and-Tracking (CAT) algorithm achieves the optimal rate $\Theta(T^{1/3})$. In the higher-cost regime, where the provider must learn whether continued service is profitable, Calibration-and-Tracking with Retirement (CAT-R) attains the optimal rate $\Theta(\sqrt{T})$. This phase transition shows that serving costs affect not only profit margins but also the fundamental difficulty of learning to price LLM services. Simulations support the predicted regret scaling and show that our algorithms outperform standard online learning baselines in the evaluated settings.

authors.name: Pinyan Lu
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

authors.name: Xiang Yan
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
papers.abstract:
Recently, harness self-evolution has emerged as an important paradigm for improving agent performance. Prior studies show that evolving the agent harness can effectively enhance agent capabilities without modifying the foundation model's parameters. We find that existing approaches largely study agent evolution on a single task. In practice, coding agents may need to handle multiple task types over time. Whether an agent harness can continuously evolve across multiple tasks without suffering from catastrophic forgetting remains an important open question.
  In this paper, we investigate this open question through a comprehensive empirical study of continual harness self-evolution. We organize three software engineering task datasets into six different evolution directions and apply two representative harness evolution methods to perform continual evolution along these directions. Our experimental results show that evolution on a subsequent dataset can substantially undermine the performance on previously seen datasets. For example, with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, Meta-Harness improves its performance on SWE-Bench to 94.0% after evolution. However, after further evolution on FeatureBench, its performance on SWE-Bench drops to 32.0% by the fifth round, corresponding to a 66% relative decrease. Finally, based on our experimental findings, we identify several insights, providing directions for the continual self-evolution of agent harnesses. Code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/continual-harness-evolution.

authors.name: Yitong Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jia Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: On covering systems over finite nilpotent groups and lattices
papers.abstract: We prove a quantitative non-covering theorem for finite nilpotent groups. As a consequence, every finite covering of $\Z^d$ by affine full-rank sublattices with pairwise distinct indices contains a member of bounded index, uniformly in $d$. We also establish a summability criterion allowing repeated indices, which extends to finite groups containing a normal nilpotent subgroup of bounded index.

authors.name: Biao Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Dynamic Merging Mutually-Distilled Multi-View Networks for RGB-Event-based Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Multi-modal fusion algorithms combining conventional frame-based cameras and event cameras have recently attracted substantial research attention. Typically, existing approaches convert event streams into frames, voxels, or tensors, and then learn the required spatiotemporal information from these transformed event representations for fusion with conventional frame-camera data. Obviously, such paradigms only exploit the limited representational capacity of event data. Moreover, standard training pipelines fail to fully leverage diverse model parameters obtained throughout the learning process. In this paper, we propose a novel mutual distillation method leveraging multi-view teacher network weights to better integrate multiple event representations and achieve model-parameter level fusion. Specifically, we employ multiple encoders to extract different types of event representations and perform mutual knowledge distillation at both the feature-level and logit-level in this process. Afterwards, we perform a dynamic hierarchical model merge strategy on the model parameters from the first stage to yield a unified multi-modal RGB-Event representation model. Experimental results across multiple event-based datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements.

authors.name: Fan Zhang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Jin Tang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The Prior-Force Family of Implicit Denoiser Priors and Its Decisions in Linear Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Implicit priors given by Gaussian denoisers successfully regularize a wide range of inverse problems in approaches such as plug-and-play (PnP), regularization by denoising (RED) and score-based methods. Such a prior depends on the noise level, and how it selects among signals consistent with the data remains largely uncharacterized. To put implicit and explicit priors on the same footing, we define the prior-force family $W_t=t^{-1}(D_t^{-1}-I)$ of any Gaussian denoiser $D_t$ at noise variance $t>0$ (inverse in the graph sense), the normalized denoising residual as an operator on clean signals. At a common effective prior weight, the equilibrium equations differ only in their prior terms: PnP uses $W_t$, RED/score-based methods the score force (the normalized residual as an operator on noisy inputs), and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation the MAP force (the negative log-prior gradient). For the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) denoisers of a prior $\pi$, we compare the corresponding energies at three levels. Without observation, raising the noise level favors PnP minima that retain more posterior variance. On signals consistent with the data, the leading-order PnP energy for separated modes is the proximal hull of the MAP energy, which lets PnP select signals between modes; modes of equal data fit are ranked by peak height at small noise levels and by mass at large ones. For recovery, $W_t$ at the truth bounds the local bias, and an oracle noise level balances this bias against denoiser error. These results show that the noise level is a parameter of the prior rather than a step size. Experiments with exact priors support these predictions, including the mixture components that PnP selects on unseen data.

authors.name: Jian Lu
authors.institution: Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science

papers.title: DADKC: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification
papers.abstract: Lifelong Person Re-identification (LReID) aims to match the same person using sequentially collected data. In practical long-term deployments, however, the model must handle both domain shifts across cameras and scenes, and irregular clothing changes of the same identity. This gives rise to the Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification (CH-LReID) task, which demands balancing cloth-relevant and cloth-irrelevant knowledge in streaming data. While existing LReID methods have explored replay-based or distillation-based anti-forgetting strategies, they typically fail to sufficiently model stage-aware domain distributions and cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training. To address this problem, we propose a Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DADKC) framework. The core idea is to enhance the existing Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DKC) paradigm with adaptive distribution modeling. To this end, three lightweight modules are designed: (1) an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) to retrieve learnable anchor cues for refining identity features; (2) a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) to perform stage-aware expert routing for integrating domain-specific distribution paths; and (3) a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module to regularize the continuity of base, anchor, and path representations between adjacent stages. Extensive experiments on the CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks show that DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and lowers weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%, while storing neither historical images nor per-image features. The code is available at https://github.com/fire667/DADKC.

papers.title: One Offset, Two Directions: Baseline Adjustment via Subgroup Offsets
papers.abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) estimates advantages against the within-prompt mean reward, a baseline shared across the group. In practice, rollouts within a prompt are not always homogeneous, differing in their solution strategies and reasoning trajectories, along which they may group into subgroups. We further find that these heterogeneous subgroups may exhibit distinct reward distributions. The global baseline, however, collapses them onto a single credit axis, where the credit reflects neither a rollout's standing within its subgroup nor the subgroup's standing relative to the rest. We therefore study how to adjust the baseline when the rollouts of a prompt fall into heterogeneous subgroups. We define the \emph{subgroup offset} as the deviation of a subgroup mean from the global mean, and shift the baseline along it by a single signed coefficient $\lambda$. The sign of $\lambda$ yields two opposing directions: \emph{Alignment} ($\lambda{>}0$) adds the offset to the baseline, drawing credit toward a rollout's relative position within its subgroup; \emph{Contrast} ($\lambda{<}0$) subtracts it, drawing a rollout's credit toward the relative quality of the subgroup it belongs to. The adjustment acts on the baseline alone, leaving the reward signal and the optimization objective unchanged. In this work, we induce subgroups from strategies, grouping rollouts that share a strategy into the same subgroup. We evaluate both directions on Qwen3-8B-Base and Olmo3-7B-Base across four competition-level math benchmarks, against a $\lambda{=}0$ anchor that shares the same strategy-conditioned sampling and differs only in the baseline. Against this anchor each direction yields modest but consistent gains in multi-sample coverage, with Contrast the stronger of the two.

authors.name: Jiaying Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TreePIN$^{2}$: Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Fitted decision trees provide predictive knowledge for neural network initialization. We present Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks (TreePIN$^{2}$), a method that translates split rules, decision paths and leaf predictions into initial network weights and biases for classification and regression. Sigmoid units encode split responses, hidden units combine them along decision paths, and leaf predictions initialize the output layer. We calibrate split softness using local training margins, sample support and impurity reduction, relating the initial responses to the data at each node. All weights and biases remain trainable, allowing gradient-based optimization to refine the transferred decisions and their combinations. Across six classification and six regression tasks with twenty paired seeds, TreePIN$^{2}$ improves mean initial and early validation performance over initialization baselines on most tasks. After fifty epochs, it achieves the best or tied-best mean validation performance among the six compared methods on ten tasks. Paired ablations show how split calibration and leaf-informed output initialization contribute to the starting predictor and its subsequent learning.

papers.title: Global classical solutions of the repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system
papers.abstract: Global classical existence for general large data in the three-dimensional repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system has long been an open problem. We give an affirmative answer: every nonnegative $C^1$ initial datum satisfying \[ f_0(x,p)+|\nabla_{x,p}f_0(x,p)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-a}\langle p\rangle^{-b},\qquad a>1,\quad b>3, \] generates a unique global classical solution. No smallness or symmetry is assumed. The result covers finite and infinite mass and energy, including infinite kinetic energy density. The power thresholds are sharp for general pure-power bounds ensuring finite density and an absolutely convergent Coulomb field. The proof rests on two new mechanisms: local energy recovery for a population selected by energy growth, and a corrected moment--action closure based on nonnegative transverse interactions. The argument also yields global classical solutions of the nonrelativistic equation in the same initial class, allowing infinite mass with polynomial velocity tails of any order $b>3$.

authors.name: Jingpeng Wu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Electrical Insulation and Power Equipment

papers.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.

papers.title: Toward Executable Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation with Self-Correction
papers.abstract: Generating codes from UI screenshots has recently benefited from MLLMs, yet existing methods centered on HTML targets and transfer poorly to multi-frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular. However, unlike HTML, which does not entail compilation issues, generating executable code in multi-framework settings is more challenging due to framework-specific differences in syntax and failure modes, as well as the need to maintain global consistency across files. To address this problem, we study executable multi-framework front-end code generation and propose MESCoder, a tree-structured self-corrective generation framework. Our method first extracts a structural scaffold from the screenshot and then constructs sub-trees and assembly relations step by step, transforming large project generation into a sequence of localized decisions. On top of this scaffold, we introduce a unified Project Agent that continuously revises its own partial project under runtime sandbox feedback and dynamically chooses between local repair and cluster level repair. For training, we adopt a two-stage strategy that first initializes the policy offline to learn basic multi-framework generation and repair priors, and then refines it with online reinforcement learning to optimize long horizon executability and final page quality. The resulting framework models multi-framework executability as a conditioned project state transition process and improves the stability and quality of complex front end generation through self correction. Experiments show that our method improves executability, while narrowing the visual-fidelity gap to HTML-based generation. Code is available at https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/MESCoder.

authors.name: Jiaye Lin
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: Same Path, Less Time: Training-Free Fast Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models under Inference Latency
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, yet deployed robots waste time in two ways that are independent of model capability: they halt while the next chunk is inferred, and they move at the speed of slow, cautious demonstrations. Existing remedies remove one loss each, and stacking them fails, because asynchrony and speed-up each change the correspondence between planned progress and executed motion. We present Path-preserving Time Scaling (PTS), a training-free execution layer for frozen action-chunking policies built on one principle: the robot's motion is a time reparameterization of a reference path, and the path changes only in response to new observations. A path layer decodes every replan deterministically in one step and enters it at the progress consumed during inference. A time layer sums the planned increments, keeps the arm at 1x while the gripper moves, and caps the rate by the actuator's linear range and by chunk feasibility under latency. We show that misaligned entry and stochastic sampling add a bias and a variance to the continuation error, and derive a break-even success rate that states when speeding up pays off. On LIBERO with two frozen VLAs under injected inference latency, PTS raises task throughput over the strongest deployable baseline by 33% for pi0.5 and 104% for SmolVLA while matching or improving the success rate, is best on all six model-suite combinations, and exceeds zero-latency 1x execution. Against asynchronous 1x execution with the same one-step decoder, the time layer alone adds 28% and 38%. On LIBERO-Dynamic it improves on stop-and-wait execution by 38% and is comparable to asynchronous 1x execution.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
papers.abstract: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{\tau,\delta\tau,\tau\delta,\delta\tau\delta\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $\delta$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\delta\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.

papers.title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
papers.abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. Second, physics-informed methods impose a specified physical equation as a reconstruction constraint, but often require environment-dependent parameters that are difficult to acquire. As a result, practical 3D acoustic field reconstruction that is both physically grounded and robust to uncertain environmental information remains largely unexplored. This work takes an alternative route: instead of solving a fully specified wave equation, it extracts a structured representation from wave physics and learns its components from data. From the Helmholtz equation and normal mode propagation, we derive a structured spatial-angular tensor representation, termed the S/c representation. Under a low-rank specialization, it takes the form of a rank-(L,L,1) block-term tensor decomposition, which connects structured sampling patterns/routes used in ocean sensing to sufficient conditions for field recovery. Building on this tensor representation, we propose TIDAL, a neural reconstructor that uses the S/c representation as an inductive bias for structured decoding and aligns information aggregation with the sampling geometry. The neural learner removes the need for known model parameters required by conventional physics-based recovery methods. Experiments across three structured sampling geometries show that TIDAL achieves the best reconstruction performance and fastest inference among baselines, with benefits from the physics-derived representation under limited data and model capacity.

authors.name: Yifan Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Phase-wise MLLM Tuning for Multi-framework WebUI Code Generation
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance in translating WebUI screenshots into HTML/CSS. However, when they faced multiple frameworks (React/Vue/Angular), they often suffer from negative transfer that leads to compilation failures. These failures commonly stem from mixing framework specific syntax and violating framework constraints. This paper studies supervised fine-tuning for multi-framework WebUI code generation and proposes a phase-wise MLLM tuning method driven by compatibility and heterogeneity signals across frameworks. We first apply a normalization mapping that preserves each framework's native syntax while suppressing noise from variable naming and literal content. We then estimate cross framework heterogeneity and compatibility offline, and automatically derive training groups and their ordering by maximizing a phased objective. Finally, we perform phase-wise adapter tuning to reduce cross framework interference. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our proposed method improves both generation quality and compilation success rate compared with baselines.

papers.title: Propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam with conserved topology
papers.abstract: We report the generation and control of a propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam through the digitally controlled superposition of a first-order petal- and Gaussian- mode each marked with orthogonal polarizations. We present a detailed analysis of the spatial and polarization profiles and unveil their intricate topological features, showing that they have properties that are invariant to the propagation dynamics, in addition to their preserved intensity. The differential Gouy phase between the spatial components is shown to rotate the great circle traced by the polarisation distribution on the Poincar\'e sphere. Finally, we assess the beams for laser cutting and optical trapping, highlighting the relevance of topological structured light to these applications.

papers.title: Training-Free Motion-Corrected 3D Brain MRI Reconstruction via Event-Guided References
papers.abstract: Head motion causes artefacts in 3D brain MRI and can bias structural measurements. Model-based correction alternates between image and motion estimation, but artefacts in the reconstructed reference can reinforce motion errors. Learned priors can reduce these artefacts but require pretraining and may add test-time computation. We propose EventMC (event-guided motion correction), a training-free method for interleaved Cartesian acquisitions. It iteratively detects motion events and estimates motion using reference images reconstructed from stable intervals. It then refines the image and motion from low to high spatial frequencies. In a fair comparison in simulation (same reconstruction), EventMC's motion estimates improve mean PSNR by up to 4.0 dB over those of the learning-based MotionTTT. A single run of EventMC is up to 7.5 times faster than MotionTTT with less than half the GPU memory. On in vivo motion-corrupted scans, EventMC achieves similar mean image quality to MotionTTT without any training. Code is available at https://github.com/bayesbreeze/EventMC.

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: CertClaim: Towards Certified Model-Claim Verification for Coding-Agent Services
papers.abstract: Coding-agent services are priced by the model they claim, making the verification of such model claims crucial for their users. In this paper, we reveal that existing model auditing methods rely on a latent assumption that the deployment is static, i.e., the claimed model is always served in one reference configuration. This assumption does not hold for coding-agent services, whose providers may legitimately change the sampling preset, the reasoning mode or the system prompt without changing the model. As a result, existing methods either falsely accuse honest providers or miss cheap derivatives of the claimed model. To address this problem, we propose a certified model-claim verification method (dubbed CertClaim). Instead of testing the service against one reference deployment, we make the authorized deployments part of the claim and test whether some authorized deployment explains all the evidence of the service, by calibrating multiple evidence channels in every authorized deployment and fusing them within each deployment. We provide theoretical analyses of its false-accusation rate and detection condition. Extensive experiments on eight claims, two agent harnesses and three task suites verify the effectiveness of CertClaim, which is valid in every setting while separating substitutes far better than existing methods, as well as its resistance to potential adaptive attacks.

authors.name: Qixuan Yang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Resource Engineering

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: A Novel Federated Learning Framework for Defending Against Gradient Inversion Attacks
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a paradigm for collaborative machine learning model training among clients, preserving data privacy by avoiding direct data sharing. However, the gradient information exchanged in FL has been shown to be vulnerable to Gradient Inversion Attacks (GIA), which can reconstruct sensitive user data. To counter these threats, various privacy-enhancing technologies like Secure Multi-party Computing (SMC), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Differential Privacy (DP) have been integrated into FL. While effective, these methods often introduce significant trade-offs between privacy and model utility. By revisiting the key to privacy exposure in FL under GIA, which lies in the frequent sharing of model gradients that contain private data, we take a new perspective by designing a novel privacy-preserving FL framework that effectively ``breaks the direct connection'' between the shared parameters and the local private data to defend against GIA. Our proposed framework, HyperFL++, leverages hypernetworks to generate local model parameters, where only the hypernetwork parameters are aggregated by the server. To ensure practicality, HyperFL++ incorporates a Row-wise Kronecker Decomposition (RKD) to mitigate the memory and communication overhead from the hypernetwork. Comprehensive theoretical analysis and extensive experiments validate our method's effectiveness in protecting data privacy while maintaining high model utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Pengxin-Guo/HyperFL/tree/hyperfl%2B%2B.

authors.name: Weihong Ren
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Robotics and Systems

papers.title: Towards Multi-Value Alignment via Value Localization in LLMs
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with multiple, potentially conflicting human values remains challenging, as existing multi-objective alignment methods often require costly fine-tuning and provide limited insight into the internal mechanisms underlying value-related behaviors. In this work, we investigate multi-value alignment from a mechanistic interpretability perspective by identifying value-sensitive attention heads (value heads) in LLMs. Using a probing-based value localization framework, we discover sparse sets of attention heads associated with diverse dimensions, spanning both human values (e.g., harmlessness, honesty) and stylistic preferences (e.g., coherence, complexity). Analyses across multiple LLM families reveal functional specialization and structured interactions among value heads, including conflicts between certain values. Targeted head ablations further induce substantial, value-specific behavioral changes, providing causal evidence of their functional importance. Building on these findings, we propose an inference-time activation steering strategy that enables controllable alignment with individual values or combinations of values without updating the underlying model parameters, supported by theoretical analysis. Experiments across multiple value alignment benchmarks demonstrate effective single- and multi-value control while largely preserving non-target model performance. Our findings connect mechanistic interpretability with flexible multi-value alignment, offering a foundation for more interpretable and pluralistic LLM behavior. The code is available at https://github.com/sihuo-design/ValueHeads.

authors.name: James Bailey
authors.institution: University of Tennessee Health Science Center

papers.title: Spectral radius and size conditions for 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs to contain a $k$-factor with $k\ge 3$
papers.abstract: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$ is called the spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of $G$. If $S$ is a vertex cut of a connected graph $G$, then $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of connected components of $G-S$. The toughness $t(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as $t(G) = \min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}: S \subset V(G), \text{ and } c(G-S) > 1\right\}$. A graph \( G \) is \( t \)-tough if \( |S| \ge t c(G - S) \) for every proper subset \( S \subset V(G) \) satisfying \( c(G - S) > 1 \). Combining the toughness and spectral conditions, we provide spectral radius and size conditions for the existence of $k$-factors in 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs. This settles a problem posed by Chen, Fan and Lin in [Discrete Appl. Math. {\bf 355} (2024), 223--231].

authors.name: Jinxuan Ren
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University

authors.name: Jiayao Song
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The dual Orlicz-Minkowski problem for capillary hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $\phi(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+h\nu$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.

authors.name: Ya Gao
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Cluster Condensation and Symmetry-Protected Thermal Rigidity of Bose gases on the Haldane Sphere
papers.abstract: We show that a spinless Bose gas on a Haldane sphere with a small monopole charge \(q\) realizes, in the lowest Landau level (LLL), an exactly solvable SU(2)-protected cluster condensate: a Hafnian condensate of two-boson singlets for \(q=1\), analogous to resonating-valence-bond singlet coverings, and a four-boson singlet condensate for \(q=3/2\). Unlike topologically protected quantum Hall states, the exactness of these states relies only on SU(2) symmetry and repulsiveness, with no pseudopotential fine-tuning. Their SU(2)-protected degeneracy renders the single-particle correlations exactly temperature-independent even as the clusters dissociate, a thermal rigidity absent in conventional Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs). Increasing the interaction drives a transition to a vortex BEC with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry.

authors.name: Meng-Jie Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: OmniOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Joint Audio-Video Generation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) elevates joint audio-video generation, but optimizing heterogeneous, modality-specific audio and video rewards often introduces cross-modal interference. On-policy distillation (OPD) alleviates this issue by transferring the capabilities of specialized audio and video RL teachers into a single student model. However, a significant imbalance in cross-modal token counts leaves audio with sparse supervision, causing unstable distillation. We observe that naively increasing the audio loss weight fails to solve this problem since audio learning relies heavily on visual context, indicating richer visual cues are crucial to offset sparse audio signals. To address this, we propose OmniOPD, a modality-wise on-policy distillation framework designed for balanced and stable audio-video generation. First, we construct privileged visual information using asymmetric noise scheduling, allowing the audio teacher to generate more informative targets from cleaner video context. Second, we introduce grouped multi-noise sampling to expand audio supervision coverage and stabilize training. Third, we introduce timestep-wise importance weighting based on teacher-student transition divergence, preserving reliable supervision while down-weighting unreliable learning signals, to stabilize fluctuations in audio learning. Evaluated on JavisBench and VBench demonstrate OmniOPD preserves audio quality while significantly enhancing video generation, achieving effective joint distillation.

authors.name: Xueyang Fu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zheng-Jun Zha
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Global Well-posedness of Incompressible MHD System with Density-dependent Viscosity in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible Magnetohydrodynamic equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum. For initial data with positive mass, finite second moment of density, and zero total momentum, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions when the viscosity is sufficiently close to one in $L^\infty$. The smallness threshold may depend on the initial data, while no separate smallness condition is imposed on the initial velocity or magnetic field. We obtain uniform-in-time bounds for the density second moment and its $H^1\cap W^{1,q}$ norm, where $q>2$. Moreover, for every $\eta\in(0,1)$, $\|\sqrt{\rho}u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}+\|b(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}$ decays at the rate $t^{-\eta/2}$, and the $H^1$ norms of $\nabla u$, $P$, and $\nabla b$ decay at the rate $t^{-(1+\eta)/2}$. The proof combines a velocity decomposition based on Hardy-space estimates with magnetic-field integrability and time-weighted energy estimates.

authors.name: Xue Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schr\"odinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: Strain-tunable electronic transport in disordered borophene nanoribbons with line defects
papers.abstract: Resonant tunneling intrinsically exists in disordered borophene nanoribbons (BNRs) with randomly distributed line defects (LDs), providing a versatile platform for transport modulation. Here, we theoretically investigate the effects of in-plane mechanical strain on the electronic transport properties of disordered BNRs coupled to metallic electrodes. Our results demonstrate that the resonant peaks in disordered BNRs of different widths remain robust against variations in electrode parameters and can be efficiently modulated via mechanical strain. Specifically, uniaxial strain significantly modulates the energies, widths, and amplitudes of these resonant peaks, and can even suppress the peaks selectively and induce new ones. In particular, the response of the resonant energies to the applied strain exhibits remarkable anisotropy, where strains along the longitudinal and transverse directions induce opposite energy shifts. Moreover, identical resonant peaks recurring in different nanoribbon widths respond uniformly to applied strain. Biaxial strain enables highly efficient conductance switching across multiple distinct levels, with the modulation frequency increasing for wider nanoribbons. Our findings establish a promising defect-strain-engineering strategy for manipulating electronic transport in borophene and other gapless materials.

authors.name: Pei-Jia Hu
authors.institution: Anhui University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Jia-Le Yu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Qing-Feng Sun
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: Hidden variable $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in a bilayer kagom\'e antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: Topological orders in realistic systems are quite rare, raising one fundamental question of whether they might be harbored with hidden degrees of freedom rather than directly exposed in conventional spins or electrons. We here propose a set of hidden variables and their effective interactions in a bilayer kagom\'e antiferromagnet. By properly organizing four local states of the spin dimer into two pseudospin-$1/2$ variables ($\boldsymbol{\tau}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mu}$), we identify a regime where an effective Balents-Fisher-Girvin model emerges, realizing a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in the hidden $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ sector while the auxiliary $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ sector remains a trivial paramagnet. This hidden nature drastically alters the experimental manifestations. Physical spins map to composite objects, typically convolving fractionalized anyon continua with non-topological magnon excitations. Nevertheless, specific symmetry-selected channels, such as the longitudinal intralayer response, exclusively reveal the bare two-vison continuum without collective-mode dressing. Our findings demonstrate that the topological order could be buried in certain hidden and emergent degrees of freedom, pointing to a promising pathway for seeking elusive topological states disguised within hidden internal degrees of freedom.

authors.name: Gang v. Chen
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: AIDA: An AI Outage Registry with Evidence from On-Chain MEV
papers.abstract: Generative AI coding tools have lowered the cost of writing trading software, but no systematic dataset records when these services fail. We introduce the AI Incident and Disruption Archive (AIDA), a multi-vendor registry of 5,868 deduplicated outage incidents across 30 providers from 2025 to 2026, with foundation-model incidents verified against primary status-page or postmortem URLs. Pairing AIDA with 5,041,034 verified maximal extractable value (MEV) transactions by 8,516 Ethereum addresses, their contract creations, and a 22-month Base Layer-2 panel of 1,099,593,191 swaps and 29,120 private executors, we establish two findings. First, entry into MEV expanded where code and public state suffice, as active arbitrage addresses quadrupled from late 2024 to late 2026 and liquidators grew by a third, while sandwich attackers, who need private order flow and builder access, declined. Execution nonetheless remained concentrated, with the top fifty addresses executing two thirds of verified trades. Second, AI outages stall new trading code while deployed bots keep trading. On Ethereum, addresses releasing a private executor fall to 0.67 on the day of an eight-hour disruption (0.68 for executor creations during OpenAI outage hours) and to 0.66 at lag two before rebounding on day three; on Base, operator top-level creations fall to 0.76 during OpenAI hours and executor-deploying operators to 0.88 at lag two. Non-trading creations, automated factory clones, and live arbitrage and sandwich execution across both chains remain unchanged. Cheaper code thus lowers the barrier to building MEV contracts, while private order flow, latency and capital still determine who wins execution.

authors.name: Wenbin Wu
authors.institution: Institute of Agricultural Resources and Regional Planning

papers.title: Radial and nonradial solutions for nonlinear scalar field equations and a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on the plane
papers.abstract:
A nonlinear scalar field equation is studied, which takes the form
  \begin{equation*}
  - \triangle{u}=g(u) \ \textrm{in} \ R^{N}, \quad \quad u \in E,
  \end{equation*} where $E$ is a suitable Banach space.. The nonlinear term $g(s)$ has subcritical growth at infinity. Near $s=0$, the nonlinear term $g(s)$ grows like $s^q$ for any $q>0$ if $N=2$ and for any $q \in (0,\ (N+2)/(N-2))$ if $N\ge 3$.
  Through the technique of adding one dimension of space, by mountain pass theorem and symmetric mountain theorem, we prove the multiplicity of radial solutions if $N\ge 2$ and the multiplicity of nonradial solutions if $N\ge 4$. Unlike [1] and [2], the proof presented here does not rely on any decomposition results. During the treatment for $N=2$, we provide a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on $R^2$, which is originally due to [3]. Based on this inequality we get a Trudinger-Moser type inequality involving gradient norm through Taylor expansion. Eventually we construct a special path to obtain the least energy level for solutions.
  [1] J. Mederski, Nonradial solutions of nonlinear scalar field equations. Nonlinearity 33 (2020), 6349--6380.
  [2] L. Jeanjean, S.S. Lu, Nonlinear scalar field equations with general nonlinearity. Nonlinear Anal. 190 (2020), 111604.
  [3] D.E. Edmunds, A.A.Ilyin, Asymptotically sharp multiplicative inequalities. Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995) 71--74.

authors.name: Shuolei Liu
authors.institution: Hebei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem. When the stop is bounded subanalytic singular isotropic, we prove a Morita equivalence between the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category and a microlocal sheaf category.

papers.title: Beyond the Last Layer: Global Inter-Layer Aggregation for AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative models has made AI-generated images increasingly close to real images. It has also brought several challenges to detectors, including rapid generator updates, large changes in data distribution, and limited cross-dataset generalization. Many existing methods based on pretrained vision encoders primarily use the global representation from the last layer, potentially leaving useful information from intermediate layers underexplored. To address this issue, we propose Global Inter-Layer Aggregation (GILA). GILA extracts global representations from different depths of a frozen encoder, models interactions among layer representations through inter-layer self-attention, and adaptively aggregates the resulting contextualized representations. The method is not tied to a single pretraining objective and does not require fine-tuning the pretrained encoder. We evaluated GILA on three vision backbones with different pretraining objectives, ten seen generators, and three external datasets. The experimental results show that GILA makes better use of multi-layer information in pretrained encoders and improves detection performance and cross-dataset generalization.

authors.name: Zhichao Lian
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation
papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers have achieved remarkable success in image generation, but accelerating attention while preserving generation quality remains a major challenge at high resolutions. Inspired by statistical physics and the widespread occurrence of scale-free laws in nature, we introduce Scale-Free Attention (SFA), which preserves fine local interactions while summarizing distant regions at progressively coarser scales. For $N$ tokens, mean pooling, token-count correction, and a shared softmax over a scale-free spatial hierarchy give SFA $O(N\log N)$ complexity in both forward and backward passes. Our Triton implementation achieves $357.3\times$ forward and $265.6\times$ backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens. After 40 epochs of PixelFlow training from scratch on ImageNet at $256\times256$ resolution, SFA achieves the best generation quality among five attention mechanisms, including full attention. Fr\'echet inception distance evaluated on 50,000 generated samples (FID-50k) improves from 13.25 for full attention to 12.51, and the advantage over full attention persists through 80 epochs. SFA also achieves the best generation quality among the compared efficient-attention methods on Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ). Beyond training from scratch, Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium with attention replaced by SFA retains the generation quality of its full-attention counterpart under matched fine-tuning budgets. We obtain similar results when fine-tuning pretrained PixelFlow on ImageNet. SFA establishes scale-free structure as an effective design principle for efficient, high-quality diffusion transformers.

authors.name: Tianhao You
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: TopoMix: Continuous Spatial Mixing for Long-Tailed Data Augmentation
papers.abstract: Most mixing-based augmentation methods improve generalization through a simple idea: combine two training samples with a fixed global ratio or a hard spatial replacement. While effective, this design leaves little room for local variation, which becomes a more visible limitation in long-tailed recognition, where minority classes are especially sensitive to the quality of augmented samples. We propose TopoMix, a training-free augmentation method that replaces fixed mixing with continuous spatial mixing. TopoMix constructs a smooth spatially varying mask from a low-resolution random control grid, bicubic interpolation, and stochastic non-linear shaping, and uses this mask for element-wise image mixing and label reweighting. Without introducing trainable parameters or auxiliary networks, TopoMix offers a simple way to make mixing more flexible in the input space. Experiments on standard long-tailed benchmarks show that it consistently improves over representative mixing-based baselines, indicating that smooth spatial mixing is an effective augmentation strategy for long-tailed recognition.

papers.title: Memorix: Managing Memory Selections for AI Agents
papers.abstract:
AI agents now handle a growing share of tasks across sessions within a persistent project. Their behavior depends not only on the model, but heavily on the persistent state they read from the environment. Existing systems assemble this memory at use time, splicing selected files into the prompt as a one-off payload. As a result, per-task assembly is costly and can still miss critical material, failures cannot be traced or replayed, and agents can read documentation written for the wrong version. Our key insight is that what an agent should read is mostly determined by its project, so the selection can be computed once, ahead of time, and reused across tasks.
  We propose Memorix, an agent memory system that realizes this insight. Memorix achieves this via three key mechanisms: (1) an immutable and versioned Store pins every source by identity and reproduces historical layouts cheaply, (2) a View that splits selection (Derivations) from composition (Environment), making the result reproducible and shareable, and (3) Quests and Profiles keep a delivered view refreshable and available inside the project as sources evolve. We implement Memorix and evaluate it on SWE-ContextBench and LibEvolutionEval against mainstream agent memory systems. Precomputed Environments raise resolved rate by up to 1.5X and deliver the correct library version on every version-conditioned task, while cutting amortized cost by up to 100X and build time by up to 38X.

papers.title: Faithful Where You Look: Anchor-Based Evaluation Hides Text Fabrication in Image-Conditioned Video Generation
papers.abstract: Image-conditioned video models are used to show real places, so whether their output stays faithful to the place they were shown is a practical question. The text benchmarks we found that check fidelity against a reference do so at an anchor - an annotated region, typically the sign the task is about. We show that this choice hides most of the failure. We conditioned four models from three vendors on 48 street-level references of Tokyo storefronts and measured text fidelity at the annotated sign and in the periphery, the other text the reference covers. At the anchor, all four models are close to a no-model control (anchor text fidelity 0.90-0.94 against 0.996) and are not reliably separated from one another.
