The reported anomaly-based cross-validation results favored the voting ensemble over the compared base models on the evaluated metrics. In anomaly-based cross-validation, VOTE improved prediction errors compared with MLP (256,128,64); improvements varied in the single-split comparison. Specifically, the hybrid model reduced MAE by 9.82%, MSE by 3.12%, RMSE by 1.76%, and MAPE by 6.77%. In the reported cross-validation comparison, the best anomaly-based hybrid model had lower MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE than the best IQR-based hybrid model by 9.81%, 34.30%, 18.99%, and 0.66%, respectively.

papers.title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
papers.abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.

authors.name: Zihao Wang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Symbolic Computation and Knowledge Engineering of Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
papers.abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.

authors.name: Zihao Wang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Symbolic Computation and Knowledge Engineering of Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: FORCE: Factorized Object Relations for Counterfactual Editing in Video World Models
papers.abstract: World models predict how scenes evolve, but they are difficult to interrogate: given a model that forecasts a video, one cannot easily ask what would have happened had a particular interaction between two objects been different. We present Factorized Object Relations for Counterfactual Editing (FORCE), a world model that infers pairwise interactions from raw video without supervision and represents each as an explicit latent per object pair, so that a relation can be removed, changed, transferred or introduced directly. Objects are extracted by slot attention over frozen self-supervised features; a relation encoder infers each pair latent from a short observation window, and an interaction head turns it into a force. The latent is held fixed across the rollout, so an edit persists rather than being recomputed, and every edit acts on the model's own quantities with no mapping to simulator parameters. We evaluate in a simulated environment where the true outcome of an edit is available, scoring the change each edit induces against the change the simulator produces under the same operation. On held-out clips, FORCE's edits made from video agree with the simulator's response at 0.19 to 0.37 on our effect-based score; trained and scored on exact object positions instead, the same architecture reaches 0.57 to 0.85. The gap therefore lies not in the learned relational dynamics but in perception: what bounds an edit is how precisely objects can be located from video, and the precision editing needs lies just beyond what current object-centric perception delivers. Closing that gap is a concrete target for making counterfactual world models work from video.

papers.title: Networked Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web
papers.abstract: Several genuine AI services may repeat one unsupported source, and correcting that source may leave later reports unchanged. We examine these networked consequences of synthetic social engineering (SSE), deliberately misleading influence intended to redirect AI recipients from authorized objectives. Our framework connects social influence, information aggregation, and misinformation correction research to observable evidence and permission boundaries. It separates originating attempts from legitimate intermediaries' work and distinguishes identity, evidentiary support, and authorization. We test four relationships using Qwen3-4B and two briefing tasks across 1,080 research units in our Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC). Multiple dependent publishers produced no supported increase in unsupported verification (78.3% versus 75.0%); publication availability left downstream violation reach at 40.0% in both arms. These comparisons direct attention to weaknesses already present in the reference workflows. High reference error rates and retained private handoffs preclude claims of immunity to social pressure. Without scope revalidation, corrections identifying dependent reports reduced residual invalid decisions from 14.4% to 8.1% at equal notification coverage and increased successful report repairs from 16/63 to 36/63. Scope revalidation added no demonstrated protection, and clearing dialogue offered no established recovery advantage. Unapproved requests persisted, all blocked by an external gateway. For designers, the findings caution against treating publisher count as independent evidence, notification as repair, or cleared histories as recovery. They support targeting corrections at reused reports, assessing factual and permission recovery separately, and enforcing authorization at execution.

papers.title: Seeing Less in a Sparse World: Cross-View Geolocalization from Limited Field-of-View Observations
papers.abstract:
Cross-view geolocalization aims to determine the geographic location of a ground-level image by retrieving its corresponding satellite image, offering a promising alternative for localization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied or degraded environments such as urban canyons, dense forests, and disaster scenarios. Despite recent progress, existing approaches remain limited by the lack of globally diverse training datasets and benchmarks that are often geographically restricted. Furthermore, most benchmarks rely on panoramic ground views, which do not reflect the limited field-of-view imagery captured by real world cameras.
  To address these challenges, we introduce Cross-View World 500k (CVW500k), a large-scale globally distributed dataset containing over 500,000 ground-satellite image pairs collected across diverse geographic regions and environments. Unlike previous datasets, CVW500k uses limited field-of-view ground images, providing a more realistic and challenging setting for cross-view geolocalization. In addition, we propose GeoQueryNet, a query-based cross-view fusion transformer framework designed to bridge the viewpoint gap between ground and satellite images. The model leverages a CLIP-based visual encoder with parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation and introduces a Cross-View Alignment Module that uses learnable query tokens to extract geographically consistent features across viewpoints. Our code can be found here: https://github.com/Fahim17/Cross_View_World_Dataset.git .

papers.title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
papers.abstract: We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.

papers.title: Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the representation of contiguous spectral signatures and spatial context under limited labeled supervision. Vision test-time training (TTT) offers an alternative to fixed-weight token mixing by performing self-supervised inner-model updates on the input sequence, but its application to center-pixel HSI classification remains insufficiently characterized. We present ViTTT-HSI, a spectral-spatial adaptation of the vision test-time training (ViT3) architecture. A spectral-aware embedding stem extracts ordered-band information using spectral convolution and forms spatial tokens without reducing their spatial resolution. Two ViT3-based TTT encoder blocks perform patch-conditioned token mixing, followed by the fusion of center-pixel and neighborhood-average features for classification. We evaluate the framework on Indian Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and Houston 2013 using ten random seeds and dataset-specific training fractions of 1% or 5%. The mean overall accuracies are 97.6390%, 98.8753%, 99.3292%, and 98.4283%, respectively. Ablations reveal a substantial contribution from the TTT inner update on Indian Pines and a smaller positive contribution on Pavia University, while the relative benefits of the spectral stem and feature fusion depend on the dataset. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using patch-conditioned vision TTT for spectral--spatial HSI classification and highlight the role of the inner adaptation mechanism.

authors.name: Xiang Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
papers.abstract: Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon. We prove that for $6\le n\le9$ the maximum is $(n-1)^{n-1}r_n^{n(n-1)}$, where $r_n=\sqrt{n/(n-1)}$. Up to the same symmetries, the unique maximizer consists of the origin and the vertices of a regular $(n-1)$-gon of radius $r_n$. For six points, algebraic elimination reduces the proof to an exact comparison of stationary values. For seven points, we compare all twelve classes in a published classification of equilibria. For eight and nine points, rigorous interval arithmetic establishes an inequality for every admissible pair. Summing over pairs gives the sharp global bound, and the equality conditions determine the configuration. An explicit ten-point comparison and a known instability result together exclude Chalk's configuration for every $n\ge10$. For each $n$ from two through eight, Mordell's problem and the minimum-diameter problem studied by Bateman and Erd\H{o}s have a common optimal configuration.

authors.name: Wensheng Yu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Online carpooling against an oblivious adversary
papers.abstract: In the online carpooling problem, edges on $n$ vertices arrive one at a time and must be oriented immediately, so as to keep the difference between the indegree and the outdegree of every vertex small. We give a randomized online algorithm which bounds the largest absolute difference over the first $T$ edges by $O((\log T)^{1/3})$ with high probability on every input sequence fixed in advance. This proves a conjecture of Kulkarni, Reis and Rothvoss and matches the known worst case lower bound. The algorithm keeps the law of the discrepancy vector dominated in the convex order by a Gaussian measure, and forces the endpoint with the smaller discrepancy to receive the edge whenever the two discrepancies are far apart. In the analysis we show that a vertex of discrepancy $D$ is preceded by a set of $O(D)$ vertices with total discrepancy $\Omega(D^2)$.

papers.title: Unbiased Low-Rank Approximation for Repeated Matrix-Vector Multiplication: Stability and Optimal Sampling
papers.abstract: Replacing the matrix in an iteration with random low-rank matrices can reduce the cost of matrix-vector multiplication. However, even if the sampled matrices equal the original matrix in expectation, the expected squared norm of the random iterates may grow while the original iteration converges. Under a fixed rank bound, we study how to choose the distribution of these random matrices to minimize this growth when sampling independently at each step. We derive an exact formula for the optimal asymptotic growth factor and use it to determine when the expected squared norm can converge to zero. We then characterize precisely when a fixed sampling distribution achieves this optimal factor and construct finite-support optimal distributions in every attainable case. These results determine the minimum rank required for stability and provide optimal sampling designs under the prescribed rank constraint.

papers.title: Nonlinear kink modes for nonisentropic supersonic vortex sheets
papers.abstract: In this paper, planar nonisentropic vortex sheets of the two-dimensional Euler equations under the stability condition are studied via nonlinear geometric optics, focusing on the interaction induced by a small-amplitude, high-frequency incident wave impinging on a planar vortex sheet. It is found that there exist three asymmetric critical incident angles at which resonance occurs, leading to a significant amplification of the reflected and refracted oscillatory waves. Moreover, by refining the asymptotic expansion, we deduce that the leading profiles of the highly oscillatory waves are described by initial-boundary value problems for Burgers transport equations, while the leading profile of the contact discontinuity front satisfies an initial value problem for a Hamilton--Jacobi-type equation, which reduces to a forced linear transport equation on one resonant branch. These results extend the resonant amplification mechanism from the isentropic setting to the nonisentropic Euler flow and reveal the asymmetric influence of entropy variations on the nonlinear evolution of compressible vortex sheets.

papers.title: Some variants of function domination
papers.abstract: We investigate whether classical recursion-theoretic notions defined by function domination remain unchanged when success is required only on sets of prescribed asymptotic density. We establish robustness for many such notions and uncover unexpected connections between familiar degree properties by comparing upper and lower density. In contrast, pdomination, as defined by Chong, Hoi, Stephan and Turetsky, is not robust under density weakenings. We also answer a question of Kjos-Hanssen and Nies by characterizing superhighness as domination with a threshold boundedly limit recursive in the oracle. As an application, we introduce supermaximal sets, a strengthening of maximality whose degrees are exactly the superhigh r.e. degrees.

papers.title: Effective Hausdorff dimension one is cofinal in the K-degrees
papers.abstract: Every K-degree has an upper bound of effective Hausdorff dimension one and Kurtz random sequences are cofinal in the K-degrees.

papers.title: Global weak solutions with vacuum for isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the unit disk under Dirichlet boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We construct global weak solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson systems in the unit disk under no-slip boundary conditions, allowing vacuum and unbounded densities for sufficiently small initial energy. Such solutions particularly possess uniform $L^{q_0}$ density bounds for some $q_0>4\gamma$, beyond the natural energy class. Our analysis combines Green function representations with the mean-value property of harmonic functions to isolate a pressure-generated harmonic component of the effective viscous flux and obtain a purely interior potential representation valid for both systems. These results complement Perepelitsa's half-space theory (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 212 (2014), pp. 709-726) and our recent half-plane work (arXiv:2601.11852, 2026), treating bounded-domain geometry and Poisson coupling with nonnegative initial density.

authors.name: Xin Zhong
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Engineering

papers.title: Faces or Models? Where the Age Gap in Facial Expression Recognition Comes From
papers.abstract: Facial expression recognition (FER) systems are increasingly used in elder care, yet their accuracy on older faces is rarely measured. This study evaluated five open-source FER models on the FACES database, which holds 2,052 posed photographs of 171 adults aged 19 to 80. The models cross three architectures (ResNet-18, POSTER++ and QCS) with two training datasets (RAF-DB and AffectNet). All models lost accuracy on older faces by 11.7 to 15.2 percentage points. Older faces were harder for people too: human raters lost 8.6 points, a classifier using only facial geometry lost 8.3, and for anger, fear, and happiness older adults differed more from one another when posing. On specific expressions the models fell much further than people did. AffectNet-trained models misread older neutral faces as sad or angry 62% of the time. RAF-DB-trained models lost fear, disgust, and anger instead. The gap persisted after controlling for architecture, image quality, cropping, and expression intensity. When only the final classification layer was refitted on older faces, the gap shrank from 11 to 21 points to 4 points or less, suggesting that the models' learned features can represent older faces and that the deficit lies in how the final layer was trained.

authors.name: Jessica Wang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

papers.title: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
papers.abstract: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

authors.name: Yuya Hattori
authors.institution: National Institute of Technology, Kure College

papers.title: CogRSI: Evolving and Auditing Cognitive Reasoning Strategies
papers.abstract: Can a language model learn better ways to reason about other people's minds by improving its own strategies, and are the strategies it learns actually right? We study this with cogrsi. A grounded reader marks who saw each event in a story and uses a short written principle to settle disagreements between its readings. With a principle written by experts, it beats self-consistency at the same token cost. A self-improvement loop then writes the principle itself. It keeps an update only if accuracy rises by a calibrated margin, and in one variant only if it also passes counterfactual test pairs. The learned principles transfer: on 800 BigToM pairs that no system had seen, each of them scores higher than the expert principle. We then check what the learned rules actually say. Each rule is translated into code and run on thousands of small stories with known answers. Most of them give a wrong answer in at least one situation they claim to cover, for example by treating a character who is in the room as knowing what happened even while asleep. Accuracy does not reveal which rules are wrong, and the counterfactual test does not fix this. A strategy can help in practice and still be wrong as a rule, so both need checking. Our code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: A Computational Verification of the Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for $z\leq 10^{500000}$
papers.abstract: We describe a finite computational verification of Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for normalized positive integer solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ with $z \leq 10^{500000}$. The archived run reports $239\,536\,376\,556$ triples with distinct maximal coordinates.The method combines a disjoint tree decomposition, certified fixed-point range bounds, a deterministic 48-bit candidate screen,and replay modulo $2^{128}$. We give the mathematical justification and a reproducibility procedure covering package checks,retained-data auditing, and a full rerun. The conclusion depends on correct execution of the exhaustive screen and replay; the retained audit does not regenerate the deleted screening buckets.

papers.title: Contracting for Experimentation with Private Findings
papers.abstract: A principal hires an agent to work on a project of unknown quality. Success is contractible, but before it occurs, the agent may privately obtain a favorable finding. For example, a scientist developing a drug may observe a promising microscope reading. An informed agent may conceal the finding; an uninformed agent may fake one. The agent's private information could guide both the project's duration and his pay. Yet I show that an optimal contract pays only success bonuses tied to time, not reported findings, consistent with time-based payment schedules often used in research funding. Dynamically arriving private information drives this simplicity: the agent can conceal good news to retain higher bonuses, so deterring concealment limits pay differences across report histories. Bonuses are high and rising in a research stage that induces learning, then fall to a low, constant level in a development stage where only an informed agent continues working. Rising bonuses reflect a novel force: rents from private learning motivate effort but shrink as fewer research periods remain.

authors.name: Hongcheng Li
authors.institution: The Affiliated Yongchuan Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

papers.title: Uniform cubic bounds for irrational values of the dilogarithm
papers.abstract: We study explicit denominator conditions ensuring the irrationality of the dilogarithm at positive and negative rational points. We prove that $\operatorname{Li}_2(p/q)$ is irrational whenever $q>(4e^4/27)p^3$, and obtain an explicit, slightly smaller threshold for $\operatorname{Li}_2(-p/q)$. The positive argument specializes the Rhin--Viola integral family and uses a uniform estimate for a restricted prime divisor. The negative argument combines the same arithmetic construction with three adjacent integral moments and an explicit maximization. We also give finite-numerator refinements by interpolating certified partition bounds and by introducing a comparison measure with a quadratic tail. In particular, $\operatorname{Li}_2(5/q)$ is irrational for every integer $q\ge418$. The proof separates the established integral and determinant constructions from the parameter estimates and finite certificates used here.

papers.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Vel\'azquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
papers.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.

authors.name: Junyu Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Comparison Principle and Semi-Lagrangian Methods for a Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman System with Recursive Utility
papers.abstract: We consider a system of coupled first-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations arising in continuous-time heterogeneous agent models with recursive utility, a class of models that has attracted increasing attention in macroeconomics. The first part of the paper establishes a comparison principle for the system when preferences exhibit early resolution of uncertainty. A key ingredient in the proof is an ordinally equivalent transformation of the recursive utility representation. In the second part, we develop semi-Lagrangian schemes and iterative algorithms for solving the associated nonlinear discrete systems. For preferences exhibiting late resolution of uncertainty, we establish a first-order error estimate for the semi-Lagrangian approximation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods yield results consistent with those obtained using the previously developed finite difference schemes.

papers.title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture for Borel Combinatorics
papers.abstract: The 1-2-3 Conjecture asserts that every finite graph without isolated edges admits edge weights from $\{1,2,3\}$ such that the sum function forms a vertex coloring. We study its Borel analogue for locally finite Borel graphs without isolated edges, proving that five weights suffice in general and four suffice for regular graphs. We obtain three weights for acyclic graphs admitting a Borel selection of a nonempty finite set of ends from each component. We also obtain $\mu$-measurable and Baire measurable vertex-coloring $3$-edge weightings from $3$-colorings of the same definability, under probability measure-preserving and Baire quasi-invariance conditions, respectively.

authors.name: Junhao Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The multivariate Berry-Esseen theorem with an absolute constant
papers.abstract: We prove that the multivariate Berry--Esseen inequality for sums of independent random vectors holds with the same constant in every dimension. For independent centered random vectors $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ whose covariance matrices sum to $I_d$, we show that the distance between the distribution of their sum and $N(0,I_d)$, measured uniformly over convex sets, is at most $C_0\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\|X_i\|_2^3$ for a universal constant $C_0$. The bound requires only finite third moments and holds uniformly in the dimension, the number of summands, and their distributions. It also yields the corresponding bound for independent and identically distributed vectors. In particular, $C_0$ can be chosen to be $980$.

authors.name: Zhi Ling
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Edge Mappings of Graphs
papers.abstract: The study of extremal problems for set mappings was initiated by Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal in 1958. Alon and Caro, and later Caro, Patk\'os, Tuza and Vizer, studied related problems for edge mappings of graphs. For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $g_0(G)$ be the minimum integer $N$ such that every mapping $f:E(K_N)\to E(K_N)$ satisfying $f(e)\cap e=\varnothing$ for every $e\in E(K_N)$ admits a copy $G^*$ of $G$ in $K_N$ with $f(e)\notin E(G^*)$ for every $e\in E(G^*)$. Gishboliner, Jin and Sudakov conjectured that $g_0(G)=O(n+m/\sqrt n)$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by constructing a family of graphs. We then prove that $g_0(G)=O(n+m^{3/4})$. Furthermore, for every $n\ge2$ and $m$ satisfying $\lceil n/2 \rceil\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}$, there exists a graph $G_*$ with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and no isolated vertices satisfying $g_0(G_*)=\Omega(n+m^{3/4})$. Thus the upper bound is best possible in terms of $n$ and $m$.

papers.title: Wasserstein accelerated proximal gradient algorithms
papers.abstract: We propose accelerated proximal gradient methods for composite optimization problems on the quadratic Wasserstein space of probability measures, including Kullback--Leibler divergence minimization. The objective function consists of a smooth geodesically convex functional and a possibly nonsmooth regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics. The convexity and smoothness conditions on the smooth component are imposed only on the feasible set. As a preliminary result, we establish the equivalence between geodesic convexity of the smooth functional on the feasible set and convexity of its Hilbert-space lift on the corresponding feasible set. Assuming exact proximal steps, we prove an $O(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the objective gap when the smooth component is geodesically convex and accelerated linear convergence when it is geodesically strongly convex. We also describe particle approximations of these algorithms.

authors.name: Noboru Isobe
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project

papers.title: On the complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials V: over commutative rings
papers.abstract:
Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, $2\times 2\times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over finite commutative rings closely correspond to finite nilpotent groups of class 2 (Baer, Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 1938).
  In this work, we study isomorphism testing of tensors over commutative rings from a complexity-theoretic viewpoint, and its applications. Some of our main results are: 1. Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a commutative ring. We introduce two complexity classes: $\mathsf{3TI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three modules over $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three free modules over $\mathrm{R}$. 2. We show that some classical problems considered by Grunewald and Segal (ibid.), and the problem of classifying Calabi--Yau threefolds, are $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathbb{Z}$-complete. We also show that many natural problems are complete for $\mathsf{3TI}_{\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z}}$. 3. We show that testing isomorphism of tensors in $\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2$ is polynomial-time equivalent to the principal ideal problem in algorithmic number theory. 4. We present an $N^{O((\log N)^{8/9})}$-time algorithm for testing isomorphism of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ and odd order $N$.

papers.title: Symbol-based residual certification of reduced and neural surrogates for tempered-fractional CGMY pricing
papers.abstract: We certify reduced and neural approximations of European-put price trajectories under the Carr--Geman--Madan--Yor model by residual bounds for the spline Galerkin discretisation of the tempered-fractional pricing equation. The Galerkin matrices are Toeplitz sections of an explicit periodised Fourier symbol; summing the alias series to a stated tail makes the assembled system exact to $10^{-8}$. A L\'evy--Khintchine argument gives the parameter-explicit bound $\lambda_{\min}(S_I)\ge r\,m_{\min}$ for the symmetric part, valid for $Y\in(0,2)\setminus\{1\}$, replacing numerical spectral estimates. A banded comparison norm built from the mass and stiffness symbols yields a rigorous certificate at $O(N)$ cost with explicit effectivity, and empirical interpolation of the symbol makes the operator affine in about 36 terms with a rigorous error transfer, so a reduced model is certified at a cost independent of $N$; a three-stage rule escalates to the full-order bounds only when needed. At the resolution that prices the whole parameter box to one cent ($N=1024$), the full-order certificate costs 6% of a direct solve, and the certified POD--Galerkin model of rank 80 costs 3% of it and settles 99.8% of $10^4$ queries without touching the full space. No false accept occurs on any query with a reference solution (150 inside the parameter box, 264 outside), and outside the box the certificate accepts 193 of the 210 queries on which the reduced model is still within one cent. The neural reduced models trained here miss the one-cent tolerance by a factor of at least 46; the certificate detects this at every query in a few milliseconds and explains it as a trade-off between temporal smoothness and coefficient accuracy. A residual certificate for the American put is proved as an outlook.

papers.title: A complete characterization of graphs with second largest eigenvalue at most $(\sqrt5-1)/2$
papers.abstract: In 1993, Cao and Hong posed the problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is greater than $1/3$ and less than $(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Subsequent work extended the question to the non-strict bound. We give a complete structural characterization of connected graphs $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge2$ satisfying $\lambda_2(G)\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$. Their complements are described by disjoint unions of graphs from an explicit family with least adjacency eigenvalue at least $-(1+\sqrt5)/2$, possibly together with a cone or a thin or thick spider constructed from disjoint unions of members of the same family, subject to explicit numerical inequalities. This provides a positive characterization of the class, going beyond the classical result of Cvetkovi\'c and Simi\'c that the bound $\lambda_2\le(\sqrt5-1)/2$ admits only finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs.

papers.title: MATE: Multi-Agent Traffic Engineering for Topology-Aware Distributed SRv6 Scheduling under Bursty Traffic
papers.abstract: As network traffic becomes increasingly dynamic and bursty, conventional centralized traffic engineering (TE) suffers from long control-loop delays caused by network-state aggregation, centralized computation, and policy distribution. In this paper, we propose MATE, a multi-agent TE method for proactive distributed scheduling in hybrid networks with partial deployment of Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6). MATE uses historical traffic stability to characterize the burst risk of each traffic demand and path sensitivity to quantify the ability of candidate paths to accommodate additional traffic, thereby enabling differentiated proactive scheduling tailored to heterogeneous traffic characteristics. MATE adopts an offline-centralized training and online-distributed execution architecture. During training, a shared global critic evaluates joint actions under a reward combining maximum link utilization (MLU) with variability-weighted path sensitivity, while counterfactual difference rewards provide agent-specific credit for actor learning. During online execution, edge agents generate traffic-splitting policies from local observations and apply them through SRv6, avoiding centralized optimization in each scheduling interval. Experiments on the China Environment for Network Innovations (CENI) testbed and simulations on the Sanet topology show that MATE outperforms a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) ablation baseline without agent-specific credit assignment, COPE, and TEAL in most evaluated scenarios and approaches centralized FIGRET on measured traffic traces. On CENI-Abilene, MATE achieves MLU within 10% of the linear-programming optimum in up to 90.1% of test instances. MATE also achieves lower median normalized MLU than FIGRET in most tested failure scenarios, with mean neural-inference times of 2.05--3.14~ms.

authors.name: Chengdi Lu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Fengqian Guo
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Hancheng Lu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Self-Normalized Inference from Riemannian Stochastic Gradient Paths
papers.abstract: Riemannian stochastic gradient paths estimate constrained parameters, but confidence regions usually require estimating the Hessian and gradient-noise covariance. We develop self-normalized inference from one path by expressing retained iterates in a common random tangent space. Their average and centered partial sums share an unknown covariance factor that cancels in a Brownian bridge pivot. Under suitable regularity conditions, a joint expansion of the averaged estimator and integrated path controls nonlinear coordinate errors using conditional second moments. The procedure uses fixed-dimensional memory and extends to nondegenerate smooth functionals and alternative local coordinates. Numerical studies show competitive coverage relative to plug-in Wald inference while avoiding Hessian and residual-density estimation.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Sharp Critical Rates for Locally Private Distribution Estimation
papers.abstract: We determine sharp minimax rates for distribution estimation under pure local differential privacy at critical query smoothness. For the integral probability metric generated by the unit ball of $B^d_{2,q}$, $1\le q\le\infty$, over fixed periodic Sobolev density balls with positive smoothness and interior slack at the uniform density, the expected risk is of order $N^{-1/2}(\log N)^{3/2-1/q}$, where $N=n\varepsilon^2$; expected squared risk has the squared order. The fine index governs aggregation across resolutions that share one private information budget. A single noninteractive release with a measurable proper density output attains these rates, and matching lower bounds allow finite public blackboard interaction and repeated participation under each user's total privacy budget. A known $L^2$ radius permits the same rates without using density smoothness, with output in the $L^2$ density ball. Separately, for positive smooth densities on $[0,1]$, integrated squared CDF risk has minimax order $(\log N)^2/N$, with sharp quantile, Wasserstein, and transport map consequences. The rates hold uniformly for $0<\varepsilon\le1$ as $N\to\infty$, with class parameters fixed.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Minimax estimation of linear functionals in the Darcy inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study estimation of linear functionals $\int f\psi$ of the conductivity $f$ in the Darcy problem $\nabla\cdot(f\nabla u)=g$ from observations of $u$ in Gaussian white noise of level $N^{-1/2}$. When the potential has a single nondegenerate minimum, we determine the minimax rates over Sobolev balls in the linearised experiment. Unless a compatibility condition along the gradient flow holds, the rate is governed by an effective dimension $T$ of the Hessian at the minimum, not by the ambient dimension: it is $N^{-(2s+T)/(4s+8)}$ for $T<4$, has an elbow at $T=4$ with an extra logarithmic factor, and is parametric for $T>4$. In the nonlinear experiment we show that these lower bounds persist when compatibility fails at the reference and $T\le4$, and we prove the minimax rate on classes with isotropic critical Hessians, and the parametric rate near references with $T>4$. In dimension at most four, no nonzero linear functional is uniformly $\sqrt N$-estimable on a Sobolev neighbourhood of the constant conductivity, even when it is regular there.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Infinite Quantiles Inference under Local Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: We study simultaneous quantile inference under local differential privacy for a number of target probabilities that grows with the sample size. Each user participates once, so learning unknown quantile locations and calibrating their joint uncertainty must share the same private information. We fuse complementary cumulative distribution function (CDF) scores from a single tree report using their exact covariance; the variance at the correct anchor is no larger than that of either score, and anchor error incurs only quadratic excess variance. Three consecutive cohorts then localize the quantiles, estimate their densities, and supply fresh scores for a one-step correction and joint multiplier calibration. Under mild conditions, a uniform representation controls localization and density errors and yields asymptotically valid simultaneous coverage. A fixed-privacy regime permits every polynomially growing target grid. Simulations show consistent same-report precision gains, while comparisons with CDF-band inversion expose the sample cost of learning target locations. Census microdata illustrates how the resulting joint intervals support wage-percentile ratios.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Density and distribution of quotients associated with Goldring's $w$-function
papers.abstract: For primes $p,q,r$ that are not all equal, let $n=pqr$ and define Goldring's $w$-function by $w(n)=P(p+q)P(p+r)P(q+r)$, where $P(a)$ denotes the largest prime factor of $a$. In this paper, we resolve three problems of Chen, Shi and Wu. As $n\to\infty$ through such products, the sets of finite limit points of $P(w(n))/P(n)$ and $w(n)/n$ are $[0,1]$ and $[0,\infty)$, respectively. The same conclusions hold when $n$ is restricted either to $p^2q$ with distinct primes $p,q$ or to squarefree products of three primes. Nevertheless, on each of these three sets, the proportion of integers $n\le X$ satisfying $P(w(n))/P(n)>\alpha$ tends to zero as $X\to\infty$, for every fixed $\alpha>0$. We also determine the complete set of finite joint limit points of the two quotients for $n=p^2q$ with $p\ne q$.

authors.name: Jun-Jia Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: EEFA: A Framework for the Ethical Evaluation of AI Agents
papers.abstract: The rapid deployment of autonomous AI agents across consequential domains including healthcare, legal services, nancial management, and enterprise workows has created an urgent governance challenge. While the eld of AI evaluation has produced sophisticated benchmarks for measuring agent capability, these frameworks measure exclusively what agents can do rather than how they do it. The ethical dimensions most critical to responsible agent deployment, in- cluding respect for human autonomy, harm avoidance, transparency and non-deception, privacy compliance, and accountability, are systematically absent from current evaluation practice. This paper addresses that gap through three contributions. First, a structured literature review of twelve leading AI agent benchmarks characterizes the ethical dimensions those bench- marks do and do not measure. Second, the Ethical Evaluation Framework for AI Agents (EEFA) is introduced as a comprehensive, operationalizable instrument for ethical agent evaluation, grounded in established AI ethics principles and designed for use by developers, auditors, and regulators. Third, a reproducible validation protocol is specied for applying the EEFA to deployed agent systems, with illustrative test scenarios across all ve framework dimensions. The EEFA is organized across ve primary dimensions: Autonomy Preservation, Harm Avoid- ance, Transparency and Non-Deception, Privacy Compliance, and Accountability and Traceabil- ity. The framework maps directly onto the requirements of the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, positioning it as a practical compliance assessment instrument for high-risk AI applications. Empirical application of the framework across diverse benchmarks and agent systems is identied as a priority direction for future work.

papers.title: Periodic Fisher-KPP equations on a regular tree
papers.abstract: We study Fisher-KPP equations on regular trees with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in distance from a vertex or a bi-infinite geodesic. For nonzero finitely supported data, we characterize the spectral threshold between uniform extinction and persistence, including critical extinction. We establish Bramson corrections for Busemann step data at positive, zero and negative speeds and, above the periodic extinction threshold, for the largest Busemann coordinate and radial level positions of finitely supported solutions. When the periodic spectral minimum is nonpositive but the geodesic spectral threshold is positive, we construct a smallest positive stationary solution with exponential transverse decay, prove uniqueness under an exponential bound, and determine longitudinal spreading with its logarithmic correction. We also classify positive stationary solutions depending only on distance from the geodesic and prove existence and stability results for moving and stationary fronts.

papers.title: Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We study Fisher-KPP equations on hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in the distance from a point or a geodesic. We determine spectral thresholds for extinction and persistence, including critical extinction from $L^2$ data, and characterize the signed speeds of horospherical fronts. In the hyperbolic plane, we construct a smooth periodic reaction admitting a positive stationary solution that decays away from a geodesic, and determine the spreading speed along the geodesic. For constant linear growth, we obtain logarithmic level positions with bounded error for balls, horoballs and geodesic tubes.

papers.title: Quantitative spectral rigidity for negatively curved manifolds and Outer Space
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed manifold with fundamental group $G$. A subset of conjugacy classes $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$ is said to be spectrally rigid if when two negatively curved Riemannian metrics have the same marked length spectra on $E$, then their length spectra agree on all conjugacy classes. In this work we study spectrally rigid subsets from a quantitative perspective. We show that, if the density of $E \subset \text{conj}(G)$, measured with respect to a fixed reference metric, decays more slowly than $T^{-1/2}$ then $E$ is spectrally rigid. We establish analogous rigidity results for Culler-Vogtmann Outer Space and show that the $T^{-1/2}$ threshold is sharp in this setting.

papers.title: A local limit theorem for singularity visits on translation surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a translation surface with at least one singularity. We investigate the distribution of the number of singularity encounters along prime closed geodesics on $X$. Writing $\ell(\gamma)$ for the geometric length of a closed geodesic and $m(\gamma)$ for the number of singularities it encounters, we establish a uniform counting local limit theorem for the values of $m(\gamma)$ sampled over $\ell(\gamma)<T$. The key technical step is to introduce and study a trace-class operator whose spectral data encodes the Fourier transform of our counting distribution. Our results hold for every translation surface, without genericity assumptions.

papers.title: Finite Groups with Few Almost Maximal Subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group. L. Morgana, C. E. Praeger, A.E. Zalesski \cite {MOR} introduced the notion of almost maximal subgroup of $G$. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be almost maximal in $G$ if $N_G(H)$ is maximal in $G$. In this paper, let $AM(G)$ denote the number of conjugacy classes of all almost maximal subgroups of $G$. First, we prove that $G$ is Dedekindian if and only if $AM(G)=0$. Second, we show that the finite groups with $AM(G)\leq 1$ are supersolvable. Furthermore, we characterize the structure of finite groups with $AM(G)=1$. Final, we investigate a lower bound of $AM(G)$ for certain non-solvable groups.

papers.title: Mutual Information Estimation via Triangular Transport Maps: Finite Sample Guarantees and Sample Allocation
papers.abstract: We study finite sample guarantees for transport based mutual information estimation. Mutual information can be estimated by first learning the conditional and marginal densities and then evaluating their log-density ratio by Monte Carlo. Given training samples, we use triangular transport maps to learn these densities and then compute the mutual information estimate on an independent batch of evaluation samples. For conditional density estimation using triangular transport maps, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees over realizable H\"older classes by viewing the conditional density as an ordinary density with respect to the product of the law of the conditioning variable and Lebesgue measure. This allows standard density estimation techniques to be applied directly to the conditional density estimation. These results yield finite sample guarantees for the resulting mutual information estimator and characterize how a fixed sample budget should be allocated between training and evaluation in order to minimize the mean squared error. Numerical experiments support the predicted training and evaluation error rates and illustrate the resulting sample allocation tradeoff.

authors.name: Fengyi Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses
papers.abstract: We compute the limit of free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses with possibly non-convex interaction and couplings satisfying a finite fourth-moment assumption. The couplings need not be Gaussian. The limit is given by a logarithmic-determinant variational formula, equivalently by a finite-dimensional matrix Dyson equation, and its zero-temperature limit yields the ground-state energy. The limiting formulas depend only on the covariance of the couplings. We also study fluctuations: at an interior minimizer, an explicit variance bound transfers the limiting law of a logarithmic linear statistic to the free energy. For Gaussian couplings, this yields Gaussian fluctuations. At a boundary minimizer, assuming a simple regular edge with GOE Tracy-Widom fluctuations and a one-edge reduction, we transfer the edge fluctuations to the free energy.

authors.name: Yanjin Xiang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Higher dimensional Kleinian groups of small Hausdorff dimension are classical Schottky groups II
papers.abstract: This is the higher dimensional continuation of our works on Hausdorff dimension of Kleinian groups \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020}. In this paper we prove that for all $r\ge 2$ there exists $\lambda_r>0$, which is independent of the dimension $N$ of the hyperbolic space, such that any finitely generated non-elementary torsion-free Kleinian group of $\Isom(\mathbb{H}^N)$ generated by $r$ elements with limit set of Hausdorff dimension $<\lambda_r$ is a classical Schottky group. For two generators the bound can be taken to be $1/3$. The proof relies on our previous works in \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020} and on a metric carrier graph reduction. Our result can also be considered as the complete converse to the well-known theorem of Phillips-Sarnak \cite{PS} for spaces of any dimension $N$.

papers.title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
papers.abstract: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. We introduce a finite-exceedance dependence principle: if the finite-exceedance dependence error vanishes at every fixed order and high-order exceedances are mildly controlled, then a finite-order Bonferroni argument yields asymptotic independence between the sum and the maximum. We further give an independent-proxy criterion for verifying this: for each finite set of exceedances, it suffices to construct an exactly independent proxy for the sum-type statistic whose approximation error is negligible in aggregate. Local deletion under dependency graphs and Gaussian regression and residualization are two examples. The framework gives modular derivations of existing sum--max independence results.

authors.name: Hongjian Shi
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
papers.abstract: We reassess five economic claims about the cryptocurrency trend factor (CTREND): cross-sectional return predictability, high risk-adjusted performance, incremental information beyond market, size, and momentum, the ability to replace momentum in factor models, and robustness among large and liquid coins and after trading costs. Our reconstruction and code audit identify issues in information timing, technical indicators, forecast coverage, portfolio formation, and return accounting. We first correct future-information use and related settlement rules, then implement broader corrections to indicators, forecast availability, and portfolio accounting. Without additional coin exclusions, the first stage changes CTREND's mean weekly gross return from 4.07% to 4.25%, annualized Sharpe ratio from 2.08 to 1.48, and weekly alpha relative to published market, size, and momentum factors from 2.77% to 3.06%. After comprehensive correction, these become 0.05%, 0.01, and -1.38%; the alpha is no longer significant. Replacing momentum with CTREND yields an advantage in maximum squared Sharpe ratios of 0.058 in the original implementation, 0.024 after the first-stage correction, and -0.0185 after comprehensive correction, with a statistically significant overall decline. Mean weekly gross returns for the largest 100 coins change from 2.93% to 3.99% to 1.00%, while mean weekly net returns for the full long-short portfolio under the lowest assumed trading costs change from 2.93% to 3.35% to -0.87%. These findings show that reported performance and factor-substitution gains depend materially on implementation and sample composition. We distinguish predictive information, an independent return premium, and the incremental value of replacing an existing factor as separate economic claims.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for Products of Cubic Polynomials over Prime Fields
papers.abstract:
We study exact representations of explicit signed modular predicates on $\{-1,1\}^n$ as products of bounded-degree polynomials over prime fields, measured by total variable-occurrence cost. Our main result is an exponential lower bound for products of cubic polynomials. Over $\mathbb F_3$ the proof is self-contained: every cubic factor in a nonvanishing product is a unit on the sign cube, the unit identity forces bounded affine-observation complexity, and a simultaneous clustering argument converts this structural compression into an exponential occurrence lower bound. We also give an alternative reconstruction route that isolates the quadratic structure behind the cubic classification.
  We then extend the cubic theorem to every fixed prime field $\mathbb F_p$ of characteristic greater than three for odd target modulus $q$ coprime to $p$. The only non-elementary structural input in this extension is Karam's restricted-range rank theorem; the conversion from multiplication to parity and the $p$-tuple clustering argument are proved explicitly. Finally, we establish a coefficient-field-independent degree-lifting principle. If a lower bound is known at one fixed degree, restriction to a large independent set yields a quantitative lower bound at the next degree. In particular, the exponential cubic theorem implies $
L^{(p,q)}_4(n)=\Omega_{p,q}\!\left(\frac{n^4}{(\log(2+n))^3}\right). $
For the characteristic-three core this already gives a lower bound for a restricted mixed-modulus circuit class.

papers.title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.

papers.title: Discovering Semantic Granularity in Images through Clustering of Pretrained Visual Representations
papers.abstract: Semantic granularity, which refers to the levels at which visual representations organize image content into meaningful entities, is fundamental to image understanding. However, whether pretrained visual representations inherently encode semantic structures at multiple granularities remains poorly understood. This paper presents a representation-driven approach for discovering semantically meaningful image regions at different granularities through clustering of pretrained visual representations without semantic supervision. Specifically, we concatenate selected feature maps extracted from a pretrained visual model and apply a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based projection to derive pixel-wise principal representation maps (PRMs). The resulting PRMs capture implicit semantic structures embedded in pretrained visual representations, making them accessible to subsequent semantic clustering. We then introduce the semantic continuity rate (SCR), based on the silhouette principle, to quantify the coherence of pixel-wise representations within and between clusters at different candidate granularities. Furthermore, we analyze the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of SCR profiles to assess representation suitability for discovering semantic regions at multiple granularities. Our results indicate that PRMs exhibiting higher SNR values over an initial range of cluster numbers tend to yield more semantically meaningful regions across multiple granularities. We evaluate the proposed approach on the COCO-2017 and VOC-2012 validation datasets using Hungarian-matched intersection over union (HIoU). The results demonstrate competitive segmentation performance among the compared methods, supporting the feasibility of discovering useful semantic granularities through clustering PRMs without semantic supervision.

papers.title: Constructing Budgeted KGW Evasion through Token-Event Evidence Replacement
papers.abstract: KGW watermarks bias sampling to accumulate keyed detection evidence. We construct budgeted evasion through token-event evidence replacement using ordinary phrase rewrites. Our construction jointly selects compositions of LLM-proposed alternatives from an independent model and measures global token-edit distance on complete outputs. At the largest attainable cost within the budget, exact coverage search maximizes removal of original scored token pairs. It uses a known tokenizer without the key, detector feedback or queries to the watermarked model. Exact accounting separates source evidence removed, evidence created and length effects, with initial strength setting the required reduction. Separate signed-event analysis found that mean suppression arose mainly from removing watermark-enriched source events. In controlled, occurrence-counted, one-token-context KGW tests on short passages, 39 of 82 qualified, initially detected sources yielded rewrites with terminal detector score Z < 4 that passed blinded source-relative model review, at a mean actual token-edit cost of 16.0% under a 20% allowance. To examine whether this initial requirement can be inferred, a separate historical 95-passage study estimated initial detector score Z0 from generation traces with correlation 0.793 and an in-sample association beyond length. This aggregate information did not establish improved allocation, and the separate no-trace stopping test did not reliably exploit cheaper reviewed crossings in the candidate bank. Comparisons did not establish an advantage over simpler selection and ordinary constrained rewriting. The construction makes budgeted evidence replacement executable while exposing limits in signed reduction and recognition of sufficient editing.

papers.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
papers.abstract: We establish a near-optimal upper bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{1+o(1)}))$ for the $N$-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow, improving on the bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{2}))$ of Gu, Quastel, and Tsai. Near-optimality follows from the lower bound $\exp(\exp(cN))$ of Ganguly and Nam. These estimates establish the exponential scale of the ground-state energy of the two-dimensional $N$-body delta-Bose gas predicted by Rajeev's conjecture, up to a vanishing error in the exponent. As a further step toward this conjecture, we derive, for each fixed $N$, a formula for the ground-state energy in terms of the bottom of the spectrum of a principal operator.

papers.title: Herding or Racing? Decomposing Cross-Account Order-Flow Persistence in On-Chain Markets
papers.abstract: Most of the autocorrelation in trade signs on decentralized exchanges comes from pairs of trades sent by different wallets. For Uniswap v3, this has been read as herding dominating order splitting -- the reverse of what equity markets show. We show that this herding share mixes two quantities: the probability $p$ that consecutive orders come from the same account, which is small when thousands of wallets are trading, and the ratio $\kappa$ of cross-account to same-account sign correlation. For any $p$, $\kappa$ equals one under the public-signal benchmark of T\'oth et al. and zero under independent order splitting. On Uniswap v3 USDC-WETH (one week each in 2023 and 2024), the herding share is 0.65-0.86, but $\kappa$ is only 0.05-0.10. On a fully on-chain EVM limit order book, the herding share is similar (0.61-0.87), but $\kappa$ is 0.72-0.76; among Uniswap swaps above USD 100k, it is 0.34-0.52. Where $\kappa$ is high, cross-account co-movement is mostly a race for the price on a centralized exchange. It is concentrated in orders a few blocks apart, and a cross-fitted gradient-boosted filter that sees only Binance data removes about three quarters or more of it. This race flow accounts for most of the losses of liquidity providers. We recommend reporting $\kappa$ alongside the herding share and modeling on-chain order flow as splitting traders plus arbitrageurs who respond to the centralized-exchange price.

papers.title: An exhaustion-aware product moment and zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions
papers.abstract: We refine the ordinary product moment in the cubic-theta comparison by allowing a returned prime product to be exhausted. The return stops either when the positive-prime length inequality holds or when the established prime-free ordinary estimate applies. Keeping the extracted central coefficients gives a local normalization inequality on a larger domain. On the critical ordinary-length interval this yields a net first-mean gain of $1/20000$. We prove the complementary-class, short-sum and algebraic comparison inequalities directly, and obtain the endpoint $B_*-1/160000=0.87446205769353\ldots$, where $B_*$ is Liu's algebraic boundary. The zero-free conclusion is conditional on the cited general-field theta, detector, prior-bound and Mellin input theorems in their stated uniform forms. The proof includes the actual return weights, both approximate-functional-equation arms, the principal-residue normalization and descent to arbitrary number fields.

papers.title: Real zeros of $w$-polynomials: cycles and complete cutsets
Selection principle for Weak KAM solutions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via large deviation principle for diffusions
papers.abstract: Stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equations generally admit many weak KAM solutions. The question is how to select one weak KAM solution that reflects a meaningful physical principle. In this paper, we propose a selection principle for Hamilton-Jacobi equations arising from the large deviation principle of general drift-diffusion processes on $\mathbb{R}^n$ based on the exponential asymptotics of invariant measures. We first characterize the Aubry set as the finitely many equilibria of the drift, using an action estimate from the orthogonal decomposition of the drift. For any boundary data on the Aubry set compatible with the Peierls barrier, we construct the unique coercive weak KAM solution with these boundary data, which is also the maximal locally Lipschitz viscosity solution. The Freidlin-Wentzell graph formula then provides the boundary data on the Aubry set that select the unique weak KAM solution. The selected solution is exactly the rate function in the large deviation principle for invariant measures in the zero noise limit. We also show that this rate function is the vanishing viscosity limit, to which the viscous approximations converge locally uniformly. Finally, under additional regularity assumptions, we show that the long-time and zero-noise limits commute for suitably prepared initial densities.

papers.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
papers.abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. To produce the radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed to be most likely an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of $-(6.8-9.6)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$ when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD ($1.4~M_\odot$). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than $1.4~M_\odot$ if the measured period derivative exceeds $-9.6\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra-contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a $1.0-1.6~M_\odot$ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of $-(4.9-13.5)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of $1.35-1.5~M_\odot$. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be $0.006$ when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

papers.title: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail
papers.abstract: An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks. We design a posterior-sampling agent for it. Each period it draws a market from an exact posterior and posts the bid and discount of that market's exactly solved season plan, so every action is one a fully informed seller could take. In a simulated online florist it has the lowest regret averaged over markets. In weak markets it gives up 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons, four to seven times less than drawing once per season. A planner acting on point estimates can stop bidding and never learn that bidding pays. The agent escapes after about three seasons on average, against fifty with one draw per season. Where displayed scarcity keeps willingness to pay above the posted price, the discount needs no learning. Customers waiting for the discount to return to its recent level look like lost sales, so frequent waiting makes the agent underrate its market. One discount per season removes waiting at a cost of 5.9% of clairvoyant revenue in a weak market and none in a strong one.

authors.name: Hadi Mohammadi
authors.institution: University of British Columbia, Okanagan Campus

papers.title: Chemotaxis-Stokes system with $p$-Laplacian slow diffusion: global boundedness across the full $p>2$ range
papers.abstract:
The global boundedness problem for three-dimensional chemotaxis-fluid systems with nonlinear diffusion presents substantial analytical challenges, particularly in the near-linear diffusion regime. Indeed, the porous-medium and p-Laplacian diffusion operators approach the classical Laplacian as $m\searrow1$ and $p\searrow2$, and the extra a priori control afforded by nonlinear structures becomes increasingly difficult to exploit. This difficulty is reflected in the porous-medium setting, where establishing boundedness throughout $m>1$ required a sequence of substantial developments spanning more than a decade (2010-2024). For the p-Laplacian case, despite significant progress, the problem remained open in the near-linear range $2<p\le p^*(\approx2.01)$, due to the saturation of classical Moser-type iterations as $p\searrow2$.
  In this paper, we establish global bounded strong solutions for a three-dimensional chemotaxis-Stokes system with p-Laplacian slow diffusion and signal consumption. Our approach departs from the conventional $L^q$-iteration framework and develops a weighted energy method that directly exploits the coercive structure of the nonlinear diffusion operator. A weighted Rellich identity yields density estimates. To control the resulting boundary contribution on general smooth domains, we first use tangential differentiation along the boundary to lower its order, and then apply a trace-embedding estimate. Combined with a high-gradient/low-gradient decomposition, these estimates allow us to control the mixed chemotactic terms and close the coupled estimates for the density, signal, and fluid. The resulting estimates hold throughout $2<p\le 3$, thereby resolving the previously open range $2<p\le p^*$. Together with existing results for $p>p^*$, our work establishes boundedness throughout the entire slow-diffusion range $p>2$.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Extend Their Agentic Capabilities to Goal Pursuit in Open-Ended Multi-Turn Interaction?
papers.abstract: Goal pursuit in open-ended dialogue requires agents to adapt their actions to interaction feedback across successive exchanges. We investigate whether agentic capabilities developed for multi-step tool use carry over to dialogue organized through the model's native tool interface, and how this changes interaction behavior. We define Tool-Mediated Interaction (TMI) as a training-free protocol that represents dialogue actions as tool calls and counterpart responses as tool results, maintaining a continuous reasoning-action-observation loop with retained reasoning and interaction history. We evaluate TMI across social interaction, emotional support, persuasion, and price negotiation using two models and 15,678 main-experiment episodes. Across both models, TMI improves social goal attainment, emotional-support preference, donation amounts, and buyer negotiation margins over conversational baselines with and without thinking. A Qwen ablation further shows that TMI outperforms ordinary conversation with retained reasoning on all four primary outcomes. Behavioral analyses associate the improvements with task-specific patterns in initial proposals and responses to interaction feedback. Alongside these gains, TMI reduces mean reasoning tokens per decision by 42.0-81.5% relative to the thinking baseline and lowers mean cross-turn phrase reuse across all eight model-environment pairs. These findings show that interaction organization shapes both goal attainment and reasoning across dialogue turns.

authors.name: Mingyu Chen
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Empirical rather than simulated spectral band adjustment of MODIS to Sentinel-3 OLCI for European vegetation monitoring
papers.abstract: Spectral band adjustment derived from convolved spectra describes sensor differences under controlled conditions, but its applicability to operational products requires assessment. We compare this approach with adjustment estimated directly from MODIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI observations for European vegetation monitoring. Both streams undergo atmospheric correction and Ross-Thick/Li-Sparse Reciprocal BRDF normalization to nadir viewing and local solar noon. Using observations from 2019-2024, we derive annual OLCI/MODIS reflectance-ratio relationships with unadjusted MODIS NDVI. The operational correction uses quadratic red and linear near-infrared (NIR) functions. We compare these relationships with irradiance-weighted canopy simulations and assess the empirical correction at 460 locations. Simulated and empirical relationships differ, particularly for red reflectance at high NDVI. Background-dependent simulated ratios also demonstrate the limitations of a single NDVI-based function. The empirical correction reduces red and NIR root-mean-square error (RMSE) at 66.3% and 71.1% of locations, with median paired reductions of 5.98% and 13.67%. Median paired RMSE decreases by 0.86% for NDVI but increases by 0.95% for EVI2, 0.74% for NIRv and 7.07% for the Plant Phenology Index (PPI), calculated with stream-specific historical references. This study establishes an operational empirical adjustment and shows that the specified spectral simulation does not reproduce the relationship between the normalized products. It provides evidence for improved reflectance consistency while demonstrating that vegetation-index benefits require separate assessment.

papers.title: Adaptive Surface Cleaning under Uncertain Cleaning Response
papers.abstract: Surface cleaning requires robots to adapt both where they clean and how they interact with contamination whose response to cleaning may vary spatially and remain unobservable prior to interaction. We formulate adaptive surface cleaning as a partially observable Markov decision process and propose a belief-aware planning framework that uses observed cleaning outcomes to update a latent local cleaning-response model and adapt subsequent cleaning motions, forces, and passes. Preliminary grid-world simulations demonstrate the resulting closed-loop planner adapting its spatial decomposition and cleaning actions as the surface evolves.

papers.title: Behavior-Discriminative Reward Shaping for Reward-Robust Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reward-robust RL typically models misspecification by specifying an uncertainty set that constrains the discrepancy of plausible rewards from a base reward. However, such reward space discrepancies can be behaviorally irrelevant: under potential-based reward shaping (PBRS), many distinct rewards preserve policy ordering. This can introduce substantial redundancy into standard uncertainty sets and degrade optimization performance. We propose Shaping-Aware Reward-Robust RL, which constructs uncertainty sets over PBRS equivalence classes by projecting each reward to a canonical representative, ensuring that the resulting set contains only rewards that induce behaviorally distinct policy rankings.
