We prove that this projection preserves the optimal robust value while shrinking the uncertainty set and improving empirical performance. Using the connection between robustness and regularization, we obtain a practical algorithm to solve the shaping-aware reward-robust RL problem and enjoy convergence guarantees under standard assumptions. Experiments on benchmarks spanning diverse task domains and levels of complexity show consistent improvements over representative robust RL baselines and exhibit improved robustness to reward perturbations.

papers.title: Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity from a universal cumulant lifting
papers.abstract: Using probabilistic methods, we establish universal cumulant lifting criteria for Stieltjes and Hamburger moment sequences. In the Stieltjes case, we characterize coefficientwise Hankel total positivity after convolution with every initial moment sequence by requiring each once-shifted cumulant sequence to be Stieltjes. We also prove equivalence with the numerical moment property at every nonnegative intensity. In the Hamburger case, we use twice-shifted cumulants to obtain coefficientwise-positive leading Hankel determinants, a degree bound, an explicit highest-degree component, and drift invariance. We work with formal series and require neither exponential moments nor moment determinacy. We establish composition, binomial-convolution, and substitution results, and apply them to implicit equations and autonomous differential equations, tree and forest families, and lognormal compound-Poisson moments in a unified approach. From known moment sequences, we obtain general coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive families containing the classical Bessel, Lah, and Laguerre polynomials. We not only give new proofs of coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of many combinatorial polynomials, but also prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity for the component polynomials of functional digraphs confirming a conjecture of Sokal and establish fixed-shape Schl\"afli--Gessel--Seo polynomials positivity supporting another conjecture of Sokal.

papers.title: Sampling Design and Confidence Tubes for Integral Curves on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: We estimate the integral curve of an unknown vector field from noisy tangent vector field on a known compact Riemannian manifold. We consider two sampling settings: independent observations at random locations that have already been collected, and a fixed response budget that allows subsequent locations to be chosen using pilot information. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the passive kernel estimator has curve error of order $n^{-2/(d+3)}$ in probability, with sample size $n$ and manifold dimension $d$. Its functional central limit theorem has a limit characterized by a linear stochastic differential equation. For active sampling, an independent pilot directs one new batch of measurements to neighborhoods of the target curve. Under localization, smoothness and design conditions, this concentration yields expected maximum curve error of order $N^{-1/2}$, including the pilot in the total response budget $N$. Both methods provide simultaneous geodesic confidence tubes with asymptotically exact coverage under mild conditions. Simulations show narrower active tubes in most reported settings, with improved small-sample coverage in some three-dimensional examples. Ocean-drifter observations illustrate mean-flow reconstruction on the sphere, and a canopy-flow LDA application uses retrospective active sampling to quantify lateral and vertical departures of local mean streamlines.

papers.title: A Bounded Evaluation Protocol for Representational Systematicity
papers.abstract: Multiple studies have shown that neural networks can be behaviorally systematic, producing correct outputs for novel combinations of familiar parts. Whether they are also representationally systematic, that is, whether they represent these parts and their roles and use them to produce the outputs, remains hard to test, because each kind of evidence can mislead on its own: correct outputs can come from shortcuts, a decodable signal need not be used, an intervention can act through unintended pathways, and a failed search does not show absence. We propose a bounded evaluation protocol for representational systematicity (Bounded-RS): for an explanation that attributes a systematic behavior to a declared representation, it tests on a matched behavioral contrast whether that representation is recoverable and whether it is causally used, checks the validity of this evidence, and assigns the explanation one of four bounded states, Unsupported, Present-only, Causal-use, or Undetermined, through control-calibrated scores, gates, and stop rules. On a semantic-parsing testbed of 96 matched sets that we release, the tested role-filler Binding explanation of fine-tuned T5 models is Causal-use and the distributed Geometry explanation is Unsupported within its declared search space, verdicts that hold across calibration-compatible parameter configurations, training seeds, and T5-base. On 41 cases with known causal status, full adjudication licenses a false Causal-use in 1 of 34 noncausal cases, against 13 when recoverability is taken as use, without missing any causal case. Bounded-RS thus turns the question of representational systematicity, debated since Fodor and Pylyshyn, into comparable and falsifiable verdicts on declared explanations, each reported with the evidence pattern that licenses it and, for a negative, the search space that bounds it.

authors.name: Wenshuo Wang
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: From Apparent Search Gains to Selection Failures: Auditing Test-Time Inference in Structured Workflow Planning
papers.abstract: Test-time search can improve structured planning, but when methods differ in prompts, post-processing, and selection, it is unclear what an observed gain should be attributed to. We study this question on DisasterBench, where models compose typed multi-tool workflows, by decomposing inference into three observable stages: whether a correct workflow is discovered, whether it survives structural validation, and whether it is finally selected. Comparing independent sampling, a nominal tree-search configuration, and multi-operator search under controlled inference budgets on two model families, we find that (i) the nominal tree-search configuration realizes non-adaptive complete-workflow sampling, and independent sampling with its expansion prompt reproduces its candidate discovery without constructing a tree; (ii) structural validation never removes the last correct workflow in our evaluated candidate pools, whereas majority voting leaves a discovered correct workflow unselected on 10-19% of tasks per pool, with an audit confirming substantive tool-choice or information-flow errors in 57 of 60 examined cases; and (iii) a tool-specification-aware verifier recovers some of these losses but overturns more correct decisions than it fixes. Our results motivate auditing realized rather than nominal inference pipelines, and reporting discovery, validity, and selection separately.

authors.name: Zhiyuan Wang
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: Exact Tie-Breaking and Tight Degree Bounds for Minimum-Degree Greedy on Interval Graphs
papers.abstract: Minimum-degree greedy repeatedly selects a vertex of minimum current degree and deletes its closed neighborhood; let $B(G)$ and $W(G)$ be its largest and smallest output sizes over complete legal executions. Given a closed interval representation of an $n$-vertex graph, we compute both values and construct attaining executions in $O(n^3)$ time and $O(n^2)$ space using endpoint-window dynamic programming and legal interleaving. For interval graphs with $\Delta(G)\le4$, we prove the tight bound $B(G)\ge3\alpha(G)/4$ by reduction to unit interval graphs and induction with virtual boundary vertices. A connected unit interval family $J_t$ attains equality, with $B(J_t)=W(J_t)=3t$ and $\alpha(J_t)=4t$. For each degree bound $d\ge5$, a degree-five family $H_t$ approaches the known $2/3$ lower bound, giving infimum $2/3$. Together with known optimal favorable tie-breaking for $d\le3$, these results determine the favorable guarantee for every degree bound.

papers.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.

papers.title: What Must Be Done Here? Using a Bounded Application-Security Ontology at the Point of Change
papers.abstract: The security guidance that bears on code is real but scattered. It lives across secure-development frameworks, verification standards, controls catalogues, threat taxonomies, and, increasingly, normative regimes such as the EU's NIS2 -- and most of it is written for readers other than the engineer, or the AI assistant, at a point of change. Existing cybersecurity ontologies largely model attacks, indicators, and risk for detection and analysis, not the engineering-practice substance one must act on. This paper presents a use case for an existing bounded application-security ontology, AppSec Core, whose construction and validation are reported separately. We show how it is used. It makes the engineering-actionable fraction of those authorities addressable as a typed working set: the control objectives that apply, the practices that realize them, the mechanisms that implement them, and the evidence artifacts they expect, each traceable to the sources that justify it. We reach that working set from two entry points that recur in practice. Forward, from a code change: a change to authentication middleware scopes to its governing domain slice and returns the obligations the change must satisfy. Inverse, from a normative obligation: "make this NIS2-compliant" resolves a generic legal duty into the concrete engineering obligations it implies across slices, surfacing precisely the fraction of a mostly-governance regulation that lands in code. The same working set is what a human engineer reads and what an LLM-grounded assistant is handed as grounding. The use turns "read every applicable authority" into "satisfy this typed working set", for a code change or a compliance duty alike. The contribution is the demonstrated use; the artefact, its validation, and its governance are companion work.

papers.title: Learning momenta for Hamiltonian-based models
papers.abstract: There has been increasing interest in methodologies that incorporate physics priors into neural network architectures to enhance their modeling capabilities. Among these methodologies, Hamiltonian neural networks (HNNs) and their variants have gained considerable attention. These architectures explicitly encode Hamiltonian mechanics both in their structure and loss function, resulting in desirable properties and additional modeled information. A crucial limitation of HNNs is their reliance on data on the target system's generalized momenta. This severely hampers their applicability when the analytical form of the generalized momenta is unknown, which frequently is the case in real-world applications. The goal of the present work is to develop a general extension of Hamiltonian-based architectures that addresses this issue by simultaneously learning the system's generalized momenta, Hamiltonian structure, and dynamics from data. The proposed architecture learns the generalized momenta when their analytical form is unknown, and only (potentially non-sequential) data on the state and its derivatives is available. A dissipative mass-spring system, a double pendulum, and a rolling disk under nonholonomic constraints are considered as canonical examples to assess the performance of the proposed architecture.

papers.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
papers.abstract: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $\sigma$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $\sigma/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.

papers.title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
papers.abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

papers.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<\rho<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloor\rho n\rfloor,n-\lfloor\rho n\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.

papers.title: The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.

papers.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
papers.abstract:
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(A\mathbf{1})$, and let $\Lambda_G=\mathbb{Z}\langle A,D\rangle\mathbf{1}$. We prove $\Pr[\Lambda_G\ne\mathbb{Z}^n]\le n^{-3/20+o(1)}$. Thus two dependent graph operators generate the entire vertex lattice from the constant vector, simultaneously over every prime field. Adjacency alone has a modulo-two rank obstruction for every simple graph of order greater than one, even though its rational word span is typically full.
  The proof first constructs words containing at most two adjacency operations whose integer span contains $\Delta_G^3\mathbb{Z}^n$, where $\Delta_G$ is the product of the pairwise differences between distinct degree values. This confines all possible arithmetic obstructions to a finite prime range on a single event. We then remove the remaining obstructions using conditional alternating forms, symmetric random-matrix code estimates, and uniform counts of degree-graded invariant subspaces.
  We connect the integer lattice to graph reconstruction through pointed moments. Saturation forces every pointed orthogonal AD intertwiner to be a vertex permutation. The short-word construction also shows that a fixed polynomial-size family of ordinary caterpillars, of diameter at most seven and order $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$, identifies almost every graph among all finite simple graphs. For nonsaturated full-rank lattices, we give an exact description of the moment fibre by admissible unimodular overlattices; at index two, the only possible ambiguity is a specified four-vertex Godsil--McKay switch.

authors.name: Zhipeng Lu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.

papers.title: DIKT: A Diagnostic and Interpretable Knowledge Tracing Framework for Prediction and Model-based Learning Analysis
papers.abstract: Knowledge tracing is a key component of intelligent educational systems. However, most existing methods mainly focus on response prediction, providing limited support for explaining predicted outcomes and improving students'learning states. This paper proposes Diagnostic and Interpretable Knowledge Tracing (DIKT), which integrates response prediction, skill-level diagnosis, and model-based learning analysis. DIKT generates bounded cognitive-state trajectories and decomposes the final response probability into skill-wise probabilities. The trajectories reveal students'evolving strengths and weaknesses, while the skill-wise probabilities identify the skills that most strongly constrain the prediction. Based on these diagnostic results, DIKT supports direct cognitive-state intervention and effective-learning-duration-based what-if analysis to examine how hypothetical adjustments affect current predictions and subsequent state evolution. DIKT combines Bayesian multi-head attention, conditional variational recurrent inference, a logistic-growth decoder, and multiplicative skill-wise prediction. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that DIKT outperforms all evaluated baselines, with an average absolute AUC gain of 2.04 percentage points. Other experiments further demonstrate that DIKT supports educationally meaningful diagnostic analysis and provides informative diagnostic indicators for downstream applications, extending knowledge tracing from response prediction to interpretable diagnosis and model-based learning analysis.

authors.name: Shaohui Chen
authors.institution: Hubei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling
papers.abstract: Actor--critic methods rely on critic gradients to improve continuous-action policies, yet finite-sample guarantees must control both value and gradient errors and their propagation through the actor. We develop a neural actor-critic procedure that combines a regularized minimax Bellman estimator over sigmoid networks with a finite reflected Langevin sampler driven by the fitted critic gradient. Under uniform Bellman regularity and covered reset sampling, a positive high-order action-derivative penalty yields value and action-gradient risk bounds with classical nonparametric minimax exponents up to logarithmic factors. We propagate estimation, mixing, discretization, temperature, and policy-iteration errors to obtain return guarantees, with refinements for bounded multimodal potentials and strongly concave regimes. Empirical studies across controlled simulations, logged continuous-control data, and a simulated decision task show favorable performance relative to the considered baselines.

authors.name: Kunqi Huang
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

authors.name: Jincheng Ying
authors.institution: Guangdong University Of Finances and Economics

papers.title: A Physics Informed Neural Network Approach to Decipher Environmental Confinement of Molecular Clouds in the Third Galactic Quadrant
papers.abstract: Recent high-sensitivity and high-resolution surveys of the Third Galactic Quadrant [$219.75 \leq l \leq 229.75$ and $-5.25 \leq b \leq 5.25$], such as the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting ( MWISP) survey, have revealed a significant population of molecular clouds (MCs) that appear virially unbound ($\alpha_{vir} > 2$) according to traditional isolated MC models. However, these apparently unstable cloud structures are actually found long-lived and actively undertaking star formation. This inconsistency presents a Virial Paradox. In the present work, we employ a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to address this discrepancy by re-evaluating the stability of 2,091 MCs . Unlike traditional machine learning, our PINN model embeds the complete Eulerian Virial Theorem including external surface pressure support ($P_{ext}$) directly into the network's loss function. This model autonomously discovers a global Galactic pressure field that scales inversely with vertical height ($|z|$) and Galactocentric radius ($R_{GC}$), consistent with the properties of the Galactic Flare. By incorporating this AI-derived pressure support, we demonstrate a dramatic shift in the stability census: 99.9\% of previously thought unbound clouds are found to be in a state of pressure confined equilibrium ($\alpha_{AI} \leq 2$). Furthermore, we find a robust log-log correlation ($R = 0.64$) between our corrected stability parameter and the star formation rate (SFR). This correlation provides independent physical validation that environmental confinement is a primary regulator of star forming efficiency in the outer Galaxy.

papers.title: The sum of sizes of nontrivial cross-intersecting families
papers.abstract:
Families $\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_m\subseteq\binom{[n]}k$ are cross-intersecting if every member of one family meets every member of each other family. A family is nontrivial if its members have no common element.
  For $n>2k$ and $m\ge3$, we determine the maximum sum of the sizes of $m$ nonempty, nontrivial cross-intersecting families. We prove the sharp bound \[ \sum_{i=1}^{m}|\mathcal A_i| \le \max\bigl\{m\,h(n,k,1),\ g(n,k)+3(m-1)\bigr\}, \] where \[ h(n,k,1)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+1 \] and \[ g(n,k)=\binom nk-2\binom{n-k}k
  -\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}k. \] We also characterize all equality cases. Two types of extremal configurations arise: copies of a maximum nontrivial intersecting family, and copies of a specific three-member nontrivial intersecting family together with its full cross-intersecting companion. The proof applies a known restricted lexicographic comparison to obtain the weighted bound for shifted families, and uses local generator reductions for critically shifted families. These reductions exploit shiftedness after removing the common core of a section, while preserving nontriviality and the required shadow relations between sections.

papers.title: Large Maximal Intersecting Families with Covering Number Three
papers.abstract: Let $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$. The largest size of an intersecting family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ with covering number at least three is \[ g_1(n,k)=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-2}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k}{k-1}+3, \] attained by a unique family up to isomorphism. We prove that every other maximal intersecting family $\mathcal F$ with covering number three satisfies \[ |\mathcal F|\le M(n,k)=\max\{q(n,k),g_2(n,k)\}, \] where \begin{align*} q(n,k)&=\binom{n-1}{k-1}-3\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-k-3}{k-1}+\binom{n-2k+1}{k-1}+3,\\ g_2(n,k)&=g_1(n,k)-\binom{n-k-3}{k-3}+1. \end{align*} This bound is attained for every $n>2k$ and $k\ge4$, so $M(n,k)$ is the second largest distinct size. For $k=4$, $g_1(n,4)=13n-69$ and $M(n,4)=12n-61$. For $k\ge5$, we have $M(n,k)=q(n,k)$ when $2k<n\le3k-2$ and $M(n,k)=g_2(n,k)$ when $n\ge3k-2$; the two terms coincide only at $n=3k-2$. We also classify all families attaining $M(n,k)$ that admit a critically shifted labeling, including additional nonisomorphic families at $n=2k+1$. The proof combines local replacements with an inverse-shift estimate and gives a new proof of the known maximum and its uniqueness.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Cervical Cytology Screening: Methods, Algorithms, Challenges and Prospects
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer death among women, with more than 90\% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries, where cytology screening is constrained by a shortage of trained cytopathologists. Deep learning has made automated cytology screening increasingly feasible, but the literature is fragmented across cell, patch and whole-slide-image scales, task formulations and supervision regimes, hindering comparison and clinical translation. This Review synthesizes the deep learning literature for cervical cytology screening, organizing the field along three axes---data scale, functional task and supervision---and distinguishing two clinical roadmaps: whole-slide-image confidence aggregation and cell-level detection with Bethesda classification. We examine 16 publicly available or publicly documented cytology datasets alongside the CAISHI histopathology dataset, compare quantitative performance while exposing incomparable metrics and data leakage, and assess commercial systems, regulatory status, HPV-era screening pathways and low-resource deployment. Single-cell accuracy on Herlev and SIPaKMeD has plateaued, but this reflects benchmark saturation rather than clinical readiness; prospective and randomized evidence is emerging but remains limited. We consolidate the evidence into five challenge areas---data and benchmarks, architecture and label-efficient learning, trustworthy AI, clinical translation and health economics, and evaluation and reproducibility---and provide an evidence-to-agenda map and a deployment decision matrix. Progress now depends on multi-center benchmarks, externally validated label-efficient methods, calibrated and fair predictions, and pragmatic clinical trials rather than further gains on saturated single-cell benchmarks.

authors.name: Jiang Yangbo
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Maswao: An automatically collected, prepared, and benchmarked dataset for the South African Sign language
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in sign language processing can be attributed to developments in both large-scale dataset collection and algorithmic complexity in areas such as pose estimation techniques, signal processing through Transformer models, and model optimization. However, only a handful of sign languages, such as the American, British, and German, from over 200 globally recognized sign languages, reap the benefits of such advancements, while the rest lag behind. In this study, we aim to address this technological disparity by proposing a framework for the automatic collection and preparation of sign language datasets, with very minimal human-labour intervention, using the South African Sign Language (SASL) as a testbed. Specifically, we automatically collect SASL video content using public resources such as news broadcasts. Additionally, we convert their accompanying audio streams into text using available Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) tools. Furthermore, we crop the sign language area in the videos and use gradient descent to locate valleys of non-motion to determine end-of-sentence points within long videos to create our weakly sentence-aligned parallel corpora -- the Maswao (Signs) dataset. Finally, we benchmark the weakly aligned dataset on the task of Sign-to-text Translation using Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformer models to compare their individual intricacies. Our results show that Transformer models proposed in the literature outperform recurrent baselines, with the best-performing Transformer achieving BLEU-1 to BLEU-4 scores of 13.78, 5.21, 2.52, and 1.54, respectively, as well as ChrF = 18.09 and ROUGE-L = 10.51. These results indicate that the task remains promising and warrants further investigations.

papers.title: Subset-system derived topologies and coreflective categories of $T_0$-spaces
papers.abstract: Given a subset system $H$ on $T_0$-spaces, we associate with each topology a closure-testing derived topology and study the fixed points of this operator. The $H$-determined topologies above a given topology are closed under intersections and hence determine a least fixed-point hull. We prove that this hull is obtained by transfinite iteration, is functorial, and defines a right adjoint to the inclusion of $H$-determined spaces into $\mathbf{Top}_0$. Consequently, the corresponding full subcategory is coreflective and complete. We isolate restriction-stability and open-locality hypotheses under which determinedness is inherited by closed and open subspaces, and we establish a general non-reflectivity criterion. If $H$ is contained in the directed-subset system, the category of $H$-determined spaces is Cartesian closed; its exponentials are obtained by coreflecting the pointwise convergence topology on continuous maps. The construction subsumes familiar monotone- and irreducible-determined cases while separating the formal consequences of the subset-system axioms from the additional hypotheses needed for heredity and exponentials. It therefore provides a uniform categorical mechanism for producing complete Cartesian closed categories of $T_0$-spaces with explicit higher-order function spaces, as required in denotational semantics.

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schr\"odinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, where $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.

papers.title: Limits and Constants of OpenAI's Claimed ETH Refutation
papers.abstract: A recent OpenAI preprint claims a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF formula in time $2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, and $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ at bounded clause density, which would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The headline bound is proved by tensor contraction; the body develops an interpolation algorithm with the weaker exponent $n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n}$. This note does four things. First, it explains the interpolation algorithm in plain terms. Second, it asks how large $n$ must be for the bounds to bite. The preprint states no constants, so we treat the hidden constant $C$ as a parameter: the general bound beats the $2^n$ of brute force only beyond $n\approx 10^{32}$ for $C=2$, $10^{126}$ for $C=3$ and $10^{3517}$ for $C=10$. We then extract the constants from the tensor-contraction proof: for every input with $m$ clauses at bounded density, the running time it certifies stays above $2^n$ unless $\log_2(n+m)>10^9$, and on random 3-CNF at the satisfiability threshold unless $\log_2 n>5\times10^{11}$. So the bounds are subexponential as $n\to\infty$, but the proof certifies no speed-up over brute force for any input of bounded density that could ever be written down. Third, for the clause-product form of the interpolation algorithm we prove limits in a cost model matching the preprint's evaluation. By a short algebraic lemma, polynomial cost needs components of $O(\log^3 n)$ variables with per-point evaluation, or primal treewidth $O(\log^2 n)$ with dynamic programming over the groups. So the scheme costs $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\mathrm{tw}})}$ at treewidth $\mathrm{tw}$, $2^{\Omega(\sqrt n)}$ with high probability on random 3-CNF above clause density 3, and $2^{\Omega(n^{1/3})}$ even on trivially countable path formulas. We explain why the preprint's sharper routes escape these limits. Fourth, we report experiments.

papers.title: Exact Asymptotics for the Harmonic Descent Chain and Extended Convergence Bounds for Recursive Statistics
papers.abstract: We give an exact asymptotic expansion of the occupation probabilities $a(n,k)$ of the harmonic descent chain, introduced by D. Aldous, as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $k\in\mathrm{o}(\sqrt{n})$. In addition, we extend the recent results of Brandenberger et al. by giving a bound on the rate of convergence of sequences defined recursively by $x_n = \frac{1}{H_{n-1}}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{x_i}{n-i}$ for more general initial conditions. This result enables the application of an existing central limit theorem, also by Brandenberger et al., to statistics of the critical beta-splitting tree which satisfy our more general initial conditions.

papers.title: Bistability in the stalling behavior of thick, cambered airfoils under elevated freestream turbulence
papers.abstract: The aerodynamic performance of a thick, cambered FFA-W3-301 airfoil section near and beyond stall was examined under elevated freestream turbulence using time-resolved surface pressure measurements for chord-based Reynolds numbers from 125,000 to 275,000. Three passive turbulence grids were used to isolate the effects of turbulence intensity and integral length scale, and the results were compared with a clean inflow. The elevated turbulence largely had a positive effect on the mean performance of the airfoil section, eliminating premature flow separation and recovering lift and drag polars more representative of a higher effective Reynolds number; however, resolving the lift in time showed that the time-averaged polars concealed bistable switching. The time-averaged lift was an occupancy-weighted average of two states, and conventional mean and standard-deviation statistics misrepresented the true post-stall unsteady loads. Beyond the maximum-lift angle of attack, the lift alternated repeatedly between two distinct levels with no characteristic frequency. At the highest tested Reynolds number, the switching persisted over an angle-of-attack range of up to nine degrees, more than an order of magnitude wider than that reported for a thin, symmetric section in a low turbulence inflow. The lift levels of the two states were also found to be nearly independent of the inflow turbulence level, whereas the fraction of time spent in each differed between turbulence conditions. conditionally averaged surface pressure distributions and proper orthogonal decomposition of the surface pressure consistently showed that neither state is fully attached; the states correspond to two positions of a single separation front on the suction side, a switching accurately captured by a single pressure mode from the decomposition.

papers.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
papers.abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

papers.title: Comparative Strategies for Handling Imbalanced QSAR Regression: A Case Study on hERG Activity Prediction
papers.abstract: Data imbalance frequently occurs in QSAR modeling, yet most studies focus on classification tasks, and few address regression tasks, as it is challenging to determine which regions of the data are sparse or dense. Data-level and algorithm-level imbalance-handling strategies can have different effects on model performance. In this study, we systematically compare various strategies across GCN and fingerprint-based machine learning models. To evaluate model performance more meaningfully, we partitioned the target region into several subregions based on both domain knowledge and data distribution. We focused on the region of greatest practical interest. Our results demonstrate that selecting models based on this interest-region metric leads to more reliable performance than using the total region metric. We also observed that different imbalance-handling strategies can have divergent effects depending on the model type. These findings highlight the importance of region-aware evaluation in regression QSAR modeling and provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate strategies for imbalanced datasets.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schr\"odingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
papers.abstract: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schr\"odingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Detection: Type-Aware Hallucination Analysis and Hierarchical Detection in Financial Question Answering
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to answer questions over financial filings, where an unfaithful answer can mislead investment, compliance, or client decisions. Hallucination detectors are a common safeguard, but they are usually evaluated with a single binary score that reveals neither which kinds of errors analysesed nor why. This paper studies hallucination detection on PHANTOM, a long-context benchmark built from SEC filings, at the level of hallucination type. We first analyze 15,443 paired hallucinated and faithful answers without any detector and find that hallucinated answers are more than twice as long as faithful ones, and that lexical grounding separates the two classes only because faithful answers are bimodal. We then generate hallucinations in nine financially motivated categories, confirm each with a separate verification pass, and diagnose an LLM-based detector on 4,086 usable examples. Generation success varies from 66.3% to 100% across categories. The detector reaches 80.2% binary accuracy but only 44.7% subtype accuracy, never assigns two of the nine categories, and misses between 5.3% and 46.8% of hallucinations depending on category; these misses are unrelated to input length but rise with how far an answer departs from the correct one. Guided by this diagnosis, we propose a two-stage hierarchical detector that first decides whether an answer is hallucinated and then assigns a subtype, raising binary accuracy to 95.6% and subtype accuracy to 56.1%. The results show that type-level evaluation exposes detector weaknesses that aggregate metrics conceal.

papers.title: Weak-coupling selection and finite-torus entropy in the triangular Ising antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: An antiferromagnetic second-neighbor interaction favors stripe order in the triangular-lattice Ising antiferromagnet, but uniform stripes cannot satisfy odd periodic boundaries. At each fixed odd size $L\geq5$, we minimize this interaction over the ground states of the zero-field nearest-neighbor model on an $L\times L$ torus. We prove a minimum total interface length of $4L$ and classify all $L^2(L^2-1)/2$ selected states. Under the uniform measure on these states, the area fractions of the three stripe orientations approach a uniform distribution over all nonnegative triples summing to one. Thus selection reduces an exponential degeneracy to polynomial growth, while the whole-sample orientation fractions remain broadly distributed. We also derive explicit two-sided entropy-density bounds for periodic spin ground states and honeycomb dimer coverings on $M\times N$ tori, where $M,N$ are the periods along the two primitive lattice directions. For all $M,N\geq3$, the errors relative to the bulk residual entropy are bounded by explicit constants times $\min(M,N)^{-2}$, without an aspect-ratio restriction. These bounds give finite-size accuracy guarantees and control the exponentially small fraction of unperturbed ground states that survive the selection.

authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Token-as-a-Utility: A Model-Agnostic Architecture for Metering and Provisioning AI Inference Services
papers.abstract: Token-based subscriptions are emerging as a commercial model for large language model inference, but extending them into interoperable utility services requires comparable consumption accounting. Raw token counts do not consistently measure inference resource use because demand varies with model architecture, context length, tokenisation, and concurrent serving conditions. This paper presents Token-as-a-Utility, a model-agnostic architecture integrating inference metering, service-level-aware provisioning, and inter-operator settlement. We prove that, under batched serving, no per-request meter can be additive, independent of co-resident traffic, and exactly cost-reflective at once. This motivates separating provisioned capacity, metered consumption, and contracted quality into distinct service products. Consumption is expressed in Reference Inference Units (RIUs) derived from prefill and decode demand, while occupancy-indexed operator ratings recover shared serving costs without altering the common unit. Versioned inference records support auditing and re-rating across operators; software-enforced capacity leases and quality-constrained routing enable provisioning on shared accelerators. The resource model is measured on three NVIDIA RTX 5000 Ada GPUs, and multi-tenant behaviour is evaluated with a trace-driven model calibrated to them. For the reference model, occupancy-indexed rating limits statement energy error to 9% under measured traffic, compared with up to 70.5% under fixed-occupancy rating. In calibrated multi-tenant experiments, tenant mispricing decreases from 7.36 times under flat token counting to 2.39 times with RIUs and 1.06 times after occupancy-based reconciliation. These findings demonstrate how portable inference accounting can be combined with load-dependent cost recovery and contract-based provisioning to support heterogeneous inference services across operators.

papers.title: Gaussian Products and an Order Dichotomy for Principal Ideals
papers.abstract: We identify the algebraic principal ideal generated by a Gaussian product of two Hilbert--Schmidt operators. Its deterministic generator is obtained by multiplying the square tails of their singular-value sequences; in a fixed diagonal basis, one probability-one event gives the identity for all decreasing square-summable weights. For the induced operation on principal ideals, we prove an order dichotomy for arbitrary families of strictly positive probes. A family jointly determines every inclusion if and only if its tail stable-rank profiles have no common eventual upper bound. Equivalently, each prescribed countable input system admits one probe from that family reflecting all inclusions. If the condition fails, one common fibre contains a copy of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/\mathrm{Fin}$ preserving finite sums and intersections. Its generators are continuously parametrized and arbitrarily close in Hilbert--Schmidt norm, while their deterministic output ratios tend to one at any prescribed rate. The order dichotomy follows from a bound on all probes that lose one noninclusion and a separated block construction under a scalar tail budget. Further consequences include generic separation under every positive summable envelope and exact cardinal thresholds for joint detection and single-probe separation.

authors.name: Guangqian Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Free energy of spherical vector spin glasses
papers.abstract: We identify the limit free energy of spherical vector spin glasses by a variational formula. The covariance function need not be convex. Using the global symmetry of the spin configurations, we introduce a family of constraint measures that gives a disintegration of the original spin distribution. We first identify the limit free energy of each constrained model and then apply the Laplace method to recover that of the original model.

papers.title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
papers.abstract: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions. Even so, a marginal test ranks expert-labelled direct above not-direct pairs within each action (AUROC 0.658) better than every null we built, so the panel does carry information about which pairs are direct. Tuned discovery methods, in configurations feasible at this panel size, recover less of it than a simple pairwise cross-correlation when pairs are ranked within each action, and no more when they are ranked within each target, which removes what the target alone predicts. Most direct pairs (132 of 222) involve actions below the support needed for 80% power against a 0.1-SD effect. For flow targets, conditioning on the target's other expert-labelled parents, often filed alongside the action, erodes the marginal discrimination, and most not-direct associations survive it: even with the graph's parent sets supplied, the expected separation does not emerge. For each property, we give a diagnostic computable before any discovery method is run.

papers.title: To Jev or Not to Jev: When Can System-1 Decision Models Replace LLM Judges?
papers.abstract: Decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer typed questions about a text (yes/no, multiple choice, or an ordinal score) with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass and without generating text, which makes them an inexpensive candidate for LLM-as-a-judge workloads. We evaluate 14 System-1 decision models, selected with a pre-stated protocol, against four generative judges (Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-5.6 with and without reasoning, and Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking) on eleven established judge benchmarks. Five of the 14 are statistically indistinguishable from GPT-5.6 without reasoning on all five pairwise and best-of-4 benchmarks, and the two strongest, DReX-Max and d1-ultra, are significantly more accurate than Haiku on JudgeBench, LLMBar and RewardBench 2. Conditioned on a reference answer generated once per prompt, eleven models reach 90.3-93.4% on JudgeBench, statistically indistinguishable from Opus 5.5 and GPT-5.6 with reasoning, and on PPE best-of-16 every reference-guided System-1 judge matches GPT-5.6 with reasoning at roughly one-sixteenth of its cost per prompt. Several System-1 judges are better calibrated than every generative judge and correlate more strongly with human helpfulness ratings. Robustness to instructions injected into the judged response is a property of the individual model rather than of the System-1 design: an appended note to the evaluator reverses 0-5% of the correct verdicts of five models but 17-49% for the other nine. Two general System-1 leaderboards that contain no judging tasks predict judging accuracy (Pearson r = 0.95-0.96), a well-calibrated System-1 first stage matches Opus on LLMBar while escalating 17% of items, and same-size controls show that the correctness deficit of a 4B decision model is a reasoning gap rather than a size gap.

papers.title: Change the Funnel, Not Who May Submit: Engineering Peer Review for the Flood
papers.abstract:
Every reviewer knows the feeling: more papers each cycle, three full reviews for each of them, and a suspicion that near the accept line the outcome is luck. The numbers bear it out. NeurIPS received 30,709 submissions in 2026, more than three times as many as in 2021, and reviewing them took some 184,000 expert hours, or 92 years of researchers' time. Three-quarters of those hours went to papers that were rejected. And when NeurIPS twice had the same papers reviewed by two committees, the second rejected half of what the first accepted.
  Conferences are responding by limiting who may submit. We simulated that answer, and an alternative, in a model calibrated to the NeurIPS experiments. The limits save little and select no better, and those based on a past acceptance fall mostly on new authors. The alternative changes how papers are judged, spending full reads only where a decision turns on them. In a staged funnel, an automated quality check first turns back papers that are not ready. The rest are ranked by their value, from short summaries, by readers that each submission brings. Only the finalists get a full read, which checks their claims and settles the final ranking. The staged funnel needs a little over half of today's expert hours, accepts 95.5% of papers in the top 3-10% (against 74% today), and makes nearly every top-0.5% paper a spotlight or oral. And because every paper brings its own reader, the funnel keeps pace with the flood.

papers.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and It\^o calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.

papers.title: Fairway: Load-Aware KV Cache Reuse for LLM Prefill Scheduling
papers.abstract: LLM-based applications often employ agentic workflows and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which build long prompts from shared context. When prefixes are shared across requests, serving engines reuse the key-value (KV) cache to skip parts of the prefill computation. Reuse is typically graded: the uncached work of requests in a queue can differ by up to 100x. In this setting, the order of scheduling determines the time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the queued requests. KV reuse-first scheduling, which prioritizes the requests with the longest KV cache hit, gives the lowest median TTFT but starves expensive requests under load spikes; first-come-first-served (FCFS) scheduling bounds the tail but raises the median TTFT. We present Fairway, a prefill scheduler built on adaptive reuse prioritization: it favors KV cache reuse while queues are short, and shifts toward fair allocation as requests wait longer relative to their own prefill time. Fairway employs a virtual dual lane model: a KV reuse-first Fast lane and a Fair lane atop the serving engine's waiting queue that enables speeding up of cheap reuse requests without starving expensive ones. This model automatically adapts to the workload without any per-workload tuning. Fairway lowers the tail TTFT at no cost to the median in transient overload. Across workloads and load levels, Fairway matches or beats the best baseline, with a p99 TTFT up to 8.6x lower than prior prefix-aware schedulers. During load spikes, it keeps the tail of FCFS at a 6x lower median TTFT.

papers.title: Joint Delay--Doppler Modeling of Multipath LEO Channels
papers.abstract: Multipath channel models for Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial network (NTN) must contend with time variability due to rapid satellite orbital motion that in turn impacts local (near terrestrial) scattering near the ground terminal (GT) receiver. While 3GPP-defined NTN channel model pipelines TR 38.811, 38.901 incorporate elevation-dependence into statistical channel generators, these are inherited largely from 2-D terrestrial propagation and are largely insufficient. Further, they do not prescribe any integrated workflow that is broadly available for generating joint delay, Doppler/phase and component multipath power profiles as a function of satellite location over a pass. This work addresses this gap by developing a geometry-based stochastic channel model driven by prescribed slant range, elevation, and azimuth over a LEO pass. A ground scene generates wall-reflected, ground-reflected, and roof-edge-diffracted components, from which joint delay-Doppler statistics and temporal channel impulse response (CIR) evolution are obtained. The resulting locally wide-sense stationary tapped-delay-line CIR enables analysis of key statistics such as the $K$-factor of the taps, multipath delay and Doppler spreads as a function of elevation and scene parameters. Depending on the scenarios (urban and rural), our model-based results show that with omnidirectional antennas, the LoS probability, delay-spread and $K$-factor trends broadly match 3GPP NTN models in TR 38.811 as a function of elevation. Beamforming instead produces a mid-elevation $K$-factor peak, which is not predicted by TR 38.811 and 6G NTN. Doppler spreads are smaller than those from our previous model and QuaDriGa because the proposed model accounts for path existence. Stationarity durations for CIR are reported and generally decrease with elevation, but with local increases at mid-elevation due to path geometry effects.

papers.title: SMILE: A Structured Multi-Agent Clinical Reasoning for Liver Ultrasound Understanding
papers.abstract: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. However, current generative vision-language models (VLMs) often rely on a single reasoning pathway that maps ultrasound appearance directly to textual descriptions. In addition to the inherent vision-language modality gap, this design is limited for liver ultrasound because disease interpretation is constrained by subtle visual evidence, heterogeneous disease patterns, and limited paired supervision. To address these limitations, we propose SMILE, a Structured Multi-agent clInicaL rEasoning framework that uses multiple complementary specialist agents to interpret ultrasound images and consolidates their outputs through a judge-guided consensus mechanism. Our approach employs three specialized agents: an image interpretation agent for morphological descriptions, a clinical-stage reasoning agent, and a visual question answering (VQA) agent for targeted queries. These agent responses are then aggregated and scrutinized by a judge VLM using a consensus filtering prompt to produce a unified, clinically coherent output. Across a public liver ultrasound dataset and an internal clinical dataset, SMILE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art VLMs, achieving up to 19.0\% improvement in ROUGE-1 and 18.8\% improvement in clinical F1-score, while reaching VQA F1-scores of 0.82 and 0.65 on public and internal datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of SMILE for data-scarce and limited-supervision clinical settings. Our models, datasets, and code are available \href{https://github.com/CMME-Lab/SMILE}{here}.

authors.name: Keungmo Yang
authors.institution: The Catholic University of Korea Yeouido St. Mary's Hospital

papers.title: Testing MAX-CUT in the Adjacency Matrix Model: Tight Non-Adaptive Bounds and a Cubic Adaptive Lower Bound
papers.abstract:
We study the query complexity of approximating the MAX-CUT value to additive error $\varepsilon n^2$ in the adjacency matrix model. This was one of the first problems studied in the area of graph property testing [GGR, JACM'1998]. Previously, the best known upper bound for both adaptive and non-adaptive algorithms was $O(1/\varepsilon^6)$ [MS, SODA'2008; GMRS, ICALP'2022]. The only known lower bound was a trivial $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^2)$ bound. We close this gap from both sides for non-adaptive algorithms, proving that its query complexity is exactly $\Theta(1/\varepsilon^4)$. We also prove an adaptive $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^3)$ lower bound.
  Our upper bound is achieved by a canonical tester that samples $O(1/\varepsilon^2)$ vertices in expectation and outputs the rescaled MAX-CUT value of the induced subgraph. We prove its correctness by applying spectral truncation to the adjacency matrix, using a geometric argument to control the sampling error of the retained low-rank part and a cut-norm restriction estimate [RV, JACM'2007] for the remainder. As an application, an analogous proof also yields a tight $O(1/\varepsilon^4)$ non-adaptive query upper bound for MAX-2CSP.
  For our lower bounds, we show indistinguishability between a uniform random graph and a distribution that plants a hidden partition. For the non-adaptive lower bound, we observe that one plus the $\chi^2$-divergence between the query transcript distributions is exactly a normalized Ising partition function, which can be bounded using Boolean hypercontractivity. For the adaptive lower bound, we view each query through the algorithm's ability to predict whether its endpoints lie in the same part of the hidden partition. We bound the combined advantage of these predictions using the completed transcript, which lets us analyze the adaptively chosen pairs together despite their dependence on earlier answers.

papers.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.

papers.title: Synergetic Autonomous Intelligence: Three Axioms for Recursive Semi-Closed Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce Synergetic Autonomous Intelligence (SAI), a theory and design program for learning systems that form, preserve, revise, and compose relations while continuing to learn. SAI is built on three axioms: consequential distinctions must not become orphaned (U); identity is determined by future-faithful continuation under a declared contract (I); and unresolved defects are repaired by the least lawful local completion at the lowest admitted grade (L). We model a model, agent, tool, team, or environment boundary as a recursive semi-closed system with a Kernel-Ring representation, a Compile-Open-Participate cycle, and a typed residual comparing actual with claimed continuation. Under explicit finite or affine contracts, we establish relative consistency and conditional non-redundancy of U/I/L, characterize a contract-relative semantic quotient, construct an exact joint stochastic refinement, derive a constrained residual contraction, prove finite-horizon continued-service viability, and give an executed-intervention identification result with an observational-confounding boundary. We define GRC-Close as the generative and repair schema for this contract. The framework also gives finite contracts for action-effect-feedback loop re-entry, partial failure, duplicate-effect idempotency, replay, concurrent delivery, causal uncertainty, and threshold-radix state representation. KREIT, the Kernel-Ring Equilibrium Information Theory layer, treats information as a typed, resource-bounded distinction; the control layer authorizes, executes, audits, and updates actions across cloud-edge-end scales. These results establish a common contract-level vocabulary for representation, relation, memory, action, communication, explanation, coordination, and growth, while marking the assumptions and open boundaries required for later generalization.

papers.title: Renting, Owning, and Moving: Housing Tenure Choice with Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: The wealth thresholds at which a household switches between renting and owning depend on its preferences, but the dates at which some owner sells or every renter buys do not. In our finite-horizon model, a household chooses consumption, a portfolio, and costly tenure changes while rents, ownership expenses, and transaction costs vary over time on announced dates. When financial markets span house-price risk, these dates are those of a deterministic minimum cost schedule for housing, discounted at the risk-adjusted housing carry and computed from a scalar reflected equation. Preferences, housing services, and labor income only locate the thresholds inside these timing windows, and house-price coefficients enter the dates only through the carry, because financial hedging offsets the exposure of the home. When owning costs at least as much as renting, the windows concern selling, and an anticipated selling surcharge closes the selling window before the surcharge peaks and keeps it closed for years afterwards. We also establish strong duality and the regularity of the thresholds and compute them by integral equations. Numerically, the windows disappear when short sales or borrowing are restricted but do not move with the preferences we vary under an uninsurable increase in the ownership cost.

authors.name: Kexin Chen
authors.institution: Central South University of Forestry and Technology

papers.title: Polarity-Programmed Topological Gating of Knotting in Spatially Patterned Active Polymers
papers.abstract: Spatially patterned tangential activity provides a route to program polymer topology through both geometry and propulsion direction. We use Langevin-dynamics simulations of a flexible, self-avoiding linear polymer to determine how active-domain placement and independently assigned propulsion polarities control nonequilibrium knotting. Reversing the polarities of two terminal active blocks switches the steady state from a nearly always-knotted regime to effective knot suppression, changing the knotting probability by more than three orders of magnitude despite identical active-block positions and activity magnitude. Across symmetric terminal two-block architectures, we further identify an approximate zero-one-two free-end-alignment rule: zero, one, and two free-end-aligned active blocks correspond, respectively, to suppressed, intermediate, and high-knotting states. A two-state kinetic decomposition shows that the conditional knot-formation rate changes only by about threefold under polarity reversal, whereas the mean knot lifetime changes by several orders of magnitude, demonstrating that knot survival and passive-region storage dominate the polarity-controlled switch. Block placement provides an additional geometrical gate: moving an active domain from the chain interior to a terminal region strongly enhances both knot formation and survival. Knot-center residence, knotted-arc distributions, and episode-resolved kymographs reveal formation near free-end-aligned active blocks, directed contour migration, tightening, and long-lived retention in passive regions. Together, these results support a source-conveyor-reservoir-sink mechanism in which signed polarity and spatial activity patterning control whether knots are generated, transported, stored, or rapidly lost, providing a route to programmable topological states in nonequilibrium active polymers.

papers.title: From Single-Agent Self-Discovery to Multi-Agent Adaptation: Scaling Laws of Partner Feedback and Convention Rigidity in Meta Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
papers.abstract: A key milestone toward Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) is replacing hand-crafted optimizers with meta-learned update rules (such as Disco103 and OPEN) that discover how agents learn. Yet when a self-discovered RL model trains with adapting teammates, does co-evolution sustain capability gains or trap agents in brittle conventions? Across 1,800+ runs in continuous collective robotics (VMAS) and discrete coordination (Overcooked), we establish five laws of multi-agent adaptation. First, four-cell counterfactual partner swaps expose an evaluation illusion: apparent team progress often masks focal regression (+1.066 team gain concealing -0.119 focal loss) and inflates transfer by +0.649 to +1.210. Second, a 288-run physical-coupling sweep ($\alpha \in [0, 1.5]$) reveals a linear scaling law ($\beta = +0.255$, $p = 0.000488$, Spearman $\rho = 1.0$): live reciprocal feedback keeps Disco103 invariant (AUC 0.297--0.322), whereas severing feedback triggers a monotonic collapse (-0.172 to -0.490), with OPEN establishing a sensitivity spectrum (Disco103 > OPEN > MAPPO). Third, extending navigation training eightfold (1.05M steps) enables Disco103 to overtake MAPPO (+0.087 team return, +0.133 bank gain), while decoupled training boosts cross-partner completion by +10.16% (56.25% vs. 46.09%). Fourth, in Overcooked, MAPPO's self-play conventions induce a 28.13% cross-partner collision rate, whereas Disco103 cuts collisions to 12.77% and achieves 3.33x higher bank return (9.96 vs. 2.99; net gain +6.43), further improved by decoupled meta-adaptation (+1.39 with scripted partners). Finally, perturbation pulses ($p=0.00098$), auxiliary entropy diagnostics (8.485 nats), and 48 multi-lifetime meta-evolved rules ($L_2 \in [2.11, 4.91]$) trace these dynamics to partner-gradient blindness and auxiliary drift, informing multi-agent self-discoverd algorithms.

papers.title: The 3-Tier Integrated Technology Risk Model for Occupational Safety and Health
papers.abstract: This paper presents the 3-Tier Integrated Technology Risk Model, a progressive framework for Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) management that integrates Job Safety Analysis (JSA), dynamic risk assessment using leading and lagging indicators, and predictive analytics powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). The model provides organizations with a structured pathway to evolve from static, reactive safety practices to a sophisticated, predictive safety paradigm. Each tier builds upon the previous one, creating a comprehensive, data-driven approach that enables just-in-time training and preemptive risk mitigation.

authors.name: Ramiro Pesina
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Tyler

papers.title: Unconditional optimal convergence of a relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for 2D space-fractional NLS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a linearly implicit relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for the two-dimensional space-fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger (SFNS) equation, where the fractional Laplacian is approximated by a simple fractional central difference scheme. The proposed scheme is uniquely solvable and conserves discrete mass for general real-valued nonlinear coefficients, and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case. By introducing a modified error system employing a cut-off technique, we establish the optimal-order error estimates without mesh-ratio restriction. Specifically, the primary variable achieves second-order temporal and spatial convergence in the discrete $H_h^{\alpha/2}$-norm, and the relaxation variable satisfies the same convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm. Some numerical experiments confirm the relevant theoretical results.

papers.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
papers.abstract:
Suppose an optimization problem is randomly restricted, independently on each variable, and re-optimized after the restriction is revealed. For multilinear objectives, every fixed solution is unbiased after rescaling, but re-optimizing introduces an upward bias. We bound this excess, the hindsight gain, over products of arbitrary compact local domains in Euclidean unit balls.
  For interactions $A=(A_e)_e$ among $r$ distinct variables and independent random weights $\zeta_i$, the gain is at most $O_r(\|A\|_F M^{(r-1)/2}\sigma_{\max})$, where $\|A\|_F^2$ is the sum of squared coefficients, $M=\sum_i\mathbb{E}\zeta_i^2$, and $\sigma_{\max}^2=\max_i\mathrm{Var}(\zeta_i)$; only second moments are needed. Under uniform retention with probability $p$, we sharpen this to $O_r(p^{r-1/2}\sqrt{1-p}\,n^{(r-1)/2}\|A\|_F)$, which is tight for every fixed $r$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Our proof combines a comparison principle along a single support direction with tensor projection, vector contraction, and repeated thinning.
  Applications: (i) For fixed arity and alphabet size, solving the subproblem induced by $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sampled variables estimates a dense Max-$r$CSP optimum within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, and this sample size is optimal. (ii) The same approach estimates MaxCut and the distance to bipartiteness within $\pm\varepsilon n^2$ using $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ nonadaptive queries and $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ examined vertices, both optimal. (iii) We answer a question of Yufei Zhao: vertex percolation at rate $p$ preserves the max-cut fraction whenever $p\,e(G)/v(G)\to\infty$, and this condition is sharp. (iv) For bounded $r$-local quantum Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ uniformly sampled particles suffice to estimate the ground-state energy within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bound.

papers.title: Solvable dynamics model of in-context learning
papers.abstract: Pretrained Transformer architectures display a surprising in-context learning ability without additional training. How the learning process guides the network to achieve this intriguing capability remains unsolved. In this study, we focus on a single-layer, single-head linear attention model, where empirical risk minimization is defined for learning. Given a finite amount of training examples, we determine the exact solution of network parameter dynamics, which is linked to the training error and generalization error, characterizing how memorization and generalization emerge from learning and how these transitions are related to curvatures of the empirical risk landscape. Furthermore, we calculate a data-dependent free energy, from which the training and generalization errors in the long-time limit of learning dynamics can be well predicted. Our work adds insights toward understanding the mechanism of in-context learning, especially from a learning dynamics perspective.

authors.name: Haiping Huang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
papers.abstract: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors, with alternating small differences, then lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for countable DSS families and uniform nuclear tails for norm-compact DSS families, together with common Hilbert-space factors and arbitrarily small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. The main equality is a candidate real-field proof; no complex-field equality is asserted.

authors.name: Ma Yicen
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Wilker property, function spaces and hyperspaces
papers.abstract: The Wilker property requires that a compact set covered by two open sets admit compact covering pieces inside those open sets. We study this property through products, compact-open function spaces and hyperspaces. We construct countable compact Fr\'echet--Urysohn $T_1$ hereditarily Wilker spaces with non-Wilker products and squares. For spaces whose compact subsets are closed, Wilker-ness is equivalent to every compact subspace being Hausdorff; this yields a positive product theorem when one Wilker factor has closed compact subsets. For an irreducible subset system $H$, we characterize preservation of $H$-sobriety by compact-open function spaces in terms of $H$-supercompactness of compact subsets of the domain, and show that Wilker spaces satisfy this criterion.
