The Hoare hyperspace of a space is Wilker exactly when binary union on the Scott space of its open-set lattice is jointly continuous for the ordinary product topology. Consequently, the Hoare construction preserves and reflects Wilker-ness on consonant bases, although preservation fails in general. We also identify core-compactness of the base with local compactness of its Hoare hyperspace and prove that the Smyth construction reflects Wilker-ness.

papers.title: Spin-induced lateral acoustic forces on chiral and achiral particles
papers.abstract: Acoustic spin enables intriguing chiral sound-matter interactions, yet its mechanical consequences remain much less explored. Here, we demonstrate spin-induced lateral acoustic forces on chiral and achiral particles coupled to a substrate. Under plane-wave incidence, left- and right-handed chiral particles scatter fields with opposite acoustic spin that selectively couple to counterpropagating guided waves, generating lateral forces of opposite signs on the enantiomers. The lateral forces can also be realized for achiral particles by employing acoustic vortex-beam illumination. We experimentally validate the spin-dependent excitation of guided waves and lateral forces. Our results provide a route to spin-controlled acoustic manipulation and chirality-selective particle transport.

authors.name: Yurou Jia
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

papers.title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
papers.abstract: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory. Under a Gorenstein condition, satisfied in the Calabi--Yau setting, the functor is induced by restriction of modules. We give algebraic criteria that ensure equivalence and obtain an identification of Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers
  of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere.
  Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves
  $
  X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x),
  $
  where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$
  has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$.
  After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic
  if its Newton polygon is minimal
  as $f$ varies over all Laurent
  polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$.
  For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$
  and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing
  of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$.
  Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize:
  there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$
  in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$
  and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in
  $U(\overline{\Q})$,
  the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large
  rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field.
  This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Complexity Across the Computational Phase Transition
papers.abstract:
How does a computational problem transition from easy to hard? In the hard-core model, approximate counting and sampling are polynomial-time tractable up to tree uniqueness, but worst-case intractable at any constant relative distance above it unless $\mathsf{NP}=\mathsf{RP}$.
  We quantify the transition from polynomial to exponential mixing for classical Glauber dynamics. On $n$-vertex graphs of maximum degree $d\ge3$, at fugacity $\lambda=(1+\delta)\lambda_{\mathrm c}(d)$ with sufficiently small $\delta\ge0$ that may vanish with $n$, its worst-case mixing time has the form $\exp\{\Theta(n\delta^2/d)\}n^{1+\Theta(1)}$. The upper bound is degree-uniform, and the matching lower bound holds for every fixed $d$. Annealing gives approximate counting with the same running-time upper bound at fixed accuracy.
  For general sampling and counting algorithms, we establish a robust fine-grained reduction from SAT without assuming a lower bound on SAT's running time. For any fixed $d\ge3$ and $0<\gamma<1$, a sampling or approximate-counting algorithm running in $\exp\{O((n\delta^2/d)^{1-\gamma})\}\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time along any one suitable inverse-polynomial distance sequence $\delta=\delta(n)$, yields a randomized SAT algorithm running in $\exp\{\widetilde O(s^{1-\gamma})\}$ time on inputs of binary length $s$. This power-saving transfer identifies $n\delta^2/d$ as the analogue of SAT input length for hard-core sampling and counting at relative distance $\delta$ above criticality: beating the Glauber exponent by a fixed power through any sampling or counting method would yield a corresponding power improvement for SAT.
  At criticality, we establish $O(\sqrt{n/d})$ spectral independence, optimal in $n$ at fixed degree, and degree-uniform Glauber mixing in $\widetilde O(n(n/d)^{1+1/(d-2)})$ time, improving the previous $\widetilde O(n^{4+4/(d-2)})$ bound.

papers.title: What Drives the Zero-to-One Jump? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved mathematical reasoning, yet progress on hard prompts often stalls: a prompt can remain unsolved for many training steps before abruptly transitioning to solved--a discrete "zero-to-one" jump whose underlying dynamics and steerability remain poorly understood. We investigate two questions: what drives this transition, and can it be steered? Through event-based analysis measuring the time-to-first-positive (TTFP), we find that negative rollouts preceding successful transitions consistently retain higher early-stage generation entropy, distinguishing near-solvable failures from dead ends. This signal motivates NAPO (Negative-Augmented Policy Optimization), a method integrated with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that ranks negatives in unsolved groups via an early-branching driver and assigns graded advantages, injecting informative gradients precisely where standard group-relative updates vanish. Under fixed rollout budgets, NAPO accelerates early solution discovery and improves Pass@256 by 10.0 points on AIME24 and 6.6 points on AIME2025, demonstrating that zero-to-one transitions are diagnosable and steerable through driver-guided negative learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/jameszhu-pixel-time/Z2O.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning for Phase I Dose Allocation
papers.abstract: Phase I dose-finding trials must learn from sparse toxicity observations while limiting exposure to overly toxic doses. We develop a single reinforcement-learning policy for trials with different numbers of ordered dose levels. Each dose is represented as a token containing its normalized position, accumulated patient count, observed dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), and current-dose indicator. A Transformer encoder summarizes the dose tokens, trial-conditioned cross-attention produces a fixed-dimensional trial representation, and a three-action policy chooses de-escalation, staying, or escalation. The final maximum tolerated dose (MTD) decision is deliberately kept outside the learned policy: after the planned sample size, weighted isotonic regression and a prespecified safety cap select the dose closest to the target toxicity probability. In the simulations, toxicity-penalized policies reduce DLT burden while unpenalized policies improve selection accuracy at the cost of greater toxicity. These results demonstrate a controllable safety--accuracy trade-off but do not establish superiority over conventional dose-finding designs.

authors.name: Shijie Yuan
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Pollution Control and Resource Reuse

papers.title: Unified dynamics of training, learning, inference, and reinforcement in neural networks
papers.abstract: Despite their remarkable success, neural networks remain largely black boxes, and the mechanisms underlying their behavior are still poorly understood. Nine nanoGPT experiments established training-learning-inference relations: realized updates elicit state-dependent finite-amplitude responses; learning persistently reorganizes distributed functional support, with target-specific readout-boundary crossings determining capability transitions; inference recruits learned support without changing the learned state. Factors identified in the fifth experiment yielded a direct predictor of post-update capability transitions, achieving 91.43% accuracy and 91.49% four-way macro recall across 5,088 targets. We tested these relations and prediction across five additional neural architectures. In a seventh system, concentrated correct feedback eroded previously mastered skills; rebalanced feedback restored their accuracy from 70.31% to 99.48%. Linking inference consequences to subsequent training closes these relations into unified training-learning-inference-reinforcement dynamics.

papers.title: MedICL: Modality-Anatomy-Aware Visual In-Context Learning for Medical Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Training-free adaptation of medical vision-language models (LVLMs) is a deployment requirement, yet visual in-context learning (ICL) injects modality- and style-mismatched demonstrations into medical contexts, teaching a frozen model the wrong answering style. We present MedICL, which curates demonstrations instead of retraining the model. MADS selects modality-anatomy aligned demonstrations that cover complementary interpretation dimensions; W2C curates them with weak retrieval signals and a strong verification vote that checks demonstrations rather than the model's own outputs; ECC answers with W anchored demonstration sets, aggregates by abnormality-aware signatures, and re-answers once on conflict. On VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA under the LLaVA-Med zero-shot protocol, MedICL improves the strongest zero-shot baseline by +11 - +14 points on open-ended and +7 - +14 on closed questions, recovers 71% of fine-tuned open-ended performance on VQA-RAD at zero training cost, and stays robust to shifted or corrupted demonstration banks.

papers.title: Total dominating sets and four-colorings of planar triangulations
papers.abstract:
In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every planar triangulation on at least four vertices has two disjoint total dominating sets. It was proved by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad in 2024. As a strengthening of this result, Goddard and Henning also conjectured that every planar triangulation with at least four vertices has a proper $4$-coloring with color classes $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4$ such that $C_1\cup C_2$ and $C_3\cup C_4$ are total dominating sets. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture: for every $n\ge 36$ there is a planar triangulation with $n$ vertices without such a coloring.
  As another strengthening of the result by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad, they conjectured that every near-triangulation has a $4$-coloring, not necessarily proper, in which every vertex $v$ sees at least $\min \{ \operatorname{deg}(v),3 \}$ colors on its neighbors. We prove this conjecture for all planar triangulations.

papers.title: Capable but Not Scalable: Requirements and Interaction Costs of Building Multi-View CAD Datasets for Design Research
papers.abstract: Transforming CAD models into consistent multi-view image datasets is increasingly important for AI-driven product design research, yet existing workflows can impose substantial burdens on researchers without programming expertise. We examine this challenge from a human-computer interaction (HCI) perspective by analyzing ten reported rendering practices and deriving fourteen requirements spanning dataset quality, visual consistency, and user interaction. We then assess eleven development- and design-oriented tools against an illustrative task involving STEP models, interpreting potential interaction costs through the cognitive dimensions framework. Our analysis reveals a gap between technical capability and practical scalability: programming-based frameworks offer flexible automation but require coding expertise, while graphical design tools provide accessible functionality yet retain repetitive per-product operations. No assessed workflow combines a low programming threshold, low repetition viscosity, and flexible protocol configuration. Based on these findings, we propose design directions including reusable rendering presets, collection-wide previews and corrections, mixed-initiative orientation assignment, and automatic provenance recording. This work reframes CAD dataset generation as an end-user interaction design problem and establishes requirements for more accessible, scalable dataset creation tools.

authors.name: Danyal Sarfraz
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ulugbek Vahobjon Ugli Ismatullaev
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: KwanMyung Kim
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
papers.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors to evaluate TGVs

authors.name: Herve Hugonnet
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: MIRA: Mutual Information guided calibration for Reliable Test-Time Adaptation
papers.abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) updates a deployed model using only unlabeled target data, but standard entropy-based methods often rely on deterministic confidence and can reinforce overconfident errors under distribution shift. We propose MIRA, Mutual Information guided calibration for Reliable Test-Time Adaptation, a source-free online adaptation method that uses lightweight last-layer Gaussian perturbations to probe prediction reliability. For each target batch, MIRA reuses a single feature extraction pass and samples perturbed classifiers around the source classifier, forming an efficient local predictive distribution. Rather than fitting a Bayesian posterior, MIRA treats the perturbation scale as a local probing radius and selects a batch-specific scale using mutual information (MI) and prediction agreement. The resulting perturbation-sensitivity signal identifies predictions that are confident and locally stable under classifier perturbations, while suppressing brittle predictions with high stochastic disagreement. MIRA then performs adaptation with an MI-confidence weighted entropy loss, which down-weights perturbation-sensitive or low-confidence samples before they drive entropy minimization. This weighted loss reduces the influence of brittle predictions that can otherwise cause harmful adaptation under distribution shift. The method requires no source data, retraining, model ensembles, or offline posterior fitting, and can be applied as a plug-and-play modification to entropy-minimization TTA. Experiments on distribution-shift benchmarks show improvements in accuracy, calibration, and negative log-likelihood, suggesting that mutual-information-guided perturbation probing and weighted adaptation yield more robust online TTA than deterministic confidence.

authors.name: Mingyeong Jang
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Consumption and Investment with Multiple Job-Switching Opportunities
papers.abstract: We study finite-horizon optimal switching with affine rewards in a consumption-investment model with finitely many occupational regimes. Directed shortest-path costs yield the exact natural borrowing limit. A dual transformation reduces the control problem to a one-dimensional system of variational inequalities with interconnected obstacles. Convexity and a distributional waiting inequality give local spatial $C^{1,1}$ regularity and smooth fit, including destination ties. These estimates establish strong duality and recover optimal consumption, investment, and switching strategies. A reflected backward stochastic differential equation representation yields a set-based integral formula without prescribed boundary geometry. Every connected component of the spatially regular locus is a maximal smooth graph over time. Exact examples exhibit disconnected contact sets, temporal boundaries under strict triangle costs, and a corner in an individual boundary component under additive route costs. A convergent time discretisation completes the analysis.

papers.title: Toward Bounding Coding-Agent Autonomy in Software Maintenance: A Pilot Study of Boundary Contracts
papers.abstract:
As coding agents gain greater autonomy to modify software repositories, relevant context alone does not define their operational authority. An artifact may be relevant to a maintenance task while being inappropriate to edit; conversely, another artifact may be required even when it is not explicitly mentioned in the request. We explore Boundary Contracts, a machine-readable abstraction that makes task-specific artifact roles (editable, inspect-only, required, and protected) explicit before repository modification begins.
  We conduct a pilot study on 40 maintenance tasks from a real enterprise repository, comparing the same Codex-based coding agent with and without Boundary Contract information. The boundary-informed condition improves macro edit-selection F1 from 0.440 to 0.682, required-behavior coverage from 0.429 to 0.673, and the number of strictly acceptable patches from 9 of 40 to 18 of 40. To probe whether these gains are explained only by improved file localization, we additionally analyze 21 tasks in which both conditions modify at least one identical file. Differences remain in edit selectivity and patch outcomes, providing initial evidence that explicit artifact roles may influence maintenance behavior beyond localization alone.
  This pilot does not establish the general effectiveness of Boundary Contracts. Rather, it provides initial evidence for a broader research question: how should the operational boundaries of coding agents be generated, validated, revised, and ultimately enforced as repository-level maintenance becomes increasingly autonomous?

papers.title: Sonny-ENS: demystifying machine-learning ensemble weather forecasting
papers.abstract: Every weather forecast is uncertain, and decisions from flood warnings to energy trading depend on how well that uncertainty is quantified. Machine-learning (ML) ensembles now quantify it better than the best physics-based ensemble, yet two things about them remain opaque: whether their skill requires hundreds to thousands of accelerator-days of training, and how a network with a simple source of randomness produces a spread that follows the flow. Here we introduce Sonny-ENS, an ensemble of three 68.9-million-parameter networks with Monte Carlo dropout, trained on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in 2.7 A40 GPU-days. On 2022, it has a lower CRPS than the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble (ENS) on 96% of 570 targets and an 8.3% lower mean CRPS at lead times of 1-10 days. It outperforms the operational GenCast on 69% of the targets, and a 51-member, 15-day forecast takes 69 s on one GPU. Ablations identify the ingredients of this skill, and a Kolmogorov-Arnold sparse autoencoder shows that dropout injects uncertainty mainly in the tropics, whereas the spread grows where the atmosphere is baroclinically unstable (spatial correlation 0.91 with the Eady growth rate). Skillful probabilistic weather forecasts are therefore within reach of a single GPU server.

papers.title: Fr\'echet Oral Distance: A Coordinate-Free Metric and Benchmark for Speech-Driven Oral Animation
papers.abstract: Recently, speech-driven facial and oral animation technologies have been used in various fields such as education, speech therapy, and healthcare. But methods to objectively evaluate the quality of generated results are still limited. Accordingly, we propose the Fr\'echet Oral Distance (FOD), which uses embeddings from an Oral Motion Encoder (OME) and a TIMIT-Vis reference distribution. In experiments, FOD reproduced model rankings similar to the coordinate-based metric, Lip Vertex Error (LVE), and showed trends consistent with user preference. Our framework provides objective and reproducible benchmarking without relying on expensive equipment or subjective evaluation, and it can be extended to compare a variety of 2D/3D models.

papers.title: Finite-horizon Optimal Consumption and Investment with Costly Income Adjustment
papers.abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment for an investor who receives labor income until a fixed retirement date, can raise the income rate irreversibly at a constant price per unit of income flow, and cannot borrow against future income. A pathwise argument shows that no income is purchased during a final period before retirement whose length depends only on the interest rate and the price. Before this period the dual problem has two free boundaries: a lower one generated by the borrowing constraint and an upper one, at which income is purchased, that escapes to infinity as the final period begins. The analysis of this problem is our main mathematical contribution. During the final period it is a single obstacle problem, which we solve, together with the regularity of its free boundary, by established methods. Before that period a partial hodograph transformation straightens both free boundaries and turns the problem into a quasilinear parabolic equation with oblique boundary conditions on a fixed interval. Comparison principles, explicit barriers and regularity theory for quasilinear equations then give existence, uniqueness and smoothness. Transforming back and gluing the two constructions yields global regularity: both free boundaries are infinitely differentiable and the value function is a classical solution at every positive wealth level. A dual budget process verifies optimality. We also derive coupled Volterra integral equations for the free boundaries, prove exponential convergence to the perpetual problem under a scalar condition, and find numerically a purchase threshold that is U-shaped in the time to retirement.

papers.title: Integer-Exact Microscaling: Running MXFP4 Language Models on INT8 Matrix Units
papers.abstract: On hardware whose fastest matrix datapath is INT8$\times$INT8, such as the Neural Accelerators of Apple's M5 GPUs, 4-bit weights must become INT8 operands. Existing MXFP4 kernels already map FP4 (E2M1) values to integers by doubling them, but apply every 32-element block scale inside the reduction. We show when no per-block work is needed: a row of MXFP4 weights is exactly one INT8 vector times one power-of-two scale if its block exponents span at most three, so a linear layer becomes a single INT8 GEMM with one rescale per output. Enforcing the condition adds at most 1/16 of a row's largest rounding error to the blocks it changes, and real weights already satisfy it: 97.9-99.97% of rows across seven models, including 99.93% of the 95M rows of a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. The resulting spread-constrained MXFP4 files stay standard MXFP4. With integer instead of power-of-two block multipliers, an integer-exact format (16-wide blocks, multipliers 1..10, 4.26 bits) runs as one exact INT8 GEMM and is more accurate than NVFP4 (4.5 bits) with its standard scale rule on five small models, within 0.06 perplexity of NVFP4 with scale search. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's routed experts with INT8 activations it is as close to the FP8 model as NVFP4 with scale search (KL divergence 0.0557 vs. 0.0553) and closer than MLX's MXFP4 and affine INT4; with every matrix quantized it solves 94.8% of GSM8K vs. 91.0% for MLX's MXFP4. Quantizing only the 74k routed expert matrices (96% of the parameters) to either of our formats with INT8 activations costs at most 0.2% perplexity. A complete W4A8 system on the M5 produces outputs bit-identical to the quantized reference; prefill is 1.34-1.74x faster than MLX on a dense model, 1.10-1.57x on two MoE models up to 35B parameters and 1.22-1.29x on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, where shared non-GEMM work bounds the gain.

papers.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
papers.abstract: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used both a single-turn and a conversational multi-turn text-to-SQL interface over the MIMIC-IV database in a within-subjects design; dialogue analyses additionally drew on interaction logs from 21 healthcare professionals across the main study and two pilot studies. The conversational interface was consistently favored: mean System Usability Scale scores rose from 68.2, near the industry average, to 85.9 (p<0.001), with significant advantages across technology-acceptance constructs including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, self-efficacy, and behavioral intention. In post-study forced-choice comparisons, 93% of participants reported greater overall satisfaction with the conversational interface, 86% preferred it for real-world adoption, and 71% trusted its results more; no participant preferred or trusted the single-turn interface more. Turn-level analysis of 425 logged user turns showed that freely composed queries triggered clarification requests in 24.8% of cases versus 1.8% for predefined, fully specified questions, and 64.3% of clarification episodes stemmed from EHR- or clinical-domain knowledge. Conversational interaction is a practical prerequisite, rather than a convenience, for natural-language EHR access. The frequent need for clarification in realistic clinical queries further underscores the importance of conversational interfaces, while benchmark-style evaluation can substantially underrepresent the ambiguity of real clinical use.

authors.name: Edward Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Robust 3DMA GNSS Positioning in Urban Areas Using Conservative Candidate Set Determination Based on GNSS Shadow and Reflection
papers.abstract: In urban environments, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning is often degraded by signal blockage and reflection caused by surrounding buildings. To address this problem, various three-dimensional mapping-aided (3DMA) GNSS techniques have been proposed. Among them, zonotope shadow and reflection matching (ZSRM) has demonstrated effective positioning performance by determining the candidate receiver position set using predicted GNSS shadow and reflection regions. However, ZSRM remains vulnerable to satellite signal misclassification, which may lead to positioning failure. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a conservative candidate set determination strategy for robust ZSRM positioning. Instead of using only the most probable signal reception condition from an artificial intelligence (AI)-based classifier, the proposed method combines the candidate regions associated with the two most probable classes. This allows the candidate receiver position set to be determined more conservatively, reducing the risk of positioning failure under signal misclassification. The proposed method was evaluated using real-world urban GNSS data. Experimental results show that the proposed method improved the positioning success rate to 100% for RF, GBDT, and SVM classifiers, compared with 8.2%-30.1% for the existing ZSRM algorithm using individual classifier outputs and 96.6% for ZSRM with unanimous voting. Although the proposed method increased the position bounds by retaining additional candidate regions, it produced smaller position bounds than ZSRM with unanimous voting. These results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially enhances the robustness of ZSRM under satellite signal misclassification in urban GNSS environments.

papers.title: From Static Models to Editable CAD: A Design-Intent-Aware Framework for Reverse Parametrization
papers.abstract: Neutral CAD formats such as STEP typically preserve geometry but not feature histories or parameter dependencies. Thus, they are inherently limited for iterative design that requires modifications, a critical limitation for design optimization that relies on iterative processes. This study presents a design-intent-aware reverse-parametrization framework that converts history-free STEP parts into editable Grasshopper definitions and represents their assembly relations. Without task-specific training, the framework combines kernel-measured features, geometric relations, a compressed attributed adjacency graph, and multiview renderings. An LLM assigns dimensions independent, fixed, or dependent roles, confirms candidate joints, and interprets verification reports. Kernel- and rule-based modules perform measurement, parameter binding, geometry construction, and verification. Evaluation distinguishes default-shape preservation, design-intent reflection, and edit validity, with the latter examined through assembly-level editing examples involving checks for geometry regeneration, joint alignment, interference, and mechanism closure. As an example, five components of a mechanical mechanism were used, and across 25 runs, the mean global and analytic-feature-region intersection over unions (IoUs) were 0.984 and 0.983, respectively; all runs passed the combined shape-preservation criterion. In a separate request experiment, the requested dimension was selected as an independent variable in 19 of 20 runs. Product-level examples show coordinated changes in part geometry and assembly design while preserving assembly relations and avoiding inter-part interference. These results demonstrate editable reconstruction of history-free CAD models under the evaluated geometric and assembly constraints, indicating potential for subsequent design optimization.

authors.name: Namwoo Kang
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
papers.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. GRAPE integrates a stable global predictor based on interpretable representations with two lightweight streaming adapters that correct feature-level and environment-level shifts through online updates. Experiments on two real-world semiconductor manufacturing datasets, including chronologically held-out blind-test streams, show that GRAPE improves robustness and generalization under real temporal drift compared with both conventional batch-learning methods and existing online learning baselines.

authors.name: Sungyoon Ryu
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: ShiftRAG: Bypassing the Textual Bottleneck via Decoupled Learning and Continuous Soft Tokens
papers.abstract: Despite advances in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), suppressing hallucinations during complex reasoning remains a persistent challenge. We identify that existing RAG pipelines suffer from a textual bottleneck: by passing only raw text to the generator, they discard discriminative signals of the retriever. Furthermore, recent attempts to unify retrieval and generation within a single LLM induce severe objective conflict and exacerbate the rank collapse of decoder-only architectures, degrading performance on both tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce ShiftRAG, a decoupled RAG framework that employs a single LLM backbone but isolates discriminative retrieval learning from autoregressive generation. To bridge these decoupled modes, we project retrieval alignments into continuous soft tokens, establishing a high-bandwidth interface that infuses the generator with retrieval-side signals. Concurrently, our soft orthogonality objective mitigates rank collapse, while layer-wise relevance dynamics preserve the fine-grained latent space required for highly discriminative evidence separation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ShiftRAG significantly improves retrieval and question answering performance over state-of-the-art baselines. ShiftRAG preserves foundational capabilities of the backbone while maintaining a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off on general text encoding and generative tasks.

authors.name: Jihong Jeong
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hyunjoon Kim
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Task-Specialized Language-Conditioned Models for Fine-Grained Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Fine-grained robotic manipulation requires instruction grounding, robust perception, and precise contact control. We describe our submission to the MetaFine Open Competition at CoRL 2026. Five independently trained models use a common architecture with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP encoders, trainable language-conditioned feature modulation, and task-specific action heads. We improve demonstrations through contact-aware grasp filtering, instruction-matched data, and expert correction of insertion failures. At inference, task-dependent strategies include photometric test-time augmentation, stochastic action averaging, and uncertainty-triggered replanning. Our submission achieves an official overall score of 0.914 and ranks third among 15 teams. We analyze the models and their task-specific behavior.

papers.title: Finite-Time Tracking Success or Failure in the Pursuer--Evader Model
papers.abstract: We investigate a sufficient framework for determining the success or failure of finite-time tracking in pursuer--evader dynamics. To this end, we design a nonsmooth coupled multi-agent system by adopting a previously established pursuer--evader model from the existing literature, which characterizes asymptotic tracking success and failure, as the backbone. We then provide appropriate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of initial data, system parameters, and kernel functionals, under which some pursuers can successfully track evaders within a finite time, while others fail to do so. In particular, we show that the pursuer--evader subsystem associated with the pursuers that successfully track the evader, together with the corresponding evaders, exhibits finite-time stability.

papers.title: When Does Exploration Prevent Collapse? Three Regimes and the Path of the Reward in Self-Consistency Training
papers.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts a model without labels by rewarding answers that agree with the majority, but it collapses the policy onto its majority answer and can remove the correct answer from the samples. Exploration can prevent this collapse, yet its strength is chosen by trial and error, and how the training algorithm changes the required strength is unclear. We model training on a single problem as a continuous flow of the logits of a softmax policy and analyze which policies are stable as the exploration coefficient varies. Only collapsed policies are stable below a lower boundary and only policies spread over many answers above an upper boundary, and we derive these boundaries in closed form for an agreement reward with smoothing toward the uniform policy, compute them for the majority reward of TTRL on policies with one leading answer and bound them with interval arithmetic for actions on ordered bins. We prove that under exact gradients, the learning rate and, in a mean-field model, the normalization of GRPO leave these boundaries unchanged when exploration passes through them together with the reward but shift them when exploration bypasses them. Exact sums on these policies then show that a bonus for rare answers needs a coefficient above $1/\log(G-1)$ for groups of $G$ samples before the normalization and about two to three times that after it. In free-form TTRL on MATH-500, a bonus placed before the normalization prevented collapse and kept more correct answers among the samples, although it lowered pass@1.

papers.title: Measurement Error and Nonlinear Confounding: Structural Equation Modeling Versus Double Machine Learning
papers.abstract: A latent confounder measured by fallible indicators can be adjusted for with structural equation modeling (SEM), which corrects measurement error but requires a specified functional form, or with double machine learning (DML), which learns the form but ignores measurement error. We derive both population biases and the crossover reliability, the composite reliability above which DML with the indicators or their mean as inputs is less biased than linear SEM; it depends on the nonlinear share of confounding and falls when covariates predict the confounder. A 46-condition Monte Carlo study confirmed both biases and the predicted ordering. With gradient boosting, learning the conditional means raised the DML bias by up to 0.05 and moved the finite-sample crossover upward. A quadratic SEM was unbiased when its form was correct and removed two thirds of the linear-SEM bias under a saturating nonlinearity but little of it under a cubic one.

papers.title: ContactCut: A Partition-Aware Contact Selection Framework for False-Merge Correction in Connectomics
papers.abstract: Localized false-merge correction in connectomics requires converting an identified error into an executable native 3D partition. Still, neither intermediate correction predictions nor seeded graph solvers alone determine which native source-sink constraints should define that partition. We formulate this problem as a 3D-native partition-aware contact selection problem: selecting candidate contacts based on the complete partitions they induce. Our solution comprises two components: ContactCut (CC)-Auto, which uses learned single-contact selection, and ContactCut (CC)-Search, which enables bounded paired-contact search, generates compact alternatives, and applies learned panel ranking. On historical two-way false-merge corrections from MICrONS and FlyWire, CC-Auto improves failure-aware 3D partition (FA-3D Part.) mIoU by 5.9 and 3.4 points over the strongest graph-based controls and by 12.5 and 10.0 points over the best learned baselines. A MICrONS-trained ranker transfers to FlyWire with negligible degradation. CC-Search expands oracle reachability and prioritizes near-oracle alternatives. The code is available at https://github.com/bentake/ContactCut.

authors.name: Chaoli Wang
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs
papers.abstract: Vector databases are now core infrastructure for AI retrieval systems, yet many real deployments must serve queries over multiple independently constructed vectorDBs built with different embedding models. This creates a systems problem of federated retrieval over heterogeneous vectorDBs: vectors and similarity scores are not directly comparable across embedding spaces, while fully resolving this incompatibility through corpus-wide re-embedding and re-indexing is often operationally prohibitive. Existing methods therefore face a difficult trade-off between retrieval quality, construction cost, and query throughput. We present HVMap, a lightweight compatibility layer for federated retrieval across heterogeneous vectorDBs. Instead of rebuilding databases into a unified space, HVMap learns bidirectional mappings between embedding spaces using a fuzzy contrastive loss, enabling calibrated cross-database scoring without corpus migration or index reconstruction. HVMap is system-agnostic and further scales to multi-vectorDB settings while preserving ranking fidelity through a hub-based architecture. We evaluate HVMap in open-domain, cross-domain, and scale-out settings, and also construct a new benchmark for heterogeneous cross-domain federation. Across these settings, HVMap consistently achieves a better quality--cost--throughput trade-off than baselines, achieving up to 3.59X higher nDCG@10, up to 2.01X higher query throughput, and construction time as low as 0.3% of baseline methods. These results show that HVMap makes heterogeneous vectorDB federation practical at scale.

papers.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.

authors.name: Junil Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: Inference for conditional Fr\'echet means via Riemannian Robust Bias Correction
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic framework for inference on conditional Fr\'echet means with predictors and responses taking values in finite-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. We derive a second-order expansion of the smoothing bias, represented in the tangent space via the logarithm map, and show that this bias can affect first-order inference. We propose Riemannian robust bias correction (RRBC), which estimates the leading smoothing bias using a local quadratic regression in the response tangent space and corrects the estimator through the exponential map. Our leave-one-out (LOO) covariance estimator uses intrinsic displacements between the full-sample and LOO RRBC estimates, accounting for the variability of the estimated bias correction and its covariance with the local linear estimator. We establish asymptotically valid pointwise confidence sets and simultaneous confidence tubes without undersmoothing. Simulations on spheres and symmetric positive-definite matrices show that RRBC can improve coverage when smoothing bias is nonnegligible. Cardiovascular and ocean-current applications illustrate simultaneous hypothesis testing and inference for smooth functionals.

papers.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
papers.abstract: LLM-based agentic systems are increasingly combined with CoT reasoning to solve tasks that require accurate reasoning, external knowledge, and multi-step deliberation. Yet, explicit CoT incurs substantial generation overhead, while implicit CoT, which replaces textual rationales with compact continuous tokens, does not naturally support the explicit communication interface required for agentic tool-use. We propose TAC-CoT, a tool-empowered adaptive implicit CoT framework that replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent reasoning segments while retaining textual tokens only for tool calls, observations, and final answers. This interleaved design enables agentic tool-use without verbalizing every intermediate reasoning step. Experiments on agentic math and QA benchmarks show that TAC-CoT improves accuracy by up to 8.8 points while reducing model forward passes by up to 6.8x. Furthermore, analyses show that TAC-CoT improves tool-use quality in both single- and multi-tool settings.

authors.name: Sangmin Bae
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hwanjun Song
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: VLSplat: Vision-Language Guided Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting via Scene Graph
papers.abstract: Learning semantic representations for 3D Gaussian Splatting has recently emerged as a promising direction for 3D scene understanding. However, existing 2D-to-3D semantic lifting approaches rely primarily on 2D segmentation supervision and lack object-level priors, causing the learned representation to be driven by local mask evidence rather than holistic object structure. In this paper, we present VLSplat, a vision-language guided approach for object-centric semantic lifting in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our method augments mask-based lifting with object-level semantic priors derived from vision-language models and refines Gaussian representations using an object-group scene graph. The refinement is performed through two language-guided modules: intra-group refinement suppresses semantic noise within object groups, while inter-group acquisition expands object support regions by incorporating structurally relevant candidates from neighboring groups. Extensive experiments on indoor scene datasets demonstrate that VLSplat improves the semantic consistency and structural completeness of object-level categories. Our code and models are available at https://vlsplat.github.io/.

authors.name: Younho Jeon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sungho Jo
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hippocampal consolidation without replay in fully fine-tuned networks
papers.abstract: Networks that keep learning overwrite what they know. Prevailing remedies replay stored data, distil from old models or freeze the backbone. The brain suggests a different division of labour: the hippocampus indexes where experience lies in cortex while the cortex keeps learning. We show that this division lets a fully trainable network keep learning without cross-task replay, a teacher or inference-time memory. After each task, a training-only hippocampal memory indexes the input geometry of every group of synapses sharing an input, residual energy included, and limits each synapse's movement per direction before and after the optimizer. This class-free geometry carries most of the protection; with conflict detection on top, the method cuts absorption of established classes by near-duplicates several-fold against every compared method. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of one principle keeping whole networks learning across four architecture families and models up to 8 billion parameters. Methods that freeze the backbone hold up only as far as its representation already separates the classes; here the whole network keeps learning to tell near-duplicates apart, leading the frozen-backbone baseline by 17.5 points on TACRED. Without the memory, much old knowledge stays decodable but beyond the network's reach.

papers.title: Unified Loss-Aware Density Control for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: The efficiency and fidelity of 3D Gaussian Splatting critically depend on adaptive density control, which grows and suppresses Gaussian primitives throughout optimization. However, the standard pipeline still relies on heuristic view-space gradients, scale thresholds, and global opacity resets, rather than explicitly assessing the loss-reducing effect of each split, clone, or opacity update. This mismatch can allocate primitives to already-sufficient regions, miss under-reconstructed structures, and destabilize training through blanket opacity changes. In this work, we recast adaptive density control as a collection of local loss-reduction decisions. We derive efficient Taylor-based per-Gaussian surrogates that predict the objective change caused by three primitive-level operations: splitting, cloning, and opacity decay. This yields a unified loss-aware framework with three components. First, we extend second-order splitting to a normalized joint position-scale space, enabling children to adapt not only their locations but also their anisotropic extents. Second, we formulate duplicate cloning as a surrogate minimization problem, selecting only Gaussians whose duplicated contribution is predicted to improve reconstruction and assigning each child a principled opacity. Third, we replace global opacity reset with selective soft opacity decay that weakens harmful primitives while preserving useful ones. Across standard 3DGS benchmarks, our method produces more targeted primitive allocation and achieves improved rendering quality with comparable or smaller Gaussian budgets compared to baselines.

papers.title: Same Function, Different Gradients: Evaluating Gradient Reliability under Reparameterization
papers.abstract: Gradients are no longer used only to train models: Gradient magnitudes are now measurement instruments, used to rank attention heads for pruning, to decide per-example clipping in private training, to allocate adapter rank budgets, and to debug models. Across these workflows, larger gradient magnitudes are taken to mean greater importance. Even for a fixed input--output function, these gradients are computed in one of many possible parameter coordinate systems. For example, attention scores depend on the query and key projections only through the paired product $W_QW_K^\top$. Scaling a head's query projection by $c$ and the corresponding key projection by $1/c$ therefore leaves every output logit unchanged. This change in parameter coordinates rescales the corresponding query and key gradient norms by $1/c$ and $c$, respectively. To test whether gradient-based decisions remain unchanged under these coordinate changes, we introduce Gradient Reliability under Reparameterization (GRR). GRR rewrites a trained model in new parameter coordinates that compute exactly the same function, verifies that predictions are unchanged, and then tests whether the decisions derived from the gradients are unchanged too. Our audits span GLUE classifiers, a ViT on CIFAR-10, GPT-2-medium and GPT-2-large, a 1.1B-parameter Llama-style model on WikiText-2, and six trained LoRA adapters. Empirically, predictions are preserved throughout, but both the gradients and the gradient-based decisions change. Across 66 GLUE attention audits, the median top-3 overlap of raw head-gradient rankings is only $1/3$, and rankings and pruning masks change even under the mildest rescalings we test. In the largest of 14 global-pruning audits, the shifted ranking selects head masks that differ in four of 22 pruned heads and reach $50.92\%$ and $94.84\%$ validation accuracy on one ELECTRA SST-2 model.

papers.title: A Global Routing Method for Electronic Circuit Design Integrating Flow Matching and Constrained A*
papers.abstract: Global routing is a fundamental issue in the design of electronic circuits, as it directly relates to the efficiency, reliability, and compactness of the overall layout of integrated systems. As the demand for higher functionality and reliability within a limited chip area increases, the importance of routing as a design consideration has never been greater. Efficient global routing optimization techniques are therefore required to connect all pins with minimal wirelength (WL), while avoiding congestion and interference across multiple nets within the design space. As the number of nets to be routed increases, global routing inherently suffers from a combinatorial explosion in the design space, making it increasingly difficult to obtain feasible solutions. In this paper, we focus on solving constrained global routing problems based on a heuristic A*-based framework. Based on this concept, a hybrid approach is proposed by integrating constrained A* with flow matching (FM). The method utilizes FM to construct a global cost map that captures routing tendencies across the design space, which is then used to guide the constrained A* search process. This enables efficient exploration of the solution space while satisfying routing constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable WL and via usage to baseline methods while maintaining constraint satisfaction across a wide range of scenarios. Notably, the framework shows strong capability in solving complex routing instances that are difficult to handle using conventional approaches. Additionally, the method shows robust generalization performance across different problem sizes and net configurations.

authors.name: Namwoo Kang
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
papers.abstract: HfO$_2$ heterostructures with La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO$_2$ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO$_2$, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO$_2$ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ and ZrO$_2$ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO$_2$-based materials.

papers.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
papers.abstract: Private information retrieval (PIR) hides which record a client retrieves by scanning the entire database, and batching is an effective technique to improve throughput by sharing this scan across queries. However, existing CPU-based solutions gain little from batching because each query still requires its own multiplications, and vector instructions perform only a few at a time. GPUs and other discrete accelerators can accelerate these computations, but require extra hardware and can constrain database size due to their limited memory capacity. In this paper, we present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that leverages on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. AltoPIR keeps the accelerator fed from the CPU caches, reading each database byte from memory once for all queries in a batch and never writing intermediate products to memory. This enables high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. Our evaluation shows that AltoPIR achieves up to 50.1x higher throughput than existing CPU-based solutions and serves databases larger than a GPU's memory.

papers.title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
papers.abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite signals have recently attracted increasing attention as opportunistic signals for positioning, navigation, and timing. Most Doppler-based LEO positioning studies rely on tracked satellite signals or raw in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples that preserve signal-level structures for acquisition, Doppler tracking, or satellite association. In contrast, passive software-defined radio (SDR) monitoring systems often retain only time-frequency power scans, in which LEO Doppler traces appear as unlabeled ridges without raw IQ samples or identifiable signal structures. This paper proposes a clock-shift-aided segment-based blind Doppler matching method that associates unlabeled Doppler traces with candidate satellites predicted using two-line element (TLE) data. The proposed framework consists of slope-consistent Doppler segment generation, clock-shift-aided temporal alignment, and multi-metric satellite matching based on Doppler-rate and trajectory-shape consistency. The proposed method was evaluated using a three-hour subset of open Starlink/OneWeb monitoring data collected in the United Kingdom. The clock-offset search selected an effective offset of +19 s, for which 56 of 69 segments had at least one slope-compatible candidate, compared with 19 segments at zero shift. Using the resulting satellite associations, the batch positioning error over the full three-hour period was 104.2 m, whereas the RMSE-based and slope-based simple-segment baselines failed to converge near the reference receiver location.

papers.title: A Parameter-Free Best-of-Both-Worlds Policy for Queueing Bandits
papers.abstract: We study online channel scheduling for a single queue served by $K$ channels under bandit feedback. We propose a simple best-of-both-worlds policy that explores when the queue is empty. During busy periods, it selects the empirical best channel while the prescribed conditions hold and, if any condition is violated, switches to a robust bandit policy to clear the queue. For arbitrary arrivals and services determined by an oblivious adversary, our policy achieves $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{K L_T})$ worst-case queue length regret with high probability, where $L_T$ is the longest busy-period length. This result improves the previous $T^{3/4}$ dependence and matches the worst-case lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Under bounded i.i.d. stochastic models with a unique best stabilizing channel, we show that the cumulative queue length regret converges to a finite problem-dependent constant, and further establish the logarithmic expected worst-case queue length regret bound.

papers.title: A balloon effect: ban one channel and a hidden trait finds another
papers.abstract: Language models trained on the outputs of other models can acquire traits that those outputs never mention, such as a preference for an animal carried by lists of numbers. Such subliminal learning can pass on unwanted traits. The intuitive defence is to find and forbid the tokens through which a trait shows, but how a trait's trace behaves under such bans, and what of it a student learns, has not been resolved. We closed a trait's outlets one by one in two stress tests, a preference chain and a name chain, across two models, six output formats and 16 traits. Bans did not remove the trait. Much as squeezing a balloon in one place makes it bulge in another, the trait moved to wherever the format still allowed, an effect we call the balloon effect. Decomposing this transfer, which bans on surface features cannot stop, down to single heads and neurons, we show that it can be cut at the circuit that writes the trait into the output. Patching that circuit while the teacher writes numbers stopped the chains, sharply reduced the overt name leak and halved the trait passed to a student, whereas the same number of random heads produced no detectable reduction. These results give a mechanistic account of how unwanted hidden traits are transferred and a route to preventing it.

papers.title: Latent Diffusion-GAN: Adversarial Learning in the Autoencoded Latent Space
papers.abstract: Diffusion models are powerful generative frameworks for producing high-quality images by denoising latent variables from random noise. However, training with likelihood-based objectives, such as denoising score matching, can lead to locally over-smoothed high-frequency details, including fine textures and sharp edges, thereby limiting perceptual fidelity and structural detail. Adversarial training with GANs enhances sharpness but typically requires additional discriminator networks, increasing computational costs and destabilizing training. To this end, we propose Latent Diffusion Generative Adversarial Networks (LD-GAN), a novel framework that seamlessly integrates adversarial learning into diffusion models without modifying their original pipeline. LD-GAN leverages the pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) in latent diffusion models as an energy-based discriminator, enabling adversarial training without extra parameters and preserving the structured latent priors learned from large datasets. We also introduce a structural consistency energy that aligns encoder and decoder feature representations, thereby enhancing perceptual quality and compatibility with the pretrained latent space. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LD-GAN significantly improves sample fidelity, perceptual sharpness, and diversity over state-of-the-art baseline methods across various generation tasks while ensuring efficient training dynamics.

papers.title: UniCross3D: Unified Cross-View and Cross-Domain Diffusion for Consistent Single-Image 3D Generation
papers.abstract: Reconstructing detailed geometry and realistic appearance from a single RGB image is essential yet fundamentally challenging due to inherent ambiguities such as occlusion, lighting variations, and texture-geometry entanglement. While recent diffusion-based generative models have significantly improved novel view synthesis, existing approaches suffer from two critical limitations: lack of cross-view geometric consistency and insufficient cross-domain semantic alignment. To address these issues, we introduce UniCross3D, a unified cross-view and cross-domain diffusion framework designed explicitly for consistent and physically coherent 3D generation. UniCross3D features two novel contributions: (1) a cross-view latent regularization that enforces cross-view geometric consistency across synthesized viewpoints by penalizing latent variance, and (2) a cross-domain mutual information objective grounded in the physics of image formation, explicitly aligning synthesized color and normal maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniCross3D achieves significantly improved view consistency and semantic alignment over state-of-the-art methods and yields higher-fidelity reconstructions, particularly under challenging textures and ambiguous viewpoints.

papers.title: Probe-Guided Gradient Balancing for Multimodal Learning
papers.abstract: Jointly trained multimodal networks frequently underutilize weaker modalities, as faster-learning modalities dominate the shared fusion objective and suppress gradients reaching slower ones. Most existing approaches throttle dominant modalities, whereas directly boosting weaker modalities often fails because monitoring signals derived from the joint loss remain dominated by stronger modalities. We propose Probe-Guided Gradient Boosting (PGGB), a gradient modulation approach that boosts weaker modalities while preserving the strength of dominant ones. PGGB attaches lightweight linear classifiers to stop-gradient features from each modality to estimate representation quality independently. The gap between these scores, termed the utilization gap, provides an imbalance signal used to adaptively scale weaker-modality gradients through bounded and smoothed modulation. PGGB is composable with throttling methods, as it leaves the loss function and fusion architecture unchanged. Experiments across eight benchmarks spanning four domains and 2-4 modalities demonstrate that PGGB outperforms state-of-the-art methods on highly imbalanced multimodal datasets while remaining competitive under low or negligible imbalance. We further establish bounded scaling, self-attenuation, and a descent bound for standard SGD under smoothness and bounded-variance assumptions. Code is available at https://github.com/VuVoCodes/PGGB.

authors.name: Thuy Nguyen
authors.institution: National Institute Of Hygiene And Epidemiology

papers.title: Pair-Relative Partial Equivariance for Rotation-Robust Keypoint Descriptor Matching
papers.abstract: Learned keypoint descriptors trained on upright imagery often fail under large in-plane rotation. Steerers address this by applying a single exact SO(2) representation to the descriptor space, but this global group constraint can be too rigid for keypoint descriptors, whose angular responses need not follow a single group representation. We propose pair-relative partial equivariance, which measures equivariance under the empirical distribution of relative rotations in image pairs, and PaSteer, a relaxed descriptor-steering framework that allows the steering map to leave the exact representation manifold while retaining the lightweight, backbone-free design of steering. PaSteer instantiates this relaxation with two variants: an identity-preserving residual steerer (PaSteer-soft) and a free-form Fourier steerer (PaSteer-free). We show that the per-angle optimal linear steerer for a fixed non-equivariant descriptor generally does not obey the group composition law, explaining why exact representations can be suboptimal in the frozen-descriptor regime. On Roto-360, MegaDepth-1500, AIMS, and IMC-PT, PaSteer consistently improves rotation-robust matching over an exact steerer on frozen DeDoDe descriptors, especially under large relative rotations, with minimal upright degradation.

papers.title: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider mixed-motive games (MMGs) which model various real-world multi-agent scenarios where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. We identify an issue with existing gifting methods, where agents become overly dependent on incoming gifts and fail to learn reward-yielding behaviors, a phenomenon we call gift over-reliance. To address this, we propose a refusal-augmented gifting framework that balances cooperation and competition in MMGs. Our approach introduces an adaptive refusal mechanism that allows agents to selectively reject a portion of received gifts from their policy-update signals, thereby mitigating gift over-reliance and preventing the agents from being exploited by other agents. This mechanism is gifting-method-agnostic, serving as a plug-in for existing schemes while enabling decentralized learning. We demonstrate that across diverse MMG environments and gifting schemes, our mechanism consistently reduces gift over-reliance and prevents lock-in to sacrificing policies, improving $\alpha$-fairness as a result, without necessitating major changes to existing training pipelines.

authors.name: Woojun Kim

papers.title: AnchorHEC: Targetless Hand-Eye Calibration of Wrist and Fixed Cameras
papers.abstract: Recent robot systems combine wrist and fixed cameras, requiring camera-to-robot transforms for both. Most hand-eye calibration methods rely on targets or robot-body observations. Scene-based methods using 3D reconstruction require neither but address only wrist cameras. We introduce AnchorHEC, a targetless hand-eye calibration framework for wrist and fixed cameras in a single procedure using RGB images, forward kinematics (FK), and known camera intrinsics. We initialize both camera types using FK and a shared 3D foundation model reconstruction. FK-constrained wrist-image bundle adjustment reduces the impact of reconstructed pose and scale errors. If this refinement fails or retains too few inliers, we relax the constraints on potentially inaccurate FK poses and lens parameters. We use the refined wrist transform and FK to triangulate metric points and estimate fixed-camera poses. Across three backbones, calibration errors in simulation decrease by 86.4% in translation and 71.6% in rotation, averaged over both camera types, relative to reconstruction-based baselines. We also validate AnchorHEC on a physical robot. Project page: https://hwanggb.github.io/AnchorHEC/

authors.name: Guebin Hwang
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sungho Jo
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Action Verification through Conjecture and Refutation for Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Language model agents increasingly act on users' behalf by manipulating external environments through tools, often from high-level instructions that leave critical task- and environment-specific context unstated. To prevent resulting misaligned actions, recent work verifies proposed actions before execution, largely by establishing whether the conditions supporting them hold. We argue that this confirmation-oriented view leaves a fundamental blind spot: a wrong action often passes every check that asks whether it is right. This motivates a different question for verification: rather than asking what evidence supports an action, can the agent find evidence that refutes it? We pursue this direction with BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented, expect-suspect-test procedure that predicts the intended effect of each state-mutating action, formulates specific and empirically testable hypotheses for how it could be wrong, and tests them using existing observations or additional non-mutating actions, executing the action only if none survives testing. On challenging AppWorld tasks, BlackSwan improves success rate over the strongest baseline by 14.9 and 25.2%p with and without the backbone model's thinking mode, respectively. Even without thinking or in-context demonstrations, it outperforms stronger baselines equipped with them. The gains also transfer beyond AppWorld, with BlackSwan improving WebShop performance by 12.7%p. More broadly, our results suggest that language model agents have an underused capacity to recognize and self-correct misaligned actions, which can be systematically elicited through active conjecture and refutation before execution.

authors.name: Minhyeon Oh
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology
