authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces. To verify the correctness of the formula, we provide a sample code for Singular which computes the spectral pairs and compares the output with that of sppairs in Singular for the three variable case.

authors.name: Youngho Yoon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
papers.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions as a route to low-power temperature sensors while providing insight into carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions.

papers.title: Variance-reduced First-order Methods for Finite-sum Function Constrained Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper studies finite-sum convex optimization with convex function constraints, where both the objective $f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and the constraint mapping $g(x)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n g_j(x)$ may have a large number of components. We propose a variance-reduced anchored constraint extrapolation method (VaRAn-ConEx), which combines stochastic component sampling with primal--dual extrapolation for nonlinear function constraints. Relative to stochastic approximation schemes such as ConEx, VaRAn-ConEx~method reduces gradient complexity by using epoch-wise full-gradient correction and variance-reduced estimators for both the objective and constraint components. In the semi-finite case where $n=1$, the method attains gradient complexities $O(\sqrt m/\epsilon)$ under constant steps and $O(m/\epsilon^{1/2}+1/\epsilon^{3/2})$ under nonconstant steps. In the fully finite-sum case, we establish boundedness of the Lagrange multiplier sequence and derive convergence and gradient-complexity bounds for constant and nonconstant step-size policies. Under these policies, we then prove similar gradient complexity with $m$ replaced by $\max\{m,n\}$. We also show acceleration when the finite-sum objective $f$ is strongly convex, irrespective of components $f_i$.

papers.title: On Stochastic Continuous-Time Linear System Identification for Adaptive Stabilization
papers.abstract: Learning to stabilize an unknown continuous-time stochastic linear system is a central problem in control theory and reinforcement learning. This paper numerically studies data-driven identification of such systems with possibly unstable dynamics for the purpose of stabilization. We present a method that learns a stabilizing gain from observed trajectories, and examine how the failure probability, namely the probability that the learned gain does not stabilize the system, depends on the amount of data, dimension, noise intensity, excitation, and controllability. Numerical experiments on an unstable batch-reactor benchmark show that the squared identification error decays inversely with the aggregate observation time, that is, the combined length of all trajectories, while the failure probability decays exponentially in the same quantity. Hence, despite instability, a single long trajectory can achieve similar stabilization performance to that of many short trajectories of the same total length. We also observe \emph{signal saturation}: stronger excitation improves stabilization only logarithmically with the excitation strength. Finally, we show experimentally that accurate identification of the full dynamics is \emph{not} necessary for successful stabilization.

papers.title: A structure-preserving finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a fully discrete finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility. The scheme combines a standard two-point flux approximation of diffusion, the L1 approximation of the Caputo derivative on a uniform time grid, and a semiconvex splitting of the potential, and it discretizes the inverse mobility by a secant average multiplying the entire L1 derivative. The key estimate is a lower bound for the accumulated pairing of this weighted L1 derivative with the solution increments in terms of the accumulated L1 quadratic form. Using this lower bound, we derive a discrete energy estimate and the time regularity required for compactness. For twice continuously differentiable semiconvex potentials satisfying sign conditions outside $(-1,1)$ and initial data in $H^1(\Omega)$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, we prove existence of at least one fully discrete solution on every admissible finite volume mesh and every uniform time grid. Every such solution satisfies the maximum bound principle and a discrete energy bound relative to the initial energy, without a time-step restriction. In up to three space dimensions, under a mesh regularity condition with a constant independent of the mesh size, we prove that any sequence of fully discrete solutions has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$ to a weak solution of the continuous problem as the mesh size and time step tend to zero. As a consequence, we obtain existence of a weak solution in one and two space dimensions, and in three dimensions whenever such meshes exist.

authors.name: Yonghyeon Jeon
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Hierarchical direct solver for Lippmann-Schwinger equations based on boundary traces
papers.abstract: A high-order hierarchical direct solver for variable-media scattering in two dimensions is presented. Standard discretizations for these problems produce dense linear systems that are commonly solved iteratively, requiring a new global solve for each incident field. The method proposed here instead constructs a reusable scattering operator for the inhomogeneous medium, based on a hierarchical subdivision of the computational domain. First, high-accuracy leaf scattering operators are built from discretized local integral equations. Up the hierarchy, neighboring boxes are merged to build the scattering operators for successively larger boxes. A key feature of the method is that each scattering operator is represented as a map of incoming traces to outgoing traces. Consequently, volume unknowns appear only in the leaf computations; all higher levels of the hierarchy operate entirely on boundary traces. The hierarchical solver is presented first at the continuum level and discretized only afterward using high-order local volume quadrature, polynomial trace representations, and boundary integral techniques. For a discretization involving $N$ degrees of freedom, the method requires $O(N^{3/2})$ work and $O(N\log N)$ storage to build all scattering operators. Once these are available, any incoming field can be processed at cost $O(N)$ if only the outgoing field is required, and cost $O(N\log N)$ if the full field is required. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy on a range of challenging scattering problems including cavities, back-scattering, limited regularity, and high wavenumber, that pose significant challenges to iterative methods.

papers.title: On the Hasse-Sugawara problem and its application to Hilbert's twelfth problem
papers.abstract: We give an analytic proof of the Hasse-Sugawara problem by treating the seven remaining families of moduli. We also construct an explicit integer translate of a Weber value whose relative norms generate every intermediate field, and express these generators using extended form class groups.

authors.name: Ja Kyung Koo
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
papers.abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories. The method combines explicit external-field coupling with self-consistent updates of electronic density while retaining the computational efficiency of the classical-path approximation. Benchmarks against regular TDDFT methods show close agreement for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses. Applications to the linear absorption spectrum of crystalline and amorphous SiO$_2$ demonstrate its capability to large and structurally complex systems. This method is also applied to the 2D hybrid perovskite $(\mathrm{BA})_2\mathrm{CsPb}_2\mathrm{Br}_7$. Finite-temperature calculations show that the second-order opto-current response is strongly affected by structural fluctuations. Real-space DC current density further reveals pronounced Br-centered vortex currents, and its microscopic origin is investigated.

papers.title: Directional Dual-Head Supervision for Real-Time Source-Free Polyp Segmentation
papers.abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) is critical for medical image segmentation as it adapts a model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data, thereby preserving data privacy. However, its effectiveness is often limited by confirmation bias: self-training models tend to miss small polyps, hallucinate foreground, and produce imprecise contours. We propose MedRT-SFSeg, a real-time SFDA framework built on a dual-head one-to-one/one-to-many YOLO segmentation architecture. Mask-DHF fuses precision- and recall-oriented predictions into stable pseudo-instances, while DURR uses the sign of pixel-level dual-head disagreement as a directional cue to expand or shrink masks, and additionally recovers missed instances and suppresses hallucinations. Seg-MARD further regularizes feature representations through mask-guided, region-stratified sampling. Experiments on bidirectional adaptation between Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB show that MedRT-SFSeg achieves 80.43%/80.77% Dice and 5.53/8.44 mm ASD, improving the non-adapted baseline by 7.7 and 9.8 Dice points while running at more than 62 FPS end-to-end. These results suggest that segmentation-aware dual-head supervision can improve pseudo-label quality without sacrificing real-time inference. Project page: https://danielnguyen-05.github.io/MedRT-SFSeg

authors.name: Huu-Thuan Huynh
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: Fidelity Collapses with Table Size, Not Turn Count: Delivery Architecture in a Deployed Tool-Using Agent
papers.abstract: When a multi-turn agent delivers a tool's structured records into the model's context and re-emits them each turn, every turn can corrupt data the tool computed correctly. We measure this in a production award-travel agent: two architectures over identical frozen payloads, lineage-matched prompts and sampling, differing only in delivery architecture. SYNTHESIS feeds full record sets into the planner's context and answers follow-ups in-head; BYPASS, the deployed system, keeps records in session state, translates follow-ups into arguments for a deterministic filter, and delivers rows over a typed side channel. Across 24 dialogues (339 scored turns per condition), BYPASS scores 92.3% of turns fully correct, SYNTHESIS 45.7% (paired gap +46.6pp [+35.7, +57.1]). Varying delivered-table size by capture date, SYNTHESIS collapses from near-perfect at 10 rows or fewer to 8% or less beyond about 74 rows. On a content-controlled prefix ladder the collapse threshold orders by model capability, from under 10 rows (GPT-4o-mini) to about 198 or more (Gemini 2.5 Pro), while BYPASS stays size-flat for all four models. The collapse is expensive: beyond 100 rows, where almost no SYNTHESIS answer is correct, each correct one costs roughly 200x BYPASS's flat \$0.012. Practitioners converged on typed side-channel delivery for rendering, not correctness; we show it was, unknowingly, also a correctness decision.

papers.title: Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization
papers.abstract: Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters. Project page: https://vdkhoi20.github.io/CoPFB/.

authors.name: Dinh-Khoi Vo

papers.title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: https://magnusdtd.github.io/CoreCalib/ .

authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: SAVIER: Source-Anchored Visual Inspection and Evidence-Guided Repair for Vietnamese Cultural Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: We present SAVIER, a training-free, one-pass framework that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a generated image while preserving the scene details requested by the user. The problem is hard because a plausible scene can miss the cues that identify the entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image it produces. SAVIER starts from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt; a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from prompt-preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns the discrepancies into at most three positive instructions before one regeneration with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs. On the 50 bilingual prompts of ViCuP, evaluated with SDXL and FLUX.1-dev against a frozen, human-verified visual contract, SAVIER raises contract fulfillment from 55.6 to 69.6 and from 59.1 to 67.3 over Culture-TRIP and raises CAIRE cultural relevance on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation that removes the agent repair shows that SAVIER's photographs account for most of the contract gain; the agent roles add country-level relevance on FLUX.1-dev without lowering adherence to the original prompt under the official VQAScore. Project page: https://oxyzgiahuy.github.io/savier/

authors.name: Gia-Huy Thai
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.

authors.name: Nguyen Bich Van
authors.institution: Viện Nghiên cứu Điện tử, Tin học, Tự động hóa

authors.name: Nguyen Trung Kien
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Nonradial entire solutions of the critical H\'enon equation for every $\alpha>2$
papers.abstract: We consider the critical H\'enon equation $-\Delta u=|x|^{\alpha}u^{(N+2+2\alpha)/(N-2)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$. Gladiali, Grossi, and Neves (\emph{Advances in Mathematics}, 2013) constructed nonradial continua bifurcating at $\alpha_k=2(k-1)$, $k\ge2$, and conjectured that these continua are confined to the even parameters. Jiang and Xiong (2026) disproved this conjecture by obtaining nonradial solutions in punctured neighborhoods of $\alpha_k$ for even $k>(N-2)/2$. We prove that positive nonradial finite-energy entire solutions exist for every $\alpha>2$ in every dimension $N\ge3$. The proof introduces a global variational construction by direct minimization on a monotonicity cone on the Emden--Fowler cylinder. Angular and axial order restore compactness in every finite $L^r$, $r>2$, despite Sobolev supercriticality, and invariance of the linear resolvent yields the full equation. This constructs a solution at each prescribed parameter without continuing local bifurcation branches. The solutions have Newtonian decay, are invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and the Kelvin transform, and have energy strictly below the radial level. We also obtain a second solution for every $\alpha>6$ in even dimensions, nonvertical branches at every $\alpha_k$ with $k\ge2$ even without dimension restrictions, a cubic energy law, and rigidity near $\alpha=0$ under bounded cylindrical amplitude.

papers.title: The polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjecture
papers.abstract: We study positive classical solutions of the polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden system $(-\Delta)^m u=|x|^\alpha v^p$, $(-\Delta)^m v=|x|^\beta u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $m\ge2$, $p,q\ge1$, $pq>1$, and $\alpha,\beta\ge0$. We prove that there is no such solution whenever $\frac{n+\alpha}{p+1}+\frac{n+\beta}{q+1}>n-2m$, in every dimension and without any assumption on the behavior of the solutions at infinity. Combined with an existence result of Villavert, this proves the polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjecture of Phan for $m\ge2$: for these exponents and weights, a positive classical solution exists if and only if $\frac{n+\alpha}{p+1}+\frac{n+\beta}{q+1}\le n-2m$. The proof has two parts. We first show that positivity forces $(-\Delta)^i u>0$ and $(-\Delta)^i v>0$ for $1\le i\le m-1$. For $m$ even this needs $pq>1$, and explicit radial examples show that it fails when $pq<1$ and when $p=q=1$. The system is then equivalent to a weighted integral system with a Riesz kernel of order $2m$. For such integral systems we prove the corresponding Liouville theorem for every Riesz order $\mu\in(1,n)$, adapting a recent argument for the second-order case that combines a localized virial identity with an interval comparison along source layers.

papers.title: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
papers.abstract: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

papers.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
papers.abstract: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.

papers.title: Harmonic Quasiconformal Mappings in the BMO-Teichm\"uller space
papers.abstract:
Let $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the class of increasing homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathbb{R}$
  that admit harmonic quasiconformal extensions to the upper
  half-plane $\mathbb{H}$. Kalaj and Pavlovi\'c proved that a
  homeomorphism $h$ belongs to $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ if and only if $h$ is
  bi-Lipschitz and the Hilbert transform of $h'$ belongs to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$,
  and asked whether $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ is a group under composition.
  We give a negative answer to this question. Further, we show that the Beltrami coefficients of harmonic quasiconformal mappings of $\mathbb{H}$ can be identified with the open unit ball of $H^\infty(\mathbb{H})$.
  Finally, we study the topology of $\text{HQS}(\mathbb{R})$ and prove that
  it is contractible in the topology inherited from
  the BMO-Teichm\"uller space.

papers.title: Where Beam Search Loses Top-Ranked Items:First-Step Coverage in Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation can reproduce a wider beam's ranked output with roughly half the prefix-capacity budget by reallocating retention capacity across semantic-ID positions. We identify a \emph{first-step coverage bottleneck}: across six full-test settings of the TIGER generative recommender spanning three domains and two identifier constructions, every pruned exact top-10 path is first lost at the initial decoding step. An exact-catalog reference isolates search losses and guides a controlled budget intervention. Moving width to the first step raises Search Recall@10 by 0.96--10.90 percentage points at Beam-50's unchanged budget. Across all 77,373 test users with residual-quantized variational autoencoder (RQ-VAE) tokenization, the reallocated schedule reproduces Beam-100's ordered top-10 at nominal budgets of 151 rather than 301, without retraining or changing identifiers or scores. Matched-output timing saves 6.35--6.39\% of decoder latency; profiling identifies the execution costs that limit the translation from reduced search work to runtime savings. Larger-candidate experiments reveal how output size changes retention requirements. These findings make budget placement an actionable serving decision: locate ranking loss, redirect search capacity, and preserve downstream inputs before increasing uniform beam width.

authors.name: Hanwei Zhu
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: SyncHeC: Markerless Spatio-Temporal Hand-Eye Calibration via Differentiable Rendering and Continuous-Time Joint Optimization
papers.abstract: Markerless hand-eye calibration under continuous motion requires jointly resolving camera geometry and the time offset between images and joint states. We present SyncHeC (Synchronized Hand-Eye Calibration), a dense differentiable-rendering framework that estimates both from a single robot trajectory. Continuous-time forward kinematics makes latency differentiable, metric depth complements mask contours, and an offline planner combines spatial sensitivity with temporal excitation. Alternating updates support Eye-to-Hand, Eye-in-Hand, and multi-camera calibration. On a 7-DoF arm, one $6.5$\,s motion yields $0.21$\,cm translation error against a marker-board reference, $0.34$\,cm touch-test error, and $2.7$\,ms latency error relative to an $87$\,ms reference with $95\%$ uncertainty of $\pm1.5$\,ms. Against CM-Calib on matched recordings, translation and nominal latency errors improve by $3.7\times$ and $2.3\times$. Experiments span seven arms and four depth sensors. Compensating the recovered offset during policy training and deployment increases success by $8.1$ percentage points across six families and six tasks ($1{,}800$ matched pairs; paired $95\%$ confidence interval $[6.3,9.9]$ points).

authors.name: Zhengdong Hong
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University

papers.title: Reducible fibers of polynomials over integers: the Hilbert-Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$ and its applications
papers.abstract:
Given a polynomial $f\in \mathbb{Q}[X]$, the Hilbert--Siegel problem asks for a description of the set of all values $t_0\in \mathbb{Z}$, possibly up to a finite set, such that $f(X)-t_0$ is reducible. Reducibility occurs trivially for $t_0$ in the value set of some non-linear left-composition factor of $f$. The problem therefore reduces to determining the polynomials having infinitely many further reducible values. The biggest step towards a solution so far was taken in joint work of the author with Behajaina and Neftin. We strengthen some of the methods obtained in that work to present the complete solution of the Hilbert--Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$.
  We give applications to the problem of newly reducible iterates of polynomials, and to an unlikely intersection problem on simultaneous reducible fibers of two polynomial maps over $\mathbb{Q}$, generalizing a result by Bilu and Tichy.

papers.title: Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutional Network with Contrastive Score Refinement for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
papers.abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition is a pivotal task in computer vision; however, conventional Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are often constrained by pairwise joint modeling, which fails to capture the intricate high-order interactions inherent in human movement. While recent hypergraph-based methods attempt to address this limitation, they typically rely on static structures derived from anatomical priors, lacking the flexibility to capture dynamic, action-specific joint correlations. To this end, we propose DyGCN, a Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Convolutional Network for skeleton-based action recognition. At the core of DyGCN is the Dynamic Hypergraph Construction Network with Contrastive Score Refinement (DyGCT) block, which comprises two novel components: the Geometry-Constrained Dynamic Hypergraph Construction (GeoHC) module and the Contrastive Score Refinement (CSR) module. Specifically, GeoHC dynamically constructs action-specific hyperedges by leveraging geometry-constrained second-order compatibility, transcending the limitations of static hyperedge structures. Furthermore, CSR explicitly refines the pairwise compatibility scores during hypergraph construction through prototype-based contrastive learning, fostering more discriminative action-specific hyperedges, with zero inference-time overhead as CSR operates only during training. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120, and Northwestern-UCLA validate the effectiveness of DyGCN, achieving state-of-the-art performance on widely used benchmarks. The source code is available at https://github.com/marvineta0405/DyGCN.

papers.title: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Toward Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Post-incident analysis of a robot foundation model poses a singular causal question: which internal components caused this failure, and to what degree? Mechanistic interpretability (MI), however, establishes general causal claims by decoding the concepts a policy has learned, yet knowing which concepts are encoded is insufficient for identifying the actual cause of a specific incident. In this position paper, we analyze this concept-malfunction gap by posing fault isolation in the framework of actual causality. Specifically, we formalize a fault-isolation query as a tuple of intervened internal components, counterfactual values, contingencies, and read-outs, and lay out conditions for it to be well-specified. Through this lens, we identify shortcomings of current MI approaches: they assume fixed contingencies and read out only immediate effects, letting backups obscure actual causes. We demonstrate on a toy example that these shortcomings can lead to conflicting verdicts. Lastly, based on the well-specification conditions, we outline four open research tasks toward closing the gap.

authors.name: Gihyuk Ko
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: Less but Sufficient: Relation Knowledge Selects Compact Knowledge-Graph Contexts, and What External Checks Can and Cannot Catch
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) read knowledge-graph facts ranked by relevance, leaving open whether they suffice or conflict. Our checks use relation knowledge, written by hand or learned from training questions labelled with their relation paths. It selects a compact context of facts yielding an answer, and derives it; a derivability check tests whether an answer follows, a consistency check whether facts conflict, and a validation-chosen routing gate decides where the derived answer replaces the LLM's. Seven open LLMs read the compact context better in exact match than relevance-ranked facts; on ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ) they match SubgraphRAG's facts at a quarter of the prompt tokens, and stronger LLMs read SubgraphRAG's better. Where the routing gate passes, ours leads SubgraphRAG's in exact match in all 53 LLM, benchmark and prompt settings. A precision gate, returning the derived answer only when the check passes with exactly one derived entity, answered 18 and 5 percent of held-out WebQSP and CWQ questions in a pre-specified test, right for 90 and 96 percent. The consistency check judges facts by path evidence only where another path joins their entities, true of 2.5 percent of named-entity facts in our compact WebQSP and CWQ contexts.

papers.title: Vehicle Speed-Aware Jammer-Resilient Receiver for Multi-User MIMO V2X Systems
papers.abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication plays a crucial role in enabling connected and autonomous driving by supporting the reliable exchange of safety-critical information among vehicles and infrastructure. However, due to the open nature of wireless channels, V2X systems are vulnerable to various physical-layer attacks, among which jamming is one of the most intuitive and severe threats. In this paper, we propose a vehicle speed-aware jammer-resilient reception framework for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) V2X systems. The proposed method exploits the fundamental difference in Doppler characteristics between stationary jammers and moving vehicles. By transforming the received signal into the Doppler domain, the receiver identifies low-Doppler components associated with static interference and suppresses them through Doppler-domain filtering. Notably, the proposed approach does not require prior knowledge of the jammer channel or its spatial direction, making it suitable for practical V2X environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates strong jamming signals and significantly improves the achievable sum-rate compared with conventional receivers.

papers.title: MURFormer: Attention-Based Lightweight Multi-Scale Uncertainty-Guided Refinement Framework for PPG Denoising
papers.abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a widely used physiological signal for its convenience but is highly susceptible to motion artifacts that degrade waveform quality and limit downstream analysis. This paper proposes MURFormer, a lightweight multi-scale uncertainty-guided refinement framework for PPG denoising through noisy-to-clean PPG mapping. MURFormer employs a newly proposed Multi-Scale Attention-Conv Fusion (MACF) block, which is designed to efficiently capture multi-scale temporal dynamics of PPG, as the fundamental building block and performs uncertainty-guided two-pass refinement prioritizing unreliable regions. The method was evaluated on the publicly available CIME dataset and on a Daily Activities dataset collected in this work, comprising paired noisy-clean PPG recordings from 24 subjects. Experimental results show that MURFormer improves both signal quality and physiological fidelity over the raw noisy input, yielding 129\% and 105\% relative signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvements, and 66\% and 81\% relative reductions in heart-rate mean absolute error (MAE), on the Daily Activities and CIME datasets, respectively. MURFormer also outperforms an existing denoising baseline on both datasets with a relatively small parameter count while preserving beat-level timing and waveform morphology. In addition, the model maintains strong denoising performance across varying input window lengths, suggesting that MURFormer is an effective and robust framework for practical PPG denoising. The implementation of MURFormer is publicly available at https://github.com/k-hram/MURFormer.git

authors.name: Haram Kwon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sungho Jo
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Some Remarks on the Asymptotic Behavior of Mean Field Games of Controls
papers.abstract: We analyze the asymptotic behavior of several mean field games of controls. First, in the time-dependent case, we examine the behavior of solutions to discounted mean field games of controls as the discount factor $\lambda$ tends to infinity. Next, we study three stationary models of mean field games of controls, finding that solutions to the first-order discounted problem and the second-order ergodic problem can be obtained from solutions to the second-order discounted problem by taking $\nu \to 0$ and $\lambda \to 0$, respectively. Finally, we investigate the long-time average behavior of solutions to the time-dependent system with no discount, finding that solutions converge to the solution to the second-order ergodic problem as $T \to \infty$.

papers.title: Scalable Fully Implicit Runge-Kutta Solvers for Time-Dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard Convection
papers.abstract: We consider the efficient numerical solution of time-dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection governed by the incompressible Boussinesq equations. The coupled velocity-pressure-temperature system presents significant computational challenges arising from incompressibility, buoyancy coupling, convection, and the simultaneous resolution of multiple physical time scales. We present a systematic study of fully implicit Runge-Kutta methods for time-dependent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, together with scalable finite element solvers for the resulting stage-coupled systems. We employ high-order, L-stable Radau IIA methods for temporal integration and investigate Taylor-Hood and Alfeld-Sorokina finite elements in two dimensions, along with Taylor-Hood and enriched macroelement discretizations in three dimensions. The macroelement approaches offer strong local inf-sup stability and patch structures well suited to Vanka-type relaxation. In two dimensions, monolithic multigrid achieves nearly stage-independent outer Krylov iteration counts and maintains robust convergence under mesh refinement. On the same mesh with incremental pressure correction, selected Radau configurations reduce elapsed solve time by 18-32% and yield smaller sampled transient differences relative to a numerical reference solution. Three-dimensional experiments demonstrate favorable parallel scalability with Taylor-Hood elements and substantially improved discrete mass conservation with the enriched macroelement discretization. These results identify regimes in which coupled multistage fully implicit integration is computationally competitive when equipped with appropriate multigrid preconditioners.

papers.title: GRIPS: An Empirical Study of Pre-SQL Grounding Information for SQL Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems answer natural language questions over structured data, but can fail before SQL generation by linking question mentions to the wrong table, column, value, or relation. Even valid SQL can then return an incorrect answer. This raises a central question: What pre-SQL information helps a SQL generator, and when does additional information cease to help? We investigate this question on TempTabQA-C and BIRD. Among the audited SQL Static failures, grounding errors form the largest category on both benchmarks. We introduce GRIPS (Grounding Representation and Input Processing for SQL generation), a three-stage method that derives structured pre-SQL information to make these decisions explicit before query generation. Across GPT-5-nano and Llama-70B, GRIPS-Adaptive improves over SQL Static in 18 of 20 settings, with an average accuracy gain of 11.8 percentage points, while reducing model-call token usage by 47.8%. Our controlled analysis shows which grounding information can improve SQL generation, whereas adding more pre-SQL information does not consistently help. By separating question-input grounding from SQL generation, GRIPS makes text-to-SQL more accurate, efficient, and easier to diagnose.

papers.title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
papers.abstract: We rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from the electoral court's section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. A projection published live on the night gave the eventual winner, Lula, a probability of 0.998 from 19:15, with 1.6% of sections counted. The markets reached 0.9 at 20:24, with 46% counted. Read as the projection's central estimate with a wider uncertainty, their prices imply a standard deviation of the final margin about four times the live projection's, and about twice that of a section-level projection calibrated on the 2018 runoff, the earlier night with the largest errors. Valued at these projections, takers' purchases of Lula after the count resumed had an expected profit of 4 to 18 cents per Kalshi contract after fees; valued at a state-level extrapolation of the count, it was zero. During a two-hour suspension of the count the markets gave Lula 0.25 to 0.44, below every reading we compute afterwards from the sections then public, none of which was available live. On the first-round night, when the headline count showed the eventual leader ahead from its first file, the same markets were faster than our projection.

papers.title: MoRE-GS: Motion-Regime Experts for Future Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract:
Future dynamic novel-view synthesis requires extrapolating multiple motion regimes within the same scene. A single dynamics model may not simultaneously represent stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. We introduce Motion Regime Expert Routing for Gaussian Splatting (MoRE-GS), a causal, render-aware framework for forecasting dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian representation reconstructed exclusively from the observed temporal prefix and forecasts its control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid motion constraints. A compact routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, while a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation. Across D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, MoRE-GS achieves improved performance against other methods, and these results demonstrate that renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors improves causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes.
  Project page: https://advanced-vision-and-learning-lab.github.io/MoRE-GS-website/

papers.title: Governing Equations of Human Sleep Macro-Structure:Symbolic Discovery from 1,106 Nights
papers.abstract: Human sleep is organized into a small number of cycles per night: deep sleep dominates early cycles, REM lengthens toward morning, and light sleep clusters at cycle boundaries. These regularities have long been described qualitatively but never distilled into closed-form laws from large-scale data. A total of 1,106 nights (Sleep-EDF 153 + SHHS 953) are segmented into REM-anchored cycles, and four cycle-indexed statistics follow simple closed-form equations: cycle length declines nearly linearly (R^2=0.996), REM duration follows an inverted U (R^2=0.873), deep-sleep (N3) run length decays exponentially (R^2=0.987) with a time constant of 2.94 cycles, consistent with the homeostatic Process S of the two-process model, and light-sleep (N1) run length follows a U shape (R^2=0.956), confirming a "long-short-long" pattern across the night. The laws are reproduced by per-night differentiable fitting (142/142 and 773/773 nights converge), by unconstrained symbolic regression (PySR), and by a 500-night generative synthesizer built from them. Their robustness is established against the two main methodological threats: bootstrap CIs computed by resampling whole nights (1,000 replications) exclude zero for every shape term, and a five-level scan of the REM-merge segmentation threshold preserves every qualitative form. These appear to be the first closed-form laws governing the macro-structure of sleep, distilled and tested across an age-mixed sample (healthy young adults and community-based older adults).

papers.title: OCBI: Order-Sensitive Cross-Branch Interaction for Image Manipulation Localization
papers.abstract: Image manipulation localization combines semantic structure with forensic traces to identify modified pixels. Within-branch spatial mixing and RGB-guided cross-branch mixing can produce different messages when composed in opposite orders. We propose OCBI, an extension of Co-Transformers that models the discrepancy between these two composition orders for localization. A local cross-branch fusion module uses the commutator of RGB-guided cross-attention and forensic self-attention to add a learnable signed correction to feature transfer. Pixelwise adaptive multiscale aggregation then combines spatial contexts before prediction. OCBI uses the Co-Transformers backbone and supervision. We compare OCBI with retrained Co-Transformers using CASIA-only task training, a 50-epoch budget, and final-epoch evaluation. Across five clean test datasets, OCBI achieves a macro PixelF1 of 0.5773, exceeding the baseline by 0.43 percentage points. Under JPEG compression, Gaussian blur, and resizing on three datasets, its average PixelF1 over 21 dataset-transformation conditions exceeds the baseline by 0.95 percentage points.

papers.title: When GL(2) cusp forms meet CM points in GSp(4)
papers.abstract: Duke's equidistribution theorem shows that the nonconstant contribution of the $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ automorphic spectrum to CM packets becomes asymptotically negligible. CM packets on the Levi base index the fibers of Bessel quotients in $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$, and the symmetric cube correspondence carries $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ cusp forms to $\mathrm{GL}(4)$. In the holomorphic setting considered here, these two constructions meet inside $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$. We prove averaged decay for the resulting class group periods over imaginary quadratic fields, expressed as averages of conditional fiber integrals. More precisely, let $f$ be a non-CM holomorphic Hecke newform with trivial central character. The mean absolute value of the associated class-group averages tends to zero along the transverse unipotent direction.

papers.title: Geometry of Confabulation and Refusal in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Faced with an unanswerable question, small language models can either refuse or confabulate: confidently produce a wrong answer. Can the hidden state before the first generated token provide a clue? Can we flip confabulations into refusals? I introduce ConfabQA, a 784-item benchmark whose obscure-pre-cutoff category breaks the typical correctness/knowledge-cutoff confound and map the geometry of the hidden state with linear probes, a sparse autoencoder (SAE), and direct optimization of intervention directions. On Qwen3-1.7B and Gemma 2 2B the probe separates upcoming refusals from confabulations well beyond prompt features (+7.4/+16.3 pp); on Llama 3.2 3B the ConfabQA margin is within fold-to-fold spread, but a direct refusal probe on PopQA and TriviaQA recovers +18-25 pp. On Qwen I closely inspect three candidate directions for the refusal vector: probe-recovered, Qwen-Scope SAE feature, and directly optimized. Although the three directions are pairwise 50-81 degrees apart, a push at or below the state's own norm along any of them flips most confabulations into refusal openings dominated by the "As..." family. Forcing the opener without touching the hidden state yields the same one-in-three judged-refusal rate as any push. The opposite push collapses refusals mostly into confabulations, yet leaves originally correct answers intact, so the direction gates the opening speech act rather than the knowledge behind it. Confabulations do not resolve into a concentrated feature in a dictionary or a token signature on Qwen3-1.7B. Scoring every probe on the margin over the strongest of four prompt-feature baselines extracts the hidden state's own contribution. Correctness signal is model-dependent and portable only for Llama 3.2 3B: 81% of the probe's margin over test majority survives transfer between ConfabQA, PopQA, and TriviaQA. Benchmark, judge, and code are released.

papers.title: Bounds for the binary quartic Weyl sum
papers.abstract:
We prove that
  $$ \sum_{1\le x,y\le N} e(\alpha F(x,y)) \ll_{F,\alpha,\epsilon}N^{5/3+\epsilon} $$
  for every $\epsilon>0$, real quadratic irrational $\alpha$, and integral binary quartic form $F$ that is not the fourth power of a linear form over $\mathbb{C}$. The proof uses the two-dimensional $q$-analogue of van der Corput's method, following Heath-Brown's work in the one-variable case. The heart of our argument rests on new bounds for complete binary cubic Weyl sums with linear terms, which retain the dependence on the cubic discriminant and the linear coefficients.

More recently, Maynard [15] used the circle method together with sieve methods to prove that there are infinitely many primes omitting any one prescribed decimal digit.

papers.title: Written Once, Read Differently How Language Models Own Answers Steer Their Next Ones
papers.abstract: When a language model answers a yes/no question, that answer changes how it answers a different question about the same entity. We study this \emph{self-commitment} in 22 open-weight models from four families (0.5B--72B parameters), fixing the model's first answer and measuring the shift in its second across 3,600 question pairs about 120 entities. Each answer writes a \emph{commitment direction} into the residual stream. The similarity of two questions' directions predicts their coupling on held-out entities ($\rho = 0.43$--$0.85$), and ablating a single direction shared across topics leaves at most 17\% of the effect in every model. How this direction is read is far less stable: the reading circuit spreads across more attention heads as models grow, instruction tuning makes more questions read it in the opposite sense, and in one model changing only the system prompt reverses the circuit's sign. Ablating the direction while sparing the attention sink removes most of the coupling at under 1.3\% perplexity cost in 18 of 19 instruction-tuned models, though it shifts standalone answers in two. Without the sink spared, the direction's alignment with the leading principal component of ordinary text predicts which models pay a high cost. Written once, the commitment is read differently across scale, training and prompt.

papers.title: Completing the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras obtained from abelian extensions. Using this family and bosonization, we complete the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also determine the duals of the semisimple classes with nonzero odd part and give tables of the complete classification.

papers.title: Quantum Generalized Cluster Algebras from Scattering Diagrams: Positivity and Mutation
papers.abstract: We construct generalized quantum cluster scattering diagrams over a ring of formal reciprocal exchange coefficients, for compatible seeds satisfying \(\widetilde B^T\Lambda=[I_n\mid0].\) A central lattice extension records the roots of the exchange polynomials as independent degrees. Applying Davison--Mandel positivity in this extension and proving a positive cylinder projection theorem yields positive wall factorizations and theta coefficients in the root variables. Their regular classical limits recover generalized cluster scattering diagrams. Nonvanishing under classical specialization, together with control of the mutated positive monoids, gives quantum mutation compatibility. The resulting scattering atlas has the generalized cluster fan, and every reachable cluster monomial is a theta function. Classical detection of theta coefficients gives a geometric proof of the Laurent phenomenon, with positivity after adjoining the polynomial roots. Evaluation of the exchange coefficients recovers the generalized quantum cluster algebras with this normalization. The Fock--Goncharov mutation product becomes a wall-crossing action, identifying extended \(g\)-vectors with leading theta exponents and \(F\)-polynomials with the coefficient factors on their right. Constructing these polynomials before evaluation gives the separation formula for arbitrary prescribed reciprocal Laurent polynomial coefficients, without requiring positivity at \(t=1.\) Positivity in the roots is distinguished throughout from positivity in the exchange coefficients.

papers.title: Promotion and Extension of General Escape-Covering Duality Relationship
papers.abstract:
Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, Moser's worm problem, Lebesgue's universal covering problems, and the classical 'fits and covers' questions can be organized by a common obstruction principle: an object fits a region if some admissible group action places it in the region, whereas an escape object is one for which every placement fails to remain in the interior.
  In this paper, we develop a general theory of escape-covering duality for any dimension and explore several applications. For convex translation covers of all closed planar curves of Euclidean length one, we prove $
  W \ge f(\sqrt3/9)+c_1>0.15545785378555,c_1=0.000009944944227372... $ Here $f(\sqrt3/9)$ is Wetzel's classical lower bound.
  For a rational polytopal Minkowski gauge and prescribed rational facet directions, we express universal closed-loop cover feasibility as a rational polyhedron in the facet offsets. After removing translations, minimum volume is attained at a vertex. Refining the facet directions gives explicit two-sided rational bounds for the unrestricted fixed-gauge worm constant. Four exact benchmarks recover known sharp values. The construction uses an elementary circuit--circumradius form of the established non-fitting-polygon and capacity theory. We supply its support and ledger derivation, the finite complete test family in arbitrary dimension, a cover vertex bound, and the resulting algebraicity statement.
  The surrounding escape--covering framework includes endpoint placement, attainment, gauge stability, and finite-to-continuum error bounds. For nonsymmetric gauges the objects are parametrized closed curves, so orientation-dependent length is retained. Through the published capacity identity, the improved Wetzel estimate gives a product volume--capacity factor below $1.023781939711102$ for every planar ellipsoidal gauge.

papers.title: LADS: Lease-Aware Delivery Scheduling of Tool Results for Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Web agents complete multi-step online tasks through repeated browser actions and model calls. Their returned observations lie on the critical path to subsequent decisions. When concurrent browser actions finish in bursts, observations can accumulate on a constrained return path to a shared inference service, while waiting histories compete for reusable cache state. Conventional delivery rules prioritize short transfers or immediate cache reuse but overlook how sending a result earlier can help a request resume sooner and free cache-protection capacity for other waiting requests. We present LADS (Lease-Aware Delivery Scheduling), a tool-result scheduler that couples cache-aware delivery with bounded prefix leases. Its key insight is that resumption lets extra protection references retire, making lease quota available to protect another waiting history. LADS prioritizes timely handoffs using current lease ownership and an estimated resumption delay, with bounded departures from Cache-first order. Compared with ReAct using first-in, first-out (FIFO) tool-result delivery, LADS reduces mean complete-workflow latency by 44.6% under bursty tool returns and by 42.4% on Web-derived burst replay.

authors.name: Linshan Jiang
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks
papers.abstract: The absolute trajectory error (ATE) is the standard measure of camera-motion accuracy, from SLAM to feed-forward 3D reconstruction. On the common Sintel protocol, a constant-velocity straight line using no images has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code. Two properties of ATE's alignment explain this. First, it maps any constant-velocity prediction onto the best-fitting line through the true path, so the line scores the path's regression residual. A residual signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion predicts when moving a prediction towards its constant-velocity fit lowers ATE. It gives the outcome for 95% of 1056 model-clip pairs, 98% of 792 held-out pairs and 97% of 1034 ScanNet pairs, and it separates Sintel (median SNR 0.86) from TUM, ScanNet and full-length Bonn and Wild-SLAM (2.7 to 27), where straightening raises every model's mean ATE. Second, position-only alignment ignores where cameras look: rotating a trajectory by 30 degrees against its orientations leaves ATE unchanged, yet worsens the reprojection of static points for every model on Sintel, TUM and ScanNet in the main setting, and the line, second by mean ATE on Sintel, places them worst by geometric mean: a lower ATE need not mean better geometry. Fitting the alignment's rotation to the predicted orientations gives pose-anchored ATE, a one-function change in ATE's units costing 0.17 ms per clip (ATE: 0.11 ms). It ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel, tracks the reprojection error under rotation and straightening, where ATE does not (Spearman 0.61 vs. 0.32), largely preserves the models' order, and ties 10-frame translational relative pose error (RPE) and the discernible trajectory error (DTE) on our rotation and reference tests. Code, predictions and results will be released.

papers.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds FTRL for Linear Bandits: The Interplay of Information Acquisition, Corruption, and Geometry
papers.abstract: We study \textit{best-of-both-worlds} (BOBW) algorithms for linear bandits, which aim to simultaneously guarantee $\gO(\sqrt T)$ regret in the adversarial regime and $\gO(\log T)$ regret in the stochastic regime over $T$ rounds. For finite action sets, we introduce \emph{information-acquisition follow-the-regularized-leader} (\IAFTRL{}), the first BOBW algorithm based purely on the follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) framework that attains an $\gO(\cstar\log T)$-type regret in the stochastic regime, where $\cstar$ is the information-acquisition complexity that characterizes instance-dependent optimality in linear bandits, while retaining the $\gO(\sqrt{T})$ regret guarantee in the adversarial regime. This resolves the open problem posed in~\cite{LeeEtAl2021,KongZ023,ItoT23,ZhaoItoLi2025}.

papers.title: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.

papers.title: S1CogBench: What System One Decision Models Can and Cannot Do on Cognitive Experiments
papers.abstract: Language models are no longer used only to generate text. Software also asks them for decisions, in routing, guardrails, and automated gates. System One decision models, also called typed decision models, such as Jev and Laya, return one fast decision over the legal options, leaving no text to inspect. However, a fast, well-formed decision does not show that the model used the evidence. Cognitive experiments can test this, because they vary task demands and measure how behavior changes, yet existing cognitive benchmarks evaluate language and multimodal models. We introduce S1CogBench to ask what these models can and cannot do on 24 cognitive tasks, evaluating five open models and Jev and keeping conditions and scoring apart from disclosed adaptations. We find that decision models vary widely in reliability, acting well does not imply predicting humans, aggregate scores hide how decisions respond to conditions, and speed comes mainly from answering without generation. To our knowledge, S1CogBench is the first benchmark of System One decision models on established cognitive experiments, and it gives a shared test of whether their decisions respond to evidence, feedback, memory load, and future opportunities before software relies on them.

papers.title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
papers.abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain \Omega in \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (\Delta t=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);

papers.title: Optimal L^2 Error Estimates for CSLDG Ideal Numerical Solutions in Time-Dependent Compressible Periodic Flows
papers.abstract: We study the characteristic Galerkin-type semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element (CSLDG) method for conservative linear transport equations. When the characteristic maps and upstream regions are exact, each update of the ideal CSLDG scheme is equivalent to exact conservative transport of the current numerical solution followed by L^2 projection onto the background DG space. The conventional estimate obtained by accumulating projection errors over successive time steps loses one order when \Delta t\asymp h, but this loss does not represent the actual accuracy of the scheme. For smooth velocity fields \A(\x,t) on a common periodic lattice, we construct local correctors used only in the analysis on uniform Cartesian meshes, assuming that \Delta t/h is fixed and that every component of the local Courant vector remains uniformly separated from the integers throughout the space-time domain. We prove strict contraction of the reference-cell transport-projection operator on the zero-mean polynomial space, establish uniform solvability of the corrector equation and Lipschitz estimates with respect to its parameter, and control the difference between the exact flow map and a local frozen translation through weak integral moments. This yields a one-step residual of order O(h^{K+2}), and, while retaining the step-by-step update and the standard L^2-projected initial data, gives, for the P^K approximation, an optimal O(h^{K+1}) error bound. The velocity may depend on both space and time, and incompressibility is not required. An appendix extends the analysis to a compact-support setting, in which the velocity field and the solution need not share a common spatial period.

papers.title: Cutoff and a Gaussian-shift profile for the Rudvalis shuffle
papers.abstract:
The Rudvalis shuffle removes the top card and reinserts it uniformly at random in one of the bottom two positions. Hildebrand proved the classical upper bound $O(n^3\log n)$, and Wilson later proved the sharp lower coefficient $1/(8\pi^2)$, establishing the correct order but leaving the leading upper constant, cutoff, and the cutoff profile open. We prove that the full labelled shuffle has total-variation cutoff at \[
  \frac{n^3\log n}{8\pi^2} \] with a window of order $n^3$.
  The upper bound is obtained by writing one deterministic rotation of the shuffle as a nonnormal sweep of adjacent averaging projections, comparing that sweep to a weighted interchange generator, and controlling the entire regular-representation heat trace. The key sharp-window ingredients are heat-kernel smoothing through the Octopus Inequality, zero extension of deletion-harmonic ordered-tuple functions, a representation-theoretic multiplicity payment, and a sectorwise entrance estimate that disposes of all large Young-diagram deficits. For the profile, an exact complex one-card eigenfunction yields a deck statistic whose surviving first Fourier mode converges to a Gaussian shift. A matching full-deck $L^2$ bound then shows that this one-dimensional Gaussian likelihood ratio asymptotically exhausts all remaining information, giving the exact total-variation profile.

papers.title: Adhesive riffle shuffles: one-parameter models and mixing bounds
papers.abstract: We compare four simple shuffles with one adhesion parameter $p$: a card-weighted sticky riffle, a block-weighted riffle, a midpoint-interpolation shuffle, and a correlated-label inverse riffle. Independent surviving contacts create contiguous blocks; no force or energy constants are fitted. We give polynomial upper bounds with explicit dependence on $p$, common adjacency-survival lower bounds, and a sharper information lower bound for interpolation. For fixed deck size $n\ge4$, the mixing time diverges as $\Theta((1-p)^{-1})$ for the three cut-first models, but as $\Theta((1-p)^{-2})$ for the correlated-label model. The latter distinction comes from whether one or two additional contact breaks are needed to escape cyclic rotations. For even $n$, unglued interpolation retains the lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt n\log n)$ and upper bound $O(n^{5/2}\log n)$. We distinguish proved bounds from conjectured scales, recover classical riffle cutoff under sufficiently small perturbations, and explain precisely where established results on clumpy shuffles apply. The fixed-parameter asymptotic orders of the new cut-first families and their possible cutoff remain unresolved.

papers.title: Optimal Fan-Out and Break-Even Routing Loss in Waveguide-Integrated Ge-on-Si SPAD Arrays
papers.abstract: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts. We quantify this trade-off with the asymptotic count-based information rate, which prices dark counts and dead time in one unit and is attained by an optimally weighted moment estimator. For a non-paralyzable pixel, the information per pre-dead-time signal event peaks at a signal rate $y^*=\sqrt{D(D+1/\tau)}$ with exact efficiency $(\sqrt{1+D\tau}-\sqrt{D\tau})^2$, which sets the optimal fan-out and a critical flux above which equal splitting is optimal. We then compare four routing architectures on 64 simulated 16-pixel arrays: an equal passive tree, static trees (uncalibrated, and an idealized calibration-informed benchmark), an ideal programmable tree, and a thermo-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) tree with 1.32 dB excess loss. Ideal programmability gains up to 15.9 dB over equal splitting at low flux. At one known flux, however, the calibrated static splitter beats the MZI tree by 0.14-2.7 dB, and the penalty tends to twice the excess loss when dark counts dominate. In ensemble-median worst-case regret, the MZI tree breaks even only for flux windows wider than 2.55 decades, and not within six decades above about 3.4 dB excess loss. Event-level Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the count statistics and the predicted estimator variances within bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses cover dark-count level, heterogeneity, detector model and random seed. All results are simulations with representative literature parameters.

authors.name: Pittaya Pannil
authors.institution: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang

papers.title: ICJ-Graph: A Citation Graph and a Layered Document Corpus of the International Court of Justice
papers.abstract: We present ICJ-Graph, a machine-readable resource connecting documents of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to cited cases, legal provisions and United Nations resolutions. Court decisions, written pleadings and oral records form distinct document layers, preserving the distinction between the Court's reasoning and the parties' submissions. The collection contains 6,396 ICJ documents and 505 documents from other courts and legal bodies, together with 12,375 provisions and 20,291 UN resolutions. The data files contain text, metadata and embeddings. The accompanying pipeline lets users load the graph and generate embeddings for use in their own retrieval systems. To illustrate the resource's use, we evaluate five models on citation prediction for 199 decisions using documents available before each decision. Tools designed for citation research improve citation-prediction F1 over answering without tools for all five models across case, provision and resolution citations.

authors.name: Pawitsapak Akarajaradwong
authors.institution: Vidyasirimedhi Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: EffComp: Efficient Prompt Compression via Hybrid Reinforcement & Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: Prompt compression is aimed at reducing input prompt lengths to enable cheaper, faster, and potentially higher-quality LLM predictions. However, existing prompt compression methods are often limited by modest compression gains, a risk of hallucination, and/or high compression latency. We propose EffComp, an Efficient prompt Compression framework for RAG-based question answering (QA). EffComp employs BERT-style document reranker and sentence selector models to allow fast extractive prompt compression at the sentence level. Its extractive nature prevents hallucinations in the compressed prompts. Additionally, the training process using a hybrid reinforcement and supervised learning approach is designed to optimize the compression ratio while preserving LLM accuracy. Experiments on various QA datasets demonstrate that EffComp outperforms state-of-the-art prompt compression methods achieving the best trade-off between compression ratio and accuracy with minimal latency. This makes it practical for real-world applications.

papers.title: NitiBench+: A Temporal Thai Legal Question Answering Benchmark Across 17 Domains
papers.abstract: Law changes over time. A court decides a case under the law in force on that day, and legal QA benchmarks grade answers against today's law. We checked 156,650 decisions of four Thai courts. Up to 67% of them cite law that has since been amended or repealed. We introduce NitiBench+, the sequel of our NitiBench, a Thai legal QA benchmark with 1,670 items across 17 domains, built from decisions of three courts. For each cited section it holds both the text in force on the decision date and the current text, and its retrieval corpus holds every dated version of every Thai statute section. Answers are graded on the Thai Bar Council rubric, the Bar-standard score, and on the overlap between the cited sections and the court's. The report has two parts. Part I measures the cost of the wrong text on 13 open-weight models. Reading the current text of amended law drops the Bar-standard score by 0.25 and missing repealed law drops it by 0.79. The penalty comes from rule changes, 0.45 on the 428 rule-changed items and none on the 331 wording-only items, and Citation F1 does not see it. The text in force is the fair setting. Part II benchmarks today's models on that setting. A public leaderboard ranks 26 models on a held-out test split of 500 items stratified by domain, with a validation split of the same shape released for public use, from memory alone, with the court's sections provided, and as a retrieval agent over the law in force, with the cost per item and the hallucinated citations. The best model scores 7.78 out of 10 and the best open-weight model 6.39. Without a search tool only five open-weight models recall any Thai law, and with it twenty of the 26 models gain and six lose. Leaderboard will take new models as they are released. Legal benchmarks must track dates, and on the right text today's models still leave a wide gap on Thai law.
